- `command`:

```
jq --version && mkdir -p .claude/hooks docs/agent-log && cat > .claude/hooks/transcript-to-md.jq <<'EOF'
# Render a Claude Code JSONL transcript as readable Markdown.
#
# Usage: jq -rs --arg h "##" -f transcript-to-md.jq transcript.jsonl
#   $h  heading prefix for each turn ("##" for the main session, "###" for subagents)
#
# One record per JSONL line. Only user / assistant / non-meta system records are
# rendered; bookkeeping records (attachment, mode, snapshots, ...) are skipped.
# Assistant records arrive one content block per line, so consecutive records
# from the same role are merged under a single heading. Tool results (user
# records that only carry tool_result blocks) are kept inside the assistant turn.

def fence(s):
  ([s | scan("`+") | length] | max // 0) as $m
  | ("`" * ([3, $m + 1] | max)) as $f
  | "\($f)\n\(s)\n\($f)";

def escape_tags:
  gsub("<(?<t>/?system-reminder)>"; "&lt;\(.t)&gt;");

def details(summary; body):
  "<details>\n<summary>\(summary)</summary>\n\n\(body)\n\n</details>";

def ts:
  (.timestamp // "") | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z");

def inline_ok:
  (test("[`\n]") | not) and (length <= 120);

def render_input:
  if type == "object" then
    [ to_entries[]
      | .key as $k | .value as $v
      | if ($v | type) == "string" then
          if ($v | inline_ok) then "- `\($k)`: `\($v)`"
          else "- `\($k)`:\n\n\(fence($v))" end
        else "- `\($k)`: `\($v | tojson)`" end
    ] | join("\n")
  else fence(tojson) end;

def result_text:
  .content
  | if type == "string" then .
    elif type == "array" then
      [ .[] | if .type == "text" then .text
              elif .type == "image" then "[image]"
              else tojson end ] | join("\n")
    else (. // "" | tostring) end;

def block:
  if .type == "text" then (.text | escape_tags)
  elif .type == "thinking" then details("Thinking"; (.thinking // "") | escape_tags)
  elif .type == "tool_use" then
    "**Tool call:** `\(.name)` <sub>\(.id)</sub>\n\n\(.input | render_input)"
  elif .type == "tool_result" then
    ("**Tool result" + (if .is_error == true then " (error)" else "" end)
      + "** <sub>\(.tool_use_id)</sub>") as $s
    | details($s; fence(result_text | escape_tags))
  elif .type == "image" then "[image]"
  else fence(tojson) end;

def is_tool_result_only:
  .type == "user"
  and (.message.content | type) == "array"
  and (.message.content | length) > 0
  and all(.message.content[]; .type == "tool_result");

def role:
  if is_tool_result_only then "assistant" else .type end;

def label:
  if .type == "user" then "User"
  elif .type == "assistant" then "Assistant"
  else "System" end;

def heading:
  "\($h) \(label) <sub>\(ts)</sub>";

def body:
  if .type == "system" then
    "> **system\(if .subtype then " (\(.subtype))" else "" end):** \((.content // "") | tostring | escape_tags)"
  elif (.message.content | type) == "string" then
    (.message.content | escape_tags)
  else
    [ .message.content[] | block ] | join("\n\n")
  end;

def renderable:
  ((.type == "user" or .type == "assistant") and .message != null)
  or (.type == "system" and .isMeta != true and .content != null);

map(select(renderable))
| reduce .[] as $r ({prev: null, out: []};
    ($r | role) as $role
    | .out += (if $role != .prev then [($r | heading)] else [] end) + [($r | body)]
    | .prev = $role)
| .out
| join("\n\n")
EOF
echo written
```

````
cat > .claude/hooks/export-session.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SessionEnd hook: export the session transcript (plus any subagent transcripts)
# to docs/agent-log/<session-id>.md and commit that file.
#
# Reads the hook payload on stdin:
#   {"session_id": "...", "transcript_path": "...", "cwd": "...", "reason": "..."}
# Can also be run by hand with the same JSON on stdin.
#
# Dependencies: bash, jq, git.
set -uo pipefail

here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
filter="$here/transcript-to-md.jq"

input=$(cat)
sid=$(jq -r '.session_id // empty' <<<"$input")
tp=$(jq -r '.transcript_path // empty' <<<"$input")
reason=$(jq -r '.reason // "manual"' <<<"$input")
cwd=$(jq -r '.cwd // empty' <<<"$input")
root=$(git -C "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-${cwd:-$here}}" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$(git -C "$here" rev-parse --show-toplevel)

if [[ -z "$sid" || -z "$tp" ]]; then
  echo "export-session: missing session_id or transcript_path in hook input" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [[ ! -s "$tp" ]]; then
  echo "export-session: transcript $tp missing or empty, nothing to export" >&2
  exit 0
fi

outdir="$root/docs/agent-log"
out="$outdir/$sid.md"
mkdir -p "$outdir"

render() { # render <heading-prefix> ; records on stdin
  jq -rs --arg h "$1" -f "$filter"
}

meta() { # meta <jq expr> over the main transcript
  jq -rs "$1" "$tp"
}

{
  echo "# Agent session $sid"
  echo
  echo "| | |"
  echo "|---|---|"
  echo "| Project | \`$(meta '[.[] | .cwd // empty] | first // ""')\` |"
  echo "| Branch | \`$(meta '[.[] | .gitBranch // empty] | first // ""')\` |"
  echo "| Claude Code | $(meta '[.[] | .version // empty] | first // ""') |"
  echo "| Started | $(meta '[.[] | .timestamp // empty] | min // ""') |"
  echo "| Last record | $(meta '[.[] | .timestamp // empty] | max // ""') |"
  echo "| Exported | $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) (reason: $reason) |"
  echo "| Source | \`$tp\` |"
  echo
  jq -c 'select(.isSidechain != true)' "$tp" | render "##"

  # Subagent transcripts, newer layout: <transcript-dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-*.jsonl
  subdir="${tp%.jsonl}/subagents"
  if [[ -d "$subdir" ]]; then
    for f in "$subdir"/*.jsonl; do
      [[ -s "$f" ]] || continue
      name=$(basename "$f" .jsonl)
      echo; echo "---"; echo
      echo "## Subagent \`$name\`"
      echo
      echo "Source: \`$f\`"
      echo
      jq -c '.' "$f" | render "###"
    done
  fi

  # Subagent transcripts, older layout: sidechain records inside the main file.
  for agent in $(jq -r 'select(.isSidechain == true) | .agentId // "sidechain"' "$tp" | sort -u); do
    echo; echo "---"; echo
    echo "## Subagent \`$agent\` (inline sidechain)"
    echo
    jq -c --arg a "$agent" 'select(.isSidechain == true and ((.agentId // "sidechain") == $a))' "$tp" | render "###"
  done
} > "$out.tmp" && mv "$out.tmp" "$out"

echo "export-session: wrote ${out#$root/}" >&2

# Commit only this file, leaving any other staged or unstaged work untouched.
git -C "$root" add -- "$out"
if git -C "$root" diff --cached --quiet -- "$out"; then
  echo "export-session: no changes to commit" >&2
  exit 0
fi
if git -C "$root" commit -q --only -m "docs(agent-log): export session $sid" -- "$out"; then
  echo "export-session: committed $(git -C "$root" rev-parse --short HEAD)" >&2
else
  echo "export-session: commit failed, export left in working tree" >&2
fi
EOF
chmod +x .claude/hooks/export-session.sh
cat > .claude/settings.json <<'EOF'
{
  "hooks": {
    "SessionEnd": [
      {
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/.claude/hooks/export-session.sh",
            "timeout": 120
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF
cat > docs/agent-log/README.md <<'EOF'
# Agent session log

Every Claude Code session run in this repository is exported here as Markdown
when the session ends, by the `SessionEnd` hook configured in
`.claude/settings.json` (`.claude/hooks/export-session.sh`).

- One file per session, named `<session-id>.md`. A resumed session keeps its
  id, so it overwrites its own earlier export.
- The export contains the full main transcript (user prompts, assistant text,
  thinking, tool calls and tool results) followed by one section per subagent
  transcript spawned from that session.
- The hook commits the exported file on its own (`docs(agent-log): export
  session <id>`), touching nothing else in the index.

To export the current session by hand:

```sh
printf '{"session_id":"%s","transcript_path":"%s","cwd":"%s","reason":"manual"}' \
  "$SID" "$HOME/.claude/projects/<encoded-project-path>/$SID.jsonl" "$PWD" \
  | .claude/hooks/export-session.sh
```
EOF
jq . .claude/settings.json >/dev/null && echo settings ok; git status --short
````

The transcript export hook is in place, verified by a real run, and the export is committed.

**What was added** (all committed on `main`, tree is clean):

- `.claude/settings.json` registers a `SessionEnd` hook that runs the export script.
- `.claude/hooks/export-session.sh` reads the hook payload from stdin, renders the transcript, writes `docs/agent-log/<session-id>.md`, and commits only that file. It uses `git commit --only`, so other staged or unstaged work is never swept into the commit. If rendering fails it aborts before writing or committing.
- `.claude/hooks/transcript-to-md.jq` is the jq filter that turns the JSONL into Markdown. User and assistant turns get headings with timestamps. Tool calls show their inputs, and tool results and thinking are collapsed in `<details>` blocks. Fences grow when content itself contains backticks.
- Subagent transcripts are appended as their own sections, from both the `<session-id>/subagents/*.jsonl` directory layout and from inline sidechain records in the main file.
- `docs/agent-log/README.md` explains the layout and how to run the export by hand.

**Proof run:** I piped a SessionEnd-style payload for this session into the script. It wrote `docs/agent-log/31d666d4-9d83-44bd-bae6-ef26e807eeb3.md` and committed it as `docs(agent-log): export session …`. The first attempt exposed two bugs, which I fixed and committed: `label` is a reserved jq word, and the script originally committed even when jq failed.

**Two things to know:**

- Claude Code snapshots hook config at startup, so this session may not fire the new hook on exit. Run `/hooks` to approve the change or start a new session. Every future session picks it up automatically.
- Most thinking blocks in the transcript are stored empty by Claude Code, so only the few with content appear in the export.

I read the brief. The main things it adds to your description: a **3 to 5 hour timebox**, the agent log must be scrubbed of personal info, data must be reproducible from a committed sample, and the README must carry the run command, provenance and limitations. The hook export is already committed and only leaks your home directory path, which I will redact in the hook before we start. Below are the stack options, my recommendation per item, and the questions I need answered before writing `docs/DECISIONS.md`.

## Stack options

**1. Backend and data layer**
- (a) **FastAPI + pandas over committed CSV/Parquet rate tables, loaded in memory (recommended).** The rate cards are a few thousand rows. No database, no migrations, trivial Docker.
- (b) FastAPI + DuckDB. Nice SQL for aggregations over uploaded parcel sets, one more dependency.
- (c) FastAPI + SQLite. Only worth it if we want to persist user uploads between runs.
- Tooling either way: `uv`, Pydantic models for the rate engine, pytest.

**2. Data collection**
- Python scripts under `data/` that download carrier rate documents, parse them with pdfplumber or straight CSV, and write normalized tables that we commit. The app never fetches live, which satisfies the brief and earns the scraping bonus if documented.

**3. Frontend**
- Vite + React + TypeScript is fixed. Chart library options:
  - (a) **Recharts (recommended).** Declarative React, small bundle, good for the line and stacked bar charts in questions 1, 3 and 4. The breakeven map in question 2 is a weight by distance grid, which I would render as a plain SVG heatmap component, since that is about 40 lines and avoids a heavy library.
  - (b) Chart.js via react-chartjs-2. Fine, needs a matrix plugin for the heatmap.
  - (c) Plotly. Heatmaps and contours out of the box, but over 1 MB of JavaScript, and it fights the mobile layout.
- Styling: plain CSS with design tokens, or Tailwind. I lean plain CSS with tokens, with a deliberate visual direction rather than a generic dashboard grid.

**4. Docker**
- (a) **docker compose with two services (recommended):** backend on uvicorn, frontend built by Vite and served by nginx, which proxies `/api` to the backend. One command: `docker compose up --build`.
- (b) One multi-stage image where FastAPI serves the built static files. Simpler for the reviewer, worse for development.

**5. Tests**
- Data pipeline: pytest with golden samples of each source document.
- Rate engine and API: pytest, including hand-checked prices from the published rate cards.
- Frontend: Vitest plus Testing Library for components.
- End to end: Playwright at 1440 and 375 wide, with screenshots that an agent reviews for UX, not just assertions.

**6. Workflow**
- GitHub issues per task, a branch and worktree per issue, parallel agents each in their own worktree, pull requests merged with merge commits so the history shows the evolution. Each agent session exports its own log through the hook we just set up.

## Data sources I know of (to be verified in the data task)

- **USPS:** PostalPro publishes price change files per rate event as CSV or XLSX, covering Ground Advantage, Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express by zone and weight. Nonstandard and peak surcharges are listed in Notice 123. Multiple increases per year.
- **UPS:** yearly "Daily Rates" PDF with Ground, 3 Day Select, 2nd Day Air and Next Day Air by zone and weight, plus a surcharge table. Older years likely only via the Wayback Machine.
- **FedEx:** yearly "Standard List Rates" PDF with the same structure, plus residential, delivery area, additional handling and oversize surcharges.
- **Fuel surcharges:** weekly percentages for UPS and FedEx, with historical tables on their sites. This is the largest surcharge and changes weekly, so it needs a design decision (see question 6).
- **Announced increases:** the general rate increase each carrier announces for the year, used as the benchmark in question 4.
- **Distance to zone:** carriers use origin and destination ZIP pairs, but zones map closely to distance bands, so a documented distance to zone table covers your "distance it travels" input without scraping zone charts.

## Questions

1. **Timebox.** The brief asks for 3 to 5 hours of focused work. Issues, parallel agents, full test coverage and screenshot reviews on two viewports will go beyond that. Are you fine exceeding it, or should I size the issue list to fit?
2. **GitHub repo.** There is no remote yet. Should I create `aivuk/parcel-rates` on GitHub, and public or private? Do you want pull requests per issue, or branches merged locally?
3. **Years.** Which range counts as a good range? I propose 2023 through 2026, since USPS Ground Advantage only exists since mid 2023 and older carrier PDFs get hard to find. If 2027 increases are already announced, we can add a projection.
4. **Services.** Three speed tiers across the three carriers: ground, 2 to 3 day, and next day. Weight cap at 70 lb, which is the USPS maximum. Agree?
5. **Parcel input.** Both a CSV upload and a built in sample mix? Proposed columns: weight, length, width, height, distance in miles or destination ZIP, residential flag, required speed, price charged to the customer. Do your parcels have dimensions? Dimensional weight changes the answer a lot for light bulky boxes.
6. **Fuel and peak surcharges.** These vary by week and season. I propose a per year default taken from the published history, plus a slider so the user can stress test, and a peak season toggle. Agree?
7. **Margin check.** Is the price charged to the customer a per parcel column, or a rule such as a flat rate or free shipping above an order value?
8. **Price increase what-if.** For "potential yearly price increase", do you want a slider for next year's increase on top of the historical comparison in question 4?
9. **Zone from distance.** Accept a distance band to zone mapping, documented as a limitation, or do you want real ZIP to ZIP zones, which means scraping zone charts?
10. **Agent log scrubbing.** I will redact the home directory path in the export. Anything else you want stripped, such as the GitHub username?

Once you answer, I will write `docs/DECISIONS.md`, open the issues, and start with the data availability and quality analysis.

a month, has no negotiated carrier contract, and pays the published list
prices of FedEx, UPS and the Postal Service. Today the carrier is chosen by
habit. The dashboard helps the owner choose the carrier per kind of parcel,
and check whether the flat shipping price charged to customers still covers
the real cost once surcharges and yearly price increases are included.

**Questions the dashboard answers.**

1. For a given parcel (weight, dimensions, distance, residential or business,
   required speed), which service is cheapest once surcharges are included,
   and what are the line items of that price?
2. Where are the breakeven points between the Postal Service and FedEx or UPS
   ground, by weight and distance?
3. For the owner's whole set of parcels, what is the blended cost per parcel
   with each carrier, and how much of it is surcharges rather than base rate?
4. How did that blended cost change year by year under each year's published
   prices, compared with the average increase the carriers announced, and
   which kinds of parcels in the mix drove the change?

**Scope decisions.**

- Timebox: issues are sized to fit about five hours of focused work (the
  brief's upper bound). Extras are tracked separately and only started if
  time remains. Time actually spent is recorded by the owner, not estimated.
- Services: three speed tiers across the three carriers — ground, two to
  three day, and next day. Weight capped at 70 lb (the USPS maximum).
- Years covered: decided after the data survey (issue 1), based on what can
  actually be downloaded and parsed reliably.
- Parcel input: CSV upload plus a bundled illustrative sample mix. Columns:
  weight, length, width, height, distance in miles, residential flag,
  required speed, and an optional per-parcel price charged to the customer.
  Dimensional weight is computed from the dimensions.
- Price charged to the customer: a single flat price is the MVP control. The
  optional per-parcel column overrides it when present.
- Fuel and peak surcharges: a documented per-year default taken from the
  published history, a slider to stress test the fuel percentage, and a peak
  season toggle. A next-year increase slider sits on the year-over-year view.
- Zone from distance: a documented distance-band to zone mapping. Real
  ZIP-to-ZIP zones are a bonus, not MVP.
- The app never fetches live data; all rate tables are committed.

## 2026-10-22 — Stack

| Area | Decision | Alternatives considered | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend | FastAPI, Pydantic models, pandas over committed CSV tables loaded in memory, managed with `uv` | DuckDB; SQLite | Rate cards are a few thousand rows. No database keeps Docker and setup trivial. |
| Data collection | Python scripts under `data/` that download the carriers' published rate documents, parse them (pdfplumber for PDFs), and write normalized CSVs that are committed | Hand-typed tables | Reproducible, documents provenance, and qualifies for the scraping bonus. |
| Frontend | Vite + React + TypeScript, Recharts for line and bar charts, a custom SVG heatmap for the breakeven map, plain CSS with design tokens | Chart.js (needs a matrix plugin for heatmaps); Plotly (over 1 MB, poor on mobile); Tailwind | Small bundle, declarative, the heatmap is a trivial grid. |
| Docker | `docker compose` with two services: uvicorn backend and an nginx container serving the Vite build and proxying `/api` | Single multi-stage image with FastAPI serving static files | Clean separation, one command for the reviewer. |
| Tests | pytest for pipeline, rate engine and API; Vitest + Testing Library for components; Playwright end to end at 1440 and 375 px with screenshots reviewed for UX | — | Required by the brief and by us. |
| Workflow | Private GitHub repo, one issue per task, a branch and git worktree per issue, parallel agents each in their own worktree, pull requests merged with merge commits | Commit straight to main | Keeps history and lets agents work in parallel without stepping on each other. |
| Agent log | `SessionEnd` hook exports every session (and subagent) transcript to `docs/agent-log/<session-id>.md` and commits it; home directory path redacted | Manual export | Required by the brief, zero effort once set up. |
EOF
git add docs/DECISIONS.md && git commit -q -m "docs: record scope and stack decisions" && gh repo create aivuk/parcel-rates --private --source=. --push 2>&1 | tail -2 && git remote -v | head -1
```

mk "Survey published carrier rate data and assess its quality" "MVP (5h)" "data,docs" "$(cat <<'EOF'
**Goal (~45 min).** Find what rate data USPS, UPS and FedEx publish for list prices, download what is usable, and write a quality assessment that decides which years and services the project covers.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Locate per-year published rate documents for USPS (Ground Advantage, Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express), UPS (Ground, 3 Day Select, 2nd Day Air, Next Day Air Saver) and FedEx (Ground, Home Delivery, Express Saver, 2Day, Standard Overnight), plus their surcharge tables (residential, delivery area, additional handling/oversize, peak) and fuel surcharge history.
- [ ] Locate the announced average general rate increase per carrier per year.
- [ ] Download raw sources into `data/raw/<carrier>/<year>/` with a `SOURCES.md` recording URL, retrieval date and method (direct download, Wayback Machine, scraping).
- [ ] Write `docs/data/QUALITY.md`: per source, format (CSV/XLSX/PDF/HTML), parse difficulty, years available, coverage gaps, licensing notes, and a recommended year range.
- [ ] Record the chosen year range in `docs/DECISIONS.md`.

**Done when** the raw sources are committed, the quality report exists, and the year range decision is written down.
EOF
)"
mk "Parse raw rate documents into normalized rate tables" "MVP (5h)" "data,tests" "$(cat <<'EOF'
**Goal (~45 min).** Turn the raw sources from #1 into committed, tested CSV tables the backend loads.

**Tables** (under `data/processed/`)
- `base_rates.csv`: carrier, service, year, zone, weight_lb, price
- `surcharges.csv`: carrier, year, surcharge, applies_to (service or all), amount, unit (flat or percent), condition (residential, delivery_area, additional_handling, oversize, peak)
- `fuel_surcharge.csv`: carrier, year, default_percent, note
- `announced_increase.csv`: carrier, year, percent, source
- `zone_from_distance.csv`: zone, min_miles, max_miles

**Tasks**
- [ ] Python parsers under `data/pipeline/` (pdfplumber for PDFs), one module per carrier, runnable with `uv run python -m data.pipeline`.
- [ ] Golden-sample tests: a handful of hand-checked prices per carrier and year must match the parsed output exactly.
- [ ] Schema validation of the output tables (no gaps in weight or zone coverage per service and year).

**Done when** the tables are committed, tests pass, and the pipeline is reproducible from the raw files.
EOF
)"
mk "Rate engine and FastAPI endpoints for the four dashboard questions" "MVP (5h)" "backend,tests" "$(cat <<'EOF'
**Goal (~60 min).** A pure-Python rate engine plus a thin FastAPI layer, with tests.

**Rate engine** (`backend/app/engine/`)
- [ ] Zone from distance (band table), billable weight = max(actual, dimensional) using each carrier's divisor and rules, rounding up to the next pound.
- [ ] Quote for one parcel and one service: base rate + each applicable surcharge as a line item (residential, delivery area, additional handling/oversize, peak, fuel percent applied to the right base), total.
- [ ] Cheapest service per speed tier for a parcel.
- [ ] Breakeven grid: for a weight × distance grid, which carrier's ground service wins and by how much.
- [ ] Blended cost for a parcel set per carrier, split into base vs surcharges, and the margin against the flat price charged (or the per-parcel column).
- [ ] Year-over-year blended cost under each year's prices vs the announced increase, with a breakdown by parcel segment (weight band, distance band, residential, speed) showing which segments drove the change.

**API** (`backend/app/api/`)
- [ ] `POST /api/quote`, `GET /api/breakeven`, `POST /api/blended`, `POST /api/yearly`, `GET /api/sample-parcels`, `GET /api/meta` (years, services, defaults).
- [ ] Parcel set input as JSON (the frontend parses CSV) with Pydantic validation and clear 422 errors.
- [ ] Controls as request fields: year, fuel percent override, peak toggle, flat price, next-year increase percent.

**Tests**
- [ ] pytest with hand-computed quotes, breakeven sanity (USPS wins light/near, loses heavy/far), blended totals, API contract tests.

**Done when** all endpoints work against the committed tables and tests pass.
EOF
)"
mk "Frontend scaffold, layout, parcel input and global controls" "MVP (5h)" "frontend,tests" "$(cat <<'EOF'
**Goal (~45 min).** Vite + React + TypeScript app with a deliberate visual direction, the parcel-set input, and the global controls shared by all views.

**Tasks**
- [ ] Scaffold under `frontend/` with Vite, React, TypeScript, Recharts, Vitest + Testing Library. Plain CSS with design tokens (`styles/tokens.css`), light theme by default, responsive down to 375 px.
- [ ] Pick and document a visual direction (editorial/Swiss, not a generic card grid). Clear hierarchy: the answer first, the controls second.
- [ ] Parcel set input: CSV upload (parsed client side, columns per `docs/DECISIONS.md`) and a "load sample mix" button. Show a summary of the loaded set (count, weight and distance distribution).
- [ ] Global controls: year, fuel surcharge slider with per-year default, peak toggle, flat price charged to customers. State mirrored to the URL.
- [ ] API client with typed responses; loading and error states.
- [ ] Component tests for the CSV parser and the controls.

**Done when** a reviewer can load the sample set, change controls, and see the set summary on desktop and mobile.
EOF
)"
mk "Views: single-parcel quote (Q1) and breakeven map (Q2)" "MVP (5h)" "frontend,tests" "$(cat <<'EOF'
**Goal (~30 min).**

**Q1 — Quote a parcel**
- [ ] Form: weight, dimensions, distance, residential, required speed.
- [ ] Result: cheapest service per carrier for the chosen speed, ranked, with the line items (base, each surcharge, fuel) and the margin against the flat price.

**Q2 — Breakeven map**
- [ ] Custom SVG heatmap, weight (rows) × distance (columns), cell colored by the winning ground carrier, intensity by the saving vs the runner-up; hover/tap shows the prices.
- [ ] Toggle residential vs business; reacts to the global fuel/peak/year controls.
- [ ] Short plain-language readout of where the breakeven lines sit.

**Done when** both views render from the API, respond to controls, and have component tests.
EOF
)"
mk "Views: blended cost per carrier (Q3) and year-over-year change (Q4)" "MVP (5h)" "frontend,tests" "$(cat <<'EOF'
**Goal (~30 min).**

**Q3 — Blended cost**
- [ ] Per carrier: blended cost per parcel, stacked bar of base vs each surcharge group, share of surcharges, and margin vs the flat price (and the share of parcels shipped at a loss).
- [ ] Segment filter: weight band, distance band, residential, speed.

**Q4 — Year over year**
- [ ] Line chart of blended cost per parcel per carrier per year under that year's published prices, with the carrier's announced average increase as a dashed reference.
- [ ] Driver breakdown: which parcel segments contributed most to the change between consecutive years.
- [ ] Next-year increase slider projecting the following year.

**Done when** both views render from the API, respond to controls and filters, and have component tests.
EOF
)"
mk "Docker compose, README and reviewer run path" "MVP (5h)" "infra,docs" "$(cat <<'EOF'
**Goal (~20 min).**
- [ ] `backend/Dockerfile` (uv, uvicorn), `frontend/Dockerfile` (Vite build, nginx serving static and proxying `/api`), `docker-compose.yml`.
- [ ] `docker compose up --build` brings the app up at a documented URL with the sample data available; no credentials, no manual steps.

**Done when** a clean clone runs with the README command and the dashboard is usable.

)"

Carrier: **USPS (United States Postal Service)**, domestic retail (published, non-contract) list prices.

What to find, per year, trying years 2022 through 2026 (today is 2026-10-22; note that USPS changes prices more than once a year, e.g. January and July):

Be strictly factual: never invent URLs, prices or percentages. If you quote a price or percentage, it must come from a document you fetched, and say which one. If something is unverified, say so.

Final report (to me, not a file): a concise summary of (a) which years/services are covered with usable files, (b) format and parse difficulty per year, (c) gaps, (d) your recommended year range for this carrier, (e) the exact list of files written.

cd ~/parcel-rates-issue-1 && cat > docs/data/QUALITY.md <<'EOF'
# Data availability and quality report

Issue #1. Survey date: 2026-10-22. Three agents, one per carrier, searched for
the published (non-contract, retail) US domestic parcel rates of USPS, UPS and
FedEx for 2022 through 2026, downloaded what they could, and recorded every
file with its URL, retrieval method and parse notes in
`data/raw/<carrier>/SOURCES.md`. This report consolidates their findings and
records the decisions that follow from them.

## Summary

| | USPS | UPS | FedEx |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base rate tables | Every price change 2022–2026 (15 events) | Yearly Daily Rates guide, 2022–2026 | Yearly Standard List Rates, 2022–2027 |
| Best format | CSV zip per price change (clean) | Text PDF only (tables span ~4 pages per service) | XLSX for 2022, 2025, 2026, 2027; text PDF for 2023, 2024 |
| Surcharge rules | Footnotes in Notice 123 PDFs | Surcharge section of the same guide (3-column prose) | Yearly "surcharge and fee changes" PDFs (2022, 2024–2026) plus Service Guides |
| Residential / delivery area | None (confirmed) | Residential, DAS, extended DAS amounts in guide; ZIP list not downloaded | Residential, DAS amounts; DAS ZIP lists downloaded for every year |
| Dimensional weight | Over 1 cu ft, greater of actual and dim weight; divisor not printed in Notice 123 (reported 166, then 139 from 2026-07-12; unverified) | Divisor 139, round up to next pound (verified in 2026 guide) | Divisor 139 (verified in every Service Guide 2022–2026) |
| Fuel surcharge | None | No weekly history retrievable; only index-to-percent tables | Weekly history page, one ~13-week snapshot saved per year |
| Peak / demand surcharges | Peak price tables per season (2022, 2024, 2025, 2026; none in 2023) | Demand surcharge PDFs 2022–2024 | Dated notices; amounts inside Service Guides, not isolated |
| Announced average increase | USPS press releases, per product (primary source) | Secondary news sources only (5.9% 2022, 6.9% 2023, 5.9% 2024–2026) | FedEx's own rate-change pages: 5.9% every year except 6.9% in 2023 (primary) |
| Access | Direct, needs a browser User-Agent | assets.ups.com blocks curl; fetched through Wayback passthrough | fedex.com blocks this host entirely; everything via the Wayback Machine |
| Raw size | 26 MB (48 files) | 40 MB (23 files) | 74 MB (56 files) |

## Per carrier

### USPS

- **Coverage.** All 15 price changes from January 2022 to October 2026, each
  with a Notice 123 PDF and a Postal Explorer CSV zip. Press releases give the
  announced average increase per product for most changes.
- **Services.** Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express 1–70 lb by zone 1–9
  in every file. Ground Advantage exists from 2023-07-09; before that the
  equivalent lineage is First-Class Package Service (up to 15.999 oz) plus
  USPS Retail Ground (1–70 lb).
- **Parse difficulty.** Low. Each CSV block has a short irregular preamble,
  then a `,Zone 1,…,Zone 9` header and one row per weight step. One float
  artifact (`15.999000000000001`). Surcharge rules are not in the CSVs; they
  are footnotes beside the tables in the PDFs, which pdftotext interleaves
  with price rows. Reading them by hand into a curated table is faster and
  safer than parsing them.
- **Gaps.** Dimensional weight divisor and zone scope are not printed in
  Notice 123 (they live in the DMM). No bulk zone matrix without an order
  form; the free per-origin zone chart is a form POST on postcalc.usps.com.
- **Quirks.** 2026 has three states: January base, a time-limited +8%
  transportation surcharge from April, and the October peak table.

### UPS

- **Coverage.** A full Daily Rates guide for every year 2022–2026, with all
  five target services, zones 2–8 plus 44–46, 1–150 lb, and the surcharge
  section. Demand surcharge PDFs for 2022–2024 and fuel index tables for
  several dates.
- **Parse difficulty.** Medium. Text PDFs; `pdftotext -layout` gives aligned
  columns on rate pages, but each service table spans about four pages with a
  repeated header strip, and page numbering shifts between the 158–165 page
  guides (2022–2024) and the 216 page guides (2025–2026). The surcharge pages
  are three-column prose with inline tables and need regex extraction.
- **Gaps.** No weekly fuel surcharge history anywhere accessible (the UPS
  page is JavaScript-rendered and Wayback snapshots carry no values). No
  UPS-authored source for the announced increases, only trade press. 2027 not
  announced as of 2026-10-13. DAS ZIP list not downloaded.
- **Editions.** Mid-year updates exist for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026; the
  December original is missing for 2024 and 2026, so those years use the
  mid-year revision.

### FedEx

- **Coverage.** Standard List Rates for 2022–2027 with all six target
  services, surcharge change documents for 2022 and 2024–2026, Service Guides
  2022–2026, DAS ZIP lists for every year, fuel trigger tables and one
  historical fuel snapshot per year, and FedEx's own rate-change pages with
  the announced increase.
- **Parse difficulty.** Low for the XLSX years (one sheet per market, stacked
  blocks per service, `Zones 2 3 4 …` header). Medium for 2023 and 2024,
  which are PDF only but consistently laid out. Surcharge change PDFs are
  four-column old/new tables with wrapped cells.
- **Gaps.** No XLSX for 2023 and 2024. No 2023 surcharge change document
  (use the 2024 one's "old" column). Demand surcharge amounts are inside the
  Service Guides rather than isolated. Only one ~13-week fuel window per year.
- **Quirks.** 2026 rates were revised on June 1 2026 and the XLSX predates
  that revision; the PDF captured on 2026-10-22 includes it.

## Decisions

1. **Year range: 2023 through 2026** for the year-over-year view, four price
   points under each year's January list prices. 2022 is excluded from the
   MVP because USPS had a different product set (the Ground Advantage lineage
   starts in July 2023). For USPS 2023 the July 2023 tables are used and
   labelled as such. 2027 FedEx rates are already published and are kept as
   an optional forward year (issue #11).
2. **Parse order by confidence.** USPS CSVs first, FedEx XLSX years next,
   then the FedEx and UPS PDF years. Each parser is validated against
   hand-checked prices from the documents.
3. **Surcharge rules are curated, not parsed.** Amounts for residential,
   delivery area, additional handling, oversize, nonstandard and peak are
   transcribed into `data/processed/surcharges.csv` with the source file and
   page for each row. The PDFs are kept as evidence, not as pipeline input.
4. **Fuel surcharge default per year.** FedEx is the only carrier with a
   retrievable history. The per-year default for both UPS and FedEx is taken
   from the FedEx historical snapshots (the two carriers' percentages track
   each other closely), recorded with its source window, and flagged as an
   approximation. The slider in the UI is the user's override. USPS has none.
5. **Announced increases.** FedEx and USPS from primary sources. UPS from
   trade press, marked as secondary in `announced_increase.csv`.
6. **Dimensional weight.** Divisor 139 for UPS and FedEx on every billable
   parcel. For USPS, dim weight applies only above 1 cu ft; the divisor is
   recorded per year as reported (166, then 139 from July 2026) and flagged
   unverified until checked against the DMM.
7. **Raw files in git.** Everything parse-ready and small is committed. The
   full-guide PDFs (UPS Daily Rates guides, FedEx Service Guides, and all but
   the January and July 2023 USPS Notice 123 PDFs) are excluded by
   `data/raw/.gitignore` because they total over 100 MB; their URLs and
   retrieval method are in each `SOURCES.md`, and the pipeline's download
   step re-fetches them when they are absent.
8. **Zones.** Distance bands stand in for ZIP-to-ZIP zones (issue #9 is the
   bonus). The band table is documented in `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv`.

## Known limitations to state in the README

- List prices only; any shipper with a negotiated contract pays less.
- Zones are approximated from distance, not looked up from ZIP pairs.
- UPS fuel surcharge history is a proxy taken from FedEx.
- UPS announced-increase percentages come from trade press.
- Peak surcharges are modelled as a toggle with that year's amounts, not by
  ship date.
- USPS dimensional weight rules are reported, not verified against the DMM.

**Done this round**

- Three agents surveyed one carrier each in parallel. PR #12 merged the raw sources, per-carrier `SOURCES.md` files, and `docs/data/QUALITY.md`.

**What the data looks like**
- **USPS** is the best source. Every price change from 2022 to 2026 has a clean CSV zip plus the Notice 123 PDF, and press releases give the announced increase per product. No residential or fuel surcharges exist. Weak spot: the dimensional-weight divisor is not printed in Notice 123.
- **FedEx** has list rates for 2022 through 2027, as XLSX for 2022, 2025, 2026 and 2027 and as text PDF for 2023 and 2024. It also has yearly surcharge-change documents, DAS ZIP lists, a weekly fuel history and its own announced increase pages. fedex.com blocks this machine, so everything came through the Wayback Machine.
- **UPS** has a full Daily Rates guide for every year, but only as 160 to 216 page PDFs where each service table spans four pages. There is no retrievable fuel history, and the announced increases come from trade press only.

W=~/parcel-rates-issue-2 && cat > $W/docs/data/SCHEMA.md <<'EOF'
# Processed data schema

All tables live in `data/processed/` as UTF-8 CSV with a header row. Column
names are snake_case. Money is a decimal string with two places in USD. Dates
are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Booleans are `true` or `false`. Empty string means null.

Two kinds of tables:

- **Parsed** tables are generated by `data/pipeline/` from the raw files and
  must never be edited by hand (`base_rates.csv`).
- **Curated** tables are transcribed by hand from the documents. Every row
  carries a citation (`source_file`, `source_ref`, `source_quote`) and the
  test suite checks that the quote, including the amount, appears on the
  cited page of the cited file.

`year` everywhere is the price-list label: the list prices that took effect
in January of that year (USPS 2023 uses the July 9 2023 tables; FedEx 2027 is
the forward year). `effective_date` records the actual date.

## Identifiers

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `carrier` | `usps`, `ups`, `fedex` |
| `tier` | `ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day` |
| `service_id` | see `services.csv` below |
| `unit` | `usd` (flat amount) or `percent` (of the base to which it applies) |

## services.csv (curated)

One row per service in scope.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | |

Invariants checked by tests:

- For each (carrier, service_id, year): every zone in the carrier's range is

- Within a zone, price is non-decreasing with weight. Within a weight step,

**Tool call:** `Bash` <sub>toolu_011tBZFR7DAuinaAo3vJXebv</sub>

- `command`:

```
W=~/parcel-rates-issue-2 && cat > $W/data/fetch_raw.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Restore raw source files listed in data/raw/manifest.csv, politely.

Fetches one file at a time, pauses between requests, retries with backoff on
429/5xx/timeouts, identifies itself with a User-Agent, verifies SHA-256
checksums, and never re-downloads a file whose checksum already matches.

Usage:
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py                 # fetch everything missing or mismatched
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py --carrier ups   # one carrier
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py --verify        # only check what is on disk
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py --record        # fill empty sha256/bytes in the manifest after fetching

Standard library only, so it runs with any Python 3.8+.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import gzip
import hashlib
import random
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

RAW_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "raw"
MANIFEST = RAW_DIR / "manifest.csv"
USER_AGENT = (
    "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) parcel-rates-dashboard/0.1 "
    "(+https://github.com/aivuk/parcel-rates; polite sequential fetcher)"
)
PAUSE_SECONDS = 3.0
JITTER_SECONDS = 2.0
BACKOFF_SECONDS = (10, 30, 90)
TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120
GZIP_MAGIC = b"\x1f\x8b"


def sha256_of(path: Path) -> str:
    digest = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as handle:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 20), b""):
            digest.update(chunk)
    return digest.hexdigest()


def read_manifest() -> list[dict]:
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))


def write_manifest(rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    fields = list(rows[0].keys())
    tmp = MANIFEST.with_suffix(".csv.tmp")
    with tmp.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=fields)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)
    tmp.replace(MANIFEST)


def fetch_bytes(url: str) -> bytes:
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": USER_AGENT})
    last_error: Exception | None = None
    for attempt, backoff in enumerate((*BACKOFF_SECONDS, None)):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS) as response:
                return response.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            last_error = error
            retryable = error.code == 429 or error.code >= 500
            if not retryable or backoff is None:
                raise
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) as error:
            last_error = error
            if backoff is None:
                raise
        print(f"    retry {attempt + 1} in {backoff}s ({last_error})", flush=True)
        time.sleep(backoff)
    raise RuntimeError(f"unreachable: {last_error}")


def maybe_gunzip(data: bytes, target: Path) -> bytes:
    """Wayback's id_ passthrough returns the original bytes, which for some
    HTML captures are still gzip-encoded. Decompress unless the target is a
    gzip file by name."""
    if data[:2] == GZIP_MAGIC and target.suffix not in {".gz", ".zip"}:
        return gzip.decompress(data)
    return data


def status_of(row: dict) -> str:
    target = RAW_DIR / row["path"]
    if not target.is_file():
        return "missing"
    if not row["sha256"]:
        return "unverified"
    return "ok" if sha256_of(target) == row["sha256"] else "mismatch"


def fetch_row(row: dict) -> None:
    target = RAW_DIR / row["path"]
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    data = maybe_gunzip(fetch_bytes(row["url"]), target)
    tmp = target.with_name(target.name + ".part")
    tmp.write_bytes(data)
    tmp.replace(target)


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--carrier", help="only this carrier")
    parser.add_argument("--verify", action="store_true", help="check only, fetch nothing")
    parser.add_argument("--record", action="store_true", help="fill empty sha256/bytes after fetching")
    parser.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="stop after N fetches")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    rows = read_manifest()
    selected = [r for r in rows if not args.carrier or r["carrier"] == args.carrier]
    fetched = failed = 0
    for row in selected:
        state = status_of(row)
        target = RAW_DIR / row["path"]
        if state == "ok":
            continue
        if state == "unverified" and not args.record:
            print(f"?? {row['path']}: present, no checksum in manifest")
            continue
        if args.verify:
            print(f"!! {row['path']}: {state}")
            failed += 1
            continue
        if state in {"missing", "mismatch"}:
            if fetched:
                time.sleep(PAUSE_SECONDS + random.uniform(0, JITTER_SECONDS))
            print(f".. {row['path']} <- {row['url']}", flush=True)
            try:
                fetch_row(row)
                fetched += 1
            except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - report and continue with the next file
                print(f"!! {row['path']}: {error}")
                failed += 1
                continue
        if args.record and target.is_file():
            digest = sha256_of(target)
            if row["sha256"] and row["sha256"] != digest:
                print(f"!! {row['path']}: checksum changed, not overwriting manifest")
                failed += 1
                continue
            row["sha256"] = digest
            row["bytes"] = str(target.stat().st_size)
        if args.limit and fetched >= args.limit:
            break
    if args.record:
        write_manifest(rows)
    print(f"done: {fetched} fetched, {failed} problems, {len(selected)} rows considered")
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
EOF

Use the Wayback timestamp given in SOURCES.md; if only the original URL is given and the method says Wayback, look up a usable timestamp via the CDX API (`https://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx?url=<url>&output=json&limit=5&filter=statuscode:200`).

**USPS dimensional weight, now verified.** Notice 123 only states the one-cubic-foot rule. The divisor lives in the Domestic Mail Manual, sections 123 (Priority Mail) and 133 (Ground Advantage). I saved both sections twice, from a March 2024 Wayback capture and from the live site today, under `data/raw/usps/dmm/`.

| Capture | Rule |
|---|---|
| March 2024 | over 1,728 cu in, divide by 166, round up |
| 2026-10-22 live | over 1,728 cu in, divide by 139, marked as changed 7-12-26 |

Neither version restricts the rule by zone. The earlier "unverified" note is replaced in the quality report.

**Raw-file policy applied.** All PDFs are untracked from git. What stays tracked is 3.3 MB of spreadsheets and CSV zips plus 4.6 MB of HTML snapshots, all under 300 KB each. Say the word and I'll move the HTML behind the fetcher too. One caveat: the PDFs merged in PR #12 remain in git history, about 30 MB, unless we rewrite main. I'd only do that with your explicit go-ahead.

**Fetcher.** `data/fetch_raw.py` is standard library only. It reads `data/raw/manifest.csv`, fetches sequentially with a 3 to 5 second pause, retries 429 and 5xx with 10, 30 and 90 second backoff, sends an identifying User-Agent, writes to a temp file, verifies SHA-256, and skips anything already correct. Wayback rows use the `id_` passthrough URL so bytes match the original.

**Schema to approve** (full detail in `docs/data/SCHEMA.md` on the branch). The decisions worth your eye:

1. **Parsed vs curated.** Only `base_rates.csv` is machine-parsed. Surcharges, fuel defaults, announced increases, dimensional weight and zone bands are hand-curated, and every row carries `source_file`, `source_page` and a verbatim `source_quote` containing the amount. A test opens the cited page and checks the quote is there, skipping with a message if the file has not been fetched.
2. **Weight steps.** One row per price cell with `max_weight_lb` as the step's upper bound. USPS Ground Advantage ounce steps become 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 0.9999, then whole pounds to 70. The engine picks the first step at or above billable weight.
3. **Services and tiers.** Fourteen services across three tiers: ground, two to three day, next day. FedEx Ground is business only and Home Delivery residential only, encoded as two flags per service.
4. **Surcharge rules** are rows with threshold columns (weight, length, length plus girth, volume, zone range), an `exclusive_group` so non-stacking rules pick the highest match, a `fuel_applies` flag, effective dates for peak windows, and `applies_to` as all, ground, air or a service list.
5. **Delivery area.** Since zones come from distance, the parcel CSV gets an optional `delivery_area` column with none, das or extended, so rural surcharges are opt-in per row rather than guessed.
6. **Parcel CSV** columns: weight_lb, length_in, width_in, height_in, distance_miles, residential, speed, optional quantity, optional price_charged, optional delivery_area.
7. **Invariants tested:** complete zone and weight coverage per service and year, prices non-decreasing with weight and zone, and at least five hand-checked golden cells per carrier and year.

W=~/parcel-rates-issue-2 && cat > $W/docs/data/SCHEMA.md <<'EOF'
# Processed data schema

All tables live under `data/processed/` as UTF-8 CSV with a header row. Column
names are snake_case. Money is a decimal string with two places in USD. Dates
are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Booleans are `true` or `false`. Empty string means null.

Two kinds of tables:

- **Parsed** tables are generated by `data/pipeline/` from the raw files and
  are never edited by hand (`base_rates.csv`).
- **Curated** tables are transcribed from the documents. Every row carries a
  citation (`source_file`, `source_ref` or `source_page`, `source_quote`) and
  the test suite checks that the quote, including the amount, appears on the
  cited page of the cited file.

`year` everywhere is the price-list label: the list prices that took effect in
January of that year (USPS 2023 uses the July 9 2023 tables; FedEx 2027 is the
forward year). `effective_date`, `effective_from` and `effective_to` record the
actual dates, because some rules change inside a year.

## Layout

Each carrier's pipeline writes only to its own directory, so parsers can be
built independently and never conflict:

```
data/processed/
  services.csv                 shared, curated
  zone_from_distance.csv       shared, curated
  usps/  base_rates.csv  surcharges.csv  fuel_surcharge.csv  announced_increase.csv  dim_weight.csv  exceptions.csv
  ups/   (same files)
  fedex/ (same files)
```

The backend loads every carrier directory and concatenates tables of the
same name. A carrier with no fuel surcharge ships a header-only file.

## Identifiers

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `carrier` | `usps`, `ups`, `fedex` |
| `rate_card` | `retail` or `commercial`. USPS publishes both; small sellers using online postage pay commercial, so the dashboard defaults USPS to `commercial` with a control to switch to `retail`. UPS Daily Rates and FedEx Standard List Rates are what a shipper without a contract pays and are stored as `retail`. The README explains this. |
| `tier` | `ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day` |
| `service_id` | see `services.csv` |
| `unit` | `usd` (flat amount) or `percent` |

## services.csv (shared, curated)

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | |
| service_id | id | `usps_ground_advantage`, `usps_priority_mail`, `usps_priority_mail_express`, `ups_ground`, `ups_3_day_select`, `ups_2nd_day_air`, `ups_next_day_air_saver`, `ups_next_day_air`, `fedex_ground`, `fedex_home_delivery`, `fedex_express_saver`, `fedex_2day`, `fedex_standard_overnight`, `fedex_priority_overnight` |
| display_name | text | Carrier's own name |
| tier | tier | Speed tier the service competes in |
| residential_allowed | bool | FedEx Ground is business only; Home Delivery is residential only |
| business_allowed | bool | |

| max_weight_lb | int | 70 for USPS, 150 for UPS and FedEx (the app caps at 70) |
| notes | text | |

## base_rates.csv (parsed, per carrier)

One row per price cell.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | |
| service_id | id | |
| rate_card | id | |
| year | int | |
| effective_date | date | |
| zone | int | USPS 1–9 (rows for both 1 and 2 even when equal); UPS and FedEx 2–8 |
| max_weight_lb | decimal | Upper bound of the weight step in pounds. USPS Ground Advantage ounce steps are `0.25`, `0.5`, `0.75`, `0.9999` (15.999 oz), then `1` … `70`. UPS and FedEx `1` … `70` |
| price | money | |
| source_file | path | Relative to `data/raw/` |
| source_ref | text | Sheet name, or PDF file page index (1-based) |

Alaska and Hawaii columns (UPS zones 44–46, FedEx AK/HI zones, USPS zone 9
when the document marks it as such) are parsed only if they fall out of the
same table; they are excluded from the dashboard and listed in
`exceptions.csv` with kind `ak_hi_zone` so the exclusion is explicit.

### Invariants: warnings, with every exception documented

The invariant checks never silently pass. Each anomaly is either listed in the
carrier's `exceptions.csv` (then the test emits a warning) or it fails the test.
This forces every oddity in a rate card to be written down.

Checks:

- For each (carrier, service_id, rate_card, year): every zone in the carrier's
  range is present with the same set of weight steps, strictly increasing,
  with no gaps up to 70 lb.
- Within a zone, price is non-decreasing with weight. Within a weight step,
  price is non-decreasing with zone.
- Prices have at most two decimals and no float artifacts (e.g. `15.999000000000001` in a weight label).
- Every `source_file` exists in `data/raw/manifest.csv`.

`exceptions.csv` (curated, per carrier):

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| carrier, service_id, rate_card, year | Scope, any of them may be empty for "all" |
| zone, max_weight_lb | Cell, or empty for a whole table |
| kind | `ak_hi_zone`, `rounding_artifact`, `non_monotonic`, `missing_cell`, `page_shift`, `step_structure_change`, `other` |
| note | What the document shows and how the parser treats it |
| source_file, source_ref | Where to look |

### Golden samples

`data/tests/golden/<carrier>_<year>.csv` holds hand-checked cells with the
`base_rates.csv` columns plus `checked_by` (person or "agent" plus date) and
`source_ref`. The parsed output must match every golden cell exactly.

Mandatory cells for each (service_id, rate_card, year), because column and
page shifts in the PDFs corrupt exactly these corners:

1. heaviest weight step (70 lb) in the farthest zone
2. heaviest weight step in the nearest zone
3. lightest weight step in the farthest zone
4. at least two interior cells on different pages or sheets of the source

Minimum five cells per (service_id, rate_card, year).

## surcharges.csv (curated, per carrier)

One row per surcharge rule, per year and effective window. A rule applies when
every non-empty threshold column is met and the `as_of` date falls inside its
window.

| Column | Type | Notes |

| carrier | id | |
| year | int | |
| rate_card | id | Empty means all rate cards |

| applies_to | text | `all`, `ground`, `air`, or a comma-separated list of `service_id` |
| min_weight_lb | decimal | Billable weight threshold |
| max_weight_lb | decimal | For banded tables such as USPS peak add-ons |
| min_length_in | decimal | Longest side |
| min_length_plus_girth_in | decimal | |
| min_volume_cuft | decimal | |
| zone_min | int | |
| zone_max | int | |
| amount | decimal | |
| unit | unit | |
| exclusive_group | text | Rules in the same group do not stack; the highest matching amount applies |
| effective_from | date | |
| effective_to | date | Empty means open-ended |
| fuel_applies | bool | Whether the carrier applies the fuel surcharge on top of this charge |
| source_file | path | |
| source_page | int | File page index, 1-based; empty for HTML or XLSX |

| notes | text | |

Peak rules apply only when the dashboard's peak toggle is on. Residential rules
apply to residential parcels. Delivery area rules apply when the parcel's

### Engine tests for fuel

The rate engine applies the fuel percent to the base rate plus every applied
surcharge whose `fuel_applies` is `true`, and to nothing else. Tests use
synthetic rows: one surcharge flagged `true`, one flagged `false`, a known
percent, and assert the fuel line item equals `percent × (base + flagged)` to
the cent, that the slider override replaces the yearly default, and that USPS
quotes carry no fuel line.

| rate_card | id | Empty means all |
| percent | decimal | |
| source_type | enum | `primary` (carrier document) or `secondary` (trade press) |
| source_file | path | |
| source_ref | text | |
| source_quote | text | |

## dim_weight.csv (curated, per carrier)

Dimensional weight parameters change over time (USPS moved from 166 to 139
on 2026-07-12), so rows carry an effective window and the engine resolves the
row by `as_of` date.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | |
| year | int | |
| effective_from | date | |
| effective_to | date | Empty means open-ended |
| divisor | int | |
| min_volume_cuin | int | 0 for UPS and FedEx; 1728 for USPS |
| rounding | text | e.g. "round each dimension to nearest inch, round dim weight up to next pound" |
| source_file | path | |
| source_ref | text | |
| source_quote | text | |

## Rules that change over time

Every parameter that can move a parcel's price is stored per year and per
effective window: base rates, surcharge amounts and thresholds, fuel defaults,
dimensional-weight divisor and threshold. The engine takes an `as_of` date
(default: the year's January effective date) and never hardcodes a value.

`uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes` diffs consecutive years of
every curated table and writes `docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md`: one line per
parameter that changed, with old and new values and the citation. The parser
agents must populate every year so this report is complete, and the report is
reviewed before the engine is built so year-over-year comparisons account for
every change, not only base rates.

The schema is updated and pushed on `issue-2-rate-tables`. Here is how each of your points landed in `docs/data/SCHEMA.md`.

**1. Rate cards.** A `rate_card` column (`retail` or `commercial`) was added to base rates, surcharges and announced increases, and `services.csv` lists which cards each service publishes. USPS gets both, parsed from the same CSV zips, which contain the commercial tables alongside the retail ones. UPS Daily Rates and FedEx Standard List Rates are stored as `retail` since that is what a shipper without a contract pays. The dashboard defaults USPS to commercial with a control to switch, and the schema states that the README must explain why.

**2. Exceptions as warnings.** The invariant checks (full zone and weight coverage, prices non-decreasing with weight and zone, no float artifacts, every source file in the manifest) no longer just pass or fail. Each anomaly must appear in a per-carrier `exceptions.csv` with a kind such as `ak_hi_zone`, `rounding_artifact`, `non_monotonic` or `page_shift`, a note on how the parser treats it, and a source reference. A listed anomaly produces a warning. An unlisted one fails the test, so nothing odd can go undocumented. Alaska and Hawaii columns are excluded from the dashboard and recorded there explicitly.

**3. Fuel tests.** The engine applies the fuel percent to the base rate plus every applied surcharge flagged `fuel_applies`, and to nothing else. The schema specifies the tests: synthetic rows with one flagged and one unflagged surcharge, the fuel line must equal the percent times base plus flagged to the cent, the slider override must replace the yearly default, and USPS quotes must carry no fuel line.

**4. Variables that change over the years.** Every price-moving parameter is stored per year and per effective window. `dim_weight.csv` now has `effective_from` and `effective_to`, because the USPS divisor changed on July 12 2026 inside the 2026 price year. The engine takes an `as_of` date and never hardcodes a value. A `report_changes` script will diff consecutive years of every curated table into `docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md`, and that report gets reviewed before the engine is built so the year-over-year view accounts for threshold and divisor changes, not only base rates.

**5. Golden corner cells.** For each service, rate card and year, the parsed output must match hand-checked cells at the heaviest weight in the farthest zone, the heaviest weight in the nearest zone, the lightest weight in the farthest zone, plus two interior cells from different pages or sheets. Minimum five.

**6. One structural change I made on my own.** Each carrier's pipeline writes only to `data/processed/<carrier>/`, and the backend concatenates. Three agents writing into one `base_rates.csv` would have conflicted.

"""Shared conventions for the per-carrier pipelines.

Column lists mirror docs/data/SCHEMA.md. Every pipeline writes only to
PROCESSED_DIR / <carrier> and reads raw files through `raw_path`, which
refuses files that are not in the manifest or not on disk.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import re
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable

DATA_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RAW_DIR = DATA_DIR / "raw"
PROCESSED_DIR = DATA_DIR / "processed"
MANIFEST = RAW_DIR / "manifest.csv"

CARRIERS = ("usps", "ups", "fedex")
RATE_CARDS = {"usps": ("retail", "commercial"), "ups": ("list",), "fedex": ("list",)}
ZONES = {"usps": range(1, 10), "ups": range(2, 9), "fedex": range(2, 9)}
MAX_WEIGHT_LB = 70
USPS_OUNCE_STEPS = ("0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "0.9999")

COLUMNS = {
    "services": [
        "carrier", "service_id", "display_name", "tier", "residential_allowed",
        "business_allowed", "rate_cards", "rate_card_notes", "max_weight_lb", "notes",
    ],
    "base_rates": [
        "carrier", "service_id", "rate_card", "year", "effective_date", "zone",
        "max_weight_lb", "price", "source_file", "source_ref",
    ],
    "exceptions": [
        "carrier", "service_id", "rate_card", "year", "zone", "max_weight_lb",
        "kind", "note", "source_file", "source_ref",
    ],
    "surcharges": [
        "carrier", "year", "rate_card", "surcharge_id", "display_name", "condition",
        "applies_to", "min_weight_lb", "max_weight_lb", "min_length_in",
        "min_length_plus_girth_in", "min_volume_cuft", "zone_min", "zone_max",
        "amount", "unit", "exclusive_group", "effective_from", "effective_to",
        "fuel_applies", "source_file", "source_page", "source_quote", "notes",
    ],
    "fuel_surcharge": [
        "carrier", "year", "service_group", "default_percent", "basis",
        "window_start", "window_end", "is_proxy", "source_file", "source_ref",
        "source_quote", "notes",
    ],
    "announced_increase": [
        "carrier", "year", "product_scope", "rate_card", "percent", "source_type",
        "source_file", "source_ref", "source_quote",
    ],
    "dim_weight": [
        "carrier", "year", "effective_from", "effective_to", "divisor",
        "min_volume_cuin", "rounding", "source_file", "source_ref", "source_quote",
    ],
    "zone_from_distance": [
        "carrier", "zone", "min_miles", "max_miles", "source_file", "source_quote",
    ],
}
CURATED_TABLES = ("surcharges", "fuel_surcharge", "announced_increase", "dim_weight")
EXCEPTION_KINDS = (
    "ak_hi_zone", "rounding_artifact", "non_monotonic", "missing_cell",
    "page_shift", "step_structure_change", "other",
)
SURCHARGE_CONDITIONS = (
    "residential", "delivery_area", "delivery_area_extended",
    "additional_handling_weight", "additional_handling_length",
    "additional_handling_width", "additional_handling_packaging", "oversize",
    "nonstandard_length", "nonstandard_volume", "peak_residential",
    "peak_additional_handling", "peak_oversize", "peak_base",
    "transportation_time_limited",
)


def money(value: Decimal | str | float) -> str:
    """Format a price with exactly two decimals, rounding half up."""
    return str(Decimal(str(value)).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def weight_label(value: Decimal | str | float) -> str:
    """Normalize a weight step label: integers as '12', ounce steps as in USPS_OUNCE_STEPS."""
    dec = Decimal(str(value)).normalize()
    if dec == dec.to_integral_value():
        return str(int(dec))
    text = format(dec, "f")
    return text if text in USPS_OUNCE_STEPS else text


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def manifest_rows() -> list[dict]:
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))


def manifest_paths() -> set[str]:
    return {row["path"] for row in manifest_rows()}


def raw_path(relative: str) -> Path:
    """Return the on-disk path of a raw file, insisting it is in the manifest and present."""
    if relative not in manifest_paths():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{relative} is not listed in data/raw/manifest.csv")
    path = RAW_DIR / relative
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{relative} is missing; run `python3 data/fetch_raw.py`")
    return path


def processed_path(carrier: str, table: str) -> Path:
    if carrier == "shared":
        return PROCESSED_DIR / f"{table}.csv"
    return PROCESSED_DIR / carrier / f"{table}.csv"


def write_table(carrier: str, table: str, rows: Iterable[dict]) -> Path:
    """Write rows with the schema's column order. Missing keys become empty strings;
    unknown keys are an error so typos cannot slip through."""
    columns = COLUMNS[table]
    path = processed_path(carrier, table)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = list(rows)
    for row in rows:
        unknown = set(row) - set(columns)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"{table}: unknown columns {sorted(unknown)}")
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=columns, lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writeheader()
        for row in rows:
            writer.writerow({column: row.get(column, "") for column in columns})
    return path


def read_table(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        return []
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))


_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")


def normalize_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Collapse whitespace and unify quotes/dashes so quotes can be matched across PDF line breaks."""
    text = text.replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'").replace("“", '"').replace("”", '"')
    text = text.replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-").replace(" ", " ")
    return _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", text).strip().lower()


def pdf_page_text(path: Path, page: int) -> str:
    """Text of a 1-based page index, via pdfplumber."""
    import pdfplumber

    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
        if page < 1 or page > len(pdf.pages):
            raise IndexError(f"{path.name} has {len(pdf.pages)} pages, asked for {page}")
        return pdf.pages[page - 1].extract_text() or ""


def html_text(path: Path) -> str:
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    raw = re.sub(r"<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>", " ", raw, flags=re.S | re.I)
    return re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", raw)


def xlsx_text(path: Path, sheet: str | None = None) -> str:
    import openpyxl

    book = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    sheets = [book[sheet]] if sheet and sheet in book.sheetnames else book.worksheets
    parts: list[str] = []
    for ws in sheets:
        for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True):
            parts.extend(str(cell) for cell in row if cell is not None)
    return " ".join(parts)


def source_text(source_file: str, source_ref: str | int | None) -> str:
    """Text of the cited location: PDF page, XLSX sheet, or whole HTML/CSV file."""
    path = raw_path(source_file)
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix == ".pdf":
        return pdf_page_text(path, int(source_ref))
    if suffix == ".xlsx":
        return xlsx_text(path, str(source_ref) if source_ref else None)
    if suffix in {".htm", ".html"}:
        return html_text(path)
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

"""Diff consecutive years of every curated table and write docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md.

Usage: uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

from data.pipeline.common import CARRIERS, CURATED_TABLES, DATA_DIR, processed_path, read_table

OUT = DATA_DIR.parent / "docs" / "data" / "RULE_CHANGES.md"

KEY_COLUMNS = {
    "surcharges": ("rate_card", "condition", "applies_to", "exclusive_group", "zone_min", "zone_max",
                   "min_weight_lb", "max_weight_lb", "min_length_in", "min_length_plus_girth_in", "min_volume_cuft"),
    "fuel_surcharge": ("service_group",),
    "announced_increase": ("product_scope", "rate_card"),
    "dim_weight": ("effective_from",),
}
VALUE_COLUMNS = {
    "surcharges": ("amount", "unit", "fuel_applies", "effective_from", "effective_to"),
    "fuel_surcharge": ("default_percent", "is_proxy"),
    "announced_increase": ("percent", "source_type"),
    "dim_weight": ("divisor", "min_volume_cuin", "rounding"),
}


def changes_for(carrier: str, table: str) -> list[str]:
    rows = read_table(processed_path(carrier, table))
    by_year: dict[int, dict[tuple, dict]] = defaultdict(dict)
    for row in rows:
        key = tuple(row.get(column, "") for column in KEY_COLUMNS[table])
        by_year[int(row["year"])][key] = row
    lines: list[str] = []
    years = sorted(by_year)
    for previous, current in zip(years, years[1:]):
        before, after = by_year[previous], by_year[current]
        for key in sorted(set(before) | set(after), key=str):
            old, new = before.get(key), after.get(key)
            label = " / ".join(part for part in key if part) or table
            if old is None:
                lines.append(f"- {previous}→{current} **{label}**: new rule, {describe(new, table)} ({cite(new)})")
            elif new is None:
                lines.append(f"- {previous}→{current} **{label}**: rule removed (was {describe(old, table)})")
            else:
                diffs = [f"{column} {old[column]} → {new[column]}" for column in VALUE_COLUMNS[table]
                         if old.get(column, "") != new.get(column, "")]
                if diffs:
                    lines.append(f"- {previous}→{current} **{label}**: {', '.join(diffs)} ({cite(new)})")
    return lines


def describe(row: dict, table: str) -> str:
    return ", ".join(f"{column} {row[column]}" for column in VALUE_COLUMNS[table] if row.get(column, ""))


def cite(row: dict) -> str:
    page = row.get("source_page") or row.get("source_ref") or ""
    return f"{row.get('source_file', '')}{' p.' + str(page) if page else ''}"


def main() -> None:
    parts = ["# Rule changes between consecutive price years", "",
             "Generated by `uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes` from the curated tables.",
             "Every parameter that moves a parcel's price and changed between years is listed here;",
             "the engine must resolve each by year and effective date.", ""]
    for carrier in CARRIERS:
        parts.append(f"## {carrier.upper()}")
        parts.append("")
        any_lines = False
        for table in CURATED_TABLES:
            lines = changes_for(carrier, table)
            if lines:
                any_lines = True
                parts.append(f"### {table}")
                parts.extend(lines)
                parts.append("")
        if not any_lines:
            parts.append("_No curated rows yet._")
            parts.append("")
    OUT.write_text("\n".join(parts) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {OUT.relative_to(DATA_DIR.parent)}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
EOF
