import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { BlendedView } from "../BlendedView";
import { BlendedPanel } from "./BlendedPanel";
import { mockBlendedResponse } from "../../api/mocks";
import { cleanSegment, surchargeKinds, blendedAnswer, OTHER_KIND, splitRows } from "./logic";
import { CARRIER_NAME } from "../../lib/format";
import type { BlendedResponse } from "../../api/types";
import { controls, meta, renderWith, sampleParcels, spyClient, stubResizeObserver } from "./testUtils";

beforeEach(() => stubResizeObserver());

describe("BlendedView", () => {
  it("asks for parcels with sample and upload actions when none are loaded", async () => {
    const { client, blended } = spyClient();
    const onLoadSample = vi.fn();
    const onUploadCsv = vi.fn();
    renderWith(client, <BlendedPanel controls={controls} meta={meta} parcels={null} onLoadSample={onLoadSample} onUploadCsv={onUploadCsv} />);
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Load the sample mix" }));
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Upload CSV" }));
    expect(onLoadSample).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(onUploadCsv).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
    expect(blended).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it("without handlers, the empty-state buttons drive the parcel panel's own controls", async () => {
    const { client } = spyClient();
    const panelSample = vi.fn();
    renderWith(
      client,
      <>
        <section className="parcels">
          <button type="button" onClick={panelSample}>
            Load sample mix
          </button>
        </section>
        <BlendedView controls={controls} meta={meta} parcels={null} />
      </>,
    );
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Load the sample mix" }));
    expect(panelSample).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });

  it("puts the cheapest carrier's cost per parcel first, with the best mix saving", async () => {
    const { client, blended } = spyClient();
    renderWith(client, <BlendedView controls={controls} meta={meta} parcels={sampleParcels} />);
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("q3-answer")).toHaveTextContent(/^USPS \$21\.09 per parcel$/);
    expect(blended).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ parcels: sampleParcels, controls }), expect.anything());
    expect(blended.mock.calls[0]![0]).not.toHaveProperty("segment");
    const mix = screen.getByTestId("q3-mix");
    expect(mix).toHaveTextContent("$19.98");
    expect(mix).toHaveTextContent("$1.11 less per parcel than USPS alone ($332.12 on these parcels)");
    expect(mix).toHaveTextContent("USPS 275 · FedEx 15 · UPS 10");
  });

  it("says plainly whether the flat price covers the cost and how many parcels lose money", async () => {
    const { client } = spyClient();
    renderWith(client, <BlendedView controls={controls} meta={meta} parcels={sampleParcels} />);
    expect(await screen.findByTestId("q3-verdict")).toHaveTextContent("No. You lose $10.98 per parcel with USPS");
    expect(screen.getByTestId("q3-loss-share")).toHaveTextContent("71% of parcels (214 of 300) ship at a loss");
    expect(screen.getByRole("heading", { name: /does your \$9\.99 shipping price cover the cost/i })).toBeInTheDocument();
    const ups = screen.getByTestId("margin-ups");
    expect(ups).toHaveTextContent("−$32.57 loss");
    expect(ups).toHaveTextContent("100%");

describe("blended logic", () => {
  it("picks the cheapest carrier and the mix saving", () => {
    const a = blendedAnswer(mockBlendedResponse)!;
    expect(a.cheapest.carrier).toBe("usps");
    expect(a.others.map((c) => c.carrier)).toEqual(["ups", "fedex"]);
    expect(a.mixSavingPerParcel).toBe(1.11);
  });

  it("keeps the three biggest surcharge kinds and folds the rest", () => {
    const k = surchargeKinds(mockBlendedResponse);
    expect(k.shown).toEqual(["residential", "nonstandard_volume", "delivery_area"]);
    expect(k.folded).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["additional_handling_packaging", "nonstandard_length", "delivery_area_extended"]));
    const usps = splitRows(mockBlendedResponse, k, CARRIER_NAME).find((r) => r.carrier === "usps")!;
    expect(usps.kinds.nonstandard_volume).toBe(1.87);
    expect(usps.kinds[OTHER_KIND]).toBe(0.14);

  it("sends no segment when every group is All", () => {
    expect(cleanSegment({ weight_band: null, residential: null })).toBeNull();
    expect(cleanSegment({ residential: false })).toEqual({ residential: false });
  });

/** Pure derivations for the Q3 blended view, kept apart from rendering so they are easy to test. */
import type { BlendedResponse, Carrier, CarrierBlended, Parcel, SegmentFilter } from "../../api/types";

export interface BlendedAnswer {
  cheapest: CarrierBlended;
  others: CarrierBlended[];
  /** Best mix minus cheapest single carrier, per parcel (negative = the mix is cheaper). */
  mixSavingPerParcel: number;
  mixSavingTotal: number;
  /** True when some carrier could not ship part of the set, so averages cover different parcels. */
  unevenCoverage: boolean;
}

/** Cheapest carrier by cost per parcel among carriers that shipped anything. */
export function blendedAnswer(r: BlendedResponse): BlendedAnswer | null {
  const shipped = r.carriers.filter((c) => c.parcels_shipped > 0);
  if (shipped.length === 0) return null;
  const sorted = [...shipped].sort((a, b) => a.cost_per_parcel - b.cost_per_parcel);
  const cheapest = sorted[0]!;
  return {
    cheapest,
    others: sorted.slice(1),
    mixSavingPerParcel: round2(cheapest.cost_per_parcel - r.best_mix.cost_per_parcel),
    mixSavingTotal: round2(cheapest.total_cost - r.best_mix.total_cost),
    unevenCoverage: r.carriers.some((c) => c.parcels_unavailable > 0),
  };
}

export const round2 = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 100) / 100;

/* ---------- stacked split ---------- */

export const MAX_KINDS = 3;
export const OTHER_KIND = "__other";

/** Surcharge kinds ordered by their total across carriers; the top MAX_KINDS get their own segment. */
export function surchargeKinds(r: BlendedResponse): { shown: string[]; folded: string[] } {
  const totals = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const c of r.carriers)
    for (const s of c.surcharges_by_condition) totals.set(s.condition, (totals.get(s.condition) ?? 0) + s.total);
  const order = [...totals.entries()].sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]).map(([k]) => k);
  if (order.length <= MAX_KINDS + 1) return { shown: order, folded: [] };
  return { shown: order.slice(0, MAX_KINDS), folded: order.slice(MAX_KINDS) };
}

export interface SplitRow {
  carrier: Carrier;
  label: string;
  base: number;
  fuel: number;
  /** per surcharge kind key (a condition or OTHER_KIND): dollars per parcel */
  kinds: Record<string, number>;
  surcharges: number;
  total: number;
  surchargeShare: number;
  fuelShare: number;
}

export function splitRows(r: BlendedResponse, kinds: { shown: string[]; folded: string[] }, names: Record<Carrier, string>): SplitRow[] {
  return r.carriers
    .filter((c) => c.parcels_shipped > 0)
    .map((c) => {
      const byKind: Record<string, number> = {};
      for (const k of kinds.shown) byKind[k] = 0;
      if (kinds.folded.length) byKind[OTHER_KIND] = 0;
      for (const s of c.surcharges_by_condition) {
        const key = kinds.shown.includes(s.condition) ? s.condition : OTHER_KIND;
        byKind[key] = round2((byKind[key] ?? 0) + s.per_parcel);
      }
      return {
        carrier: c.carrier,
        label: names[c.carrier],
        base: c.split.base.per_parcel,
        fuel: c.split.fuel.per_parcel,
        kinds: byKind,
        surcharges: c.split.surcharges.per_parcel,
        total: c.cost_per_parcel,
        surchargeShare: c.split.surcharges.share,
        fuelShare: c.split.fuel.share,
      };
    });
}

/* ---------- segment filter ---------- */

export type SegmentKey = keyof SegmentFilter;

/** Drop unset keys, so "All" everywhere sends no segment at all. */
export function cleanSegment(s: SegmentFilter): SegmentFilter | null {
  const out: SegmentFilter = {};
  if (s.weight_band != null) out.weight_band = s.weight_band;
  if (s.zone_band != null) out.zone_band = s.zone_band;
  if (s.residential != null) out.residential = s.residential;
  if (s.speed != null) out.speed = s.speed;
  return Object.keys(out).length ? out : null;
}

export const totalQuantity = (parcels: Parcel[]) => parcels.reduce((n, p) => n + (p.quantity ?? 1), 0);
```

function Answer({ data, answer, kicker }: { data: BlendedResponse; answer: BlendedAnswer; kicker: string }) {
  const { cheapest, others, mixSavingPerParcel, mixSavingTotal } = answer;
  const mix = data.best_mix;
  const mixCounts = Object.entries(mix.parcels_by_carrier)
    .filter(([, n]) => n > 0)
    .sort((a, b) => b[1] - a[1]);
  return (
    <div className="answer q3-answer">
      <p className="kicker">{kicker}</p>
      <p className="answer__figure" data-testid="q3-answer">
        <span className="carrier-tag" style={{ color: carrierVar(cheapest.carrier) }}>
          {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)}
        </span>{" "}
        {formatUsd(cheapest.cost_per_parcel)}
        <span className="answer__unit"> per parcel</span>
      </p>
      <p className="answer__caption">
        Blended over every parcel at its cheapest {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)} service for the speed it needs.
        {others.length > 0 && " "}
        {others.map((c, i) => (
          <span key={c.carrier}>
            {i > 0 && ", "}
            <strong style={{ color: carrierVar(c.carrier) }}>{carrierName(c.carrier)}</strong> {formatUsd(c.cost_per_parcel)}{" "}
            ({signedUsd(c.cost_per_parcel - cheapest.cost_per_parcel)})
          </span>
        ))}
        {others.length > 0 && "."}
      </p>
      <div className="mix" data-testid="q3-mix">
        <p className="mix__line">
          <span className="mix__label">Best mix</span>{" "}
          <span className="figure mix__figure">{formatUsd(mix.cost_per_parcel)}</span> per parcel, choosing the cheapest
          carrier for each parcel:{" "}
          {mixSavingPerParcel > 0 ? (
            <>
              <strong>{formatUsd(mixSavingPerParcel)} less per parcel</strong> than {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)} alone (
              {formatUsd(mixSavingTotal)} on these parcels).
            </>
          ) : (
            <>no saving over {carrierName(cheapest.carrier)} alone.</>
          )}
        </p>
        <p className="mix__split">
          {mixCounts.map(([c, n], i) => (
            <span key={c}>
              {i > 0 && " · "}
              <span style={{ color: carrierVar(c as Carrier) }}>{carrierName(c)}</span> {formatInt(n)}
            </span>
          ))}
        </p>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

function Verdict({ data, answer, controls }: { data: BlendedResponse; answer: BlendedAnswer; controls: ControlsState }) {
  const c = answer.cheapest;
  const loss = c.margin_per_parcel < 0;
  const charged = data.revenue_per_parcel;
  const mixedPrices = Math.abs(charged - controls.flat_price) >= 0.005;
  const rows = [
    ...[...data.carriers].filter((x) => x.parcels_shipped > 0).sort((a, b) => a.cost_per_parcel - b.cost_per_parcel),
  ];
  return (
    <section className={`verdict ${loss ? "verdict--loss" : "verdict--profit"}`} aria-labelledby="q3-verdict">
      <h3 id="q3-verdict" className="verdict__q">
        Does your {formatUsd(controls.flat_price)} shipping price cover the cost?
      </h3>
      <p className="verdict__figure" data-testid="q3-verdict">
        <span className="verdict__word">{loss ? "No." : "Yes."}</span>{" "}
        {loss ? (
          <>
            You lose {formatUsd(-c.margin_per_parcel)} per parcel with {carrierName(c.carrier)}
          </>
        ) : (
          <>
            {formatUsd(c.margin_per_parcel)} margin per parcel with {carrierName(c.carrier)}
          </>
        )}
      </p>
      <p className="verdict__loss-share" data-testid="q3-loss-share">
        {c.parcels_at_loss === 0 ? (
          <>
            Every parcel covers its cost with {carrierName(c.carrier)}
            {data.best_mix.parcels_at_loss > 0 && <>; {pct0(data.best_mix.loss_share)} would lose money with the best mix</>}.
          </>
        ) : (
          <>
            <strong>{pct0(c.loss_share)}</strong> of parcels ({formatInt(c.parcels_at_loss)} of {formatInt(c.parcels_shipped)})
            ship at a loss even with the cheapest carrier
            {data.best_mix.loss_share !== c.loss_share && <>; {pct0(data.best_mix.loss_share)} with the best mix</>}.
          </>
        )}
      </p>
      {mixedPrices && (
        <p className="verdict__note">
          You charge {formatUsd(charged)} per parcel on average: the flat {formatUsd(controls.flat_price)}, and your own
          price on rows that have one.
        </p>
      )}
      <table className="ledger-table margin-table">
        <caption className="visually-hidden">Margin per parcel and share shipped at a loss, per carrier</caption>

    expect(fig).toHaveTextContent(/USPS \(circles\) went from \$17\.80 in 2023 to \$21\.09 in 2026 \(\+18\.5%\)/);
    await userEvent.click(within(fig).getByRole("button", { name: "Show as table" }));

describe("yearly logic", () => {
  it("compares carriers at the latest year they all publish", () => {
    expect(referenceYear(mockYearlyResponse)).toBe(2026);
    expect(pickCarrier(mockYearlyResponse, 2026)!.carrier).toBe("usps");
    expect(defaultIncrease(carrier("usps"))).toBe(6.5);
  });

  it("computes the period change and compounds the announced increases", () => {
    const ch = periodChange(carrier("usps"), 2026)!;
    expect(ch.dollars).toBe(3.29);
    expect(ch.percent).toBeCloseTo(18.483, 2);
    expect(ch.announcedPercent).toBeCloseTo((1.0567 * 1.0343 * 1.065 - 1) * 100, 6);
    const path = announcedPath(carrier("usps"));
    expect(path.get(2023)).toBe(17.8);
    expect(path.get(2024)).toBe(18.81);
  });

  it("finds the biggest step and its fuel share", () => {
    const s = biggestFuelStep(carrier("fedex"), 2026)!;
    expect([s.fromYear, s.toYear, s.change, s.fuelChange]).toEqual([2025, 2026, 4.55, 2.72]);
    expect(fuelSentence(s)).toContain("(60% of it)");
    expect(biggestFuelStep(carrier("usps"))).toBeNull();
    // A carrier whose cost only ever fell has no rise to explain.
    const fedex = carrier("fedex");
    const falling: CarrierYears = {
      ...fedex,
      years: fedex.years.map((y) =>
        y.change_vs_previous ? { ...y, change_vs_previous: { ...y.change_vs_previous, dollars_per_parcel: -0.5, percent: -1 } } : y,
      ),
    };
    expect(biggestFuelStep(falling)).toBeNull();
  });

  it("sorts drivers by magnitude, negatives included", () => {
    const list: Driver[] = [
      { segment: "a", parcels: 1, change_per_parcel: 0.2, change_total: 1 },
      { segment: "b", parcels: 1, change_per_parcel: -0.9, change_total: 1 },
      { segment: "c", parcels: 1, change_per_parcel: 0.5, change_total: 1 },
    ];
    expect(sortedDrivers(list).map((d) => d.segment)).toEqual(["b", "c", "a"]);
  });

  it("names the top driver and picks the dimension it lives in", () => {
    const row = carrier("ups").years.find((y) => y.year === 2026)!;
    expect(strongestDimension(row.drivers!)).toBe("residential");
    expect(driverSentence("ups", row, "speed")).toBe(
      "Largest contributor: ground parcels (262 of them) added $2.98 per parcel of UPS's +$4.61 change from 2025 to 2026, 65% of it. " +
        "Fastest rising: next day parcels, +$21.13 each, but they are only 3% of the parcels (9), so they move the average less.",
    );
  });

  it("turns warnings into plain words and flags mid-year editions", () => {
    expect(readableWarning("No 2027 rules recorded for: oversize, delivery_area; surcharges may be understated")).toBe(
      "No 2027 rules recorded for oversize, remote area. Surcharges may be understated.",
    );
    const notes = pointNotes(mockYearlyResponse);
    expect(notes.filter((n) => n.kind === "edition").map((n) => `${n.carrier} ${n.year}`)).toEqual([
      "usps 2023",
      "ups 2024",
      "ups 2026",
    ]);
    expect(notes.filter((n) => n.kind === "warning").map((n) => `${n.carrier} ${n.year}`)).toEqual(["fedex 2027"]);
  });

  it("derives the change within a segment from its total and parcel count", () => {
    const d: Driver = { segment: "next_day", parcels: 9, change_per_parcel: 0.63, change_total: 190.2 };
    expect(withinChange(d)).toBe(21.13);
    expect(withinChange({ ...d, parcels: 0 })).toBe(0);
    const row = carrier("ups").years.find((y) => y.year === 2026)!;
    expect(fastestSegment(row.drivers!.weight_band, 4.61)!.segment).toBe("10–20");
  });

  it("indexes to the first year", () => {
    expect(toIndex(21.09, 17.8)).toBe(118.5);
  });

  it("makes round axis ticks that include zero", () => {
    expect(niceTicks(0, 1.77)).toEqual([0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2]);
    expect(niceTicks(-0.3, 1)).toContain(0);
  });
});
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import { render, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event";
import { ApiProvider } from "./api/ApiContext";
import { createMockClient, type ApiClient } from "./api/client";
import { App } from "./App";

function renderApp(client: ApiClient = createMockClient(0)) {
  return render(
    <ApiProvider client={client}>
      <App />
    </ApiProvider>,
  );
}

describe("App", () => {
  beforeEach(() => window.history.replaceState(null, "", "/"));

  it("loads the sample mix as a one-line strip, with the full summary on demand", async () => {
    renderApp();
    expect(screen.getByText("No parcels loaded yet.")).toBeInTheDocument();
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Load sample mix" }));
    const section = await screen.findByRole("region", { name: /your parcels/i });
    const strip = await within(section).findByText(/to homes/);
    expect(strip.closest("p")).toHaveTextContent(/^300 parcels\d+% to homes/);
    expect(within(section).queryByRole("table", { name: /weight/i })).not.toBeInTheDocument();

    const details = within(section).getByRole("button", { name: "Details" });
    expect(details).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    await userEvent.click(details);
    expect(details).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
    expect(within(section).getByText(/Illustrative parcel mix/)).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(within(section).getByRole("table", { name: /weight/i })).toBeInTheDocument();
    const zones = within(section).getByRole("table", { name: /distance/i });
    expect(within(zones).getByRole("rowheader", { name: /Zone 1\s*0–50 mi/ })).toBeInTheDocument();
    expect(within(section).getByText(/have their\s+own price/)).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("shows CSV problems with row numbers and keeps the previous set", async () => {
    renderApp();
    const file = new File(["weight_lb,distance_miles,residential,speed\n80,100,true,ground\n"], "march.csv", {
      type: "text/csv",
    });
    await userEvent.upload(screen.getByLabelText("Upload CSV"), file);
    const alert = await screen.findByRole("alert");
    expect(alert).toHaveTextContent("march.csv was not loaded: 1 problem to fix.");
    expect(alert).toHaveTextContent("Row 2");
    expect(alert).toHaveTextContent("over the 70 lb limit");
    expect(screen.getByText("No parcels loaded yet.")).toBeInTheDocument();
  });

  it("mirrors controls and the active question to the URL", async () => {
    renderApp();
    await screen.findByRole("option", { name: "2025" });
    await userEvent.selectOptions(screen.getByRole("combobox", { name: "Price list year" }), "2025");
    await userEvent.click(screen.getByRole("tab", { name: /blended cost/i }));
    const params = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
    expect(params.get("year")).toBe("2025");
    expect(params.get("view")).toBe("blended");
    expect(screen.getByRole("tabpanel")).toHaveTextContent(/Across all your parcels/);
  });

  it("restores state from a shared link", async () => {
    window.history.replaceState(null, "", "/?view=yearly&usps=retail&peak=1");
    renderApp();
    expect(screen.getByRole("tab", { name: /year over year/i })).toHaveAttribute("aria-selected", "true");
    expect(screen.getByRole("radio", { name: /retail/i })).toBeChecked();
    expect(screen.getByRole("switch", { name: /peak/i })).toBeChecked();
  });

  it("moves between questions with the arrow keys", async () => {
    renderApp();
    const first = screen.getByRole("tab", { name: /quote a parcel/i });
    first.focus();
    await userEvent.keyboard("{ArrowRight}");
    expect(screen.getByRole("tab", { name: /breakeven map/i })).toHaveFocus();
    await userEvent.keyboard("{End}");
    expect(screen.getByRole("tab", { name: /year over year/i })).toHaveAttribute("aria-selected", "true");
  });

  it("renders the footer limitations from /api/meta", async () => {
    renderApp();
    expect(await screen.findByText(/List prices only/)).toBeInTheDocument();
  });
});

    print(' ',y['year'],{k:v for k,v in y.items() if k not in('drivers','year')})
    if y.get('drivers'):
      for dim,lst in y['drivers'].items(): print('    ',dim,lst)

/** Pure derivations for the Q4 year-over-year view. */
import type { Carrier, CarrierYears, Driver, Drivers, YearRow, YearlyResponse } from "../../api/types";
import { formatUsd } from "../../lib/format";
import { carrierName, conditionLabel, signedPct, signedUsd, tierName } from "../blended/money";

export type Dimension = keyof Drivers;
export const DIMENSIONS: readonly Dimension[] = ["weight_band", "zone_band", "residential", "speed"];
export const DIMENSION_LABEL: Record<Dimension, string> = {
  weight_band: "Weight",
  zone_band: "Distance",
  residential: "Address",
  speed: "Speed",
};

const round2 = (n: number) => Math.round(n * 100) / 100;

/** Latest year every carrier with data publishes (2026 when FedEx alone has 2027). */
export function referenceYear(r: YearlyResponse): number | null {
  const sets = r.carriers.filter((c) => c.years.length > 0).map((c) => new Set(c.years.map((y) => y.year)));
  if (sets.length === 0) return null;
  const common = [...sets[0]!].filter((y) => sets.every((s) => s.has(y)));
  if (common.length) return Math.max(...common);
  return Math.max(...r.carriers.flatMap((c) => c.years.map((y) => y.year)));
}

export const rowFor = (c: CarrierYears, year: number) => c.years.find((y) => y.year === year) ?? null;

/** The carrier the owner would pick: cheapest per parcel in the reference year. */
export function pickCarrier(r: YearlyResponse, ref: number): CarrierYears | null {
  let best: CarrierYears | null = null;
  let bestCost = Infinity;
  for (const c of r.carriers) {
    const row = rowFor(c, ref);
    if (row && c.parcels_used > 0 && row.cost_per_parcel < bestCost) {
      best = c;
      bestCost = row.cost_per_parcel;
    }
  }
  return best;
}

export interface PeriodChange {
  fromYear: number;
  toYear: number;
  from: number;
  to: number;
  dollars: number;
  percent: number;
  /** Announced increases compounded over the same years; null when a year has none. */
  announcedPercent: number | null;
}

/** Change in cost per parcel from the carrier's first year to `toYear`, against the compounded announcements. */
export function periodChange(c: CarrierYears, toYear: number): PeriodChange | null {
  const first = c.years[0];
  const last = rowFor(c, toYear);
  if (!first || !last || last.year <= first.year || first.cost_per_parcel === 0) return null;
  let factor: number | null = 1;
  for (const y of c.years) {
    if (y.year <= first.year || y.year > toYear) continue;
    const p = y.announced_increase.percent;
    factor = p === null || factor === null ? null : factor * (1 + p / 100);
  }
  return {
    fromYear: first.year,
    toYear,
    from: first.cost_per_parcel,
    to: last.cost_per_parcel,
    dollars: round2(last.cost_per_parcel - first.cost_per_parcel),
    percent: ((last.cost_per_parcel - first.cost_per_parcel) / first.cost_per_parcel) * 100,
    announcedPercent: factor === null ? null : (factor - 1) * 100,
  };
}

/** Cost path if every year had risen exactly by the announced increase, from the first year's cost. */
export function announcedPath(c: CarrierYears): Map<number, number> {
  const out = new Map<number, number>();
  const first = c.years[0];
  if (!first) return out;
  let v = first.cost_per_parcel;
  out.set(first.year, v);
  for (const y of c.years.slice(1)) {
    const p = y.announced_increase.percent;
    if (p === null) break;
    v = v * (1 + p / 100);
    out.set(y.year, round2(v));
  }
  return out;
}

/** Default for the next-year slider: the pick carrier's latest announced increase. */
export function defaultIncrease(c: CarrierYears | null): number | null {
  if (!c) return null;
  for (let i = c.years.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {
    const p = c.years[i]!.announced_increase.percent;
    if (p !== null) return p;
  }
  return null;
}

/* ---------- fuel ---------- */

export interface FuelStep {
  carrier: Carrier;
  fromYear: number;
  toYear: number;
  change: number;
  fuelChange: number;
  /** fuel change as a share of the total change (can exceed 1 or be negative) */
  share: number | null;
  groundFrom: number | null;
  groundTo: number | null;
}

export function fuelStep(c: CarrierYears, prev: YearRow, cur: YearRow): FuelStep | null {
  if (!cur.fuel || !prev.fuel || !cur.change_vs_previous) return null;
  const change = cur.change_vs_previous.dollars_per_parcel;
  const fuelChange = round2(cur.summary.split.fuel.per_parcel - prev.summary.split.fuel.per_parcel);
  return {
    carrier: c.carrier,
    fromYear: prev.year,
    toYear: cur.year,
    change,
    fuelChange,
    share: change !== 0 ? fuelChange / change : null,
    groundFrom: prev.fuel.ground.applied_percent,
    groundTo: cur.fuel.ground.applied_percent,
  };
}

/**
 * The year step where the carrier's cost rose most, with its fuel part; null when no step is a
 * rise (the "how much of the rise is fuel" question does not apply) or the carrier has no fuel.
 */
export function biggestFuelStep(c: CarrierYears, upTo?: number): FuelStep | null {
  let best: FuelStep | null = null;
  for (let i = 1; i < c.years.length; i++) {
    const cur = c.years[i]!;
    if (upTo !== undefined && cur.year > upTo) break;
    const s = fuelStep(c, c.years[i - 1]!, cur);
    if (s && s.change > 0 && (!best || s.change > best.change)) best = s;
  }
  return best;
}

export function fuelSentence(s: FuelStep): string {
  const name = carrierName(s.carrier);
  const pct = s.share !== null && s.change > 0 && s.fuelChange > 0 ? ` (${Math.round(s.share * 100)}% of it)` : "";
  const rates =
    s.groundFrom !== null && s.groundTo !== null && s.groundFrom !== s.groundTo
      ? `; the ground fuel surcharge went from ${s.groundFrom}% to ${s.groundTo}%`
      : "";
  return `${name} ${s.fromYear}→${s.toYear}: ${signedUsd(s.change)} per parcel, of which fuel ${signedUsd(s.fuelChange)}${pct}${rates}.`;
}

/* ---------- drivers ---------- */

export function sortedDrivers(list: Driver[]): Driver[] {
  return [...list].sort((a, b) => Math.abs(b.change_per_parcel) - Math.abs(a.change_per_parcel) || a.segment.localeCompare(b.segment));
}

export function segmentLabel(dim: Dimension, segment: string): string {
  switch (dim) {
    case "weight_band":
      return `${segment} lb`;
    case "zone_band":
      return `Zones ${segment}`;
    case "residential":
      return segment === "residential" ? "Homes" : segment === "business" ? "Businesses" : segment;
    case "speed":
      return tierName(segment);
  }
}

function segmentPhrase(dim: Dimension, segment: string): string {
  switch (dim) {
    case "weight_band":
      return `parcels of ${segment} lb`;
    case "zone_band":
      return `parcels to zones ${segment}`;
    case "residential":
      return segment === "residential" ? "deliveries to homes" : "deliveries to businesses";
    case "speed":
      return `${tierName(segment).toLowerCase()} parcels`;
  }
}

/** The dimension whose largest single segment explains most of the change. */
export function strongestDimension(d: Drivers): Dimension {
  let best: Dimension = "weight_band";
  let bestV = -1;
  for (const dim of DIMENSIONS) {
    const top = sortedDrivers(d[dim])[0];
    const v = top ? Math.abs(top.change_per_parcel) : 0;
    if (v > bestV) {
      best = dim;
      bestV = v;
    }
  }
  return best;
}

/** Change per parcel *within* the segment: its own parcels' change, independent of its size. */
export function withinChange(d: Driver): number {
  return d.parcels > 0 ? Math.round((d.change_total / d.parcels) * 100) / 100 : 0;
}

/** The segment whose own parcels moved most in the direction of the overall change. */
export function fastestSegment(list: Driver[], overall: number): Driver | null {
  const withParcels = list.filter((d) => d.parcels > 0);
  if (withParcels.length === 0) return null;
  const sign = overall >= 0 ? 1 : -1;
  return withParcels.reduce((best, d) => (sign * withinChange(d) > sign * withinChange(best) ? d : best));
}

export function driverSentence(carrier: Carrier, row: YearRow, dim: Dimension): string | null {
  const ch = row.change_vs_previous;
  const list = row.drivers?.[dim];
  if (!ch || !list || list.length === 0) return null;
  const top = sortedDrivers(list)[0]!;
  const name = carrierName(carrier);
  const span = `${ch.from_year} to ${row.year}`;
  const what = segmentPhrase(dim, top.segment);
  const share = ch.dollars_per_parcel !== 0 ? Math.round((top.change_per_parcel / ch.dollars_per_parcel) * 100) : null;
  const shareText = share !== null && share > 0 ? `, ${share}% of it` : "";
  const direction = top.change_per_parcel >= 0 ? "added" : "took off";
  const first =
    `Largest contributor: ${what} (${top.parcels} of them) ${direction} ${formatUsd(Math.abs(top.change_per_parcel))} per parcel ` +
    `of ${name}'s ${signedUsd(ch.dollars_per_parcel)} change from ${span}${shareText}.`;
  const fast = fastestSegment(list, ch.dollars_per_parcel);
  if (!fast) return first;
  const verb = ch.dollars_per_parcel >= 0 ? "rising" : "falling";
  if (fast.segment === top.segment) return `${first} Its own parcels also changed fastest: ${signedUsd(withinChange(fast))} each.`;
  const fastWhat = segmentPhrase(dim, fast.segment);
  const fastShare = Math.round((fast.parcels / list.reduce((n, d) => n + d.parcels, 0)) * 100);
  return (
    `${first} Fastest ${verb}: ${fastWhat}, ${signedUsd(withinChange(fast))} each, ` +
    `but they are only ${fastShare}% of the parcels (${fast.parcels}), so they move the average less.`
  );
}

/* ---------- warnings ---------- */

const MONTHS = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"];

export function formatDate(iso: string): string {
  const [y, m, d] = iso.split("-").map(Number);
  return `${d} ${MONTHS[(m ?? 1) - 1]} ${y}`;
}

export interface PointNote {
  carrier: Carrier;
  year: number;
  text: string;
  kind: "warning" | "edition";
}

/**
 * Warnings from the response, plus a note when the year's prices took effect mid-year
 * (the backend reports `as_of`, not a warning, for that): a year priced from a mid-year
 * edition is not a January-to-January comparison.
 */
export function pointNotes(r: YearlyResponse): PointNote[] {
  const out: PointNote[] = [];
  for (const c of r.carriers) {
    for (const y of c.years) {
      for (const w of y.warnings) out.push({ carrier: c.carrier, year: y.year, text: readableWarning(w), kind: "warning" });
      if (y.as_of) {
        const [ay, am] = y.as_of.split("-").map(Number);
        if (ay === y.year && am !== undefined && am >= 3) {
          out.push({
            carrier: c.carrier,
            year: y.year,
            kind: "edition",
            text: `Priced from the edition effective ${formatDate(y.as_of)}, published mid-year, so the step into and out of ${y.year} is not January to January.`,
          });
        }
      }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

export const pctText = (n: number) => signedPct(n, 1);

/** "No 2027 rules recorded for: a_b, c; …" with the surcharge ids in the owner's words. */
export function readableWarning(w: string): string {
  const m = /^(No \d{4} rules recorded for): ([^;]+);\s*(.*)$/.exec(w);
  if (!m) return w;
  const kinds = m[2]!.split(",").map((k) => conditionLabel(k.trim()).toLowerCase());
  const rest = m[3]!.replace(/^./, (ch) => ch.toUpperCase());
  return `${m[1]} ${kinds.join(", ")}. ${rest}${/[.!]$/.test(rest) ? "" : "."}`;
}

/**
 * Small helpers shared by the Q1 and Q2 views (issue #5). Kept here rather than in src/lib
 * so this branch does not touch shared files; move to src/lib if Q3/Q4 need them too.
 */
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import type { Carrier, Meta } from "../../api/types";
import { CARRIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { formatUsd } from "../../lib/format";

/** Margins that round to $0.00 are break-even: no sign, no profit or loss colour. */
const BREAK_EVEN = 0.005;
const isBreakEven = (margin: number) => Math.abs(margin) < BREAK_EVEN;

/** "+$1.58 margin" / "−$1.90 loss": sign and word, never colour alone. */
export function marginText(margin: number): string {
  if (isBreakEven(margin)) return "$0.00, break-even";
  return margin > 0 ? `+${formatUsd(margin)} margin` : `−${formatUsd(-margin)} loss`;
}

export const marginClass = (margin: number) => (isBreakEven(margin) ? "" : margin < 0 ? "is-loss" : "is-profit");

/** Carriers that publish prices for `year`; all three when meta is not loaded yet. */
export function carriersForYear(meta: Meta | null, year: number): Carrier[] {
  if (!meta) return [...CARRIERS];
  return CARRIERS.filter((c) => meta.years[c]?.includes(year));
}

export function serviceName(meta: Meta | null, serviceId: string): string {
  const found = meta?.services.find((s) => s.service_id === serviceId);
  if (found) return found.display_name;
  return serviceId
    .split("_")
    .map((w) => (w === "usps" || w === "ups" ? w.toUpperCase() : w === "fedex" ? "FedEx" : w[0]!.toUpperCase() + w.slice(1)))
    .join(" ");
}

/** The value after it has stopped changing for `delayMs`. */
export function useDebounced<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
  const [settled, setSettled] = useState(value);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (delayMs <= 0) {
      setSettled(value);
      return;
    }
    const t = setTimeout(() => setSettled(value), delayMs);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [value, delayMs]);
  return delayMs <= 0 ? value : settled;
}

/** "2027 prices are published by FedEx only" style sentence, or null when all three publish. */
export function missingCarriersNote(available: Carrier[], year: number, names: Record<Carrier, string>): string | null {
  if (available.length === CARRIERS.length) return null;
  if (available.length === 0) return `No carrier has published ${year} prices in this data.`;
  const list = available.map((c) => names[c]).join(" and ");
  const missing = CARRIERS.filter((c) => !available.includes(c));
  const missingList = missing.map((c) => names[c]).join(" and ");
  const verb = missing.length === 1 ? "has" : "have";
  const consequence = available.length === 1 ? "so there is nothing to compare against" : "so they are left out";
  return `${year} prices are published by ${list} only. ${missingList} ${verb} not published ${year} prices yet, ${consequence}.`;
}

/** "+$1.23" / "−$1.23" (true minus sign), "$0.00" for zero. */
export function signedUsd(n: number): string {
  const r = Math.round(n * 100) / 100;
  if (r === 0) return formatUsd(0);
  return `${r > 0 ? "+" : "−"}${formatUsd(Math.abs(r))}`;
}

/** "+4.1%" / "−2.0%" with one decimal. */
export function signedPct(n: number, digits = 1): string {
  const r = Number(n.toFixed(digits));
  if (r === 0) return `0${digits ? "." + "0".repeat(digits) : ""}%`;
  return `${r > 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(r).toFixed(digits)}%`;
}

/** Share 0..1 as "71%". */
export const pct0 = (share: number) => `${Math.round(share * 100)}%`;

/* ---------- colours for Recharts ---------- */

const DARK = "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)";

/** Resolve CSS custom properties to concrete colours; re-resolves when the colour scheme flips. */
export function useCssColors<K extends string>(vars: Record<K, string>): Record<K, string> {
  const read = () => {
    const style = typeof document === "undefined" ? null : getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
    const out = {} as Record<K, string>;
    for (const k in vars) out[k] = style?.getPropertyValue(vars[k]).trim() || "currentColor";
    return out;
  };
  const [colors, setColors] = useState(read);
  const key = JSON.stringify(vars);
  useEffect(() => {
    setColors(read());
    const mq = typeof window !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia(DARK) : null;
    if (!mq) return;
    const onChange = () => setColors(read());
    mq.addEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    return () => mq.removeEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [key]);
  return colors;
}

/* ---------- loading that keeps the last answer ---------- */

/** The latest successful data, so controls re-query without blanking the view. */
export function useLastData<T>(state: Loadable<T>): T | null {
  const [last, setLast] = useState<T | null>(state.status === "ok" ? state.data : null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (state.status === "ok") setLast(state.data);
  }, [state]);
  return state.status === "ok" ? state.data : last;
}

export function LoadProblem({ error }: { error: Error }) {

  return (

      {problems.length > 0 && (

              <span>{p.message}</span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

/** Debounce a fast-changing value (slider) before it reaches the API. */
export function useDebounced<T>(value: T, ms: number): T {
  const [v, setV] = useState(value);
  useEffect(() => {
    const t = setTimeout(() => setV(value), ms);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [value, ms]);
  return v;
}

export interface ChipOption<T> {
  value: T;
  label: string;
}

/** A row of toggle chips that behaves like a radio group; "All" clears the dimension. */
export function ChipGroup<T>({
  legend,
  options,
  value,
  onChange,
  equals = (a, b) => a === b,
}: {
  legend: string;
  options: ChipOption<T>[];
  value: T;
  onChange: (v: T) => void;
  equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean;
}) {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="chips" role="group" aria-labelledby={id}>
      <span id={id} className="chips__legend">
        {legend}
      </span>
      <div className="chips__row">
        {options.map((o) => {
          const on = equals(o.value, value);
          return (
            <button
              key={o.label}
              type="button"
              className={`chip ${on ? "chip--on" : ""}`}
              aria-pressed={on}
              onClick={() => onChange(o.value)}
            >
              {o.label}
            </button>
          );
        })}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

const DEFAULT_WEIGHTS: WeightBand[] = ["≤1", "1–5", "5–10", "10–20", "20–70"];
const DEFAULT_ZONES: ZoneBandLabel[] = ["1–2", "3–4", "5–6", "7–8"];

export function SegmentChips({
  value,
  onChange,
  weightBands = DEFAULT_WEIGHTS,
  zoneBands = DEFAULT_ZONES,
}: {
  value: SegmentFilter;
  onChange: (next: SegmentFilter) => void;
  weightBands?: readonly string[];
  zoneBands?: readonly string[];
}) {
  const set = <K extends keyof SegmentFilter>(key: K, v: SegmentFilter[K]) => onChange({ ...value, [key]: v });
  return (
    <div className="segments">
      <ChipGroup<WeightBand | null>
        legend="Weight"
        value={value.weight_band ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("weight_band", v)}
        options={[
          { value: null, label: "All" },
          ...weightBands.map((w) => ({ value: w as WeightBand, label: `${w} lb` })),
        ]}
      />
      <ChipGroup<ZoneBandLabel | null>
        legend="Distance (USPS zone)"
        value={value.zone_band ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("zone_band", v)}
        options={[
          { value: null, label: "All" },
          ...zoneBands.map((z) => ({ value: z as ZoneBandLabel, label: `Zones ${z}` })),
        ]}
      />
      <ChipGroup<boolean | null>
        legend="Address"
        value={value.residential ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("residential", v)}
        options={[
          { value: null, label: "All" },
          { value: true, label: "Homes" },
          { value: false, label: "Businesses" },
        ]}
      />
      <ChipGroup<Tier | null>
        legend="Speed"
        value={value.speed ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("speed", v)}
        options={[{ value: null, label: "All" }, ...TIERS.map((t) => ({ value: t, label: tierName(t) }))]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

/** "1–5 lb · homes" for the answer kicker; empty when no segment is set. */
export function describeSegment(s: SegmentFilter | null): string {
  if (!s) return "";
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (s.weight_band) parts.push(`${s.weight_band} lb`);
  if (s.zone_band) parts.push(`zones ${s.zone_band}`);
  if (s.residential != null) parts.push(s.residential ? "homes" : "businesses");
  if (s.speed) parts.push(tierName(s.speed).toLowerCase());
  return parts.join(" · ");
}

/** `?mock=1` serves typed mock responses; the mock module is a separate lazy chunk. */
export function isMockMode(search: string = typeof window === "undefined" ? "" : window.location.search): boolean {
  return new URLSearchParams(search).get("mock") === "1";
}

export function createMockClient(delayMs = 350): ApiClient {
  const load = () => import("./mocks");
  const wait = <T>(fn: () => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T> =>
    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      setTimeout(() => {
        Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(resolve, reject);
      }, delayMs);
    });
  return {
    health: () => wait(() => ({ status: "ok" as const })),
    meta: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockMeta),
    sampleParcels: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockSampleParcels),
    quote: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockQuote()),
    breakeven: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockBreakeven()),
    blended: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockBlended()),
    yearly: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockYearly()),
  };
}

export function createClient(): ApiClient {
  return isMockMode() ? createMockClient() : createHttpClient();
}

export interface YearlyPanelProps extends ParcelActions {
  controls: ControlsState;
  meta: Meta | null;
  parcels: Parcel[] | null;
}

export const INCREASE_MIN = -10;
export const INCREASE_MAX = 20;

export function YearlyPanel({ controls, parcels, onLoadSample, onUploadCsv }: YearlyPanelProps) {
  if (!parcels || parcels.length === 0) {
    return (
      <NeedParcels
        what="Load the sample mix or upload a CSV to see how the cost of your parcels moved under each year's published prices, against the increases the carriers announced, and which parcels drove it."
        onLoadSample={onLoadSample}
        onUploadCsv={onUploadCsv}
      />
    );
  }
  return <Yearly controls={controls} parcels={parcels} />;
}

function Yearly({ controls, parcels }: { controls: ControlsState; parcels: Parcel[] }) {
  const api = useApi();
  const [increase, setIncrease] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const sent = useDebounced(increase, 250);
  const controlsKey = JSON.stringify(controls);
  const state = useLoad(
    (signal) => api.yearly({ parcels, controls, ...(sent !== null ? { next_year_increase_percent: sent } : {}) }, signal),
    [api, parcels, controlsKey, sent],
  );
  const data = useLastData(state);
  const total = useMemo(() => totalQuantity(parcels), [parcels]);

  // The slider starts at the pick carrier's latest announced increase, which the first answer tells us.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (increase !== null || !data) return;
    const ref = referenceYear(data);
    const d = ref !== null ? defaultIncrease(pickCarrier(data, ref)) : null;
    if (d !== null) setIncrease(d);
  }, [data, increase]);

  const loading = state.status === "loading";
  return (
    <div className="q4" aria-busy={loading}>
      {state.status === "error" && <LoadProblem error={state.error} />}
      {!data && loading && <p className="q-loading">Pricing {formatInt(total)} parcels under every year’s prices…</p>}
      {data && <Body data={data} increase={increase} onIncrease={setIncrease} stale={loading} />}
    </div>
  );

/** Number, money, margin and label formatting shared by every view. */
import type { Tier } from "../api/types";

const usd = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" });
const int = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US");

export const formatUsd = (n: number) => usd.format(n);
export const formatInt = (n: number) => int.format(n);
/** Share 0..1 as "71%". */
export const formatShare = (share: number) => `${Math.round(share * 100)}%`;
export const formatPercent = (n: number) => `${Number.isInteger(n) ? n : n.toFixed(2).replace(/0$/, "")}%`;

/** "+$1.23" / "−$1.23" (true minus sign), "$0.00" for zero. */
export function signedUsd(n: number): string {
  const r = Math.round(n * 100) / 100;
  if (r === 0) return formatUsd(0);
  return `${r > 0 ? "+" : "−"}${formatUsd(Math.abs(r))}`;
}

/** "+4.1%" / "−2.0%" with one decimal by default. */
export function signedPct(n: number, digits = 1): string {
  const r = Number(n.toFixed(digits));
  if (r === 0) return `0${digits ? "." + "0".repeat(digits) : ""}%`;
  return `${r > 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(r).toFixed(digits)}%`;
}

/* ---------- margin: sign and word, never colour alone ---------- */

/** Margins that round to $0.00 are break-even: no sign, no profit or loss colour. */
const BREAK_EVEN = 0.005;
const isBreakEven = (margin: number) => Math.abs(margin) < BREAK_EVEN;

/** "+$1.58 margin" / "−$1.90 loss" / "$0.00, break-even". */
export function marginText(margin: number): string {
  if (isBreakEven(margin)) return "$0.00, break-even";
  return margin > 0 ? `+${formatUsd(margin)} margin` : `−${formatUsd(-margin)} loss`;
}

/** Colour class that agrees with marginText: "is-loss", "is-profit", or none at break-even. */
export const marginClass = (margin: number) => (isBreakEven(margin) ? "" : margin < 0 ? "is-loss" : "is-profit");

/* ---------- labels ---------- */

export const TIER_NAME: Record<Tier, string> = {
  ground: "Ground",
  two_three_day: "2–3 day",
  next_day: "Next day",
};

export const tierName = (t: string) => TIER_NAME[t as Tier] ?? t;

/** Surcharge conditions (surcharges.csv) in the owner's words. */
const CONDITION_LABEL: Record<string, string> = {
  residential: "Home delivery",
  delivery_area: "Remote area",
  delivery_area_extended: "Extended remote area",
  additional_handling_packaging: "Handling: packaging",
  additional_handling_weight: "Handling: weight",
  additional_handling_length: "Handling: length",
  additional_handling_width: "Handling: width",
  nonstandard_volume: "Non-standard size",
  nonstandard_length: "Non-standard length",
  oversize: "Oversize",
};

export function conditionLabel(condition: string): string {
  return CONDITION_LABEL[condition] ?? condition.replace(/_/g, " ").replace(/^./, (c) => c.toUpperCase());
}
EOF
cat > lib/carriers.ts <<'EOF'
/** Carrier names, colours, and which carriers publish prices for a year. */
import type { Carrier, Meta } from "../api/types";
import { CARRIERS } from "../api/types";

export const CARRIER_NAME: Record<Carrier, string> = { usps: "USPS", ups: "UPS", fedex: "FedEx" };

export const carrierName = (c: Carrier | string) => CARRIER_NAME[c as Carrier] ?? c;

/** CSS variable for a carrier's colour; use in style props so dark mode follows. */
export const carrierVar = (c: Carrier) => `var(--carrier-${c})`;
export const carrierWashVar = (c: Carrier) => `var(--carrier-${c}-wash)`;

/** Resolved colour, for libraries that need a concrete value (e.g. Recharts fills). */
export function carrierColor(c: Carrier, el: Element = document.documentElement): string {
  return getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue(`--carrier-${c}`).trim();
}

/** Carriers that publish prices for `year`; all three when meta is not loaded yet. */
export function carriersForYear(meta: Meta | null, year: number): Carrier[] {
  if (!meta) return [...CARRIERS];
  return CARRIERS.filter((c) => meta.years[c]?.includes(year));
}

/** "2027 prices are published by FedEx only" style sentence, or null when all three publish. */
export function missingCarriersNote(available: Carrier[], year: number, names: Record<Carrier, string> = CARRIER_NAME): string | null {
  if (available.length === CARRIERS.length) return null;
  if (available.length === 0) return `No carrier has published ${year} prices in this data.`;
  const list = available.map((c) => names[c]).join(" and ");
  const missing = CARRIERS.filter((c) => !available.includes(c));
  const missingList = missing.map((c) => names[c]).join(" and ");
  const verb = missing.length === 1 ? "has" : "have";
  const consequence = available.length === 1 ? "so there is nothing to compare against" : "so they are left out";
  return `${year} prices are published by ${list} only. ${missingList} ${verb} not published ${year} prices yet, ${consequence}.`;
}

/** The service's display name from /api/meta, or a readable fallback built from its id. */
export function serviceName(meta: Meta | null, serviceId: string): string {
  const found = meta?.services.find((s) => s.service_id === serviceId);
  if (found) return found.display_name;
  return serviceId
    .split("_")
    .map((w) => (w === "usps" || w === "ups" ? w.toUpperCase() : w === "fedex" ? "FedEx" : w[0]!.toUpperCase() + w.slice(1)))
    .join(" ");
}
EOF
cat > hooks/useDebounced.ts <<'EOF'
import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

/** The value after it has stopped changing for `delayMs`; a delay of 0 or less passes it straight through. */
export function useDebounced<T>(value: T, delayMs: number): T {
  const [settled, setSettled] = useState(value);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (delayMs <= 0) {
      setSettled(value);
      return;
    }
    const t = setTimeout(() => setSettled(value), delayMs);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [value, delayMs]);
  return delayMs <= 0 ? value : settled;
}
EOF

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
import type { Loadable } from "../api/ApiContext";

/** The latest successful data, so controls re-query without blanking the view. */
export function useLastData<T>(state: Loadable<T>): T | null {
  const [last, setLast] = useState<T | null>(state.status === "ok" ? state.data : null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (state.status === "ok") setLast(state.data);
  }, [state]);
  return state.status === "ok" ? state.data : last;
}
EOF

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

const DARK = "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)";

/** Resolve CSS custom properties to concrete colours (for Recharts); re-resolves when the colour scheme flips. */
export function useCssColors<K extends string>(vars: Record<K, string>): Record<K, string> {
  const read = () => {
    const style = typeof document === "undefined" ? null : getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
    const out = {} as Record<K, string>;
    for (const k in vars) out[k] = style?.getPropertyValue(vars[k]).trim() || "currentColor";
    return out;
  };
  const [colors, setColors] = useState(read);
  const key = JSON.stringify(vars);
  useEffect(() => {
    setColors(read());
    const mq = typeof window !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia(DARK) : null;
    if (!mq) return;
    const onChange = () => setColors(read());
    mq.addEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    return () => mq.removeEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [key]);
  return colors;
}
EOF

import { useId, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";

/** A chart with its title, a text summary, and a table alternative behind a toggle. */
export function ChartFrame({
  title,
  summary,
  chart,
  table,
  aside,
  controls,
}: {
  title: string;
  summary: ReactNode;
  /** Controls that change the chart (e.g. a scale toggle); shown in chart mode only. */
  controls?: ReactNode;
  chart: ReactNode;
  table: ReactNode;
  aside?: ReactNode;
}) {
  const [asTable, setAsTable] = useState(false);
  const titleId = useId();
  const bodyId = useId();
  return (
    <figure className="chart" aria-labelledby={titleId}>
      <div className="chart__head">
        <h3 id={titleId} className="chart__title">
          {title}
        </h3>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="btn btn--quiet chart__toggle"
          aria-controls={bodyId}
          aria-pressed={asTable}
          onClick={() => setAsTable((t) => !t)}
        >
          {asTable ? "Show as chart" : "Show as table"}
        </button>
      </div>
      <figcaption className="chart__summary">{summary}</figcaption>
      <div id={bodyId} className="chart__body">
        {asTable ? (
          <div className="chart__table-wrap">{table}</div>
        ) : (
          <>
            {controls && <div className="chart__controls">{controls}</div>}
            <div aria-hidden="true">{chart}</div>
          </>
        )}
      </div>
      {aside}
    </figure>
  );
}

import { useId } from "react";

export interface ChipOption<T> {
  value: T;
  label: string;
}

/** A row of toggle chips that behaves like a radio group; an "All" option usually clears the choice. */
export function ChipGroup<T>({
  legend,
  options,
  value,
  onChange,
  equals = (a, b) => a === b,
}: {
  legend: string;
  options: ChipOption<T>[];
  value: T;
  onChange: (v: T) => void;
  equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean;
}) {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="chips" role="group" aria-labelledby={id}>
      <span id={id} className="chips__legend">
        {legend}
      </span>
      <div className="chips__row">
        {options.map((o) => {
          const on = equals(o.value, value);
          return (
            <button
              key={o.label}
              type="button"
              className={`chip ${on ? "chip--on" : ""}`}
              aria-pressed={on}
              onClick={() => onChange(o.value)}
            >
              {o.label}
            </button>
          );
        })}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

import { ApiError } from "../api/client";

/** A failed API call, with the field-level problems of a 422 when there are any. */
export function LoadProblem({ error }: { error: Error }) {
  const problems = error instanceof ApiError ? error.problems : [];
  return (
    <div className="problems problems--error" role="alert">
      <p className="problems__title">{error.message}</p>
      {problems.length > 0 && (
        <ul className="problems__list">
          {problems.slice(0, 8).map((p, i) => (
            <li key={i}>
              {p.field && <span className="problems__where">{p.field}</span>}
              <span>{p.message}</span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

# Parcel rates: USPS, UPS and FedEx list prices for a small online shop

A dashboard that prices a shop's own parcels at the published prices of the
three US parcel carriers, for every year from 2023 to 2026, and shows which
carrier is cheapest, where the breakeven points are, how much of the bill is
surcharges, and how the cost moved year by year.

## Run it

Requires Docker with Compose v2. No accounts, keys or database setup.

```sh
docker compose up --build
```

Then open **http://localhost:8088**. The first build takes a minute or two.
Click "Load sample mix" to load an illustrative parcel set, or upload your
own CSV (columns below). Stop with `Ctrl+C`, then `docker compose down`.

Only port 8088 is published. nginx serves the built dashboard and proxies
`/api/` to the backend container, which is not reachable from the host. The
rate tables are baked into the backend image; the app never fetches anything
from the carriers at run time.

## The problem and the user

The user is the owner of a small online shop that sends a few hundred to a few
thousand parcels a month, has no negotiated carrier contract, and therefore
pays published prices. The carrier is usually chosen by habit, and the flat
shipping price charged to customers was set once and not revisited.

The dashboard supports two decisions: which carrier and service to use for
each kind of parcel, and whether the flat shipping price still covers the real
cost once surcharges and yearly price increases are included.

### What it answers

> **Status:** the API answers all four questions today (`/api/quote`, `/api/breakeven`,
> `/api/blended`, `/api/yearly`). The dashboard views for them are being built in
> issues #5 and #6; until they merge, each tab shows "View in progress".

| # | Question | How |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | For one parcel (weight, size, distance, home or business, speed), which service is cheapest once surcharges are included, and what are the line items? | Quote for every service, cheapest per speed tier, line items with the source page of each charge |
| 2 | Where are the breakeven points between the Postal Service and FedEx or UPS ground, by weight and distance? | Heatmap of the cheapest carrier over a weight by distance grid |
| 3 | For the whole parcel set, what is the blended cost per parcel with each carrier, and how much of it is surcharges? | Cost per parcel and margin against the flat price, split into base, surcharges and fuel, segmentable by kind of parcel |
| 4 | How did that blended cost change year by year, compared with the average increase the carriers announced, and which parcels drove it? | Same parcel set priced under each year's prices, against the announced increase |

Global controls: price year, USPS rate card, fuel surcharge override, peak
season toggle, and the flat price charged per parcel.

Parcel CSV columns: `weight_lb, length_in, width_in, height_in,
distance_miles, residential, speed` (`ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day`),
plus optional `quantity`, `price_charged`, `delivery_area`,
`nonstandard_packaging`. The full schema is in
[docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md); the sample mix is generated by
`backend/scripts/make_sample_parcels.py` with a fixed seed and is not real
shipping data.

## Data provenance

All prices come from the carriers' own published rate documents:

| Carrier | Base rates | Surcharge rules | Years |
|---|---|---|---|
| USPS | Postal Explorer CSV zips per price change; Notice 123 PDFs | Notice 123 footnotes; Domestic Mail Manual for dimensional weight | 2023 (July tables, Ground Advantage launch) to 2026 |
| UPS | Daily Rates guide PDF per year | Surcharge section of the same guide; demand surcharge PDFs | 2023 to 2026 |
| FedEx | Standard List Rates XLSX (PDF for 2023 and 2024) | Yearly surcharge-change PDFs and Service Guides | 2023 to 2026, plus 2027 as a forward year |

**Collection.** Every raw file is listed in
[data/raw/manifest.csv](data/raw/manifest.csv) with its URL, retrieval method,
SHA-256 and size, and each carrier folder has a `SOURCES.md` describing what
each file is. `python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores missing files one at a
time, with a pause and jitter between requests, backoff on errors, an
identifying User-Agent and checksum verification. UPS and FedEx block direct
downloads from scripts, so 78 of the 135 files are fetched through the Wayback
Machine (`method=wayback`).

**What is committed.** Spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML snapshots (58
files, about 9 MB) are in git. The PDFs (77 files, about 137 MB) are not; run
`python3 data/fetch_raw.py` to get them. The processed tables in
`data/processed/` are committed, so the app and the backend tests never need
the raw files.

**Regenerating `data/processed/`** (needs the PDFs, so fetch first):

```sh
python3 data/fetch_raw.py                     # standard library only
uv run python -m data.pipeline.usps
uv run python -m data.pipeline.ups
uv run python -m data.pipeline.fedex
uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes # rewrites docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md
```

Base rates are parsed. Surcharges, fuel defaults, announced increases,
dimensional weight rules and the distance-to-zone bands are curated by hand
in `data/pipeline/*_rules.py`, each row with the source file, page and a
verbatim quote. Details: [docs/data/QUALITY.md](docs/data/QUALITY.md) (survey
and decisions), [docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md) (tables) and
[docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md](docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md) (every rule that
changed between years).

### Rate cards

| Carrier | Card | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| USPS | `commercial` (default) | Price paid with online postage or shipping software; no contract or volume needed |
| USPS | `retail` | Price paid at the Post Office counter |
| UPS | `list` | Published Daily Rates, what a shipper without a contract pays |
| FedEx | `list` | Published Standard List Rates, same meaning |

Commercial is the USPS default because a small online seller buys labels
through a marketplace or shipping software, which gives commercial prices to
anyone. Comparing UPS and FedEx list prices against USPS retail would
overstate what the shop pays the Postal Service. The retail card is one switch
away in the controls.

## Key choices

- **Stack.** Python 3.12, FastAPI and Pydantic for the rate engine and API,
  managed with `uv`. Vite, React and TypeScript for the dashboard, Recharts
  for line and bar charts and a hand-drawn SVG heatmap. Two containers behind
  one `docker compose` command. Reasons and alternatives are in
  [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md).
- **CSV in memory, no database.** The rate tables are about 40,000 rows of
  committed CSV, loaded once at startup. Nothing to configure.
- **Curated rules with tested citations.** Surcharge prose in PDFs is too
  irregular to parse reliably, so the amounts were transcribed by hand. A test
  opens each cited page and checks that the quote, including the amount, is
  there.
- **Golden cells.** `data/tests/golden/<carrier>_<year>.csv` holds price cells
  checked by hand against the documents, including the corners of every
  table; the parsed output must match them exactly.
- **Time-varying rules.** Every rule carries `effective_from` and an inclusive
  `effective_to`, and a quote is priced on an `as_of` date. This handles
  mid-year changes such as the USPS dimensional divisor moving from 166 to 139
  on 2026-07-12, peak windows and the 2026 USPS transportation surcharge.
- **Ledger design.** The answer to each question is the largest thing in its
  section; assumptions sit in a quiet side rail. See
  [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md).

## Known limitations

- List prices only: a shipper with a negotiated contract pays less.
- Zones are estimated from distance bands, not looked up from ZIP code pairs.
- The UPS fuel surcharge default is a proxy taken from FedEx's published
  history (no UPS history is retrievable); the slider overrides it.
- UPS announced increases come from trade press, not from UPS itself.
- UPS peak (demand) surcharge documents for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons
  are not in the sources, so UPS 2025 and 2026 peak quotes carry no peak
  charges.
- FedEx 2027 surcharges are incomplete (only the Home Delivery residential
  charge and January peak rows), so 2027 totals understate surcharges.
- Peak surcharges are a toggle that prices on December 10 of the year, not by
  ship date.
- UPS and FedEx bill a large or oversize package at a minimum of 90 lb. That
  minimum is not modelled, so the base rate of such parcels is understated;
  the surcharge itself is included (issue #18).
- Weight is capped at 70 lb, the USPS maximum. Alaska and Hawaii are out of
  scope.
- UPS 2024 and 2026 use the mid-year revision of the Daily Rates guide,
  because the December original could not be retrieved.

The same list is returned by `GET /api/meta` and shown in the app.

## What I would improve next

Open issues in the repository, in rough priority order:

- #18 model the 90 lb minimum billable weight for large and oversize packages.
- #14 capture the UPS 2025-26 and 2026-27 demand surcharge documents.
- #9 real ZIP-to-ZIP zones instead of distance bands.
- #10 per-parcel price column and order-value shipping rules (free shipping
  over a threshold).
- #11 next-year projection from announced increases.
- #13 script the source discovery so data collection runs end to end without
  an agent.
- #8 Playwright end-to-end tests at desktop and phone widths.

## Local development without Docker

Needs Python 3.12 with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 18.18 or
newer (the image uses Node 22).

```sh
# backend on http://localhost:8787
cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8787

# frontend on http://localhost:5173, proxies /api to localhost:8787
cd frontend && npm ci && npm run dev
```

`VITE_API_TARGET` points the dev proxy elsewhere. `http://localhost:5173/?mock=1`
runs the frontend alone on recorded API responses. The API contract is in
[docs/API.md](docs/API.md), with example payloads in `docs/api-examples/`
(regenerated by `uv run --directory backend python scripts/export_api_examples.py`).

## Tests

| Suite | Command | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Data | `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1 uv run pytest` (repository root) | Schema, parsers against golden cells, table invariants, manifest, citations |
| Data, full | `python3 data/fetch_raw.py && uv run pytest` | Same, with every citation checked against its PDF page |
| Backend | `cd backend && uv run pytest` | Rate engine against hand-computed quotes, rule resolution, analysis and API |
| Frontend | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Components with Testing Library and the API contract test |
| Frontend types | `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` | |

Without the PDFs, the citation and PDF parser tests fail with a message
telling you to fetch them; `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1` skips them on purpose
instead. End-to-end Playwright tests come with issue #8.

## Repository layout

```
backend/            FastAPI app (app/), tests, scripts; Dockerfile
frontend/           Vite + React dashboard; Dockerfile and nginx config
data/raw/           manifest.csv, SOURCES.md per carrier, committed raw files
data/pipeline/      parsers and curated rules that write data/processed/
data/processed/     the rate tables the app loads
data/tests/         data tests and golden cells
docs/               decisions, API contract, data docs, agent log
docker-compose.yml  the reviewer run path
```

## How this was built: the agent log

The project was built with Claude Code, one GitHub issue per task, each in its
own branch and git worktree, merged through pull requests. Every session and
subagent transcript is exported to [docs/agent-log/](docs/agent-log/) as
Markdown by a `SessionEnd` hook (`.claude/hooks/export-session.sh`), with the
prompts, the agent's responses and its tool calls. Home directory paths are
redacted. [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) is the running log of the
decisions those conversations led to.

Issue #22 and the integration clean-up are done. All checks pass: backend 80 tests, frontend 195 tests in 20 files, typecheck and build. Five commits are pushed to origin/issue-22-sample-integration (5663109, fc6e190, c81f955, ec9d6a1, 74b0e1c). No PR was opened.

**Part A: new sample**
The generator is `backend/scripts/make_sample_parcels.py` (fixed seed). It now has a `--check` mode that prices the sample with the engine at default controls and prints the segment breakdown. The engine and data were not changed.

Some counts are fixed by row rather than drawn at random, so the shares stay on target: 12 bulky rows, 12 two-to-three-day rows, 3 next-day rows, 5 delivery-area rows and 2 nonstandard-packaging rows. Expedited rows are single light parcels with `price_charged` set to $19.99 (two to three day) or $39.99 (next day). Ground rows leave it empty and use the flat price.

The mix is 200 rows, 307 parcels:
- 81% under 5 lb.
- 7.2% bulky, all boxes between 1 and 2 cu ft. I dropped the larger box because USPS adds a $21 fee above 2 cu ft, which made bulky parcels lose about $50 each.
- 3.9% two to three day, 1.0% next day.
- 80% residential by parcel (76% by row).
- 2.3% in delivery areas.

Numbers at default controls (2026, USPS commercial, $9.99, peak off), recorded in the docstring:
- **Revenue:** $10.67 per parcel (the flat price plus the expedited prices).
- **USPS, the cheapest carrier:** $10.98 per parcel, margin −$0.31 per parcel, 40% of parcels (124 of 307) at a loss.
- **UPS and FedEx:** $31.14 and $31.22 per parcel, 100% at a loss.
- **Best mix:** all 307 parcels go to USPS, so it saves nothing over USPS alone.
- **Where USPS loses:** bulky boxes −$10.69 per parcel (all at a loss); 5–10 lb −$8.17 and 10–20 lb −$6.17; zones 5–6 −$3.59 (68% at a loss) and zones 7–8 −$1.22 (61% at a loss); next day −$4.41.
- **Where USPS gains:** under 1 lb +$3.71, zones 1–4, two to three day +$8.22.
- **Delivery areas do not lose with USPS** (+$2.09), because USPS has no delivery-area surcharge. They do cost more with UPS and FedEx. This is documented rather than tuned away.

Wording and fixtures:
- **API description** is now "An illustrative home-goods shop, an example, not real shipping data (generated by …)".
- **Parcel panel:** the strip reads "Your parcels · sample mix, an example", and the empty-state text names the sample as an illustrative home-goods shop, not real data.
- **Fixtures:** `docs/api-examples` was regenerated and copied into `frontend/src/api/__fixtures__`. Only blended, yearly and sample-parcels changed. I re-requested the two 2027 fixtures through TestClient and they still match exactly, so they were kept.

Test updates:
- The Q3 and Q4 tests now expect numbers I worked out by hand from the new fixtures.
- Where the new data no longer reaches a code branch, I added a test on a modified copy of the fixture instead of dropping the case:
  - the best-mix saving branch, since the best mix now equals USPS;
  - the folding of surcharge kinds beyond three;
  - the driver-sentence variant whose top segment is also the fastest-changing one, now tested on the "residential" dimension.

**Part B: integration**
- **Empty-state buttons:** `ViewProps` now carries `onLoadSample` and `onUploadCsv` from `App.tsx`. Upload clicks the parcel panel's file input through a ref that App passes to `ParcelSetPanel`. The DOM click simulation is gone. New tests cover the views passing the handlers through, the App flow from the Q3 empty state through loading the sample to the answer, and the Q4 Upload CSV button opening the panel's file input.
- **What moved where** (old `views/quote/shared.ts`/`.css`/`.test.ts` and `views/blended/money.ts`, `common.tsx`, `common.css` are deleted):
  - `lib/format.ts`: money, signed money and percent, shares, margin text and class, tier and surcharge labels.
  - `lib/carriers.ts`: carrier names and colours, carriers per year, the missing-carriers note, service names.
  - `hooks/useDebounced.ts`, `hooks/useLastData.ts`, `hooks/useCssColors.ts`. These went into the existing `hooks/` folder rather than `lib/`, to match the codebase.
  - `components/ChartFrame.tsx`, `ChipGroup.tsx`, `NeedParcels.tsx`, `LoadProblem.tsx`.
  - `styles/views.css`, `chips.css`, `chart.css`.
  - `SegmentChips` stays in `views/blended` because only Q3 uses it; it now imports `ChipGroup`.
- **Where two versions differed, I picked:**
  - the debounce version where a delay of 0 passes the value straight through;
  - `pct0` replaced by `formatShare`, which is identical;
  - the Q3 margins use the shared `marginText`/`marginClass`, so the class changes from `money--loss` to `is-loss`. A rule in `blended.css` keeps the margin table bold. The only visible change is that a margin of exactly $0.00 reads "break-even".

- **CSS:** a diff of the built CSS shows only these intended changes.
- **New tests:** `lib/format.test.ts` (the old margin tests plus signed money, percent and shares) and `hooks/useDebounced.test.ts`. `frontend/DESIGN.md` paths are updated.
- **Mock chunk:** the dynamic `import("./mocks")` and `isMockMode` only work when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true or `VITE_MOCKS=1` was set at build time. `?mock=1` still works in `npm run dev` and in tests.
