"""Write one real request/response pair per endpoint to docs/api-examples/.

The frontend uses these files as fixtures and its contract test checks them
against frontend/src/api/types.ts. Regenerate after any engine or data change:

    uv run --directory backend python scripts/export_api_examples.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from app.main import REPO_ROOT, create_app  # noqa: E402

OUT_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "api-examples"

QUOTE_PARCEL = {
    "weight_lb": 3.2,
    "length_in": 14,
    "width_in": 12,
    "height_in": 10,
    "distance_miles": 700,
    "residential": True,
    "speed": "ground",
    "delivery_area": "das",
}


def examples(sample: list[dict]) -> list[tuple[str, str, str, dict | None]]:
    """(name, method, path, request body)."""
    return [
        ("health", "GET", "/api/health", None),
        ("meta", "GET", "/api/meta", None),
        ("sample-parcels", "GET", "/api/sample-parcels", None),
        ("quote", "POST", "/api/quote", {"parcel": QUOTE_PARCEL, "controls": {"year": 2026}}),
        ("breakeven", "POST", "/api/breakeven", {"controls": {"year": 2026}, "residential": True}),
        ("blended", "POST", "/api/blended", {"parcels": sample, "controls": {"year": 2026, "flat_price": 9.99}}),
        (
            "yearly",
            "POST",
            "/api/yearly",
            {"parcels": sample, "controls": {"usps_rate_card": "commercial"}, "next_year_increase_percent": 5.9},
        ),
        (
            "quote-422",
            "POST",
            "/api/quote",
            {"parcel": {**QUOTE_PARCEL, "weight_lb": 80, "speed": "overnight"}, "controls": {"year": 2026}},
        ),
    ]


def export(out_dir: Path = OUT_DIR) -> list[Path]:
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    written = []
    with TestClient(create_app()) as client:
        sample = client.get("/api/sample-parcels").json()["parcels"]
        for name, method, path, body in examples(sample):
            response = client.request(method, path, json=body)
            expected = 422 if name.endswith("422") else 200
            if response.status_code != expected:
                raise SystemExit(f"{name}: HTTP {response.status_code} {response.text[:300]}")
            doc = {
                "request": {"method": method, "path": path, "body": body},
                "response": {"status": response.status_code, "body": response.json()},
            }
            target = out_dir / f"{name}.json"
            target.write_text(json.dumps(doc, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
            written.append(target)
    return written


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for path in export():
        print(f"wrote {path}")

```

"""API contract tests (docs/API.md)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import pytest

from app.api import models as m
from app.engine import segments as seg
from app.main import REPO_ROOT, load_sample_parcels

PARCEL = {"weight_lb": 2, "distance_miles": 300, "residential": True, "speed": "ground"}


def _msgs(resp):
    assert resp.status_code == 422, resp.text
    return {tuple(d["loc"]): d["msg"] for d in resp.json()["detail"]}


def test_health(client):
    assert client.get("/api/health").json() == {"status": "ok"}


def test_meta(client, tables):
    body = client.get("/api/meta").json()
    m.MetaResponse.model_validate(body)
    assert body["years"]["fedex"] == tables.years_for("fedex")
    assert body["defaults"]["year"] == 2026
    assert set(body["defaults"]["as_of"]) == {"usps", "ups", "fedex"}
    assert any(s["rate_card_notes"] for s in body["services"])
    assert any(f["is_proxy"] for f in body["fuel_defaults"] if f["carrier"] == "ups")
    assert body["segments"]["weight_bands"] == list(m.WeightBand.__args__)
    assert body["segments"]["zone_bands"] == list(m.ZoneBand.__args__)
    assert len(body["limitations"]) >= 6


def test_sample_parcels(client):
    body = client.get("/api/sample-parcels").json()
    assert "illustrative" in body["description"].lower()
    assert 150 <= len(body["parcels"]) <= 250
    residential = sum(p["residential"] for p in body["parcels"]) / len(body["parcels"])
    ground = sum(p["speed"] == "ground" for p in body["parcels"]) / len(body["parcels"])
    assert 0.6 < residential < 0.9 and 0.75 < ground < 0.95


def test_quote(client):
    r = client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": {**PARCEL, "speed": "two_three_day"}})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    m.QuoteResponse.model_validate(body)
    tiers = [q["tier"] for q in body["quotes"]]
    first_other = next(i for i, t in enumerate(tiers) if t != "two_three_day")
    assert all(t == "two_three_day" for t in tiers[:first_other])
    requested = [q["total"] for q in body["quotes"][:first_other] if q["available"]]
    assert requested == sorted(requested)
    for q in body["quotes"]:
        if q["available"]:
            assert abs(sum(li["amount"] for li in q["line_items"]) - q["total"]) < 1e-9
            assert abs(q["margin"] - (9.99 - q["total"])) < 1e-9
    cheapest = body["cheapest_by_tier"]["ground"]
    ground = [q for q in body["quotes"] if q["tier"] == "ground" and q["available"]]
    assert cheapest["total"] == min(q["total"] for q in ground)


def test_quote_controls(client):
    base = {"parcel": PARCEL, "controls": {"year": 2025, "usps_rate_card": "retail", "peak": True,
                                            "fuel_override_percent": {"ground": 10}, "flat_price": 5}}
    body = client.post("/api/quote", json=base).json()
    ups = next(q for q in body["quotes"] if q["service_id"] == "ups_ground")
    assert ups["line_items"][-1]["label"].startswith("Fuel Surcharge (10")
    assert ups["as_of"] == "2025-12-10"
    only_fedex = client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": PARCEL, "controls": {"year": 2027}}).json()
    assert {q["carrier"] for q in only_fedex["quotes"]} == {"fedex"}


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "parcel, loc, msg",
    [
        ({**PARCEL, "weight_lb": 80}, ("body", "parcel", "weight_lb"), "weight_lb must be at most 70"),
        ({**PARCEL, "weight_lb": 0}, ("body", "parcel", "weight_lb"), "weight_lb must be greater than 0"),
        ({**PARCEL, "distance_miles": -5}, ("body", "parcel", "distance_miles"), "distance_miles must be at least 0"),
        ({**PARCEL, "speed": "overnight"}, ("body", "parcel", "speed"),
         "speed must be one of 'ground', 'two_three_day' or 'next_day'"),
        ({**PARCEL, "residential": "maybe"}, ("body", "parcel", "residential"), "residential must be true or false"),
        ({**PARCEL, "quantity": 1.5}, ("body", "parcel", "quantity"), "quantity must be a whole number"),
        ({**PARCEL, "length_in": 10}, ("body", "parcel"),
         "give length_in, width_in and height_in together, or none of them"),
        ({k: v for k, v in PARCEL.items() if k != "speed"}, ("body", "parcel", "speed"), "speed is required"),
    ],
)
def test_quote_422_messages(client, parcel, loc, msg):
    assert _msgs(client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": parcel}))[loc] == msg


def test_quote_422_unknown_year_and_bad_date(client):
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": PARCEL, "controls": {"year": 2019}}))
    assert msgs[("body", "controls", "year")].startswith("year must be one of 2023")
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/quote", json={"parcel": PARCEL, "controls": {"as_of": "soon"}}))
    assert "must be a date" in msgs[("body", "controls", "as_of")]
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/quote", content="{not json", headers={"content-type": "application/json"}))
    assert "not valid JSON" in next(iter(msgs.values()))


def test_breakeven(client):
    body = client.post("/api/breakeven", json={"residential": False, "weights_lb": [1, 5, 40],
                                               "distances_miles": [25, 2000]}).json()
    m.BreakevenResponse.model_validate(body)
    assert len(body["cells"]) == 6 and len(body["breakeven_weight_lb"]) == 2
    default = client.get("/api/breakeven?residential=true").json()
    assert len(default["cells"]) == 70 * 8
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/breakeven", json={"weights_lb": [0, 80]}))
    assert "at most 70" in msgs[("body",)]
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/breakeven", json={"distances_miles": [-1]}))
    assert "negative" in msgs[("body",)]
    assert client.get("/api/breakeven?year=1999").status_code == 422


def test_blended(client):
    parcels = load_sample_parcels()
    body = client.post("/api/blended", json={"parcels": parcels, "segment": {"weight_band": "1–5"}}).json()
    m.BlendedResponse.model_validate(body)
    assert {c["carrier"] for c in body["carriers"]} == {"usps", "ups", "fedex"}
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/blended", json={"parcels": []}))
    assert msgs[("body", "parcels")] == "parcels needs at least 1 item(s)"
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/blended", json={"parcels": [{**PARCEL, "weight_lb": 90}]}))
    assert msgs[("body", "parcels", 0, "weight_lb")] == "Parcel 1: weight_lb must be at most 70"
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/blended", json={"parcels": [PARCEL], "segment": {"zone_band": "9"}}))
    assert "must be one of" in msgs[("body", "segment", "zone_band")]


def test_yearly(client):
    body = client.post("/api/yearly", json={"parcels": load_sample_parcels()[:30],
                                            "next_year_increase_percent": 5}).json()
    m.YearlyResponse.model_validate(body)
    assert all(c["projected"]["increase_percent"] == 5 for c in body["carriers"])
    msgs = _msgs(client.post("/api/yearly", json={"parcels": [PARCEL], "next_year_increase_percent": 500}))
    assert msgs[("body", "next_year_increase_percent")] == "next_year_increase_percent must be at most 100"


def test_cors_allows_vite_dev_server(client):
    r = client.options("/api/quote", headers={"Origin": "http://localhost:5173",
                                              "Access-Control-Request-Method": "POST"})
    assert r.headers.get("access-control-allow-origin") == "http://localhost:5173"


def test_segment_labels_match_contract():
    assert [b[0] for b in seg.WEIGHT_BANDS] == list(m.WeightBand.__args__)
    assert [b[0] for b in seg.ZONE_BANDS] == list(m.ZoneBand.__args__)


def test_export_api_examples(tmp_path):
    from scripts.export_api_examples import export

    written = export(tmp_path)
    names = {p.stem for p in written}
    assert {"health", "meta", "sample-parcels", "quote", "breakeven", "blended", "yearly"} <= names
    models = {"meta": m.MetaResponse, "quote": m.QuoteResponse, "breakeven": m.BreakevenResponse,
              "blended": m.BlendedResponse, "yearly": m.YearlyResponse, "sample-parcels": m.SampleParcelsResponse}
    for name, model in models.items():
        model.model_validate(json.loads((tmp_path / f"{name}.json").read_text())["response"]["body"])


def test_committed_examples_match_the_models():
    folder = REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "api-examples"
    if not folder.exists():
        pytest.skip("docs/api-examples not generated yet")
    for path in folder.glob("*.json"):
        doc = json.loads(path.read_text())
        assert {"request", "response"} <= set(doc)

## Issue #3: rate engine and FastAPI backend

The engine and all the endpoints are built and the tests pass. Everything is in `~/parcel-rates-issue-3` on branch `issue-3-engine-api`, in 6 commits (43d7857 to HEAD). Nothing was pushed, no PR was opened and nothing was merged.

**Tests:** `uv run --directory ~/parcel-rates-issue-3/backend pytest` gives 63 passed, 1 skipped, in about 8 s. Coverage is 99% for `app` overall; the engine modules are 95–100%. I ran uvicorn briefly and curled `/api/health` (`{"status":"ok"}`), `/api/quote` (200 with line items and a source for each line) and an over-70 lb parcel (422 with `"weight_lb must be at most 70"`). I then stopped my uvicorn. There is another uvicorn running on port 8000 (pid 5401) that is not mine; I left it alone.

### What was built (`backend/`, its own uv project, Python 3.12)
- **Engine** (`app/engine/`, no FastAPI imports):
  - `tables.py` loads the CSVs from `DATA_DIR` (default `<repo>/data/processed`) once at startup. Tests can also build a small in-memory dataset with `RateTables.from_rows`.
  - `rules.py` covers zone, `as_of`, dimensional-weight rule, rounding, surcharge matching with exclusive groups, and fuel.
  - `quote.py`, `breakeven.py`, `blended.py`, `yearly.py` and `segments.py` hold the four questions and the segment filter.
  - Money is kept in Decimal and rounded half-up to cents only on line items. No price, divisor, threshold or percent is hardcoded.
- **API** (`app/api/`):
  - `models.py` has the Pydantic request and response models.
  - `routes.py` serves `GET /api/meta`, `/api/sample-parcels`, `/api/health`, and `POST /api/quote`, `/api/breakeven`, `/api/blended`, `/api/yearly`. There is also a `GET /api/breakeven` with the default grid, because the issue lists GET while the contract says POST.
  - `errors.py` rewrites 422 messages for a shop owner, e.g. "Parcel 3: weight_lb must be at most 70", and keeps the `{detail:[{loc,msg,type}]}` shape.
  - CORS allows `http://localhost:5173`.
- **Sample data:** `scripts/make_sample_parcels.py` (seed 20261023) writes `app/sample_parcels.csv`: 200 rows, 77% residential, 87% ground, 47 parcels big enough for USPS dimensional weight, 11 in delivery areas, 2 with non-standard packaging. It is labelled illustrative.
- **API examples:** `scripts/export_api_examples.py` writes `docs/api-examples/{health,meta,sample-parcels,quote,breakeven,blended,yearly,quote-422}.json`, each with request and response. The full default breakeven grid makes `breakeven.json` about 250 KB.
- **Tests:** quotes for USPS, UPS and FedEx computed in the test from CSV rows read with the csv module; fuel and exclusive groups on a synthetic dataset; USPS divisor 166/139 by `as_of`; UPS 2025 vs 2026 dimension rounding; peak windows; the USPS 8% transportation increase; availability; breakeven sanity; blended totals equal to the sum of per-parcel quotes; driver contributions summing to the change within a cent; 422 cases; and every example validated against the response models.

### Where `docs/API.md` was ambiguous, and what I decided
1. **Peak add-ons:** the `peak_additional_handling` and `peak_oversize` rows have no thresholds, so a literal reading puts them on every parcel in peak (+$117 oversize). The engine adds them only when an additional-handling or oversize charge already applies, which is what the row notes say ("adds to the Additional Handling Surcharge for packages meeting its criteria").
2. **Thresholds:**
   - Weight thresholds are inclusive (`billable >= min`, `<= max`), which the USPS peak bands need.
   - Dimension and volume thresholds are strict (`>`), as the quotes say ("exceeds", "over"). They use the dimensions rounded by that carrier's dimensional-weight rule.
   - Rounding inches up or to the nearest inch is read from the text of the `rounding` column.
   - The USPS 70 lb dimensional-weight cap is also parsed from that text.
3. **Weight steps:** billable weight is the first step of the service's own table at or above max(actual, dimensional). This keeps the ounce steps for Ground Advantage and also uses the 0.5 lb step that the USPS Priority Mail and Express commercial tables have. The contract only mentions Ground Advantage.
4. **Choosing the dimensional-weight row:** rows are picked by `as_of` only; the latest `effective_from` wins, then the row matching the year. This is needed because UPS rows have no end date and overlap.
5. **`as_of`:** with `peak: true` it is December 10, even if an `as_of` is given. Otherwise it is the given `as_of`, or failing that the carrier's base effective date for the year.
6. **Unavailable quotes** have `total: 0` and no line items.
7. **Default year:** `controls.year` may be omitted and then becomes the latest year all three carriers share (2026). An unknown year returns 422.
8. **Breakeven:**
   - The breakeven weight is the lightest grid weight where USPS total >= the rival's total.
   - Default distances are the USPS band midpoints rounded down, and 2000 for the last band (1800 + 200).
   - FedEx uses Ground or Home Delivery depending on whether the address is residential.
9. **Segments:** the weight band uses actual weight; the zone band uses the USPS zone for the distance.
10. **Yearly:**
    - `controls.as_of` is ignored; each year uses its own effective date, or December 10 with peak.
    - A fuel override applies to every year.
    - Only parcels the carrier can ship in every year are compared; the excluded count is reported.
    - The announced increase is the `all` row when there is one. Otherwise it is a plain, unweighted average of the rows for the services used, filtered to the selected USPS rate card. The response says which with `basis`.
    - Rounded driver contributions are adjusted so they add up exactly to the rounded total change.
11. **Fields added beyond the contract**, which the frontend types need to include:
    - Quotes: `as_of`, plus `condition` on each line item.
    - Breakeven cells: `totals` per carrier.
    - Yearly rows: `warnings`, plus `summary` with the same split as blended.

    The blended and yearly response shapes, which the contract only describes in prose, are defined in `app/api/models.py`. The contract should be updated to point to them.

### Problems in `data/processed` (reported only, not edited)
- **UPS editions:** UPS 2026 tables and rules all start on 2026-09-07 and UPS 2024 on 2024-07-01, because the December originals are missing. UPS year-over-year changes therefore compare editions published at different times of year: 2025 to 2026 is +12%.
- **UPS peak:** the rows labelled 2025 cover only the 2024-25 season, and there are no 2025-26 or 2026-27 rows. Peak adds nothing to UPS 2025 or 2026. One UPS 2023 demand row (from 2023-01-15) has no end date.
- **FedEx 2027:** only the Home Delivery residential charge and January peak rows exist, so 2027 blended cost falls 9% against 2026. The yearly response adds a warning for this.
- **Window ends:** the USPS peak and transportation notes say `effective_to` is exclusive, but `SCHEMA.md` says nothing. The engine treats it as inclusive everywhere; this only matters on the boundary day.
- **AH weight:** UPS and FedEx additional handling by weight means "more than 50 lb" of actual weight, but `min_weight_lb` is applied inclusively to billable weight. So a parcel at exactly 50 lb billable gets the charge. The schema should say whether thresholds are inclusive and which weight they use.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Curated tables


def guide_end(year: int) -> str:
    """Last day a guide's rules apply: the day before the next guide takes effect (open for the latest)."""
    following = rules.GUIDES.get(year + 1)
    if not following:
        return ""
    return (date.fromisoformat(following["effective_date"]) - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()


def surcharge_row(year: int, **values: str) -> dict:
    guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
    row = {"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD, "unit": "usd", "address_type": "any",
           "effective_from": guide["effective_date"], "effective_to": guide_end(year), "fuel_applies": "true",
           "source_file": guide["file"]}
    row.update(values)
    return row


def residential_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.RESIDENTIAL[year]
    rows = []
    for variant, applies_to in (("ground", rules.GROUND), ("air", rules.AIR_AND_3DS)):
        quote = spec[variant]
        (amount,) = rules.amounts_in(quote)
        rows.append(surcharge_row(
            year, surcharge_id=f"ups_residential_{variant}_{year}", display_name="Residential Surcharge",
    rows = []
    for criterion, quote in spec["quotes"].items():
        condition, thresholds, note = rules.AH_CRITERIA[criterion]
        rows.extend(banded_rows(
            year, quote, spec["bands"], surcharge_id=f"ups_additional_handling_{criterion}_{year}",
            display_name="Additional Handling", condition=condition, applies_to="all",
            exclusive_group="ups_handling", source_page=str(spec["page"]),
            notes=(f"Criterion: {note}. Only one Additional Handling charge applies and none when a Large Package "
                   f"Surcharge applies (same exclusive_group). {rules.FUEL_NOTE[year]}"), **thresholds))
    return rows


def large_package_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.LARGE_PACKAGE[year]
    rows = []
    for (address, criterion), quote in spec["quotes"].items():
        thresholds, note = rules.LPS_CRITERIA[criterion]
        rows.extend(banded_rows(
            year, quote, spec["bands"], surcharge_id=f"ups_large_package_{address}_{criterion}_{year}",
            display_name="Large Package Surcharge", condition="oversize", applies_to="all", address_type=address,
            exclusive_group="ups_handling", source_page=str(spec["page"]),
            notes=(f"{address.capitalize()} deliveries only. Criterion: {note}. Large Packages carry a 90 lb minimum "
                   f"billable weight (not modelled). {rules.FUEL_NOTE[year]}"), **thresholds))
    return rows


def peak_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.PEAK.get(year)
    if not spec:
        return []
    rows = []
    for item in spec["rows"]:
        amounts = rules.amounts_in(item["quote"])
        if len(amounts) != len(item["windows"]):
            raise ValueError(f"{year} {item['condition']}: {len(amounts)} amounts for {len(item['windows'])} windows")
        for amount, window in zip(amounts, item["windows"]):
            if window is None:
                continue
            start, end = window
            rows.append(surcharge_row(
                year, surcharge_id=f"ups_{item['condition']}_{year}_{start}", display_name="Demand Surcharge",
                condition=item["condition"], applies_to=item["applies_to"], amount=amount,
                address_type="residential" if item["condition"] == "peak_residential" else "any",
                exclusive_group=item["condition"], effective_from=start, effective_to=end,
                source_file=spec["file"], source_page=str(item["page"]), source_quote=item["quote"],
                notes="; ".join(filter(None, [spec["note"], item.get("note"),
                                              "fuel_applies assumed from the guide's statement that fuel may apply to surcharges"]))))
    return rows


def surcharges() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for year in rules.YEARS:
        rows += residential_rows(year) + delivery_area_rows(year) + additional_handling_rows(year)
        rows += large_package_rows(year) + peak_rows(year)
    return rows


def announced_increase() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for year, spec in rules.ANNOUNCED_INCREASE.items():
        match = re.search(r"(\d+\.\d+)%", spec["quote"])
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"{year}: no percent in {spec['quote']!r}")
        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "product_scope": "all", "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD,
                     "percent": match.group(1), "source_type": "secondary", "source_file": spec["file"],
                     "source_ref": "", "source_quote": spec["quote"]})
    return rows


def dim_weight() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for year, spec in rules.DIM_WEIGHT.items():
        guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "effective_from": guide["effective_date"],
                     "effective_to": "", "divisor": "139", "min_volume_cuin": "0", "rounding": spec["rounding"],
                     "source_file": guide["file"], "source_ref": str(spec["page"]), "source_quote": spec["quote"]})
    return rows

WEEK_ROW = re.compile(rf"({DATE})\s*[-\u2013\u2014]\s*({DATE})")
PERCENT = re.compile(r"\d+\.\d+%")


def parse_date(text: str) -> date:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Restore raw source files listed in data/raw/manifest.csv, politely.

Fetches one file at a time, pauses between requests, retries with backoff on
429/5xx/timeouts, identifies itself with a User-Agent, verifies SHA-256
checksums, and never re-downloads a file whose checksum already matches.

Usage:
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py                 # fetch everything missing or mismatched
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py --carrier ups   # one carrier
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py --verify        # only check what is on disk
  python3 data/fetch_raw.py --record        # fill empty sha256/bytes in the manifest after fetching

Standard library only, so it runs with any Python 3.8+.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import gzip
import hashlib
import random
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

RAW_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "raw"
MANIFEST = RAW_DIR / "manifest.csv"
USER_AGENT = (
    "Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) parcel-rates-dashboard/0.1 "
    "(+https://github.com/aivuk/parcel-rates; polite sequential fetcher)"
)
PAUSE_SECONDS = 3.0
JITTER_SECONDS = 2.0
BACKOFF_SECONDS = (10, 30, 90)
TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120
GZIP_MAGIC = b"\x1f\x8b"

def test_dim_weight_does_not_trigger_additional_handling_weight(tables):

    parcel = Parcel(weight_lb=10, length_in=30, width_in=20, height_in=14, distance_miles=700,
                    residential=False, speed="ground")
    q = quote_service(tables, tables.services["ups_ground"], parcel, Controls(year=2026))

    parcel = Parcel(weight_lb=weight, distance_miles=100, residential=True, speed="ground")
    q = quote_service(tables, tables.services["usps_ground_advantage"], parcel, Controls(year=2026, peak=True))
    peak = [li.surcharge_id for li in q.line_items if li.condition == "peak_base"]
    assert len(peak) == 1 and f"_{band}_" in peak[0]

new='''### Matching rules

The engine applies these rules uniformly; every row must mean what its quote says under them.

- **Windows.** A row applies on `as_of` when `effective_from <= as_of <= effective_to`.
  `effective_to` is inclusive in every table (surcharges, dim_weight): it is the last day
  the rule applies. A document that ends prices "at midnight on Jan. 19" (the day the next
  list starts) is recorded with `effective_to` = Jan. 18.
- **Weight.** When `max_weight_lb` is set the row is a band, matched inclusively on billable
  weight: `min_weight_lb <= billable <= max_weight_lb`, an empty `min_weight_lb` meaning no
  lower bound (USPS peak add-ons: "4-10 lbs" = the 4 lb to 10 lb steps). When only
  `min_weight_lb` is set it is strictly greater than the parcel's actual weight (UPS and
  FedEx additional handling "more than 50 lb", UPS 2026 Large Package "more than 110 lb");
  dimensional weight never triggers it.
- **Dimensions and volume** are strict: longest side `> min_length_in`, second-longest side
  `> min_width_in`, longest + 2 x (other two) `> min_length_plus_girth_in`, volume in cubic
  feet `> min_volume_cuft`, using the dimensions as rounded by the carrier's dim_weight rule
  for `as_of`. A parcel without dimensions meets no dimension or volume threshold.
- **Zone.** `zone_min <= zone <= zone_max`, each bound optional.
- **Peak add-ons.** `peak_additional_handling` applies only when a non-peak rule of
  condition `additional_handling_*` (or the UPS cubic-size additional handling recorded as
  `nonstandard_volume`) applied to the same parcel; `peak_oversize` only when an `oversize`
  rule applied. Both carry no thresholds of their own.

Peak rules apply only when the dashboard's peak toggle is on.'''

```
## Engine rules the endpoints share

- **Zone** from `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv` per carrier: the band
  whose `min_miles <= distance <= max_miles`.
- **Billable weight** per carrier and `as_of` from `dim_weight.csv`: dimensions
  rounded per the row's rounding rule, dimensional weight = volume / divisor
  rounded up, only when volume exceeds `min_volume_cuin`; billable = max(actual
  rounded up to the next weight step, dimensional). USPS Ground Advantage keeps
  its ounce steps for parcels under 1 lb.
- **Base rate**: the first weight step `>= billable weight` in the zone, for
  the service, rate card (`list` for UPS and FedEx, the USPS control otherwise)
  and year.
- **Surcharges**: every rule of that carrier and year whose window contains
  `as_of`, whose `applies_to` covers the service, whose `address_type`
  matches, and whose thresholds the parcel meets; peak conditions only when
  `controls.peak`. Rules in the same `exclusive_group` do not stack: the
  highest amount wins. Percent surcharges apply to the base rate.
- **Fuel**: `percent x (base + surcharges flagged fuel_applies)`, percent from
  `fuel_surcharge.csv` for the year and service group (ground services use
  `ground`, all others `express`) unless overridden. USPS has none.
- **Availability**: FedEx Ground for business addresses only, Home Delivery for
  residential only (from `services.csv`); weight over 70 lb is rejected.
- **as_of**: defaults to the base-rate `effective_date` of the year for each
  carrier. With `peak: true` it is December 10 of the year, inside every
  carrier's peak window. `as_of` therefore also selects time-varying rules such
  as the USPS dimensional divisor (166 until 2026-07-11, 139 after) and the
  2026 USPS 8 % transportation increase.
- **Cheapest per tier**: among available services of the tier, lowest total.
- **Thresholds, windows and peak add-ons**: see "Matching rules" in
  `docs/data/SCHEMA.md` (bands inclusive on billable weight, a lone minimum weight
  strict on actual weight, dimensions strict, `effective_to` inclusive, peak
  add-ons only on top of the charge they add to).
- The engine never hardcodes an amount; every number comes from
  `data/processed/`.

## Errors
```

    assert all(y["fuel"] is None for y in by["usps"]["years"])
    for y in by["ups"]["years"]:
        row = tables.fuel[("ups", y["year"], "ground")]
        assert y["fuel"]["ground"]["default_percent"] == float(row.default_percent)
        assert y["fuel"]["ground"]["applied_percent"] == float(row.default_percent)
        assert y["fuel"]["ground"]["is_proxy"] is True
    from app.engine.types import FuelOverride

+# Backend: FastAPI rate engine over the committed CSV tables.
+# Build context is the repository root (see docker-compose.yml), because the
+# image needs data/processed as well as backend/.
+FROM python:3.12-slim
+
+COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.7.9 /uv /bin/uv
+
+ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
+    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
+    UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 \
+    UV_LINK_MODE=copy \
+    UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/app/.venv \
+    DATA_DIR=/app/data/processed \
+    PATH="/app/.venv/bin:$PATH"
+
+WORKDIR /app
+
+# Dependencies first, so code changes do not reinstall them.
+COPY backend/pyproject.toml backend/uv.lock ./
+RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project --no-cache
+
+COPY backend/app ./app
+COPY data/processed ./data/processed
+
+RUN useradd --system --uid 10001 --no-create-home app
+USER app
+
+EXPOSE 8000
+HEALTHCHECK --interval=5s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=10 \
+    CMD ["python", "-c", "import urllib.request, sys; sys.exit(0 if urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health', timeout=2).status == 200 else 1)"]
+
+CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

+# Frontend: build the Vite app, then serve it with an unprivileged nginx that
+# also proxies /api to the backend service.
+FROM node:22-alpine AS build
+WORKDIR /src
+COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
+RUN npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
+COPY . .
+RUN npm run build
+
+FROM nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.28-alpine
+COPY nginx/default.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
+COPY nginx/security-headers.conf /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf
+COPY --from=build /src/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
+EXPOSE 8080

+server {
+    listen 8080;
+    server_name _;
+    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
+    server_tokens off;
+
+    gzip on;
+    gzip_vary on;
+    gzip_proxied any;
+    gzip_min_length 1024;
+    gzip_types text/css application/javascript application/json image/svg+xml text/plain;
+
+    location /api/ {
+        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
+        proxy_pass http://backend:8000;
+        proxy_http_version 1.1;
+        proxy_set_header Host $host;
+        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
+        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
+        proxy_read_timeout 60s;
+        client_max_body_size 5m;
+    }
+
+    # Hashed build assets never change under the same name.
+    location /assets/ {
+        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
+        add_header Cache-Control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable" always;
+        try_files $uri =404;
+    }
+
+    # SPA fallback: unknown paths get index.html.
+    location / {
+        include /etc/nginx/snippets/security-headers.conf;
+        add_header Cache-Control "no-cache" always;
+        try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
+    }
+}

+# Included in every location, because a location's own add_header discards the
+# server-level ones. Local app: no HSTS. The CSP allows the Google Fonts
+# stylesheet (index.html) and its font files.
+add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;
+add_header Referrer-Policy "strict-origin-when-cross-origin" always;
+add_header X-Frame-Options "DENY" always;
+add_header Content-Security-Policy "default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none'" always;

````
1	# Parcel rates: USPS, UPS and FedEx list prices for a small online shop
2	
3	A dashboard that prices a shop's own parcels at the published prices of the
4	three US parcel carriers, for every year from 2023 to 2026, and shows which
5	carrier is cheapest, where the breakeven points are, how much of the bill is
6	surcharges, and how the cost moved year by year.
7	
8	## Run it
9	
10	Requires Docker with Compose v2. No accounts, keys or database setup.
11	
12	```sh
13	docker compose up --build
14	```
15	
16	Then open **http://localhost:8088**. The first build takes a minute or two.
17	Click "Load sample mix" to load an illustrative parcel set, or upload your
18	own CSV (columns below). Stop with `Ctrl+C`, then `docker compose down`.
19	
20	Only port 8088 is published. nginx serves the built dashboard and proxies
21	`/api/` to the backend container, which is not reachable from the host. The
22	rate tables are baked into the backend image; the app never fetches anything
23	from the carriers at run time.
24	
25	## The problem and the user
26	
27	The user is the owner of a small online shop that sends a few hundred to a few
28	thousand parcels a month, has no negotiated carrier contract, and therefore
29	pays published prices. The carrier is usually chosen by habit, and the flat
30	shipping price charged to customers was set once and not revisited.
31	
32	The dashboard supports two decisions: which carrier and service to use for
33	each kind of parcel, and whether the flat shipping price still covers the real
34	cost once surcharges and yearly price increases are included.
35	
36	### What it answers
37	
38	| # | Question | How |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| 1 | For one parcel (weight, size, distance, home or business, speed), which service is cheapest once surcharges are included, and what are the line items? | Quote for every service, cheapest per speed tier, line items with the source page of each charge |
41	| 2 | Where are the breakeven points between the Postal Service and FedEx or UPS ground, by weight and distance? | Heatmap of the cheapest carrier over a weight by distance grid |
42	| 3 | For the whole parcel set, what is the blended cost per parcel with each carrier, and how much of it is surcharges? | Cost per parcel and margin against the flat price, split into base, surcharges and fuel, segmentable by kind of parcel |
43	| 4 | How did that blended cost change year by year, compared with the average increase the carriers announced, and which parcels drove it? | Same parcel set priced under each year's prices, against the announced increase |
44	
45	Global controls: price year, USPS rate card, fuel surcharge override, peak
46	season toggle, and the flat price charged per parcel.
47	
48	Parcel CSV columns: `weight_lb, length_in, width_in, height_in,
49	distance_miles, residential, speed` (`ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day`),
50	plus optional `quantity`, `price_charged`, `delivery_area`,
51	`nonstandard_packaging`. The full schema is in
52	[docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md); the sample mix is generated by
53	`backend/scripts/make_sample_parcels.py` with a fixed seed and is not real
54	shipping data.
55	
56	## Data provenance
57	
58	All prices come from the carriers' own published rate documents:
59	
60	| Carrier | Base rates | Surcharge rules | Years |
61	|---|---|---|---|
62	| USPS | Postal Explorer CSV zips per price change; Notice 123 PDFs | Notice 123 footnotes; Domestic Mail Manual for dimensional weight | 2023 (July tables, Ground Advantage launch) to 2026 |
63	| UPS | Daily Rates guide PDF per year | Surcharge section of the same guide; demand surcharge PDFs | 2023 to 2026 |
64	| FedEx | Standard List Rates XLSX (PDF for 2023 and 2024) | Yearly surcharge-change PDFs and Service Guides | 2023 to 2026, plus 2027 as a forward year |
65	
66	**Collection.** Every raw file is listed in
67	[data/raw/manifest.csv](data/raw/manifest.csv) with its URL, retrieval method,
68	SHA-256 and size, and each carrier folder has a `SOURCES.md` describing what
69	each file is. `python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores missing files one at a
70	time, with a pause and jitter between requests, backoff on errors, an
71	identifying User-Agent and checksum verification. UPS and FedEx block direct
72	downloads from scripts, so 78 of the 135 files are fetched through the Wayback
73	Machine (`method=wayback`).
74	
75	**What is committed.** Spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML snapshots (58
76	files, about 9 MB) are in git. The PDFs (77 files, about 137 MB) are not; run
77	`python3 data/fetch_raw.py` to get them. The processed tables in
78	`data/processed/` are committed, so the app and the backend tests never need
79	the raw files.
80	
81	**Regenerating `data/processed/`** (needs the PDFs, so fetch first):
82	
83	```sh
84	python3 data/fetch_raw.py                     # standard library only
85	uv run python -m data.pipeline.usps
86	uv run python -m data.pipeline.ups
87	uv run python -m data.pipeline.fedex
88	uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes # rewrites docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md
89	```
90	
91	Base rates are parsed. Surcharges, fuel defaults, announced increases,
92	dimensional weight rules and the distance-to-zone bands are curated by hand
93	in `data/pipeline/*_rules.py`, each row with the source file, page and a
94	verbatim quote. Details: [docs/data/QUALITY.md](docs/data/QUALITY.md) (survey
95	and decisions), [docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md) (tables) and
96	[docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md](docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md) (every rule that
97	changed between years).
98	
99	### Rate cards
100	
101	| Carrier | Card | What it is |
102	|---|---|---|
103	| USPS | `commercial` (default) | Price paid with online postage or shipping software; no contract or volume needed |
104	| USPS | `retail` | Price paid at the Post Office counter |
105	| UPS | `list` | Published Daily Rates, what a shipper without a contract pays |
106	| FedEx | `list` | Published Standard List Rates, same meaning |
107	
108	Commercial is the USPS default because a small online seller buys labels
109	through a marketplace or shipping software, which gives commercial prices to
110	anyone. Comparing UPS and FedEx list prices against USPS retail would
111	overstate what the shop pays the Postal Service. The retail card is one switch
112	away in the controls.
113	
114	## Key choices
115	
116	- **Stack.** Python 3.12, FastAPI and Pydantic for the rate engine and API,
117	  managed with `uv`. Vite, React and TypeScript for the dashboard, Recharts
118	  for line and bar charts and a hand-drawn SVG heatmap. Two containers behind
119	  one `docker compose` command. Reasons and alternatives are in
120	  [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md).
121	- **CSV in memory, no database.** The rate tables are about 40,000 rows of
122	  committed CSV, loaded once at startup. Nothing to configure.
123	- **Curated rules with tested citations.** Surcharge prose in PDFs is too
124	  irregular to parse reliably, so the amounts were transcribed by hand. A test
125	  opens each cited page and checks that the quote, including the amount, is
126	  there.
127	- **Golden cells.** `data/tests/golden/<carrier>_<year>.csv` holds price cells
128	  checked by hand against the documents, including the corners of every
129	  table; the parsed output must match them exactly.
130	- **Time-varying rules.** Every rule carries `effective_from` and an inclusive
131	  `effective_to`, and a quote is priced on an `as_of` date. This handles
132	  mid-year changes such as the USPS dimensional divisor moving from 166 to 139
133	  on 2026-07-12, peak windows and the 2026 USPS transportation surcharge.
134	- **Ledger design.** The answer to each question is the largest thing in its
135	  section; assumptions sit in a quiet side rail. See
136	  [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md).
137	
138	## Known limitations
139	
140	- List prices only: a shipper with a negotiated contract pays less.
141	- Zones are estimated from distance bands, not looked up from ZIP code pairs.
142	- The UPS fuel surcharge default is a proxy taken from FedEx's published
143	  history (no UPS history is retrievable); the slider overrides it.
144	- UPS announced increases come from trade press, not from UPS itself.
145	- UPS peak (demand) surcharge documents for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons
146	  are not in the sources, so UPS 2025 and 2026 peak quotes carry no peak
147	  charges.
148	- FedEx 2027 surcharges are incomplete (only the Home Delivery residential
149	  charge and January peak rows), so 2027 totals understate surcharges.
150	- Peak surcharges are a toggle that prices on December 10 of the year, not by
151	  ship date.
152	- UPS and FedEx bill a large or oversize package at a minimum of 90 lb. That
153	  minimum is not modelled, so the base rate of such parcels is understated;
154	  the surcharge itself is included (issue #18).
155	- Weight is capped at 70 lb, the USPS maximum. Alaska and Hawaii are out of
156	  scope.
157	- UPS 2024 and 2026 use the mid-year revision of the Daily Rates guide,
158	  because the December original could not be retrieved.
159	
160	The same list is returned by `GET /api/meta` and shown in the app.
161	
162	## What I would improve next
163	
164	Open issues in the repository, in rough priority order:
165	
166	- #18 model the 90 lb minimum billable weight for large and oversize packages.
167	- #14 capture the UPS 2025-26 and 2026-27 demand surcharge documents.
168	- #9 real ZIP-to-ZIP zones instead of distance bands.
169	- #10 per-parcel price column and order-value shipping rules (free shipping
170	  over a threshold).
171	- #11 next-year projection from announced increases.
172	- #13 script the source discovery so data collection runs end to end without
173	  an agent.
174	- #8 Playwright end-to-end tests at desktop and phone widths.
175	
176	## Local development without Docker
177	
178	Needs Python 3.12 with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 18.18 or
179	newer (the image uses Node 22).
180	
181	```sh
182	# backend on http://localhost:8787
183	cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8787
184	
185	# frontend on http://localhost:5173, proxies /api to localhost:8787
186	cd frontend && npm ci && npm run dev
187	```
188	
189	`VITE_API_TARGET` points the dev proxy elsewhere. `http://localhost:5173/?mock=1`
190	runs the frontend alone on recorded API responses. The API contract is in
191	[docs/API.md](docs/API.md), with example payloads in `docs/api-examples/`
192	(regenerated by `uv run --directory backend python scripts/export_api_examples.py`).
193	
194	## Tests
195	
196	| Suite | Command | What it covers |
197	|---|---|---|
198	| Data | `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1 uv run pytest` (repository root) | Schema, parsers against golden cells, table invariants, manifest, citations |
199	| Data, full | `python3 data/fetch_raw.py && uv run pytest` | Same, with every citation checked against its PDF page |
200	| Backend | `cd backend && uv run pytest` | Rate engine against hand-computed quotes, rule resolution, analysis and API |
201	| Frontend | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Components with Testing Library and the API contract test |
202	| Frontend types | `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` | |
203	
204	Without the PDFs, the citation and PDF parser tests fail with a message
205	telling you to fetch them; `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1` skips them on purpose
206	instead. End-to-end Playwright tests come with issue #8.
207	
208	## Repository layout
209	
210	```
211	backend/            FastAPI app (app/), tests, scripts; Dockerfile
212	frontend/           Vite + React dashboard; Dockerfile and nginx config
213	data/raw/           manifest.csv, SOURCES.md per carrier, committed raw files
214	data/pipeline/      parsers and curated rules that write data/processed/
215	data/processed/     the rate tables the app loads
216	data/tests/         data tests and golden cells
217	docs/               decisions, API contract, data docs, agent log
218	docker-compose.yml  the reviewer run path
219	```
220	
221	## How this was built: the agent log
222	
223	The project was built with Claude Code, one GitHub issue per task, each in its
224	own branch and git worktree, merged through pull requests. Every session and
225	subagent transcript is exported to [docs/agent-log/](docs/agent-log/) as
226	Markdown by a `SessionEnd` hook (`.claude/hooks/export-session.sh`), with the
227	prompts, the agent's responses and its tool calls. Home directory paths are
228	redacted. [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) is the running log of the
229	decisions those conversations led to.
230	
````

<details>

```
### POST /api/quote  (question 1)
Request `{ parcel: Parcel, controls: Controls }`. Response
`{ quotes: Quote[], cheapest_by_tier: Record<Tier, {carrier, service_id, total}> }`,
quotes sorted by total within the requested tier first, then the other tiers
(unavailable quotes last within a tier). Only carriers that publish the
requested year are quoted (2027 is FedEx only). A tier with no available
service maps to `null` in `cheapest_by_tier`.

### POST /api/breakeven  (question 2)
Request `{ controls: Controls, residential: boolean, weights_lb?: number[], distances_miles?: number[] }`
(defaults: weights 1..70 step 1, distances at every zone band midpoint).
Response: a grid of cells `{ weight_lb, distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, winner: {carrier, service_id, total}, runner_up: {...}, saving, totals: Record<Carrier, number> }`
for the ground tier (FedEx Ground for business, Home Delivery for residential),
plus `breakeven_weight_lb: [{ distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, vs_ups, vs_fedex }]`
per distance band: the lightest grid weight at which the USPS total is >= the
rival's total, `null` when USPS wins at every weight. The default distances are
each USPS band's midpoint (rounded down) and, for the open last band, the
previous band's upper edge + 200 miles.

### GET /api/breakeven
Same response with the default grid; query parameters `residential`
(default true), `year`, `peak`, `usps_rate_card`.

### POST /api/blended  (question 3)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, segment?: SegmentFilter }`.
Response per carrier: parcels shipped, blended cost per parcel, base vs
surcharge vs fuel split (absolute and share), surcharge breakdown by kind,
margin per parcel, share of parcels shipped at a loss, and the cheapest
carrier per parcel (a "best mix" row). Each parcel uses the cheapest service
of that carrier in the parcel's speed tier.
```

</details>

### POST /api/yearly  (question 4)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, next_year_increase_percent?: number }`.
Response per carrier and year: blended cost per parcel under that year's
prices and rules, the year-over-year change, the carrier's announced average
increase for comparison, and the driver breakdown: for each parcel segment
(weight band, zone band, residential, speed), its contribution to the change
in dollars per parcel. Optional projected next year from the slider.

Rules: each year is priced at its own base-rate effective date per carrier
(December 10 of that year when `peak`); `controls.as_of` and `controls.year`
are ignored. `fuel_override_percent` applies to every year. Only parcels the
carrier can ship in every one of its years are compared (`parcels_used`,
`parcels_excluded`). Years a carrier lacks are absent.

Shape: `YearlyResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`: `carriers[] {carrier,
parcels_used, parcels_excluded, years[], projected}`; `projected` is
`{year, increase_percent, cost_per_parcel}` or `null`. Each year row:
`year`, `as_of`, `cost_per_parcel`, `summary` (the blended `Summary`),
`services_used`, `change_vs_previous {from_year, dollars_per_parcel, percent}`
(null for the first year), `announced_increase {percent, basis, services,
source_type}` where `basis` is `"all"` (the carrier-wide row), 
`"average_of_services"` (plain average of the rows for the services used,
listed in `services`) or `"none"`, `drivers` (per dimension a list of
`{segment, parcels, change_per_parcel, change_total}`; the rounded

import json, random
random.seed(42)

    parcels.append({
        "weight_lb": round(random.uniform(0.5, 40), 2),
        "length_in": round(random.uniform(4, 24), 1),
        "width_in": round(random.uniform(4, 18), 1),
        "height_in": round(random.uniform(2, 14), 1),

        "residential": random.random() < 0.75,
        "speed": random.choice(["ground","ground","ground","two_three_day","next_day"]),
    })
payload = {"parcels": parcels, "controls": {"year": 2026}}
with open("/tmp/yearly10k.json", "w") as f:

print(len(json.dumps(payload)), "bytes")
EOF

Review of PR #20 (aivuk/parcel-rates, branch issue-7-docker -> main). Scope: `git diff main...HEAD` in ~/parcel-rates-issue-7 (Docker Compose, Dockerfiles, nginx config, README). Verified by actually building and running the stack, plus reading the diff and surrounding code.

## What I verified (all passed)

- `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml up -d --build` succeeds from a clean checkout; backend reaches `healthy` via its HEALTHCHECK, frontend starts after.
- `GET http://localhost:8088/` → 200, serves `index.html` with correct security headers and CSP.
- `GET http://localhost:8088/api/health` → `{"status":"ok"}`.
- `GET http://localhost:8088/api/meta` → 200, real rate-table metadata.
- `POST http://localhost:8088/api/quote` through the proxy → 200, full computed quote with line items/citations (real engine, not a stub).
- `POST http://localhost:8088/api/yearly` with a generated 10,000-parcel payload (1.44 MB JSON) → 200 in ~14s, well inside `proxy_read_timeout 60s` and `client_max_body_size 5m`.
- Backend port 8000 is **not** reachable from the host (`expose`, not `ports` — confirmed connection refused), matching the README's claim.
- Security headers + CSP are present identically on `/`, `/assets/...`, and `/api/...` responses (the shared `security-headers.conf` snippet is `include`d in all three locations).
- CSP (`frontend/nginx/security-headers.conf:7`) matches exactly what `index.html` loads: self script/style/asset, `fonts.googleapis.com` (style-src) + `fonts.gstatic.com` (font-src) for the Google Fonts link, nothing broader. `connect-src 'self'` is correct — the frontend API client only calls relative `/api/...` paths.
- gzip is active (`Vary: Accept-Encoding` seen on JS asset); `text/html` is gzip-compressed by nginx by default regardless of `gzip_types` config, so that's fine.
- Non-root: backend runs as `uid=10001 app`, frontend runs as `uid=101 nginx` (nginx-unprivileged image). No secrets in either Dockerfile.
- Lockfile-driven installs: `uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project` and `npm ci`, both with dependency-manifest-first `COPY` for good layer caching.
- `.dockerignore` correctly excludes `data/raw` (PDFs), `frontend` (node_modules), `**/.venv`, `.git`, and the whole `docs/` tree (which holds `docs/agent-log/`).
- No remaining references to dev ports 8000/8001 anywhere except the backend's own internal container port (`docker-compose.yml:13`, `frontend/nginx/default.conf:15`), which is intentional and not host-published — consistent with the README's "backend not reachable from the host" claim. `frontend/vite.config.ts` and `README.md`/`frontend/README.md` consistently moved local dev to port 8787.
- Data suite (`ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1 uv run pytest`): 261 passed, 593 skipped (PDF-gated, as documented). Backend: 72 tests pass (17+21+8+26, matches PR description). Frontend: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` → **92 tests pass** (not 62 as the PR description states — but that number doesn't appear in the README itself, only in the PR body, so it's not a README-accuracy bug, just a stale PR description worth fixing before merge).
- Cleaned up with `docker compose down`; confirmed only the `parcel-rates` project's containers/network were touched — the unrelated running projects (newtechlab-app, aula-grp-test, ibkr-clientportalgateway, ports 3001/3002/5000/8001) were left untouched throughout.

## Findings

**[HIGH] README claims fully working dashboard views that are actually placeholders**
File: `README.md:36-43` (the "What it answers" table), and the whole "Run it" section framing.
Issue: I confirmed in code that all four view components are stubs:
- `frontend/src/views/QuoteView.tsx`, `BreakevenView.tsx`, `BlendedView.tsx`, `YearlyView.tsx` are each 6 lines that render `QuestionPlaceholder`.
- `frontend/src/views/QuestionPlaceholder.tsx:16` literally renders `"View in progress (issue #{def.issue})."` in the running app.
- Issues #5 ("Views: single-parcel quote (Q1) and breakeven map (Q2)") and #6 ("Views: blended cost... and year-over-year change") are both still **OPEN**, not merged.

Yet README.md's "What it answers" table describes these as working features ("Quote for every service, cheapest per speed tier, line items with the source page of each charge", "Heatmap of the cheapest carrier over a weight by distance grid", etc.), and nowhere in the README (I grepped for "placeholder", "in progress", "#5", "#6" — no hits) does it disclose that a reviewer who runs the documented command and opens http://localhost:8088 will see "View in progress" instead of the described charts/heatmaps/tables. This is exactly the discrepancy the task flagged as a likely risk, and it's real: a stranger following the README's exact run command gets a working *app* (container-wise) but not the *features* the README describes as present.
Fix: Add an explicit "in progress" note to the "What it answers" table (e.g., a column or footnote referencing issues #5/#6), or soften the "How" column to describe what each view *will* show once #5/#6 land, mirroring what `QuestionPlaceholder` already tells the user in-app.

## Lower-severity notes (not blocking)

**[MEDIUM] Base images pinned by tag only, not digest**
Files: `backend/Dockerfile:5` (`python:3.12-slim`), `frontend/Dockerfile:3` (`node:22-alpine`), `frontend/Dockerfile:10` (`nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.28-alpine`).
These tags are mutable upstream; only the `uv` binary is pinned precisely (`ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.7.9`, which Docker then resolves/caches to a digest). For stricter reproducibility, pin the three base images by digest too. Not a blocker for an MVP review exercise, but worth a follow-up.

**[LOW] Frontend container has no HEALTHCHECK**
`frontend/Dockerfile` — nothing in compose depends on frontend health, so this is cosmetic, not functionally required.

**[LOW] Stale test count in PR description**
PR #20 body says "frontend 62 tests"; actual is 92. Doesn't affect README (which has no numeric test-count claims), but worth correcting before merge so the merge commit/PR history isn't misleading.

1	import { test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
2	import path from "node:path";
3	import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
4	import { isMobile, loadSample, openApp, openSettings, setBox, settled, showView, type ViewId } from "./helpers";
5	
6	/**
7	 * Full-page captures of every view for the UX review (docs/ux-review.md), run with
8	 * `npm run e2e:update-screens`. Deterministic: the fixed sample mix, default controls,
9	 * the default quote form, reduced motion, settled charts and the page scrolled to the top.
10	 */
11	const DIR = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "screenshots");
12	
13	/** Resolve once nothing inside the charts has changed for a few frames (Recharts animates in). */
14	async function chartsSettled(page: Page): Promise<void> {
15	  // A function passed to evaluate, not waitForFunction: the app's CSP forbids string eval.
16	  await page.evaluate(
17	    () =>
18	      new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
19	        let last = "";
20	        let same = 0;
21	        const tick = () => {
22	          const snap = [...document.querySelectorAll(".recharts-wrapper, .hm__svg")].map((e) => e.innerHTML).join("|");
23	          same = snap === last ? same + 1 : 0;
24	          last = snap;
25	          if (same >= 5) resolve();
26	          else requestAnimationFrame(tick);
27	        };
28	        requestAnimationFrame(tick);
29	      }),
30	  );
31	}
32	
33	async function capture(page: Page, name: string, project: string, scheme: string): Promise<void> {
34	  await settled(page);
35	  await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
36	  await chartsSettled(page);
37	  // The settings rail is sticky: without this it lands mid-page in a full-page capture.
38	  await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));
39	  await page.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r))));
40	  await page.screenshot({
41	    path: path.join(DIR, `${name}-${project}-${scheme}.png`),
42	    fullPage: true,
43	    animations: "disabled",
44	    caret: "hide",
45	  });
46	}
47	
48	const VIEWS: { name: string; view: ViewId; setup?: (page: Page) => Promise<void> }[] = [
49	  {
50	    name: "q1-typical",
51	    view: "quote",
52	    setup: async (page) => {
53	      // Open the cheapest row so the line items and their sources are in the shot.
54	      await page.locator(".qrank > li").first().getByRole("button").click();
55	    },
56	  },

58	  { name: "q2", view: "breakeven" },

1	# Parcel rates: USPS, UPS and FedEx list prices for a small online shop
2	
3	A dashboard that prices a shop's own parcels at the published prices of the
4	three US parcel carriers, for every year from 2023 to 2026, and shows which
5	carrier is cheapest, where the breakeven points are, how much of the bill is
6	surcharges, and how the cost moved year by year.
7	
8	## Run it
9	
10	Requires Docker with Compose v2. No accounts, keys or database setup.
11	
12	```sh
13	docker compose up --build
14	```
15	
16	Then open **http://localhost:8088**. The first build takes a minute or two.
17	Click "Load sample mix" to load an illustrative example parcel set, or upload your
18	own CSV (columns below). Stop with `Ctrl+C`, then `docker compose down`.
19	
20	Only port 8088 is published. nginx serves the built dashboard and proxies
21	`/api/` to the backend container, which is not reachable from the host. The
22	rate tables are baked into the backend image; the app never fetches anything
23	from the carriers at run time.
24	
25	## What it looks like
26	
27	Captured by the Playwright suite against `docker compose up` with the sample
28	mix and the default controls (2026 prices, USPS commercial, $9.99 charged per
29	parcel). The review of every capture, desktop and phone, light and dark, is in
30	[docs/ux-review.md](docs/ux-review.md).
31	
32	**Q1. One parcel.** A 3 lb box going 600 miles to a home costs $8.95 with USPS
33	Ground Advantage, $1.04 under the $9.99 the shop charges; FedEx Home Delivery
34	and UPS Ground cost about $30, partly because they bill the box at its 6 lb
35	dimensional weight. Each line item cites the rate file it came from.
36	
37	![Q1: the cheapest service for one parcel with its line items](docs/screenshots/q1-quote-desktop.png)
38	
39	**Q2. Breakevens.** For home delivery USPS Ground Advantage is cheapest at every
40	weight up to 450 miles (zones 1-4); from 800 miles on it stops winning at 27 lb,
41	UPS Ground or FedEx Home Delivery take over up to 50 lb, and USPS wins again
42	from 51 lb.
43	
44	![Q2: weight by distance map of the cheapest ground carrier](docs/screenshots/q2-breakeven-desktop.png)
45	
46	**Q3. The whole mix.** Shipping all 307 sample parcels with USPS costs $10.98 a
47	parcel against $31.14 with UPS and $31.22 with FedEx, yet the shop still loses
48	$0.31 a parcel: 40 % of parcels (124 of 307) ship at a loss even with the
49	cheapest carrier.
50	
51	![Q3: blended cost per carrier, the loss verdict and the cost split](docs/screenshots/q3-blended-desktop.png)
52	
53	**Q4. Year over year.** The same mix with USPS went from $9.17 in 2023 to $10.98
54	in 2026 (+19.7 %), 3.3 points more than the +16.4 % USPS announced over those
55	years; at its latest announced +6.5 % it would cost $11.70 in 2027.
56	
57	![Q4: cost per parcel by year against the announced increases](docs/screenshots/q4-yearly-desktop.png)
58	
59	**On a phone** the answer is on the first screen and the assumptions sit
60	behind "Adjust" (left: Q1; right: Q3 in dark mode).

67	## The problem and the user
68	
69	The user is the owner of a small online shop that sends a few hundred to a few
70	thousand parcels a month, has no negotiated carrier contract, and therefore
71	pays published prices. The carrier is usually chosen by habit, and the flat
72	shipping price charged to customers was set once and not revisited.
73	
74	The dashboard supports two decisions: which carrier and service to use for
75	each kind of parcel, and whether the flat shipping price still covers the real
76	cost once surcharges and yearly price increases are included.
77	
78	### What it answers
79	
80	| # | Question | The view |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| 1 | For one parcel (weight, size, distance, home or business, speed), which service is cheapest once surcharges are included, and what are the line items? | The cheapest total for the chosen speed comes first, with its saving over the next cheapest and the margin against your price. Below it, every carrier's cheapest service ranked, each with base rate, every surcharge (with its source page) and fuel. The form can start from one of your loaded parcels. |
83	| 2 | Where are the breakeven points between the Postal Service and FedEx or UPS ground, by weight and distance? | A weight by distance heatmap coloured by the cheapest ground carrier, for home or business delivery, with a heavy line where USPS stops winning and a plain-words readout of the breakeven weights; every cell's prices on hover, tap or focus, and the grid as a table. |
84	| 3 | For the whole parcel set, what is the blended cost per parcel with each carrier, and how much of it is surcharges? | The cheapest single carrier's cost per parcel and the "best mix" (cheapest carrier per parcel), then a yes or no on whether your shipping price covers the cost, the margin per parcel and the share shipped at a loss per carrier. A stacked chart (or table) splits the cost into base, the largest surcharges and fuel. Chips narrow everything to one kind of parcel (weight, distance, home or business, speed). |
85	| 4 | How did that blended cost change year by year, compared with the average increase the carriers announced, and which parcels drove it? | The cheapest carrier's change since the first year against the compounded announced increases, a year by year chart (dollars or index) with the announced path, how much of the biggest rise was fuel, the segments that drove each step, and a next-year slider that projects the cost. |
86	
87	Global controls: price year, USPS rate card, fuel surcharge override, peak
88	season toggle, and the flat price charged per parcel.
89	
90	Parcel CSV columns: `weight_lb, length_in, width_in, height_in,
91	distance_miles, residential, speed` (`ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day`),
92	plus optional `quantity`, `price_charged`, `delivery_area`,
93	`nonstandard_packaging`. The full schema is in
94	[docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md).
95	
96	**The sample mix** is an illustrative home-goods shop, an example and not real
97	shipping data, generated by `backend/scripts/make_sample_parcels.py` with a
98	fixed seed: 200 rows, 307 parcels, mostly light ground parcels in boxes under
99	one cubic foot (about 80 % under 5 lb), about 7 % bulky boxes over one cubic
100	foot, 4 % two to three day and 1 % next day, about 80 % to homes, distances
101	weighted toward the middle zones, and a handful in delivery areas. Ground rows
102	leave `price_charged` empty and use the flat price control; expedited rows
103	carry what a shop would charge at checkout, $19.99 for two to three day and
104	$39.99 for next day, because real shops charge more for faster shipping. At the
105	default controls (2026, USPS commercial, $9.99) the mix opens near break-even:
106	USPS, the cheapest carrier, costs $10.98 per parcel against $10.67 charged on
107	average (−$0.31 per parcel), and the 40 % of parcels shipped at a loss are
108	mostly the bulky boxes, parcels over 5 lb and the far zones.
109	
110	## Data provenance
111	
112	All prices come from the carriers' own published rate documents:
113	
114	| Carrier | Base rates | Surcharge rules | Years |
115	|---|---|---|---|
116	| USPS | Postal Explorer CSV zips per price change; Notice 123 PDFs | Notice 123 footnotes; Domestic Mail Manual for dimensional weight | 2023 (July tables, Ground Advantage launch) to 2026 |
117	| UPS | Daily Rates guide PDF per year | Surcharge section of the same guide; demand surcharge PDFs | 2023 to 2026 |
118	| FedEx | Standard List Rates XLSX (PDF for 2023 and 2024) | Yearly surcharge-change PDFs and Service Guides | 2023 to 2026, plus 2027 as a forward year |
119	
120	**Collection.** Every raw file is listed in
121	[data/raw/manifest.csv](data/raw/manifest.csv) with its URL, retrieval method,
122	SHA-256 and size, and each carrier folder has a `SOURCES.md` describing what
123	each file is. `python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores missing files one at a
124	time, with a pause and jitter between requests, backoff on errors, an
125	identifying User-Agent and checksum verification. UPS and FedEx block direct
126	downloads from scripts, so 78 of the 135 files are fetched through the Wayback
127	Machine (`method=wayback`).
128	
129	**What is committed.** Spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML snapshots (58
130	files, about 9 MB) are in git. The PDFs (77 files, about 137 MB) are not; run
131	`python3 data/fetch_raw.py` to get them. The processed tables in
132	`data/processed/` are committed, so the app and the backend tests never need
133	the raw files.
134	
135	**Regenerating `data/processed/`** (needs the PDFs, so fetch first):
136	
137	```sh
138	python3 data/fetch_raw.py                     # standard library only
139	uv run python -m data.pipeline.usps
140	uv run python -m data.pipeline.ups
141	uv run python -m data.pipeline.fedex
142	uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes # rewrites docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md
143	```
144	
145	Base rates are parsed. Surcharges, fuel defaults, announced increases,
146	dimensional weight rules and the distance-to-zone bands are curated by hand
147	in `data/pipeline/*_rules.py`, each row with the source file, page and a
148	verbatim quote. Details: [docs/data/QUALITY.md](docs/data/QUALITY.md) (survey
149	and decisions), [docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md) (tables) and
150	[docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md](docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md) (every rule that
151	changed between years).
152	
153	### Rate cards
154	
155	| Carrier | Card | What it is |
156	|---|---|---|
157	| USPS | `commercial` (default) | Price paid with online postage or shipping software; no contract or volume needed |
158	| USPS | `retail` | Price paid at the Post Office counter |
159	| UPS | `list` | Published Daily Rates, what a shipper without a contract pays |
160	| FedEx | `list` | Published Standard List Rates, same meaning |
161	
162	Commercial is the USPS default because a small online seller buys labels
163	through a marketplace or shipping software, which gives commercial prices to
164	anyone. Comparing UPS and FedEx list prices against USPS retail would
165	overstate what the shop pays the Postal Service. The retail card is one switch
166	away in the controls.
167	
168	## Key choices
169	
170	- **Stack.** Python 3.12, FastAPI and Pydantic for the rate engine and API,
171	  managed with `uv`. Vite, React and TypeScript for the dashboard, Recharts
172	  for line and bar charts and a hand-drawn SVG heatmap. Two containers behind
173	  one `docker compose` command. Reasons and alternatives are in
174	  [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md).
175	- **CSV in memory, no database.** The rate tables are about 40,000 rows of
176	  committed CSV, loaded once at startup. Nothing to configure.
177	- **Curated rules with tested citations.** Surcharge prose in PDFs is too
178	  irregular to parse reliably, so the amounts were transcribed by hand. A test
179	  opens each cited page and checks that the quote, including the amount, is
180	  there.
181	- **Golden cells.** `data/tests/golden/<carrier>_<year>.csv` holds price cells
182	  checked by hand against the documents, including the corners of every
183	  table; the parsed output must match them exactly.
184	- **Time-varying rules.** Every rule carries `effective_from` and an inclusive
185	  `effective_to`, and a quote is priced on an `as_of` date. This handles
186	  mid-year changes such as the USPS dimensional divisor moving from 166 to 139
187	  on 2026-07-12, peak windows and the 2026 USPS transportation surcharge.
188	- **Ledger design.** The answer to each question is the largest thing in its
189	  section; assumptions sit in a quiet side rail. See
190	  [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md).
191	
192	## Known limitations
193	
194	- List prices only: a shipper with a negotiated contract pays less.
195	- Zones are estimated from distance bands, not looked up from ZIP code pairs.
196	- The UPS fuel surcharge default is a proxy taken from FedEx's published
197	  history (no UPS history is retrievable); the slider overrides it.
198	- UPS announced increases come from trade press, not from UPS itself.
199	- UPS peak (demand) surcharge documents for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons
200	  are not in the sources, so UPS 2025 and 2026 peak quotes carry no peak
201	  charges.
202	- FedEx 2027 surcharges are incomplete (only the Home Delivery residential
203	  charge and January peak rows), so 2027 totals understate surcharges.
204	- Peak surcharges are a toggle that prices on December 10 of the year, not by
205	  ship date.
206	- UPS and FedEx bill a large or oversize package at a minimum of 90 lb. That
207	  minimum is not modelled, so the base rate of such parcels is understated;
208	  the surcharge itself is included (issue #18).
209	- Weight is capped at 70 lb, the USPS maximum. Alaska and Hawaii are out of
210	  scope.
211	- UPS 2024 and 2026 use the mid-year revision of the Daily Rates guide,
212	  because the December original could not be retrieved.
213	
214	The same list is returned by `GET /api/meta` and shown in the app.
215

229	## Local development without Docker
230	
231	Needs Python 3.12 with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 18.18 or
232	newer (the image uses Node 22).
233	
234	```sh
235	# backend on http://localhost:8787
236	cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8787
237	
238	# frontend on http://localhost:5173, proxies /api to localhost:8787
239	cd frontend && npm ci && npm run dev
240	```
241	
242	`VITE_API_TARGET` points the dev proxy elsewhere. `http://localhost:5173/?mock=1`
243	runs the frontend alone on recorded API responses. The API contract is in
244	[docs/API.md](docs/API.md), with example payloads in `docs/api-examples/`
245	(regenerated by `uv run --directory backend python scripts/export_api_examples.py`).
246	
247	## Tests
248	
249	| Suite | Command | What it covers |
250	|---|---|---|
251	| Data | `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1 uv run pytest` (repository root) | Schema, parsers against golden cells, table invariants, manifest, citations |
252	| Data, full | `python3 data/fetch_raw.py && uv run pytest` | Same, with every citation checked against its PDF page |
253	| Backend | `cd backend && uv run pytest` | Rate engine against hand-computed quotes, rule resolution, analysis and API |
254	| Frontend | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Components with Testing Library and the API contract test |
255	| Frontend types | `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` | |
256	| End to end | `docker compose up -d --build`, then `cd frontend && npx playwright install chromium && npm run e2e` | Playwright at 1440 × 900 and 375 × 812 (touch): the four questions, global controls, URL state, CSV upload, the phone settings sheet, and axe on every view in light and dark |
257	| Screenshots | same stack, `cd frontend && npm run e2e:update-screens` | Rewrites `frontend/e2e/screenshots/` (every view, both sizes, light and dark), reviewed in [docs/ux-review.md](docs/ux-review.md) |
258	
259	Without the PDFs, the citation and PDF parser tests fail with a message
260	telling you to fetch them; `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1` skips them on purpose
261	instead. The end-to-end suite targets `http://localhost:8088`; set
262	`E2E_BASE_URL` to run it elsewhere, for example against the dev servers
263	(`E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:5173 npm run e2e`).
264	
265	## Repository layout
266	
267	```
268	backend/            FastAPI app (app/), tests, scripts; Dockerfile
269	frontend/           Vite + React dashboard; Dockerfile and nginx config
270	data/raw/           manifest.csv, SOURCES.md per carrier, committed raw files
271	data/pipeline/      parsers and curated rules that write data/processed/
272	data/processed/     the rate tables the app loads
273	data/tests/         data tests and golden cells
274	docs/               decisions, API contract, data docs, agent log
275	docker-compose.yml  the reviewer run path
276	```
277	
278	## How this was built: the agent log
279	
280	The project was built with Claude Code, one GitHub issue per task, each in its
281	own branch and git worktree, merged through pull requests. Every session and
282	subagent transcript is exported to [docs/agent-log/](docs/agent-log/) as
283	Markdown by a `SessionEnd` hook (`.claude/hooks/export-session.sh`), with the
284	prompts, the agent's responses and its tool calls. Home directory paths are
285	redacted. [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) is the running log of the
286	decisions those conversations led to.

142	## Loading and empty states
143	
144	Not in the screenshot set (captures wait for answers), but covered by tests:
145	Q3 and Q4 show "Load the sample mix or upload a CSV" with both actions before a
146	set is loaded (`q3-blended.spec.ts`), Q1 keeps the previous answer dimmed while
147	the next one loads, and a 422 shows the server's message under the weight
148	input with `aria-invalid` (`q1-quote.spec.ts`).
149	
150	## Capture notes
151	
152	- Captures are deterministic in content (fixed sample, fixed controls,
153	  reduced motion, CSS transitions finished, charts unchanged for five frames,
154	  fonts loaded, page scrolled to the top). A recapture can still differ by a
155	  few thousand anti-aliased pixels, so the images are for review, not pixel
156	  assertions.
157	- The README images in `docs/screenshots/` are the desktop light captures
158	  cropped above the footer and resized to 1200 px wide, plus two phone first
159	  screens, quantised to 256-colour PNG and passed through `optipng`.

- Touch-target fixes (`base.css`, `controls.css`) are wrapped in `@media (pointer: coarse)` only — desktop (`pointer: fine`) is unaffected. Confirmed by reading the full diff; no unscoped min-height changes leaking to desktop.
