16	
17	export const API_BASE = "/api";
18	
19	/** A readable problem with one input field, for display to the shop owner. */
20	export interface FieldProblem {
21	  field: string;
22	  message: string;
23	}
24	
25	export class ApiError extends Error {
26	  readonly status: number;
27	  readonly problems: FieldProblem[];
28	
29	  constructor(status: number, message: string, problems: FieldProblem[] = []) {
30	    super(message);
31	    this.name = "ApiError";
32	    this.status = status;
33	    this.problems = problems;
34	  }
35	}
36	
37	/** Turn a Pydantic `loc` like ["body","parcels",3,"weight_lb"] into "parcels row 4 · weight_lb". */
38	export function describeLoc(loc: readonly (string | number)[]): string {
39	  const parts = loc[0] === "body" || loc[0] === "query" ? loc.slice(1) : loc;
40	  return parts
41	    .map((p) => (typeof p === "number" ? `row ${p + 1}` : p))
42	    .join(" · ");
43	}
44	
45	function isIssue(x: unknown): x is ValidationIssue {
46	  return (
47	    typeof x === "object" &&
48	    x !== null &&
49	    Array.isArray((x as ValidationIssue).loc) &&
50	    typeof (x as ValidationIssue).msg === "string"
51	  );
52	}
53	
54	export function problemsFromBody(body: unknown): FieldProblem[] {
55	  if (typeof body !== "object" || body === null || !("detail" in body)) return [];
56	  const detail = (body as ValidationErrorBody).detail;
57	  if (typeof detail === "string") return [{ field: "", message: detail }];
58	  if (!Array.isArray(detail)) return [];
59	  return detail.filter(isIssue).map((d) => ({ field: describeLoc(d.loc), message: d.msg }));
60	}
61	
62	async function readJson(res: Response): Promise<unknown> {
63	  const text = await res.text();
64	  if (!text) return null;
65	  try {
66	    return JSON.parse(text);
67	  } catch {
68	    return null;
69	  }
70	}

72	function statusMessage(status: number): string {
73	  if (status === 422) return "Some inputs were not accepted.";
74	  if (status === 404) return "The rate service does not know this request.";
75	  if (status >= 500) return "The rate service had a problem. Try again in a moment.";
76	  return `The rate service answered with status ${status}.`;
77	}

79	export interface ApiClient {
80	  health(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<HealthResponse>;
81	  meta(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Meta>;
82	  sampleParcels(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SampleParcels>;
83	  quote(body: QuoteRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<QuoteResponse>;
84	  breakeven(body: BreakevenRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<BreakevenResponse>;

94	export function createHttpClient({ baseUrl = API_BASE, fetchImpl }: ClientOptions = {}): ApiClient {
95	  const doFetch = fetchImpl ?? ((input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => fetch(input, init));
96	
97	  async function request<T>(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
98	    let res: Response;
99	    try {
100	      res = await doFetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, {
101	        ...init,
102	        headers: { Accept: "application/json", ...(init.body ? { "Content-Type": "application/json" } : {}) },
103	      });
104	    } catch (err) {

107	    }
108	    const body = await readJson(res);
109	    if (!res.ok) {
110	      const problems = problemsFromBody(body);
111	      throw new ApiError(res.status, statusMessage(res.status), problems);
112	    }
113	    if (body === null) throw new ApiError(res.status, "The rate service sent an empty answer.");
114	    return body as T;
115	  }
116	
117	  const post = <T>(path: string, body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal) =>
118	    request<T>(path, { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body), signal });

120	  return {

122	    meta: (signal) => request<Meta>("/meta", { signal }),
123	    sampleParcels: (signal) => request<SampleParcels>("/sample-parcels", { signal }),

142	      }, delayMs);
143	    });
144	  return {

146	    meta: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockMeta),
147	    sampleParcels: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockSampleParcels),
148	    quote: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockQuote()),

150	    blended: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockBlended()),
151	    yearly: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockYearly()),
152	  };
153	}

34	const TRUE_WORDS = new Set(["true", "yes", "1", "y"]);
35	const FALSE_WORDS = new Set(["false", "no", "0", "n"]);
36	
37	export function parseBool(raw: string): boolean | undefined {
38	  const v = raw.trim().toLowerCase();
39	  if (TRUE_WORDS.has(v)) return true;
40	  if (FALSE_WORDS.has(v)) return false;
41	  return undefined;
42	}
43	
44	function parseNumber(raw: string): number | undefined {
45	  const cleaned = raw.trim().replace(/^\$/, "").replace(/,/g, "");
46	  if (cleaned === "") return undefined;
47	  const n = Number(cleaned);
48	  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : undefined;
49	}

51	const SPEED_ALIASES: Record<string, Tier> = {
52	  ground: "ground",
53	  two_three_day: "two_three_day",

55	  "2_3_day": "two_three_day",
56	  next_day: "next_day",
57	  overnight: "next_day",
58	  "next day": "next_day",
59	};

61	type Row = Record<string, string | undefined>;
62	
63	class RowReader {
64	  readonly errors: CsvProblem[] = [];
65	  constructor(private readonly row: Row, private readonly rowNumber: number) {}
66	
67	  private fail(column: string, message: string): undefined {
68	    this.errors.push({ row: this.rowNumber, column, message });
69	    return undefined;
70	  }
71	
72	  text(column: string): string {
73	    return (this.row[column] ?? "").trim();
74	  }
75	
76	  number(column: string, required: boolean, check: (n: number) => string | null): number | undefined {
77	    const raw = this.text(column);
78	    if (raw === "") return required ? this.fail(column, `${column} is empty`) : undefined;
79	    const n = parseNumber(raw);
80	    if (n === undefined) return this.fail(column, `${column} "${raw}" is not a number`);
81	    const problem = check(n);
82	    return problem ? this.fail(column, problem) : n;
83	  }
84	
85	  bool(column: string, required: boolean): boolean | undefined {
86	    const raw = this.text(column);
87	    if (raw === "") return required ? this.fail(column, `${column} is empty; use true or false`) : undefined;
88	    const b = parseBool(raw);
89	    if (b === undefined) return this.fail(column, `${column} "${raw}" is not true/false, yes/no or 1/0`);
90	    return b;
91	  }
92

94	    const raw = this.text("speed");
95	    if (raw === "") return this.fail("speed", "speed is empty");

97	    if (!tier) return this.fail("speed", `speed "${raw}" is not one of ${TIERS.join(", ")}`);
98	    return tier;
99	  }
100	
101	  deliveryArea(): DeliveryArea | undefined {
102	    const raw = this.text("delivery_area").toLowerCase();

105	    return this.fail("delivery_area", `delivery_area "${raw}" is not one of ${DELIVERY_AREAS.join(", ")}`);
106	  }
107	}

109	const positive = (col: string) => (n: number) => (n > 0 ? null : `${col} must be more than 0`);

111	function readRow(row: Row, rowNumber: number): { parcel?: Parcel; errors: CsvProblem[] } {
112	  const r = new RowReader(row, rowNumber);
113	  const weight = r.number("weight_lb", true, (n) => {
114	    if (n <= 0) return "weight_lb must be more than 0";
115	    if (n > MAX_WEIGHT_LB) return `weight_lb ${n} is over the ${MAX_WEIGHT_LB} lb limit`;
116	    return null;
117	  });
118	  const distance = r.number("distance_miles", true, (n) => (n >= 0 ? null : "distance_miles cannot be negative"));
119	  const residential = r.bool("residential", true);
120	  const speed = r.speed();
121	  const length = r.number("length_in", false, positive("length_in"));
122	  const width = r.number("width_in", false, positive("width_in"));
123	  const height = r.number("height_in", false, positive("height_in"));
124	  const quantity = r.number("quantity", false, (n) =>
125	    Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 1 ? null : "quantity must be a whole number of at least 1",
126	  );
127	  const price = r.number("price_charged", false, (n) => (n >= 0 ? null : "price_charged cannot be negative"));
128	  const area = r.deliveryArea();
129	  const nonstandard = r.bool("nonstandard_packaging", false);
130	
131	  const dimsGiven = ["length_in", "width_in", "height_in"].filter((c) => r.text(c) !== "");
132	  if (dimsGiven.length > 0 && dimsGiven.length < 3) {
133	    r.errors.push({
134	      row: rowNumber,
135	      column: "length_in",
136	      message: "give all three of length_in, width_in and height_in, or none",
137	    });
138	  }
139	
140	  if (r.errors.length > 0 || weight === undefined || distance === undefined || residential === undefined || !speed) {
141	    return { errors: r.errors };
142	  }
143	  const parcel: Parcel = {
144	    weight_lb: weight,
145	    distance_miles: distance,
146	    residential,
147	    speed,
148	    quantity: quantity ?? 1,
149	    ...(length !== undefined && width !== undefined && height !== undefined
150	      ? { length_in: length, width_in: width, height_in: height }
151	      : {}),
152	    ...(price !== undefined ? { price_charged: price } : {}),
153	    ...(area !== undefined ? { delivery_area: area } : {}),
154	    ...(nonstandard !== undefined ? { nonstandard_packaging: nonstandard } : {}),
155	  };
156	  return { parcel, errors: [] };
157	}

159	export function parseParcelCsv(text: string): CsvResult {
160	  const parsed = Papa.parse<Row>(text.replace(/^﻿/, ""), {
161	    header: true,
162	    skipEmptyLines: "greedy",
163	    transformHeader: (h) => h.trim().toLowerCase(),
164	  });
165	  const headers = parsed.meta.fields ?? [];
166	  const missing = REQUIRED_COLUMNS.filter((c) => !headers.includes(c));
167	  if (missing.length > 0) {
168	    return {
169	      parcels: [],
170	      errors: [
171	        {
172	          row: null,
173	          message: `Missing required column${missing.length > 1 ? "s" : ""}: ${missing.join(", ")}. The first row must name the columns.`,
174	        },
175	      ],
176	      warnings: [],
177	    };
178	  }
179	  const warnings: CsvProblem[] = headers
180	    .filter((h) => h !== "" && !(ALL_COLUMNS as readonly string[]).includes(h))
181	    .map((h) => ({ row: null, column: h, message: `Column "${h}" is not used and was ignored` }));
182	
183	  if (parsed.data.length === 0) {
184	    return { parcels: [], errors: [{ row: null, message: "The file has a header but no parcel rows." }], warnings };
185	  }
186	  if (parsed.data.length > MAX_ROWS) {
187	    return {
188	      parcels: [],
189	      errors: [{ row: null, message: `The file has ${parsed.data.length} rows; the limit is ${MAX_ROWS}. Use the quantity column to group identical parcels.` }],
190	      warnings,
191	    };
192	  }
193	
194	  const parcels: Parcel[] = [];
195	  const errors: CsvProblem[] = [];
196	  parsed.data.forEach((row, i) => {
197	    const result = readRow(row, i + 2);
198	    if (result.parcel) parcels.push(result.parcel);
199	    errors.push(...result.errors);
200	  });
201	  return { parcels: errors.length > 0 ? [] : parcels, errors, warnings };
202	}

31	  flat_price: 9.99,
32	};
33	
34	export const FUEL_MIN = 0;
35	export const FUEL_MAX = 40;
36	export const PRICE_MAX = 1000;
37	
38	const KEYS = {
39	  year: "year",
40	  card: "usps",
41	  fuelGround: "fuel_ground",
42	  fuelExpress: "fuel_express",
43	  peak: "peak",
44	  price: "price",
45	  view: "view",
46	} as const;
47	
48	/** Params the app owns; anything else in the query string (e.g. mock=1) is preserved. */
49	const OWNED = new Set<string>(Object.values(KEYS));
50	
51	function num(params: URLSearchParams, key: string, min: number, max: number): number | undefined {
52	  const raw = params.get(key);
53	  if (raw === null || raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
54	  const n = Number(raw);
55	  return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= min && n <= max ? n : undefined;
56	}
57	
58	export function readState(search: string, defaults: ControlsState = FALLBACK_CONTROLS): AppState {
59	  const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
60	  const year = num(params, KEYS.year, 2000, 2100);
61	  const card = params.get(KEYS.card);
62	  const ground = num(params, KEYS.fuelGround, FUEL_MIN, FUEL_MAX);
63	  const express = num(params, KEYS.fuelExpress, FUEL_MIN, FUEL_MAX);
64	  const price = num(params, KEYS.price, 0, PRICE_MAX);
65	  const view = params.get(KEYS.view);
66	  const fuel: Partial<Record<FuelGroup, number>> = {
67	    ...(ground !== undefined ? { ground } : {}),
68	    ...(express !== undefined ? { express } : {}),
69	  };
70	  const controls: ControlsState = {
71	    year: year !== undefined && Number.isInteger(year) ? year : defaults.year,
72	    usps_rate_card: card === "retail" || card === "commercial" ? card : defaults.usps_rate_card,
73	    peak: params.has(KEYS.peak) ? params.get(KEYS.peak) === "1" : defaults.peak,
74	    flat_price: price ?? defaults.flat_price,
75	    ...(Object.keys(fuel).length > 0 ? { fuel_override_percent: fuel } : {}),
76	  };
77	  return { controls, view: (VIEWS as readonly string[]).includes(view ?? "") ? (view as ViewId) : "quote" };
78	}
79	
80	/** Serialize, leaving out values equal to the defaults so shared links stay short. */
81	export function writeState(state: AppState, currentSearch = "", defaults: ControlsState = FALLBACK_CONTROLS): string {
82	  const params = new URLSearchParams(currentSearch);
83	  for (const key of OWNED) params.delete(key);
84	  const c = state.controls;
85	  if (c.year !== defaults.year) params.set(KEYS.year, String(c.year));
86	  if (c.usps_rate_card !== defaults.usps_rate_card) params.set(KEYS.card, c.usps_rate_card);
87	  if (c.fuel_override_percent?.ground !== undefined) params.set(KEYS.fuelGround, String(c.fuel_override_percent.ground));
88	  if (c.fuel_override_percent?.express !== undefined) params.set(KEYS.fuelExpress, String(c.fuel_override_percent.express));
89	  if (c.peak !== defaults.peak) params.set(KEYS.peak, c.peak ? "1" : "0");
90	  if (c.flat_price !== defaults.flat_price) params.set(KEYS.price, String(c.flat_price));
91	  if (state.view !== "quote") params.set(KEYS.view, state.view);
92	  const out = params.toString();
93	  return out ? `?${out}` : "";
94	}
95	
96	/* ---------- reducer ---------- */
97	
98	export type Action =
99	  | { type: "year"; year: number }
100	  | { type: "card"; card: UspsRateCard }
101	  | { type: "fuel"; group: FuelGroup; percent: number }
102	  | { type: "fuelReset"; group: FuelGroup }
103	  | { type: "peak"; peak: boolean }
104	  | { type: "price"; price: number }
105	  | { type: "view"; view: ViewId }
106	  | { type: "replace"; state: AppState };
107	
108	function withFuel(c: ControlsState, group: FuelGroup, percent: number | undefined): ControlsState {
109	  const { [group]: _dropped, ...rest } = c.fuel_override_percent ?? {};
110	  const next = percent === undefined ? rest : { ...rest, [group]: percent };
111	  const { fuel_override_percent: _old, ...base } = c;
112	  return Object.keys(next).length > 0 ? { ...base, fuel_override_percent: next } : base;
113	}
114	
115	export function reducer(state: AppState, action: Action): AppState {
116	  const set = (controls: ControlsState): AppState => ({ ...state, controls });
117	  switch (action.type) {
118	    case "year":
119	      // A new year has its own fuel defaults; an override from another year would mislead.
120	      return set(withFuel(withFuel({ ...state.controls, year: action.year }, "ground", undefined), "express", undefined));
121	    case "card":
122	      return set({ ...state.controls, usps_rate_card: action.card });
123	    case "fuel":
124	      return set(withFuel(state.controls, action.group, Math.min(FUEL_MAX, Math.max(FUEL_MIN, action.percent))));
125	    case "fuelReset":
126	      return set(withFuel(state.controls, action.group, undefined));
127	    case "peak":
128	      return set({ ...state.controls, peak: action.peak });
129	    case "price":
130	      return set({ ...state.controls, flat_price: Math.min(PRICE_MAX, Math.max(0, action.price)) });
131	    case "view":
132	      return { ...state, view: action.view };
133	    case "replace":
134	      return action.state;
135	  }
136	}

12	/** App state mirrored to the query string with history.replaceState, so any view is a shareable link. */
13	export function useUrlState(defaults: ControlsState | null): [AppState, (a: Action) => void] {
14	  const effectiveDefaults = defaults ?? FALLBACK_CONTROLS;
15	  const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(reducer, undefined, () => readState(window.location.search));
16	  const adopted = useRef(false);
17	
18	  // Once the backend's defaults arrive, re-read the URL against them (fills in anything the link left out).
19	  useEffect(() => {
20	    if (!defaults || adopted.current) return;
21	    adopted.current = true;
22	    dispatch({ type: "replace", state: readState(window.location.search, defaults) });
23	  }, [defaults]);
24	
25	  useEffect(() => {
26	    const search = writeState(state, window.location.search, effectiveDefaults);
27	    if (search !== window.location.search) {
28	      window.history.replaceState(window.history.state, "", `${window.location.pathname}${search}${window.location.hash}`);
29	    }
30	  }, [state, effectiveDefaults]);
31	
32	  useEffect(() => {
33	    const onPop = () => dispatch({ type: "replace", state: readState(window.location.search, effectiveDefaults) });
34	    window.addEventListener("popstate", onPop);
35	    return () => window.removeEventListener("popstate", onPop);
36	  }, [effectiveDefaults]);
37	
38	  return [state, dispatch];
39	}

21	const STORAGE_KEY = "parcel-rates:parcel-set:v2";
22	export const MAX_FILE_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;
23	
24	function readStored(): ParcelSet | null {
25	  try {
26	    const raw = sessionStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
27	    if (!raw) return null;
28	    const value = JSON.parse(raw) as ParcelSet;
29	    return Array.isArray(value?.parcels) && value.parcels.length > 0 ? value : null;
30	  } catch {
31	    return null;
32	  }
33	}
34	
35	function store(set: ParcelSet | null) {
36	  try {
37	    if (set) sessionStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(set));
38	    else sessionStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
39	  } catch {
40	    // Storage full or blocked (private mode): the set stays in memory only.
41	  }
42	}
43	
44	/** FileReader rather than Blob.text(): same result, and it also works in jsdom. */
45	function readFileText(file: File): Promise<string> {
46	  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
47	    const reader = new FileReader();
48	    reader.onload = () => resolve(typeof reader.result === "string" ? reader.result : "");
49	    reader.onerror = () => reject(reader.error ?? new Error("read failed"));
50	    reader.readAsText(file);
51	  });
52	}
53	
54	export function useParcelSet() {
55	  const api = useApi();
56	  const [set, setSet] = useState<ParcelSet | null>(readStored);
57	  const [status, setStatus] = useState<ParcelSetStatus>({ kind: "idle" });
58	
59	  useEffect(() => store(set), [set]);
60	
61	  const loadSample = useCallback(async () => {
62	    setStatus({ kind: "loading", what: "sample" });
63	    try {
64	      const sample = await api.sampleParcels();
65	      setSet({ parcels: sample.parcels.map(fromParcelOut), source: "sample", name: "Sample mix", description: sample.description });
66	      setStatus({ kind: "idle" });
67	    } catch (err) {
68	      const message =
69	        err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : "The sample mix could not be loaded. Try again in a moment.";
70	      setStatus({ kind: "error", message, problems: [] });
71	    }
72	  }, [api]);
73	
74	  const loadFile = useCallback(async (file: File) => {
75	    if (file.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES) {
76	      setStatus({
77	        kind: "error",
78	        message: `${file.name} is larger than 5 MB. Group identical parcels with the quantity column.`,
79	        problems: [],
80	        fileName: file.name,
81	      });
82	      return;
83	    }
84	    setStatus({ kind: "loading", what: "file" });
85	    let text: string;
86	    try {
87	      text = await readFileText(file);
88	    } catch {
89	      setStatus({ kind: "error", message: `${file.name} could not be read.`, problems: [], fileName: file.name });
90	      return;
91	    }
92	    const result = parseParcelCsv(text);
93	    if (result.errors.length > 0) {
94	      setStatus({
95	        kind: "error",
96	        message: `${file.name} was not loaded: ${result.errors.length} problem${result.errors.length > 1 ? "s" : ""} to fix.`,
97	        problems: result.errors,
98	        fileName: file.name,
99	      });
100	      return;
101	    }
102	    setSet({ parcels: result.parcels, source: "upload", name: file.name });
103	    setStatus(
104	      result.warnings.length > 0
105	        ? { kind: "notice", message: `${file.name} loaded, with notes:`, problems: result.warnings, fileName: file.name }
106	        : { kind: "idle" },
107	    );
108	  }, []);
109	
110	  const clear = useCallback(() => {
111	    setSet(null);
112	    setStatus({ kind: "idle" });
113	  }, []);
114	
115	  return { set, status, loadSample, loadFile, clear };
116	}

17	export type Loadable<T> =

19	  | { status: "loading" }
20	  | { status: "ok"; data: T }
21	  | { status: "error"; error: ApiError | Error };

23	/** Run `load` whenever `deps` change; aborts the previous request. */
24	export function useLoad<T>(load: ((signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>) | null, deps: readonly unknown[]): Loadable<T> {
25	  const [state, setState] = useState<Loadable<T>>({ status: load ? "loading" : "idle" });
26	  useEffect(() => {
27	    if (!load) {
28	      setState({ status: "idle" });
29	      return;
30	    }
31	    const ctrl = new AbortController();
32	    setState({ status: "loading" });
33	    load(ctrl.signal).then(
34	      (data) => !ctrl.signal.aborted && setState({ status: "ok", data }),
35	      (error: unknown) => {
36	        if (ctrl.signal.aborted) return;
37	        setState({ status: "error", error: error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)) });
38	      },
39	    );
40	    return () => ctrl.abort();
41	    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
42	  }, deps);
43	  return state;
44	}

```
1	# Visual direction: the shipping ledger
2	
3	The dashboard reads like a printed price sheet or a merchant's ledger, not like
4	a SaaS dashboard. Warm paper, black ink, hairline rules, figures set in a
5	newspaper serif, and colour reserved for meaning.
6	
7	## Why it fits
8	
9	The user is a shop owner deciding where a few dollars per parcel go. The
10	decision lives in a handful of numbers: which carrier is cheapest, what one
11	parcel costs, whether the flat price still leaves a margin. A ledger puts those
12	numbers first, in the largest type on the page, and pushes everything else
13	(assumptions, sliders, provenance) into small, quiet type around them. Rules
14	and columns instead of cards make it feel like an account the owner keeps, and
15	they print well for an accountant.
16	
17	## Hierarchy
18	
19	1. **The answer** (cheapest carrier, cost per parcel, margin): display serif,
20	   `--text-figure`, tabular figures, carrier or money colour.
21	2. **The question** each section answers: display serif, `--text-xl`.
22	3. **The owner's parcel set**: once loaded, a one-line strip (count, share to
23	   homes, speed split) with the full summary behind "Details", so the
24	   questions and the answer stay above the fold, also on a phone.
25	
26	### Rule for every question view (issues #5 and #6)
27	
28	The answer is the largest element of its section. Put it first under the
29	question, in `.answer > .answer__figure` (`--text-figure`), with a short
30	`.answer__caption` saying what it is ("UPS Ground, $8.41 per parcel, $1.58
31	margin"). Nothing else in the section, including the question (`--text-xl`),
32	chart titles and table figures, may be set larger. Charts and tables come
33	after the answer and explain it.
34	4. **Assumptions** (year, rate card, fuel, peak, flat price): a left rail in the
35	   UI face at `--text-sm`, always visible on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones
36	   behind a one-line summary bar.
37	
38	## Palette (`src/styles/tokens.css`)
39	
40	| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
41	|---|---|---|---|
42	| `--paper` | `#F5F1E8` | `#15140F` | page |
43	| `--sheet` | `#FBF9F4` | `#1E1C17` | rail, inputs, raised panels |
44	| `--ink` | `#1C1B18` | `#EDE8DC` | text, rules, focus ring |
45	| `--ink-muted` | `#5E5A50` | `#A9A292` | secondary text (6.1:1 / 7.3:1) |
46	| `--carrier-usps` | `#1F4E9A` | `#7FA8EE` | USPS everywhere (7.1:1 / 7.7:1) |
47	| `--carrier-ups` | `#7A4E0F` | `#D9A35A` | UPS everywhere (6.4:1 / 8.2:1) |
48	| `--carrier-fedex` | `#9C2A7E` | `#E68AC9` | FedEx everywhere (6.1:1 / 7.8:1) |
49	| `--loss` | `#B3261E` | `#F2877E` | negative margin (5.8:1 / 7.5:1) |
50	| `--profit` | `#1D6B3F` | `#6FCB94` | positive margin (5.8:1 / 9.4:1) |
51	| `--mock` | `#8A5A00` | `#E8B860` | the mock-data banner only |
52	
53	Contrast ratios are against `--paper` and meet WCAG AA for body text in both
54	themes. Carrier hues follow the brands loosely (postal blue, brown, purple)
55	so the owner recognises them without a legend. Blue and purple are close for
56	some colour-vision deficiencies, so colour is never the only cue: every
57	carrier mark carries its name or initial, and money always carries a sign and
58	the word "loss" or "margin".
59	
60	Each carrier also has a `-wash` tint for backgrounds and heatmap cells
61	(issue #5 scales intensity between the wash and the full colour).
62	
63	## Type
64	
65	- **Newsreader** (display serif, optical sizes) for questions and figures.
66	  A newspaper face gives the editorial voice and has good tabular numerals.
67	- **IBM Plex Sans** for the interface: labels, controls, tables. Industrial,
68	  slightly technical, legible at 12-14 px.
69	
70	Both load from Google Fonts with `display=swap`; fallbacks are Georgia and
71	Helvetica/Arial. All figures use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so
72	columns of prices line up.
73	
74	## Spacing and shape
75	
76	A 4 px base (`--space-1` … `--space-8`: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 72 px) with a
77	deliberate jump to 48-72 px between sections, so sections read as chapters.
78	Corners are nearly square (`--radius: 2px`). Separation comes from hairline
79	rules (`--rule`) and one heavy rule under the masthead and active tab, not
80	from shadows; the only shadow is on the mobile controls sheet, which really
81	does sit above the page.
82	
83	## Motion
84	
85	Only opacity and transform, 120-220 ms, for the sheet and tab underline. All
86	of it is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
87	
88	## Charts (for issues #5 and #6)
89	
90	- Use the carrier tokens for series and cells; read them in JS with
91	  `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--carrier-usps")`
92	  or the `carrierColor()` helper in `src/lib/carriers.ts`, so dark mode works.
93	- Axis text in `--ink-muted`, gridlines in `--rule`, no chart borders.
94	- Announced increases and projections are dashed lines in the carrier colour.
95	
```

</details>

3	/** Server parcels carry every key with nulls; the UI and requests use absent keys instead. */
4	export function fromParcelOut(p: ParcelOut): Parcel {
5	  const dims =
6	    p.length_in !== null && p.width_in !== null && p.height_in !== null
7	      ? { length_in: p.length_in, width_in: p.width_in, height_in: p.height_in }

10	    weight_lb: p.weight_lb,
11	    distance_miles: p.distance_miles,

14	    quantity: p.quantity,
15	    ...dims,
16	    ...(p.price_charged !== null ? { price_charged: p.price_charged } : {}),
17	    ...(p.delivery_area !== "none" ? { delivery_area: p.delivery_area } : {}),

1	import type { Parcel, Tier, WeightBand, ZoneBand } from "../api/types";
2	import { TIERS, WEIGHT_BANDS } from "../api/types";
3	
4	export interface Bucket {
5	  label: string;
6	  detail?: string;
7	  count: number; // parcels (sum of quantity)
8	  share: number; // 0..1
9	}
10	
11	export interface ParcelSummary {
12	  rows: number;
13	  parcels: number;
14	  residentialShare: number;
15	  byTier: Record<Tier, number>; // share 0..1
16	  weight: Bucket[];
17	  distance: Bucket[];
18	  withOwnPrice: number; // parcels whose row sets price_charged
19	  meanWeightLb: number;
20	}
21	
22	/** Upper bounds (inclusive) of the contract's weight bands: ≤1, 1–5, 5–10, 10–20, 20–70 lb. */
23	const WEIGHT_UPPER: Record<WeightBand, number> = { "≤1": 1, "1–5": 5, "5–10": 10, "10–20": 20, "20–70": 70 };
24	
25	export function weightBand(lb: number): WeightBand {
26	  return WEIGHT_BANDS.find((b) => lb <= WEIGHT_UPPER[b]) ?? "20–70";
27	}
28	
29	/** USPS zone bands (docs: data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv); used until /api/meta answers. */
30	export const FALLBACK_USPS_ZONES: ZoneBand[] = [
31	  [1, 0, 50], [2, 51, 150], [3, 151, 300], [4, 301, 600],
32	  [5, 601, 1000], [6, 1001, 1400], [7, 1401, 1800], [8, 1801, null],
33	].map(([zone, min_miles, max_miles]) => ({
34	  carrier: "usps" as const, zone: zone as number, min_miles: min_miles as number, max_miles: max_miles as number | null,
35	}));
36	
37	const miles = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US");
38	
39	export function zoneLabel(b: ZoneBand): string {
40	  return `Zone ${b.zone}`;
41	}
42	
43	export function zoneRange(b: ZoneBand): string {
44	  return b.max_miles === null ? `${miles.format(b.min_miles)}+ mi` : `${miles.format(b.min_miles)}–${miles.format(b.max_miles)} mi`;
45	}
46	
47	/**
48	 * The USPS zone a distance falls in. Bands are whole miles with gaps (50, then 51), so a
49	 * fractional distance goes to the first band whose upper edge it does not pass.
50	 */
51	export function zoneForDistance(d: number, bands: ZoneBand[]): ZoneBand {
52	  const sorted = [...bands].sort((x, y) => x.zone - y.zone);
53	  return sorted.find((b) => b.max_miles === null || d <= b.max_miles) ?? sorted[sorted.length - 1]!;
54	}
55	
56	export function uspsZones(bands: ZoneBand[] | undefined): ZoneBand[] {
57	  const usps = (bands ?? []).filter((b) => b.carrier === "usps").sort((x, y) => x.zone - y.zone);
58	  return usps.length > 0 ? usps : FALLBACK_USPS_ZONES;
59	}
60	
61	const qty = (p: Parcel) => p.quantity ?? 1;
62	
63	function buckets(
64	  parcels: Parcel[],
65	  labels: readonly string[],
66	  key: (p: Parcel) => string,
67	  total: number,
68	  detail?: (label: string, i: number) => string,
69	): Bucket[] {
70	  const counts = new Map<string, number>(labels.map((l) => [l, 0]));
71	  for (const p of parcels) counts.set(key(p), (counts.get(key(p)) ?? 0) + qty(p));
72	  return labels.map((label, i) => {
73	    const count = counts.get(label) ?? 0;
74	    return { label, count, share: total ? count / total : 0, ...(detail ? { detail: detail(label, i) } : {}) };
75	  });
76	}
77	
78	/** `zoneBands`: the zone bands from /api/meta; the USPS ones bucket the distances. */
79	export function summarize(parcels: Parcel[], zoneBands?: ZoneBand[]): ParcelSummary {
80	  const zones = uspsZones(zoneBands);
81	  const total = parcels.reduce((s, p) => s + qty(p), 0);
82	  const share = (pred: (p: Parcel) => boolean) =>
83	    total ? parcels.filter(pred).reduce((s, p) => s + qty(p), 0) / total : 0;
84	  const byTier = Object.fromEntries(TIERS.map((t) => [t, share((p) => p.speed === t)])) as Record<Tier, number>;
85	  return {
86	    rows: parcels.length,
87	    parcels: total,
88	    residentialShare: share((p) => p.residential),
89	    byTier,
90	    weight: buckets(parcels, WEIGHT_BANDS, (p) => weightBand(p.weight_lb), total),
91	    distance: buckets(
92	      parcels,
93	      zones.map(zoneLabel),
94	      (p) => zoneLabel(zoneForDistance(p.distance_miles, zones)),
95	      total,
96	      (_l, i) => zoneRange(zones[i]!),
97	    ),
98	    withOwnPrice: parcels.filter((p) => p.price_charged !== undefined).reduce((s, p) => s + qty(p), 0),
99	    meanWeightLb: total ? parcels.reduce((s, p) => s + p.weight_lb * qty(p), 0) / total : 0,
100	  };
101	}

```
(unavailable quotes last within a tier). Only carriers that publish the
requested year are quoted (2027 is FedEx only). A tier with no available
service maps to `null` in `cheapest_by_tier`.

### POST /api/breakeven  (question 2)
Request `{ controls: Controls, residential: boolean, weights_lb?: number[], distances_miles?: number[] }`
(defaults: weights 1..70 step 1, distances at every zone band midpoint).
Response: a grid of cells `{ weight_lb, distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, winner: {carrier, service_id, total}, runner_up: {...}, saving, totals: Record<Carrier, number> }`
for the ground tier (FedEx Ground for business, Home Delivery for residential),
plus `breakeven_weight_lb: [{ distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, vs_ups, vs_fedex }]`
per distance band: the lightest grid weight at which the USPS total is >= the
rival's total, `null` when USPS wins at every weight. The default distances are
each USPS band's midpoint (rounded down) and, for the open last band, the
previous band's upper edge + 200 miles.

### GET /api/breakeven
Same response with the default grid; query parameters `residential`
(default true), `year`, `peak`, `usps_rate_card`.

### POST /api/blended  (question 3)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, segment?: SegmentFilter }`.
Response per carrier: parcels shipped, blended cost per parcel, base vs
surcharge vs fuel split (absolute and share), surcharge breakdown by kind,
margin per parcel, share of parcels shipped at a loss, and the cheapest
carrier per parcel (a "best mix" row). Each parcel uses the cheapest service
of that carrier in the parcel's speed tier.

Shape: `BlendedResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`: `year`,
`parcels_considered`, `revenue_per_parcel`, `carriers[]` and `best_mix`. Each
carrier row (and `best_mix`) is a `Summary`: `parcels_shipped`,
`parcels_unavailable` (quantity no service of the carrier could carry),
`total_cost`, `cost_per_parcel`, `split.{base,surcharges,fuel}.{per_parcel,total,share}`,
`surcharges_by_condition[] {condition, total, per_parcel, share_of_cost}`,
`margin_per_parcel`, `total_margin`, `loss_share`, `parcels_at_loss`; carrier
rows add `carrier` and `services_used` (service_id -> parcels), `best_mix`
adds `parcels_by_carrier`. Everything is weighted by `quantity`.

### POST /api/yearly  (question 4)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, next_year_increase_percent?: number }`.
Response per carrier and year: blended cost per parcel under that year's
prices and rules, the year-over-year change, the carrier's announced average
```

- `npm audit`: 3 vulnerabilities (2 critical, 1 moderate) — all in `vitest`/`tinypool`/`@vitest/mocker`, dev-only tooling, not shipped in the production bundle (`npm audit --omit=dev` → 0). LOW, informational only.
- Compared `frontend/src/api/types.ts`/`guards.ts` against `backend/app/api/models.py` on `origin/main` field-by-field; traced CSV parsing (`frontend/src/lib/parcelCsv.ts`) with ad-hoc inputs via `npx tsx`; read state/URL code, `useLoad`, `useParcelSet`, accessibility-relevant components.

## HIGH

1. **Runtime contract guards are never applied to live backend responses.** `frontend/src/api/client.ts:97-115` (`request<T>`) does `return body as T;` with no call into `frontend/src/api/guards.ts`. The `asX` guards are only invoked in `frontend/src/api/mocks.ts:28-34` (against static fixture JSON, used for `?mock=1` and tests) and in `contract.test.ts` (against the same fixtures). So: **a real backend field rename, type change, or dropped key is not caught at runtime for actual traffic** — it will either silently produce `undefined`/`NaN` in the UI or (once later issues add real rendering) throw inside a view component with no diagnostic. The guard infrastructure is well-built but effectively only protects "do our hand-maintained fixtures match our hand-maintained types," not "does the live backend match what we think it returns." Suggest wiring the guards into `createHttpClient`'s `request()` (e.g., `asMeta`, `asQuoteResponse`, etc. per endpoint) so drift fails loudly against real traffic too, with the existing `ContractError` surfaced through `ApiError`.

2. **CSV decimal-comma locale bug silently corrupts weight/price by 10x.** `frontend/src/lib/parcelCsv.ts:44-48` (`parseNumber`) does `.replace(/,/g, "")` unconditionally. A European-style export (common with semicolon-delimited files, which Papa.parse auto-detects and handles fine) uses `,` as the decimal separator, e.g. `2,5` meaning 2.5 lb. Verified: parsing `weight_lb;distance_miles;residential;speed\n2,5;300;true;ground` yields `weight_lb: 25` with **zero errors or warnings** — a silent 10x data error that then feeds every downstream cost calculation. Values like `7,5` (→75) happen to get caught by the `>70` cap, but plenty of legitimate values (e.g. `2,5`→25, `1,2`→12) pass validation untouched. Given the task explicitly calls out semicolon-delimited/European exports as an expected shop-owner edge case, this needs either locale-aware number parsing (detect decimal separator from the delimiter/locale) or at minimum a sanity-check/warning when a comma-containing numeric field doesn't look like a thousands-grouped integer.

## MEDIUM

3. **`useParcelSet` has no race-condition guard between `loadSample`/`loadFile`.** `frontend/src/hooks/useParcelSet.ts:61-108` — unlike `useLoad` (which correctly uses `AbortController` + `ctrl.signal.aborted` checks, verified correct, see below), `loadSample` and `loadFile` each independently `await` and then unconditionally call `setSet`/`setStatus`. If a user triggers "Load sample" and then quickly uploads a CSV (or triggers two file loads back to back), whichever request resolves last wins, regardless of which the user issued last. No request-id/generation check exists. Low likelihood in practice but a real last-writer-wins bug with no error shown to the user (silently shows stale data).

4. **Mobile control sheet has no focus trap / no `aria-modal`.** `frontend/src/App.tsx:24-40,94-99` — the sheet is an `<aside aria-label="Assumptions">`, not `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, and `useSheet` only focuses the first control on open and closes on Escape; it never restricts `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` to the sheet's own focusable elements, and the backdrop/main content behind it is not marked `inert`/`aria-hidden`. A keyboard user can tab from the sheet straight into the (visually hidden) page content behind the backdrop while the sheet is "open." Worth adding a focus trap (or `inert` on the rest of the page while open) and `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"` on the `<aside>` for the mobile breakpoint.

5. **Runtime guard for fixed-cardinality dicts doesn't check completeness.** `frontend/src/api/guards.ts:70-78` (`record`) only validates keys that are *present*; it never asserts that all three carriers are present. This is correct/intended for genuinely open-keyed maps (`services_used`, `parcels_by_carrier`), but it's also used for `cheapest_by_tier: record(tier, nullable(pick))` and `totals: record(carrier, num)` (guards.ts:183,198) where the backend model (`dict[Carrier, float]` / `dict[Tier, Pick | None]`) is really a closed 3-key set in practice. If the backend ever silently drops a carrier/tier key, the guard (when it's eventually wired to live traffic, see HIGH #1) would not catch it — only direct consumers (`totals["ups"]` → `undefined` → `NaN` in arithmetic) would, with no clear error. Consider a `closedRecord(keys, value)` variant for these three call sites.

## LOW / informational

- `frontend/src/api/types.ts:360` (`type?: string`) marks `ValidationIssue.type` optional, but `frontend/src/api/guards.ts:250` requires it unconditionally. Harmless today only because guards aren't on the live error path either (same root cause as HIGH #1) and the real fixture always includes `type`; still an internal inconsistency worth tightening either way.
- `npm audit`: 2 critical + 1 moderate advisories, but confined to `vitest`/`tinypool` (dev/test-only), not present in `npm audit --omit=dev`. No action required before merge; worth a follow-up `vitest` major-version bump at a convenient time.
- CSV parsing handles the other listed edge cases correctly — verified by direct test: UTF-8 BOM, quoted fields with embedded thousands separators (`"1,234"` → 1234), trailing blank lines, header case/whitespace (`"Speed, Residential ,DISTANCE_MILES"` → all normalized), `$` prefixed prices, speed aliases (`overnight`→`next_day`), and 10,000-row files parse in ~49ms synchronously (no Web Worker, but fast enough not to be a real concern at the documented 10k/20k scale).
- No `innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML`/`document.write`/`eval` anywhere in `frontend/src`. All API-sourced strings (`Footer.tsx` limitations, problem messages, etc.) render as JSX text, which React escapes — no XSS vector found. The downloadable CSV template (`frontend/src/lib/parcelCsv.ts:219-226`, `ParcelSetPanel.tsx:20`) is a fixed static string, not built from user/API data, so there's no CSV/formula-injection surface in this PR.
- `useLoad` (`frontend/src/api/ApiContext.tsx:24-44`) is correctly implemented: each call creates its own `AbortController`, aborts the previous request on dependency change/unmount, and checks `ctrl.signal.aborted` before committing state in both the success and error branches — verified this correctly prevents out-of-order response races for `meta` loading.
- `QuestionTabs` (`frontend/src/components/QuestionTabs.tsx`) implements the WAI-ARIA "tabs with automatic activation" pattern correctly: roving `tabIndex`, `role="tablist"/"tab"/"tabpanel"`, arrow/Home/End key handling with focus follow — verified correct, including via `App.test.tsx`'s keyboard test.
- API request/response field-by-field comparison against `backend/app/app/api/models.py` (fetched from `origin/main`) found types.ts to be accurate: optional-with-server-default fields correctly `?:` on request types, `extra="forbid"` response fields correctly required-but-nullable (e.g. `Quote.zone/billable_weight_lb/dim_weight_lb/unavailable_reason/as_of`), `Parcel`'s "all-or-none" dimension validator is mirrored in both the CSV reader (`parcelCsv.ts:131-138`) and presumably relied on for direct form input (not yet built). No contract mismatches found in the static types themselves.
- Tests reviewed (`App.test.tsx`, `ControlRail.test.tsx`, `urlState.test.ts`, `client.test.ts`, `parcelCsv.test.ts`, `summary.test.ts`, `contract.test.ts`) are substantive — meaningful assertions on behavior, not tautological/vacuous checks.
- DESIGN.md's documented contrast ratios for the token palette look plausible on inspection but weren't independently recomputed against WCAG math; worth a spot-check with a contrast tool before this becomes load-bearing in charts (issue #5/#6).

MEDIUM items #3–#5 should be fixed or explicitly deferred with a tracked follow-up, but don't need to block.

# API contract

The FastAPI backend (`backend/`) serves JSON under `/api`. The frontend talks to
it only through these endpoints. Types below are the Pydantic models
(`backend/app/api/models.py`) and the TypeScript types
(`frontend/src/api/types.ts`), which must stay in sync; a contract test in each
side checks the example payloads in `docs/api-examples/`.

Money is a number in USD rounded to cents. Weights in pounds, lengths in inches,
distances in miles. Years are price-list labels (see `docs/data/SCHEMA.md`).

## Shared types

```ts
type Carrier = "usps" | "ups" | "fedex";
type Tier = "ground" | "two_three_day" | "next_day";
type DeliveryArea = "none" | "das" | "extended";
type UspsRateCard = "commercial" | "retail";

interface Parcel {
  weight_lb: number;            // > 0, <= 70
  length_in?: number;           // all three or none; > 0
  width_in?: number;
  height_in?: number;
  distance_miles: number;       // >= 0
  residential: boolean;
  speed: Tier;
  quantity?: number;            // default 1, integer >= 1
  price_charged?: number;       // overrides Controls.flat_price for this row
  delivery_area?: DeliveryArea; // default "none"
  nonstandard_packaging?: boolean; // default false
}

interface Controls {
  year?: number;                // omitted or null: latest year with all three carriers (2026);
                                // a year no carrier publishes is a 422
  as_of?: string;               // ISO date; default the year's January effective date
  usps_rate_card: UspsRateCard; // default "commercial"
  fuel_override_percent?: { ground?: number; express?: number }; // replaces the yearly default
  peak: boolean;                // default false; when true, as_of moves into the year's peak window
  flat_price: number;           // what the shop charges per parcel; default 9.99
}

interface LineItem {
  kind: "base" | "surcharge" | "fuel";
  label: string;                // carrier's own name, e.g. "Residential Surcharge"
  amount: number;
  surcharge_id?: string;        // links to surcharges.csv
  source?: string;              // "file p.N" for display
  condition?: string;           // surcharges.csv condition, for grouping surcharges by kind
}

interface Quote {
  carrier: Carrier;
  service_id: string;
  service_name: string;
  tier: Tier;
  zone: number;
  billable_weight_lb: number;
  dim_weight_lb: number | null;
  line_items: LineItem[];
  total: number;
  margin: number;               // price charged minus total
  available: boolean;           // false when the service cannot carry this parcel
  unavailable_reason?: string;  // e.g. "FedEx Ground serves business addresses only"
  as_of: string | null;         // ISO date the rules were resolved for
}
// An unavailable quote has line_items: [] and total: 0, margin: 0; zone and
// weights are null when they were not reached. Clients must check `available`.
```

## Endpoints

### GET /api/health
`{"status": "ok"}` for the Docker health check.

### GET /api/meta
Years per carrier, services (with `rate_card_notes`), default controls
(including the default `as_of` per carrier), fuel defaults per year with
`is_proxy`, the zone bands, the segment band labels, and the data limitations
text shown in the UI footer. Shape: `MetaResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`.

### GET /api/sample-parcels
The bundled illustrative parcel mix as `Parcel[]`, with a `description`.

### POST /api/quote  (question 1)
Request `{ parcel: Parcel, controls: Controls }`. Response
`{ quotes: Quote[], cheapest_by_tier: Record<Tier, {carrier, service_id, total}> }`,
quotes sorted by total within the requested tier first, then the other tiers
(unavailable quotes last within a tier). Only carriers that publish the
requested year are quoted (2027 is FedEx only). A tier with no available
service maps to `null` in `cheapest_by_tier`.

### POST /api/breakeven  (question 2)
Request `{ controls: Controls, residential: boolean, weights_lb?: number[], distances_miles?: number[] }`
(defaults: weights 1..70 step 1, distances at every zone band midpoint).
Response: a grid of cells `{ weight_lb, distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, winner: {carrier, service_id, total}, runner_up: {...}, saving, totals: Record<Carrier, number> }`
for the ground tier (FedEx Ground for business, Home Delivery for residential),
plus `breakeven_weight_lb: [{ distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, vs_ups, vs_fedex }]`
per distance band: the lightest grid weight at which the USPS total is >= the
rival's total, `null` when USPS wins at every weight. The default distances are
each USPS band's midpoint (rounded down) and, for the open last band, the
previous band's upper edge + 200 miles.

### GET /api/breakeven
Same response with the default grid; query parameters `residential`
(default true), `year`, `peak`, `usps_rate_card`.

### POST /api/blended  (question 3)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, segment?: SegmentFilter }`.
Response per carrier: parcels shipped, blended cost per parcel, base vs
surcharge vs fuel split (absolute and share), surcharge breakdown by kind,
margin per parcel, share of parcels shipped at a loss, and the cheapest
carrier per parcel (a "best mix" row). Each parcel uses the cheapest service
of that carrier in the parcel's speed tier.

Shape: `BlendedResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`: `year`,
`parcels_considered`, `revenue_per_parcel`, `carriers[]` and `best_mix`. Each
carrier row (and `best_mix`) is a `Summary`: `parcels_shipped`,
`parcels_unavailable` (quantity no service of the carrier could carry),
`total_cost`, `cost_per_parcel`, `split.{base,surcharges,fuel}.{per_parcel,total,share}`,
`surcharges_by_condition[] {condition, total, per_parcel, share_of_cost}`,
`margin_per_parcel`, `total_margin`, `loss_share`, `parcels_at_loss`; carrier
rows add `carrier` and `services_used` (service_id -> parcels), `best_mix`
adds `parcels_by_carrier`. Everything is weighted by `quantity`.

### POST /api/yearly  (question 4)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, next_year_increase_percent?: number }`.
Response per carrier and year: blended cost per parcel under that year's
prices and rules, the year-over-year change, the carrier's announced average
increase for comparison, and the driver breakdown: for each parcel segment
(weight band, zone band, residential, speed), its contribution to the change
in dollars per parcel. Optional projected next year from the slider.

Rules: each year is priced at its own base-rate effective date per carrier
(December 10 of that year when `peak`); `controls.as_of` and `controls.year`
are ignored. `fuel_override_percent` applies to every year. Only parcels the
carrier can ship in every one of its years are compared (`parcels_used`,
`parcels_excluded`). Years a carrier lacks are absent.

Shape: `YearlyResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`: `carriers[] {carrier,
parcels_used, parcels_excluded, years[], projected}`; `projected` is
`{year, increase_percent, cost_per_parcel}` or `null`. Each year row:
`year`, `as_of`, `cost_per_parcel`, `summary` (the blended `Summary`),
`services_used`, `change_vs_previous {from_year, dollars_per_parcel, percent}`
(null for the first year), `announced_increase {percent, basis, services,
source_type}` where `basis` is `"all"` (the carrier-wide row), 
`"average_of_services"` (plain average of the rows for the services used,
listed in `services`) or `"none"`, `drivers` (per dimension a list of
`{segment, parcels, change_per_parcel, change_total}`; the rounded
`change_per_parcel` values add up exactly to the rounded change), `fuel`
(`{ground, express}` each `{default_percent, is_proxy, applied_percent}`, null
for USPS) and `warnings` (e.g. a surcharge kind present the year before but
with no rules recorded this year).

### Segments
`SegmentFilter = { weight_band?: string, zone_band?: string, residential?: boolean, speed?: Tier }`.
Weight bands: `≤1`, `1–5`, `5–10`, `10–20`, `20–70` lb. Zone bands: `1–2`, `3–4`, `5–6`, `7–8`.

## Engine rules the endpoints share

- **Zone** from `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv` per carrier: the band
  whose `min_miles <= distance <= max_miles`.
- **Billable weight** per carrier and `as_of` from `dim_weight.csv`: dimensions
  rounded per the row's rounding rule, dimensional weight = volume / divisor
  rounded up, only when volume exceeds `min_volume_cuin`; billable = max(actual
  rounded up to the next weight step, dimensional). The row is the one whose
  window contains `as_of`. Weight steps are the service's own table steps, so
  USPS Ground Advantage keeps its ounce steps under 1 lb (and the USPS commercial
  Priority Mail cards their 0.5 lb step). A billable weight above the heaviest
  step makes the service unavailable; USPS caps dimensional weight at 70 lb
  as its dim_weight row states.
- **Base rate**: the first weight step `>= billable weight` in the zone, for
  the service, rate card (`list` for UPS and FedEx, the USPS control otherwise)
  and year.
- **Surcharges**: every rule of that carrier and year whose window contains
  `as_of`, whose `applies_to` covers the service, whose `address_type`
  matches, and whose thresholds the parcel meets; peak conditions only when
  `controls.peak`. Rules in the same `exclusive_group` do not stack: the
  highest amount wins. Percent surcharges apply to the base rate.
- **Fuel**: `percent x (base + surcharges flagged fuel_applies)`, percent from
  `fuel_surcharge.csv` for the year and service group (ground services use
  `ground`, all others `express`) unless overridden. USPS has none.
- **Availability**: FedEx Ground for business addresses only, Home Delivery for
  residential only (from `services.csv`); weight over 70 lb is rejected.
- **as_of**: defaults to the base-rate `effective_date` of the year for each
  carrier, or `controls.as_of` when given. With `peak: true` it is December 10
  of the year (overriding `controls.as_of`), inside every carrier's peak window
  for which peak rows are recorded. `as_of` therefore also selects time-varying rules such
  as the USPS dimensional divisor (166 until 2026-07-11, 139 after) and the
  2026 USPS 8 % transportation increase.
- **Cheapest per tier**: among available services of the tier, lowest total.
- **Thresholds, windows and peak add-ons**: see "Matching rules" in
  `docs/data/SCHEMA.md` (bands inclusive on billable weight, a lone minimum weight
  strict on actual weight, dimensions strict, `effective_to` inclusive, peak
  add-ons only on top of the charge they add to).
- The engine never hardcodes an amount; every number comes from
  `data/processed/`.

## Errors
422 with `{ detail: [{ loc, msg }] }` for invalid input (Pydantic default),
with messages written for the shop owner, e.g. "weight_lb must be at most 70";
each entry also carries the Pydantic error `type`. Errors inside a parcel list
are prefixed "Parcel N: ". Real request/response pairs for every endpoint are
in `docs/api-examples/`, regenerated by `backend/scripts/export_api_examples.py`.
````

# Processed data schema

All tables live under `data/processed/` as UTF-8 CSV with a header row. Column
names are snake_case. Money is a decimal string with two places in USD. Dates
are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Booleans are `true` or `false`. Empty string means null.

Two kinds of tables:

- **Parsed** tables are generated by `data/pipeline/` from the raw files and
  are never edited by hand (`base_rates.csv`).
- **Curated** tables are transcribed from the documents. Every row carries a
  citation (`source_file`, `source_ref` or `source_page`, `source_quote`) and
  the test suite checks that the quote, including the amount, appears on the
  cited page of the cited file.

`year` everywhere is the price-list label: the list prices that took effect in
January of that year (USPS 2023 uses the July 9 2023 tables; FedEx 2027 is the
forward year). `effective_date`, `effective_from` and `effective_to` record the
actual dates, because some rules change inside a year.

## Layout

Each carrier's pipeline writes only to its own directory, so parsers can be
built independently and never conflict:

```
data/processed/
  services.csv                 shared, curated
  zone_from_distance.csv       shared, curated
  usps/  base_rates.csv  surcharges.csv  fuel_surcharge.csv  announced_increase.csv  dim_weight.csv  exceptions.csv
  ups/   (same files)
  fedex/ (same files)
```

The backend loads every carrier directory and concatenates tables of the
same name. A carrier with no fuel surcharge ships a header-only file.

## Identifiers

| Field | Values |
|---|---|
| `carrier` | `usps`, `ups`, `fedex` |
| `rate_card` | USPS: `retail` (counter price) or `commercial` (online postage, the default for USPS in the dashboard, switchable to retail). UPS and FedEx: `list` (Daily Rates / Standard List Rates, what a shipper without a contract pays). `services.csv` explains in one line what each card means for each carrier. The README repeats this. |
| `tier` | `ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day` |
| `service_id` | see `services.csv` |
| `unit` | `usd` (flat amount) or `percent` |

## services.csv (shared, curated)

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | |
| service_id | id | `usps_ground_advantage`, `usps_priority_mail`, `usps_priority_mail_express`, `ups_ground`, `ups_3_day_select`, `ups_2nd_day_air`, `ups_next_day_air_saver`, `ups_next_day_air`, `fedex_ground`, `fedex_home_delivery`, `fedex_express_saver`, `fedex_2day`, `fedex_standard_overnight`, `fedex_priority_overnight` |
| display_name | text | Carrier's own name |
| tier | tier | Speed tier the service competes in |
| residential_allowed | bool | FedEx Ground is business only; Home Delivery is residential only |
| business_allowed | bool | |
| rate_cards | text | Comma-separated list of rate cards published for this service: `retail,commercial` for USPS, `list` for UPS and FedEx |
| rate_card_notes | text | One line per card, `card: meaning`, separated by `;`. E.g. USPS: `retail: price paid at the Post Office counter; commercial: price paid with online postage or shipping software, no contract needed`. UPS: `list: published Daily Rates for shippers without a negotiated contract` |
| max_weight_lb | int | 70 for USPS, 150 for UPS and FedEx (the app caps at 70) |
| notes | text | |

## base_rates.csv (parsed, per carrier)

One row per price cell.

| rate_card | id | |
| year | int | |

| zone | int | USPS 1–9 (rows for both 1 and 2 even when equal); UPS and FedEx 2–8 |
| max_weight_lb | decimal | Upper bound of the weight step in pounds. USPS Ground Advantage ounce steps are `0.25`, `0.5`, `0.75`, `0.9999` (15.999 oz), then `1` … `70`. UPS and FedEx `1` … `70` |
| price | money | |
| source_file | path | Relative to `data/raw/` |
| source_ref | text | Sheet name, or PDF file page index (1-based) |

Alaska and Hawaii columns (UPS zones 44–46, FedEx AK/HI zones, USPS zone 9
when the document marks it as such) are parsed only if they fall out of the
same table; they are excluded from the dashboard and listed in
`exceptions.csv` with kind `ak_hi_zone` so the exclusion is explicit.

### Invariants: warnings, with every exception documented

The invariant checks never silently pass. Each anomaly is either listed in the
carrier's `exceptions.csv` (then the test emits a warning) or it fails the test.
This forces every oddity in a rate card to be written down.

Checks:

- For each (carrier, service_id, rate_card, year): every zone in the carrier's
  range is present with the same set of weight steps, strictly increasing,
  with no gaps up to 70 lb.
- Within a zone, price is non-decreasing with weight. Within a weight step,
  price is non-decreasing with zone.
- Prices have at most two decimals and no float artifacts (e.g. `15.999000000000001` in a weight label).
- Every `source_file` exists in `data/raw/manifest.csv`.

`exceptions.csv` (curated, per carrier):

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| carrier, service_id, rate_card, year | Scope, any of them may be empty for "all" |
| zone, max_weight_lb | Cell, or empty for a whole table |
| kind | `ak_hi_zone`, `rounding_artifact`, `non_monotonic`, `missing_cell`, `page_shift`, `step_structure_change`, `other` |
| note | What the document shows and how the parser treats it |
| source_file, source_ref | Where to look |

### Golden samples

`data/tests/golden/<carrier>_<year>.csv` holds hand-checked cells with the
`base_rates.csv` columns plus `checked_by` (person or "agent" plus date) and
`source_ref`. The parsed output must match every golden cell exactly.

Mandatory cells for each (service_id, rate_card, year), because column and
page shifts in the PDFs corrupt exactly these corners:

1. heaviest weight step (70 lb) in the farthest zone
2. heaviest weight step in the nearest zone
3. lightest weight step in the farthest zone
4. at least two interior cells on different pages or sheets of the source

Minimum five cells per (service_id, rate_card, year).

## surcharges.csv (curated, per carrier)

One row per surcharge rule, per year and effective window. A rule applies when
every non-empty threshold column is met and the `as_of` date falls inside its
window.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | |
| year | int | |
| rate_card | id | Empty means all rate cards |
| surcharge_id | id | Stable id, e.g. `ups_residential_ground_2025` |
| display_name | text | Carrier's own name |
| condition | enum | `residential`, `delivery_area`, `delivery_area_extended`, `additional_handling_weight`, `additional_handling_length`, `additional_handling_width`, `additional_handling_packaging`, `oversize`, `nonstandard_length`, `nonstandard_volume`, `peak_residential`, `peak_additional_handling`, `peak_oversize`, `peak_base`, `transportation_time_limited` |
| applies_to | text | `all`, `ground`, `air`, or a comma-separated list of `service_id` |
| address_type | enum | `any`, `residential` or `commercial`. Carriers price delivery-area and large-package surcharges differently for homes and businesses; a rule only applies to parcels of its address type |
| min_weight_lb | decimal | Lower weight threshold; see "Matching rules" below for which weight and whether it is inclusive |
| max_weight_lb | decimal | Upper end of a weight band (USPS peak add-ons); its presence makes the row a band |
| min_length_in | decimal | Longest side |
| min_width_in | decimal | Second-longest side (UPS and FedEx additional handling: over 30 in) |
| min_length_plus_girth_in | decimal | |
| min_volume_cuft | decimal | |
| zone_min | int | |
| zone_max | int | |
| amount | decimal | |
| unit | unit | |
| exclusive_group | text | Required, never empty. Rules in the same group do not stack; the highest matching amount applies. Rules in different groups stack |
| effective_from | date | |
| effective_to | date | Last day the rule applies (inclusive). Empty means open-ended |
| fuel_applies | bool | Whether the carrier applies the fuel surcharge on top of this charge |
| source_file | path | |
| source_page | int | File page index, 1-based; empty for HTML or XLSX |
| source_quote | text | Verbatim snippet containing the amount |
| notes | text | |

### Matching rules

The engine applies these rules uniformly; every row must mean what its quote says under them.

- **Windows.** A row applies on `as_of` when `effective_from <= as_of <= effective_to`.
  `effective_to` is inclusive in every table (surcharges, dim_weight): it is the last day
  the rule applies. A document that ends prices "at midnight on Jan. 19" (the day the next
  list starts) is recorded with `effective_to` = Jan. 18.
- **Weight.** When `max_weight_lb` is set the row is a band, matched inclusively on billable
  weight: `min_weight_lb <= billable <= max_weight_lb`, an empty `min_weight_lb` meaning no
  lower bound (USPS peak add-ons: "4-10 lbs" = the 4 lb to 10 lb steps). When only
  `min_weight_lb` is set it is strictly greater than the parcel's actual weight (UPS and
  FedEx additional handling "more than 50 lb", UPS 2026 Large Package "more than 110 lb");
  dimensional weight never triggers it.
- **Dimensions and volume** are strict: longest side `> min_length_in`, second-longest side
  `> min_width_in`, longest + 2 x (other two) `> min_length_plus_girth_in`, volume in cubic
  feet `> min_volume_cuft`, using the dimensions as rounded by the carrier's dim_weight rule
  for `as_of`. A parcel without dimensions meets no dimension or volume threshold.
- **Zone.** `zone_min <= zone <= zone_max`, each bound optional.
- **Peak add-ons.** `peak_additional_handling` applies only when a non-peak rule of
  condition `additional_handling_*` (or the UPS cubic-size additional handling recorded as
  `nonstandard_volume`) applied to the same parcel; `peak_oversize` only when an `oversize`
  rule applied. Both carry no thresholds of their own.

Peak rules apply only when the dashboard's peak toggle is on. Rules with
`address_type` `residential` or `commercial` apply only to parcels of that kind.
Delivery area rules apply when the parcel's `delivery_area` is `das` or
`extended`. `additional_handling_packaging` rules apply when the parcel is
flagged `nonstandard_packaging` (UPS and FedEx: non-corrugated or cylindrical
packaging; USPS from 2026: tubes or rolls, cans, wooden or metal boxes, liquids
in glass).

### Engine tests for fuel

The rate engine applies the fuel percent to the base rate plus every applied
surcharge whose `fuel_applies` is `true`, and to nothing else. Tests use
synthetic rows: one surcharge flagged `true`, one flagged `false`, a known
percent, and assert the fuel line item equals `percent × (base + flagged)` to
the cent, that the slider override replaces the yearly default, and that USPS
quotes carry no fuel line.

| percent | decimal | Negative for a decrease (USPS Ground Advantage launch, July 2023); the citation quote then reads "decrease N percent" |

## dim_weight.csv (curated, per carrier)

Dimensional weight parameters change over time (USPS moved from 166 to 139
on 2026-07-12), so rows carry an effective window and the engine resolves the
row by `as_of` date: the row whose window (inclusive at both ends) contains it.
Windows of one carrier must not overlap with different parameters; USPS repeats
an identical row under several year labels, which is allowed.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | |
| year | int | |
| effective_from | date | |
| effective_to | date | Last day the row applies (inclusive). Empty means open-ended |
| divisor | int | |
| min_volume_cuin | int | 0 for UPS and FedEx; 1728 for USPS |
| rounding | text | e.g. "round each dimension to nearest inch, round dim weight up to next pound" |
| source_file | path | |
| source_ref | text | |
| source_quote | text | |

## Rules that change over time

Every parameter that can move a parcel's price is stored per year and per
effective window: base rates, surcharge amounts and thresholds, fuel defaults,
dimensional-weight divisor and threshold. The engine takes an `as_of` date
(default: the year's January effective date) and never hardcodes a value.

`uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes` diffs consecutive years of
every curated table and writes `docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md`: one line per
parameter that changed, with old and new values and the citation. The parser
agents must populate every year so this report is complete, and the report is
reviewed before the engine is built so year-over-year comparisons account for
every change, not only base rates.

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| carrier | id | USPS bands differ from UPS and FedEx bands |

| min_miles | int | Inclusive |
| max_miles | int | Inclusive; empty for the last band |
| source_file | path | Must be a file listed in the manifest (add a row and run the fetcher; never download by hand) |
| source_quote | text | Verbatim |
| notes | text | e.g. how a band was derived when the carrier publishes zones only by ZIP pair |

## Raw manifest: data/raw/manifest.csv

| Column | Notes |
|---|---|
| carrier | `usps`, `ups`, `fedex` |
| year | or empty |
| path | relative to `data/raw/` |
| url | exact URL; Wayback URLs use the `id_` passthrough form |
| method | `direct` or `wayback` |
| sha256 | hex digest |
| bytes | size |
| in_git | `true` for spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML; `false` for PDFs |

`python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores missing files sequentially with pauses
and verifies checksums; issue #13 scripts the discovery that produces this file.

## Parcel set input (CSV uploaded in the UI)

| Column | Type | Notes |

| weight_lb | decimal | Required |
| length_in, width_in, height_in | decimal | Optional; dimensional weight only when all three are present |
| distance_miles | int | Required |
| residential | bool | Required |
| speed | tier | Required |
| quantity | int | Optional, default 1 |
| price_charged | money | Optional; overrides the flat price control for that row |
| delivery_area | enum | Optional: `none` (default), `das`, `extended` |
| nonstandard_packaging | bool | Optional, default `false`. Packaging that triggers handling fees: not a corrugated box, cylindrical, a can or wooden or metal box, liquids in glass |

The USPS rate card (`commercial` default, `retail` optional) is a dashboard
control, not a parcel column. UPS and FedEx have a single `list` card.

45	def zone_for(tables: RateTables, carrier: str, distance_miles: float) -> int | None:
46	    """Band whose min_miles <= distance <= max_miles (empty max = open)."""
47	    bands = tables.zone_bands.get(carrier, [])

50	            band.max_miles is None or distance_miles <= band.max_miles
51	        ):

234	    """Same exclusive_group: highest amount only (first listed on ties)."""
235	    best: dict[str, tuple[SurchargeRule, Decimal]] = {}
236	    order: list[str] = []

243	            best[group] = (rule, amount)

64

66	        return _unavailable(service, f"{service.display_name} serves business addresses only", as_of=as_of)
67	    if not parcel.residential and not service.business_allowed:
68	        return _unavailable(service, f"{service.display_name} serves residential addresses only", as_of=as_of)
69	
70	    zone = zone_for(tables, carrier, parcel.distance_miles)
71	    if zone is None:
72	        return _unavailable(service, "distance is outside every zone band", as_of=as_of)
73	
74	    rate_card = rate_card_for(service, controls)
75	    steps = tables.rate_steps(carrier, service.service_id, rate_card, year, zone)
76	    if not steps:

79	        )

127	                condition=rule.condition,

139	                amount=money(fuel_basis * pct / Decimal(100)),
140	                source=fuel_source,
141	            )

143	
144	    total = sum((li.amount for li in items), ZERO)
145	    return Quote(

161	def quote_all(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel, controls: Controls) -> list[Quote]:
162	    """Every service of every carrier that publishes prices for the year,
163	    sorted by total within the parcel's tier first, then the other tiers."""
164	    quotes = [
165	        quote_service(tables, s, parcel, controls)
166	        for s in tables.services.values()
167	        if (s.carrier, controls.year) in tables.base_effective
168	    ]
169	    tier_rank = {t: i for i, t in enumerate(TIERS)}
170	
171	    def key(q: Quote):
172	        return (
173	            q.tier != parcel.speed,
174	            tier_rank.get(q.tier, 99),
175	            not q.available,
176	            q.total,
177	        )
178	
179	    return sorted(quotes, key=key)

181	
182	def cheapest_by_tier(quotes: list[Quote]) -> dict[str, Quote | None]:
183	    result: dict[str, Quote | None] = {t: None for t in TIERS}
184	    for q in quotes:
185	        if not q.available:
186	            continue
187	        best = result.get(q.tier)
188	        if best is None or q.total < best.total:
189	            result[q.tier] = q
190	    return result
191	
192	
193	def cheapest_for_carrier(
194	    tables: RateTables, carrier: str, tier: str, parcel: Parcel, controls: Controls, year: int | None = None
195	) -> Quote | None:
196	    """Cheapest available service of one carrier in one tier, or None."""
197	    best: Quote | None = None
198	    for service in tables.services_for(carrier, tier):
199	        q = quote_service(tables, service, parcel, controls, year=year)
200	        if q.available and (best is None or q.total < best.total):
201	            best = q
202	    return best

72	) -> dict:

74	    carriers = [c for c in tables.carriers() if (c, controls.year) in tables.base_effective]
75	
76	    quotes_by_carrier: dict[str, list[Quote | None]] = {}
77	    results = []
78	    for carrier in carriers:

80	        quotes_by_carrier[carrier] = quotes
81	        totals = Totals()
82	        unavailable = 0
83	        services: dict[str, int] = {}
84	        for parcel, q in zip(selected, quotes):
85	            if q is None:
86	                unavailable += parcel.quantity
87	                continue
88	            totals.add(q, parcel.quantity)
89	            services[q.service_id] = services.get(q.service_id, 0) + parcel.quantity
90	        results.append({"carrier": carrier, **summarize(totals, unavailable), "services_used": services})
91

95	    for i, parcel in enumerate(selected):

97	        if not options:

99	            continue

101	        best.add(q, parcel.quantity)

15	ZERO = Decimal("0")
16	CENT = Decimal("0.01")
17	
18	
19	def _r(value: Decimal, places: str = "0.01") -> float:
20	    return float(value.quantize(Decimal(places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))
21	
22	
23	def allocate_cents(values: dict[str, Decimal], total: Decimal) -> dict[str, float]:
24	    """Round each value to cents so the rounded values still add up to the
25	    rounded total (largest remainder)."""
26	    target = total.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
27	    floors = {k: (v / CENT).to_integral_value(rounding="ROUND_FLOOR") for k, v in values.items()}
28	    remainder = int(target / CENT - sum(floors.values()))
29	    order = sorted(values, key=lambda k: (values[k] / CENT - floors[k]), reverse=True)
30	    if remainder < 0:
31	        order = list(reversed(order))
32	    step = 1 if remainder >= 0 else -1
33	    for k in order[: abs(remainder)]:
34	        floors[k] += step
35	    return {k: float(floors[k] * CENT) for k in values}
36

38	def announced_increase(tables: RateTables, carrier: str, year: int, services_used: list[str], usps_card: str) -> dict:
39	    rows = [

42	        if r.carrier == carrier and r.year == year and r.rate_card in ("", "list", usps_card)
43	    ]
44	    overall = [r for r in rows if r.product_scope == "all"]
45	    if overall:
46	        r = overall[0]

48	            "percent": float(r.percent),

54	    if not scoped:

56	    avg = sum((r.percent for r in scoped), ZERO) / len(scoped)

1	"""Question 2: USPS vs UPS / FedEx ground breakeven by weight and distance."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	from .quote import cheapest_for_carrier
6	from .rules import zone_for
7	from .tables import RateTables
8	from .types import Controls, Parcel, Quote
9	
10	GROUND = "ground"
11	USPS = "usps"
12	PRIVATE = ("ups", "fedex")
13	# docs/API.md: the open-ended last band is sampled this far past the
14	# previous band's upper edge.
15	LAST_BAND_OFFSET_MILES = 200
16	
17	
18	def default_weights(tables: RateTables) -> list[float]:
19	    """1 lb steps up to the lowest ground-service weight limit (70 lb)."""
20	    limit = min(s.max_weight_lb for s in tables.services.values() if s.tier == GROUND)
21	    return [float(w) for w in range(1, limit + 1)]
22	
23	
24	def default_distances(tables: RateTables) -> list[float]:
25	    """One distance per USPS zone band: the midpoint, or for the open-ended
26	    last band the previous band's upper edge plus LAST_BAND_OFFSET_MILES."""
27	    out: list[float] = []
28	    prev_max = 0
29	    for band in tables.zone_bands.get(USPS, []):
30	        if band.max_miles is None:
31	            out.append(float(prev_max + LAST_BAND_OFFSET_MILES))
32	        else:
33	            out.append(float((band.min_miles + band.max_miles) // 2))
34	            prev_max = band.max_miles
35	    return out
36	
37	
38	def _pick(q: Quote) -> dict:
39	    return {"carrier": q.carrier, "service_id": q.service_id, "total": float(q.total)}
40	
41	
42	def breakeven(
43	    tables: RateTables,
44	    controls: Controls,
45	    residential: bool,
46	    weights_lb: list[float] | None = None,
47	    distances_miles: list[float] | None = None,
48	) -> dict:
49	    weights = sorted(weights_lb) if weights_lb else default_weights(tables)
50	    distances = sorted(distances_miles) if distances_miles else default_distances(tables)
51	    carriers = [c for c in tables.carriers() if (c, controls.year) in tables.base_effective]
52	
53	    cells = []
54	    bands = []
55	    for d in distances:
56	        first_loss: dict[str, float | None] = {c: None for c in PRIVATE}
57	        for w in weights:
58	            parcel = Parcel(weight_lb=w, distance_miles=d, residential=residential, speed=GROUND)
59	            quotes = {
60	                c: q
61	                for c in carriers
62	                if (q := cheapest_for_carrier(tables, c, GROUND, parcel, controls)) is not None
63	            }
64	            ranked = sorted(quotes.values(), key=lambda q: q.total)
65	            usps = quotes.get(USPS)
66	            for c in PRIVATE:
67	                other = quotes.get(c)
68	                if usps and other and first_loss[c] is None and usps.total >= other.total:
69	                    first_loss[c] = w
70	            private_zone = next((q.zone for q in ranked if q.carrier != USPS), None)
71	            cells.append(
72	                {
73	                    "weight_lb": w,
74	                    "distance_miles": d,
75	                    "zone_usps": zone_for(tables, USPS, d),
76	                    "zone_private": private_zone if private_zone is not None else zone_for(tables, "ups", d),
77	                    "winner": _pick(ranked[0]) if ranked else None,
78	                    "runner_up": _pick(ranked[1]) if len(ranked) > 1 else None,
79	                    "saving": float(ranked[1].total - ranked[0].total) if len(ranked) > 1 else 0.0,
80	                    "totals": {q.carrier: float(q.total) for q in ranked},
81	                }
82	            )
83	        bands.append(
84	            {
85	                "distance_miles": d,
86	                "zone_usps": zone_for(tables, USPS, d),
87	                "zone_private": zone_for(tables, "ups", d),
88	                "vs_ups": first_loss["ups"],
89	                "vs_fedex": first_loss["fedex"],
90	            }
91	        )
92	    return {
93	        "year": controls.year,
94	        "residential": residential,
95	        "weights_lb": weights,
96	        "distances_miles": distances,
97	        "cells": cells,
98	        "breakeven_weight_lb": bands,
99	    }
100	
101

1	"""Parcel segments used by the segment filter and the yearly driver breakdown.
2	
3	Band labels and edges come from docs/API.md ("Segments"). Zone bands use the
4	USPS zone of the parcel's distance, the finest of the carriers' band tables.
5	"""

7	from __future__ import annotations
8	
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	
11	from .rules import zone_for
12	from .tables import RateTables
13	from .types import Parcel
14	
15	# (label, lower bound exclusive, upper bound inclusive)
16	WEIGHT_BANDS: tuple[tuple[str, float, float], ...] = (
17	    ("≤1", 0.0, 1.0),
18	    ("1–5", 1.0, 5.0),
19	    ("5–10", 5.0, 10.0),
20	    ("10–20", 10.0, 20.0),
21	    ("20–70", 20.0, 70.0),
22	)
23	ZONE_BANDS: tuple[tuple[str, int, int], ...] = (
24	    ("1–2", 1, 2),
25	    ("3–4", 3, 4),
26	    ("5–6", 5, 6),
27	    ("7–8", 7, 8),
28	)
29	SEGMENT_CARRIER = "usps"
30	DIMENSIONS = ("weight_band", "zone_band", "residential", "speed")
31	
32	
33	@dataclass(frozen=True)
34	class SegmentFilter:
35	    weight_band: str | None = None
36	    zone_band: str | None = None
37	    residential: bool | None = None
38	    speed: str | None = None
39	
40	
41	def weight_band(parcel: Parcel) -> str:
42	    for label, low, high in WEIGHT_BANDS:
43	        if low < parcel.weight_lb <= high:
44	            return label
45	    return WEIGHT_BANDS[-1][0]
46	
47	
48	def zone_band(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel) -> str:
49	    zone = zone_for(tables, SEGMENT_CARRIER, parcel.distance_miles)
50	    for label, low, high in ZONE_BANDS:
51	        if zone is not None and low <= zone <= high:
52	            return label
53	    return ZONE_BANDS[-1][0]
54	
55	
56	def residential_label(parcel: Parcel) -> str:
57	    return "residential" if parcel.residential else "business"
58	
59	
60	def segment_of(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel) -> dict[str, str]:
61	    return {
62	        "weight_band": weight_band(parcel),
63	        "zone_band": zone_band(tables, parcel),
64	        "residential": residential_label(parcel),
65	        "speed": parcel.speed,
66	    }
67	
68	
69	def matches(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel, f: SegmentFilter | None) -> bool:
70	    if f is None:
71	        return True
72	    if f.weight_band is not None and weight_band(parcel) != f.weight_band:
73	        return False
