S=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-aivuk-parcel-rates/31d666d4-9d83-44bd-bae6-ef26e807eeb3/scratchpad; cat > $S/dump.py <<'EOF'
import sys, pdfplumber
base="~/parcel-rates-issue-2/data/raw/ups/"
jobs = {
 "2023": ("2023/ups-2023-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates.pdf", [21,22,23,24,25,129,130,131,132,133,134,138]),
 "2024": ("2024/ups-2024-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates-updated-2024-07-01.pdf", [20,21,22,23,24,128,129,130,131,132,133,137]),
 "2025": ("2025/ups-2025-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates-2024-12-23.pdf", [21,22,23,24,25,180,181,182,183,184,185,190]),
 "2026": ("2026/ups-2026-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates-updated-2026-09-07.pdf", [21,22,23,24,25,180,181,182,183,184,185,186,205,206,207]),
 "demand2023": ("2023/ups-demand-surcharges-2023-01-15-update.pdf", [1,2,3,4,5]),
 "demand2024": ("2024/ups-demand-surcharges-2024-07-15-update.pdf", [1,2,3,4,5,6]),
 "demand2025": ("2025/ups-demand-surcharges-2024-09-16-update-peak-2024-25.pdf", [1,2,3,4,5,6]),
}
out=sys.argv[1]
for name,(f,pages) in jobs.items():
    with pdfplumber.open(base+f) as pdf, open(f"{out}/{name}.txt","w") as fh:
        for p in pages:
            fh.write(f"\n\n######## PAGE {p}\n")
            fh.write(pdf.pages[p-1].extract_text() or "")
    print(name, "done")
EOF
uv run --directory ~/parcel-rates-issue-2 python $S/dump.py $S && wc -c $S/*.txt

Applies to customers whose combined volume of Ground Residential, SurePost, Next Day Air Residential and All Other Air Residential packages has exceeded 20,000 packages in any week after October 2023, regardless of the volume of customer’

Next Day Air Residential and All Other Air Residential packages in any weekly invoice period exceeding the Baseline volume for the applicable service level. For each service level each week, the amount of the surcharge for
all packages over 105% of the Baseline for each service level is the highest applicable surcharge for the service level. For example, if the shipper has volume in a week of 175% of the Baseline average weekly volume for UPS
Ground Residential, then each UPS Ground Residential package over 105% of the Baseline average weekly volume for UPS Ground Residential will be assessed a surcharge of $2.35 (not just those over 150% of Baseline
average weekly volume for UPS Ground Residential). For holiday weeks that are not full UPS operating weeks, the surcharge will apply to all packages in that weekly invoice period exceeding 105% of the customer’s average
daily baseline volume for the applicable service level multiplied by the number of full UPS operating days in that week. Customer’s volume includes volume from any affiliated accounts and other accounts related to
customer, as determined by UPS in its sole and unlimited discretion.
6
The “Baseline” volume is the customer’s average weekly volume for the applicable service level for June 2024 (June 2, 2024 through June 29, 2024). If customer’s average weekly volume for the applicable service level
from September 1, 2024 through September 28, 2024 is less than 80% of its average weekly volume from June 2, 2024 through June 29, 2024, as determined by UPS in its sole and unlimited discretion, then customer’s average
weekly volume from September 1, 2024 through September 28, 2024 will be used as the Baseline volume.

echo "######## FEDEX FUEL"; cat > $S/fuel.py <<'EOF'
import re,sys
sys.path.insert(0,"~/parcel-rates-issue-2")
from data.pipeline.common import html_text, raw_path, normalize_text
for y,f in [(2023,"fedex/2023/historical-fuel-surcharge_page_wayback_2023-01-12.html"),(2024,"fedex/2024/historical-fuel-surcharge_page_wayback_2024-12-02.html"),(2025,"fedex/2025/historical-fuel-surcharge_page_wayback_2025-09-20.html"),(2026,"fedex/2026/historical-fuel-surcharge_page_wayback_2026-10-13.html")]:
    t=normalize_text(html_text(raw_path(f)))
    i=t.find("fuel surcharge history") if "fuel surcharge history" in t else 0
    # print the region with percentages
    ms=[m.start() for m in re.finditer(r"\d+\.\d+%",t)]
    print("=====",y,"pct count",len(ms))
    if ms: print(t[max(0,ms[0]-900):ms[-1]+120])
EOF
uv run --directory ~/parcel-rates-issue-2 python $S/fuel.py

```
"""Curated UPS rules, transcribed from the Daily Rates guides and demand-surcharge
PDFs in data/raw/ups. Every entry quotes the cited page verbatim (as pdfplumber
reads it); amounts are taken from the quote itself so a transcription error
cannot separate a number from its citation. `data.pipeline.ups` expands these
literals into the CSV tables.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re

CARRIER = "ups"
RATE_CARD = "list"
YEARS = (2023, 2024, 2025, 2026)

G23 = "ups/2023/ups-2023-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates.pdf"
G24 = "ups/2024/ups-2024-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates-updated-2024-07-01.pdf"
G25 = "ups/2025/ups-2025-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates-2024-12-23.pdf"
G26 = "ups/2026/ups-2026-rate-and-service-guide-daily-rates-updated-2026-09-07.pdf"
DEMAND23 = "ups/2023/ups-demand-surcharges-2023-01-15-update.pdf"
DEMAND24 = "ups/2024/ups-demand-surcharges-2024-07-15-update.pdf"
DEMAND25 = "ups/2025/ups-demand-surcharges-2024-09-16-update-peak-2024-25.pdf"

# The guide used for each price year and the effective date printed in it.
GUIDES = {
    2023: {"file": G23, "effective_date": "2022-12-27"},
    2024: {"file": G24, "effective_date": "2024-07-01"},
    2025: {"file": G25, "effective_date": "2024-12-23"},
    2026: {"file": G26, "effective_date": "2026-09-07"},
}

AIR_AND_3DS = "ups_3_day_select,ups_2nd_day_air,ups_next_day_air_saver,ups_next_day_air"
GROUND = "ups_ground"

FUEL_NOTE = {
    2023: ("fuel_applies assumed from the page note 'Fuel surcharges apply to other charges "
           "associated with pickup, transport and delivery.'"),
    2024: ("fuel_applies assumed from the page note 'Fuel surcharges apply to other charges "
           "associated with pickup, transport and delivery.'"),
    2025: ("fuel_applies assumed from the page note 'Fuel surcharges may apply to any or all domestic "
           "and international transportation charges and certain accessorial charges, value-added "
           "charges, surcharges and other charges.'"),
    2026: ("fuel_applies assumed from the page note 'Fuel surcharges may apply to any or all domestic "
           "and international transportation charges and certain accessorial charges, value-added "
           "charges, surcharges and other charges.'"),
}

BANDS_3 = ((2, 2), (3, 4), (5, 8))        # guide columns: Zone 2 | Zones 3-4 | Zones 5+
BANDS_4 = ((2, 2), (3, 4), (5, 6), (7, 8))  # 2026 guide: Zone 2 | 3-4 | 5-6 | 7+

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Residential surcharge (per package). Two amounts: Ground vs Air/3 Day Select.
# The air fee cell reads "UPS Domestic and International Air Services, UPS 3 Day
# Select and UPS 3 Day Select from Canada: $x" across three lines; the quote is
# the line that carries the amount.
RESIDENTIAL = {
    2023: {"page": 132, "ground": "– UPS® Ground Services: $5.25", "air": "UPS 3 Day Select® from Canada: $5.85"},
    2024: {"page": 132, "ground": "– UPS® Ground Services: $5.65", "air": "UPS 3 Day Select® from Canada: $6.20"},
    2025: {"page": 184, "ground": "– UPS® Ground Services: $6.10", "air": "UPS 3 Day Select® from Canada: $6.55"},
    2026: {"page": 185, "ground": "– UPS® Ground Services: $6.50", "air": "– UPS Domestic Air and UPS 3 Day Select®: $7.00"},
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Delivery Area Surcharge. Each quote line reads "<variant> $ground $air".
DELIVERY_AREA = {
    2023: {"page": 130, "commercial": "– Commercial $3.70 $3.70", "residential": "– Residential $5.30 $5.55",
           "commercial_extended": "– C ommercial Extended $4.50 $4.50", "residential_extended": "– R esidential Extended $7.15 $7.15"},
    2024: {"page": 130, "commercial": "– Commercial $3.95 $3.95", "residential": "– Residential $5.70 $5.85",
           "commercial_extended": "– C ommercial Extended $4.90 $4.90", "residential_extended": "– R esidential Extended $7.70 $7.70"},
    2025: {"page": 182, "commercial": "– Commercial $4.20 $4.20", "residential": "– Residential $6.15 $6.15",
           "commercial_extended": "– C ommercial Extended $5.35 $5.35", "residential_extended": "– R esidential Extended $8.30 $8.30"},
    2026: {"page": 182, "commercial": "– Commercial $4.50 $4.50", "residential": "– R esidential $6.55 $6.55",
           "commercial_extended": "– C ommercial Extended $5.70 $5.70", "residential_extended": "– R esidential Extended $8.85 $8.85"},
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Additional Handling: one quote line per criterion, amounts by zone band.
# criterion -> (condition, threshold columns, note)
AH_CRITERIA = {
    "weight": ("additional_handling_weight", {"min_weight_lb": "50"},
               "actual weight of more than 50 pounds"),
    "length_plus_girth": ("additional_handling_length", {"min_length_plus_girth_in": "105"},
                          "length plus girth [(2 x width) + (2 x height)] exceeding 105 inches"),
    "length": ("additional_handling_length", {"min_length_in": "48"},
               "longest side exceeding 48 inches"),
    "width": ("additional_handling_width", {},
              "second-longest side exceeding 30 inches (no width column in the schema; engine must check width > 30 in)"),
    "cubic": ("nonstandard_volume", {"min_volume_cuft": "6"},
              "cubic size greater than 10,368 cubic inches (= 6 cu ft)"),
    "packaging": ("additional_handling_packaging", {},

def amounts_in(quote: str) -> list[str]:
    """Dollar amounts in a quote, in order, as two-decimal strings."""
    return [m.replace(",", "") for m in re.findall(r"\$\s?([\d,]+\.\d{2})", quote)]

```
"""UPS Daily Rates pipeline.

Usage: uv run python -m data.pipeline.ups

Rewrites every file in data/processed/ups/ from the raw files listed in the
manifest: base_rates.csv is parsed from the rate-table pages of the guides with
pdfplumber word positions; the curated tables are expanded from the literals in
data/pipeline/ups_rules.py; fuel_surcharge.csv holds proxies computed from the
FedEx historical pages. Any rate row whose columns do not line up with the
table header is an error, never a guess.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import date
from decimal import Decimal

from data.pipeline import ups_rules as rules
from data.pipeline.common import (
    MAX_WEIGHT_LB, ZONES, html_text, money, raw_path, weight_label, write_table,
)

PRICE = re.compile(r"^\$?\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})*\.\d{2}$")
WEIGHT = re.compile(r"^\d{1,3}$")
LB_TOKENS = {"Lb.", "Lbs."}
SUBHEADINGS = {"Domestic", "U.S. 48 – Domestic"}
MAX_TABLE_WEIGHT = 150
COLUMN_TOLERANCE = 18.0  # points; zone columns are ~47 points apart
ROW_TOLERANCE = 3.0

# service_id -> (heading regex matched against a whole text line, header code -> zone)
SERVICES: dict[str, tuple[re.Pattern[str], dict[str, int]]] = {
    "ups_next_day_air": (re.compile(r"^UPS Next Day Air®\s*$"), {f"10{z}": z for z in range(2, 9)}),
    "ups_next_day_air_saver": (re.compile(r"^UPS Next Day Air Saver®\s*$"), {f"13{z}": z for z in range(2, 9)}),
    "ups_2nd_day_air": (re.compile(r"^UPS 2nd Day Air®\*?\s*$"), {f"20{z}": z for z in range(2, 9)}),
    "ups_3_day_select": (re.compile(r"^UPS 3 Day Select®\*?\s*$"), {f"30{z}": z for z in range(2, 9)}),
    "ups_ground": (re.compile(r"^UPS® Ground\*?\s*$"), {str(z): z for z in range(2, 9)}),
}


class ParseError(ValueError):
    """A rate page that cannot be read unambiguously."""


@dataclass
class Header:
    codes: list[str]
    centers: list[float]

    def zone_columns(self, code_map: dict[str, int]) -> tuple[dict[int, int], list[str]]:
        """Return {column index: zone} for the carrier's zones and the excluded codes (AK/HI/PR)."""
        zones, excluded = {}, []
        for index, code in enumerate(self.codes):
            bare = code.rstrip("*")
            if bare in code_map and not code.endswith("*"):
                zones[index] = code_map[bare]
            elif code.endswith("*"):
                excluded.append(code)
            else:
                raise ParseError(f"unexpected zone header {code!r} in {self.codes}")
        if sorted(zones.values()) != list(ZONES["ups"]):
            raise ParseError(f"header does not cover zones 2-8: {self.codes}")
        return zones, excluded


@dataclass
class PageTable:
    page: int
    header: Header
    rows: dict[int, list[str]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # weight -> prices per header column


def group_lines(words: list[dict], tolerance: float = ROW_TOLERANCE) -> list[list[dict]]:
    """Cluster pdfplumber words into lines by their `top`, each line sorted left to right."""
    lines: list[list[dict]] = []
    for word in sorted(words, key=lambda w: (w["top"], w["x0"])):
        if lines and abs(lines[-1][0]["top"] - word["top"]) <= tolerance:
            lines[-1].append(word)
        else:
            lines.append([word])
    return [sorted(line, key=lambda w: w["x0"]) for line in lines]


def center(word: dict) -> float:
    return (word["x0"] + word["x1"]) / 2


def parse_header(line: list[dict]) -> Header | None:
    if not line or line[0]["text"] != "Zones":
        return None
    codes = [w["text"] for w in line[1:]]
    if not codes:
        raise ParseError("empty Zones header")
    return Header(codes, [center(w) for w in line[1:]])


def tokenize_row(line: list[dict]) -> tuple[int, list[dict]] | None:
    """(weight, price words) for a rate row; None for anything else (Letter rows, notes)."""
    if not line or not WEIGHT.match(line[0]["text"]):
        return None
    rest = [w for w in line[1:] if w["text"] not in LB_TOKENS]
    if not rest:
        return None
    bad = [w["text"] for w in rest if not PRICE.match(w["text"])]
    if bad:
        raise ParseError(f"row {line[0]['text']}: non-price tokens {bad}")
    return int(line[0]["text"]), rest


def assign_columns(prices: list[dict], header: Header, tolerance: float = COLUMN_TOLERANCE) -> list[str]:
    """Match each price to the header column it sits under; exactly one price per column or error."""
    if len(prices) != len(header.centers):
        raise ParseError(f"{len(prices)} prices for {len(header.centers)} zone columns: {[w['text'] for w in prices]}")
    for word, expected in zip(prices, header.centers):
        if abs(center(word) - expected) > tolerance:
            raise ParseError(f"price {word['text']} at x={center(word):.0f} is not under column at x={expected:.0f}")
    return [money(w["text"].replace("$", "").replace(",", "")) for w in prices]


def parse_rate_page(words: list[dict], page: int) -> PageTable:
    header: Header | None = None
    rows: dict[int, list[str]] = {}
    for line in group_lines(words):
        found = parse_header(line)
        if found:
            if header is not None:
                raise ParseError(f"page {page}: two Zones headers")
            header = found
            continue
        token = tokenize_row(line)
        if token is None:
            continue
        if header is None:
            raise ParseError(f"page {page}: rate row before the Zones header")
        weight, prices = token
        if weight in rows:
            raise ParseError(f"page {page}: weight {weight} appears twice")
        try:
            rows[weight] = assign_columns(prices, header)
        except ParseError as error:
            raise ParseError(f"page {page}, {weight} lb: {error}") from error
    if header is None or not rows:
        raise ParseError(f"page {page}: no rate table found")
    return PageTable(page, header, rows)


def service_on_page(lines: list[str]) -> str | None:
    """The service whose U.S. 48 table this page holds, judged by heading plus subheading."""
    stripped = [line.strip() for line in lines]
    for service_id, (pattern, _) in SERVICES.items():
        for index, line in enumerate(stripped):
            if pattern.match(line):
                neighbours = {stripped[i] for i in (index - 1, index + 1) if 0 <= i < len(stripped)}
                if neighbours & SUBHEADINGS:
                    return service_id
    return None


def parse_guide(year: int) -> tuple[list[dict], list[dict]]:
    """base_rates rows (<= 70 lb) and ak_hi_zone exception rows for one guide."""
    import pdfplumber

    guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
    path = raw_path(guide["file"])
    tables: dict[str, list[PageTable]] = {s: [] for s in SERVICES}
    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
        for number, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
            text = page.extract_text() or ""
            if "Zones" not in text:
                continue
            service_id = service_on_page(text.splitlines())
            if service_id is None:
                continue
            words = page.extract_words(x_tolerance=1.5)
            tables[service_id].append(parse_rate_page(words, number))
    base_rows, exceptions = [], []
    for service_id, pages in tables.items():
        base, excluded = assemble_table(service_id, pages, year)
        base_rows.extend(base)
        exceptions.append(ak_hi_exception(service_id, year, pages, excluded))
    return base_rows, exceptions


def assemble_table(service_id: str, pages: list[PageTable], year: int) -> tuple[list[dict], list[str]]:
    if not pages:
        raise ParseError(f"{year} {service_id}: no table pages found")
    guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
    code_map = SERVICES[service_id][1]
    rows: list[dict] = []
    seen: dict[int, int] = {}
    excluded_codes: list[str] = []
    for table in pages:
        zones, excluded = table.header.zone_columns(code_map)
        excluded_codes = excluded or excluded_codes
        for weight, prices in table.rows.items():
            if weight in seen:
                raise ParseError(f"{year} {service_id}: {weight} lb on pages {seen[weight]} and {table.page}")
            seen[weight] = table.page
            if weight > MAX_WEIGHT_LB:
                continue
            for index, zone in zones.items():
                rows.append({
                    "carrier": rules.CARRIER, "service_id": service_id, "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD,
                    "year": str(year), "effective_date": guide["effective_date"], "zone": str(zone),
                    "max_weight_lb": weight_label(weight), "price": prices[index],
                    "source_file": guide["file"], "source_ref": str(table.page),
                })
    expected = list(range(1, MAX_TABLE_WEIGHT + 1))
    if sorted(seen) != expected:
        missing = sorted(set(expected) - set(seen))
        raise ParseError(f"{year} {service_id}: weights missing or extra, missing={missing[:10]}, extra={sorted(set(seen) - set(expected))[:10]}")
    return rows, excluded_codes


def ak_hi_exception(service_id: str, year: int, pages: list[PageTable], excluded: list[str]) -> dict:
    guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
    page_list = ",".join(str(t.page) for t in pages if min(t.rows) <= MAX_WEIGHT_LB)
    if excluded:
        note = (f"Columns {', '.join(excluded)} (Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico) sit in the same table as zones 2-8 "
                f"and are not parsed into base_rates; excluded from the dashboard.")
    else:
        note = ("The U.S. 48 table publishes zones 2-8 only; Alaska/Hawaii rates for this service are in separate "
                "tables (2025+) or not published, and are not parsed.")
    return {"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "service_id": service_id, "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD, "year": str(year),
            "kind": "ak_hi_zone", "note": note, "source_file": guide["file"], "source_ref": page_list}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Curated tables


def surcharge_row(year: int, **values: str) -> dict:
    guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
    row = {"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD, "unit": "usd",
           "effective_from": guide["effective_date"], "effective_to": "", "fuel_applies": "true",
           "source_file": guide["file"]}
    row.update(values)
    return row


def residential_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.RESIDENTIAL[year]
    rows = []
    for variant, applies_to in (("ground", rules.GROUND), ("air", rules.AIR_AND_3DS)):
        quote = spec[variant]
        (amount,) = rules.amounts_in(quote)
        rows.append(surcharge_row(
            year, surcharge_id=f"ups_residential_{variant}_{year}", display_name="Residential Surcharge",
            condition="residential", applies_to=applies_to, amount=amount, exclusive_group="residential",
            source_page=str(spec["page"]), source_quote=quote,
            notes=f"Per package, delivery to a home. {rules.FUEL_NOTE[year]}"))
    return rows


def delivery_area_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.DELIVERY_AREA[year]
    rows = []
    for variant in ("commercial", "residential", "commercial_extended", "residential_extended"):
        quote = spec[variant]
        ground_amount, air_amount = rules.amounts_in(quote)
        condition = "delivery_area_extended" if variant.endswith("_extended") else "delivery_area"
        address = variant.split("_")[0]
        for mode, applies_to, amount in (("ground", rules.GROUND, ground_amount), ("air", rules.AIR_AND_3DS, air_amount)):
            rows.append(surcharge_row(
                year, surcharge_id=f"ups_das_{variant}_{mode}_{year}", display_name="Delivery Area Surcharge",
                condition=condition, applies_to=applies_to, amount=amount, exclusive_group="delivery_area",
                source_page=str(spec["page"]), source_quote=quote,
                notes=(f"{address.capitalize()} deliveries only ({'extended' if condition.endswith('extended') else 'standard'} "
                       f"delivery-area ZIP codes); the guide prints Ground and Air amounts side by side. {rules.FUEL_NOTE[year]}")))
    return rows


def banded_rows(year: int, quote: str, bands: tuple, **values: str) -> list[dict]:
    amounts = rules.amounts_in(quote)
    if len(amounts) != len(bands):
        raise ValueError(f"{year}: {len(amounts)} amounts for {len(bands)} zone bands in {quote!r}")
    rows = []
    for (zone_min, zone_max), amount in zip(bands, amounts):
        rows.append(surcharge_row(year, zone_min=str(zone_min), zone_max=str(zone_max), amount=amount,
                                  source_quote=quote, **values))
    return rows


def additional_handling_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.ADDITIONAL_HANDLING[year]
    rows = []
    for criterion, quote in spec["quotes"].items():
        condition, thresholds, note = rules.AH_CRITERIA[criterion]
        rows.extend(banded_rows(
            year, quote, spec["bands"], surcharge_id=f"ups_additional_handling_{criterion}_{year}",
            display_name="Additional Handling", condition=condition, applies_to="all",
            exclusive_group="ups_handling", source_page=str(spec["page"]),
            notes=(f"Criterion: {note}. Only one Additional Handling charge applies and none when a Large Package "
                   f"Surcharge applies (same exclusive_group). {rules.FUEL_NOTE[year]}"), **thresholds))
    return rows


def large_package_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.LARGE_PACKAGE[year]
    rows = []
    for (address, criterion), quote in spec["quotes"].items():
        thresholds, note = rules.LPS_CRITERIA[criterion]
        rows.extend(banded_rows(
            year, quote, spec["bands"], surcharge_id=f"ups_large_package_{address}_{criterion}_{year}",
            display_name="Large Package Surcharge", condition="oversize", applies_to="all",
            exclusive_group="ups_handling", source_page=str(spec["page"]),
            notes=(f"{address.capitalize()} deliveries only. Criterion: {note}. Large Packages carry a 90 lb minimum "
                   f"billable weight (not modelled). {rules.FUEL_NOTE[year]}"), **thresholds))
    return rows


def peak_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.PEAK.get(year)
    if not spec:
        return []
    rows = []
    for item in spec["rows"]:
        amounts = rules.amounts_in(item["quote"])
        if len(amounts) != len(item["windows"]):
            raise ValueError(f"{year} {item['condition']}: {len(amounts)} amounts for {len(item['windows'])} windows")
        for amount, window in zip(amounts, item["windows"]):
            if window is None:
                continue
            start, end = window
            rows.append(surcharge_row(
                year, surcharge_id=f"ups_{item['condition']}_{start}", display_name="Demand Surcharge",
                condition=item["condition"], applies_to=item["applies_to"], amount=amount,
                exclusive_group=f"peak_{item['condition']}", effective_from=start, effective_to=end,
                source_file=spec["file"], source_page=str(item["page"]), source_quote=item["quote"],
                notes="; ".join(filter(None, [spec["note"], item.get("note"),
                                              "fuel_applies assumed from the guide's statement that fuel may apply to surcharges"]))))
    return rows


def surcharges() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for year in rules.YEARS:
        rows += residential_rows(year) + delivery_area_rows(year) + additional_handling_rows(year)
        rows += large_package_rows(year) + peak_rows(year)
    return rows


def announced_increase() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for year, spec in rules.ANNOUNCED_INCREASE.items():
        match = re.search(r"(\d+\.\d+)%", spec["quote"])
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"{year}: no percent in {spec['quote']!r}")
        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "product_scope": "all", "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD,
                     "percent": match.group(1), "source_type": "secondary", "source_file": spec["file"],
                     "source_ref": "", "source_quote": spec["quote"]})
    return rows


def dim_weight() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for year, spec in rules.DIM_WEIGHT.items():
        guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "effective_from": guide["effective_date"],
                     "effective_to": "", "divisor": "139", "min_volume_cuin": "0", "rounding": spec["rounding"],
                     "source_file": guide["file"], "source_ref": str(spec["page"]), "source_quote": spec["quote"]})
    return rows


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fuel surcharge proxies from the FedEx historical pages

MONTHS = {"jan": 1, "feb": 2, "mar": 3, "apr": 4, "may": 5, "jun": 6, "jul": 7, "aug": 8, "sep": 9, "oct": 10, "nov": 11, "dec": 12}
DATE = r"(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|June?|July?|Aug|Sept?|Oct|Nov|Dec)\.? \d{1,2}, \d{4}"
WEEK_ROW = re.compile(rf"({DATE})-({DATE})")
PERCENT = re.compile(r"\d+\.\d+%")


def parse_date(text: str) -> date:
    month, day, year = re.match(r"([A-Za-z]+)\.? (\d{1,2}), (\d{4})", text).groups()
    return date(int(year), MONTHS[month[:3].lower()], int(day))


@dataclass
class WeekRow:
    start: date
    end: date
    text: str          # row text as it appears in the collapsed page text
    percents: list[str]


def parse_fuel_rows(page_text: str) -> list[WeekRow]:
    """Weekly rows of the first (package) table on a FedEx historical fuel page."""
    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", page_text)
    starts = [m for m in WEEK_ROW.finditer(text)]
    rows = []
    for current, following in zip(starts, starts[1:] + [None]):
        end = following.start() if following else len(text)
        segment = text[current.start():end]
        segment = segment.split(" previous ")[0].split(" Previous ")[0].strip()
        percents = PERCENT.findall(segment)
        if not percents:
            continue
        rows.append(WeekRow(parse_date(current.group(1)), parse_date(current.group(2)), segment, percents))
    if not rows:
        raise ValueError("no weekly fuel rows found")
    return rows


def lower_median(values: list[Decimal]) -> Decimal:
    ordered = sorted(values)
    return ordered[(len(ordered) - 1) // 2]


def fuel_proxy_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
    spec = rules.FUEL_PROXY_SOURCES[year]
    rows = parse_fuel_rows(html_text(raw_path(spec["file"])))
    out = []
    for group, index in spec["percent_index"].items():
        values = [Decimal(r.percents[index].rstrip("%")) for r in rows]
        median = lower_median(values)
        mean = sum(values) / len(values)
        chosen = next(r for r in rows if Decimal(r.percents[index].rstrip("%")) == median)
        token = chosen.percents[index]
        quote = chosen.text[:chosen.text.index(token) + len(token)]
        out.append({
            "carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "service_group": group, "default_percent": f"{median:.2f}",
            "basis": "base rate plus surcharges flagged fuel_applies",
            "window_start": min(r.start for r in rows).isoformat(), "window_end": max(r.end for r in rows).isoformat(),
            "is_proxy": "true", "source_file": spec["file"], "source_ref": "", "source_quote": quote,
            "notes": (f"Proxy: UPS publishes no retrievable weekly fuel history. default_percent is the lower median of the "
                      f"{len(values)} weekly FedEx {group} percentages in this snapshot (mean {mean:.2f}%); the quoted row is "
                      f"the most recent week at the median. {spec['layout']}."),
        })
    return out


def fuel_surcharge() -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for year in rules.YEARS:
        rows += fuel_proxy_rows(year)
    return rows


def exceptions(parsed: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    rows = [dict(row) for row in parsed]
    for note in rules.EXCEPTION_NOTES:
        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD, **note})
    return rows


def main() -> None:
    base_rows, parsed_exceptions = [], []
    for year in rules.YEARS:
        rows, year_exceptions = parse_guide(year)
        base_rows += rows
        parsed_exceptions += year_exceptions
        print(f"{year}: {len(rows)} rate cells")
    for table, rows in (
        ("base_rates", base_rows),
        ("exceptions", exceptions(parsed_exceptions)),
        ("surcharges", surcharges()),
        ("fuel_surcharge", fuel_surcharge()),
        ("announced_increase", announced_increase()),
        ("dim_weight", dim_weight()),
    ):
        path = write_table(rules.CARRIER, table, rows)
        print(f"wrote {path.name}: {len(rows)} rows")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Unit tests for the UPS rate-table parser: line grouping, row tokenizing,
zone-column validation, and a small synthetic page fixture. A final test
parses one real page when the 2026 guide is on disk."""
from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from data.pipeline import ups
from data.pipeline.common import raw_path


def word(text: str, x: float, top: float, width: float = 24.0) -> dict:
    return {"text": text, "x0": x - width / 2, "x1": x + width / 2, "top": top}


HEADER_X = [133, 180, 227, 273, 320, 366, 413, 455, 502, 548]
HEADER_CODES = ["2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "8", "44**", "45**", "46**"]


def header_line(top: float = 186) -> list[dict]:
    return [word("Zones", 57, top)] + [word(code, x, top) for code, x in zip(HEADER_CODES, HEADER_X)]


def price_row(weight: int, prices: list[str], top: float, xs: list[float] = HEADER_X, lb: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    words = [word(str(weight), 51, top)]
    if lb:
        words.append(word("Lb.", 60, top))
    words += [word(price, x, top) for price, x in zip(prices, xs)]
    return words


ROW1 = ["$11.99", "$12.38", "$13.51", "$14.10", "$14.60", "$14.83", "$15.03", "$43.25", "$44.17", "$56.96"]
ROW2 = ["12.85", "14.15", "15.46", "15.79", "16.49", "17.18", "17.40", "48.12", "49.48", "61.80"]


def fixture_page() -> list[dict]:
    words = header_line()
    words += [word("Letter**", 57, 192)] + [word("$30.56", x, 192) for x in HEADER_X]
    words += price_row(1, ROW1, 198, lb=True)
    words += price_row(2, ROW2, 210)
    words += [word("*Visit", 40, 400), word("ups.com/holidays", 80, 400)]
    return words


def test_group_lines_clusters_by_top_and_sorts_left_to_right():
    words = [word("b", 100, 10.5), word("a", 50, 10.0), word("c", 50, 22.0)]
    lines = ups.group_lines(words)
    assert [[w["text"] for w in line] for line in lines] == [["a", "b"], ["c"]]


def test_parse_header_reads_zone_codes_and_centers():
    header = ups.parse_header(header_line())
    assert header.codes == HEADER_CODES
    assert header.centers == pytest.approx(HEADER_X)
    assert ups.parse_header(price_row(3, ROW2, 50)) is None


def test_zone_columns_separates_ak_hi_codes():
    header = ups.parse_header(header_line())
    zones, excluded = header.zone_columns(ups.SERVICES["ups_ground"][1])
    assert zones == {0: 2, 1: 3, 2: 4, 3: 5, 4: 6, 5: 7, 6: 8}
    assert excluded == ["44**", "45**", "46**"]


def test_zone_columns_maps_three_digit_air_codes():
    codes = ["102", "103", "104", "105", "106", "107", "108", "124*"]
    header = ups.Header(codes, [float(i) for i in range(len(codes))])
    zones, excluded = header.zone_columns(ups.SERVICES["ups_next_day_air"][1])
    assert list(zones.values()) == [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]
    assert excluded == ["124*"]


def test_zone_columns_rejects_unknown_code():
    header = ups.Header(["2", "3", "4", "5", "6", "7", "9"], [0.0] * 7)
    with pytest.raises(ups.ParseError):
        header.zone_columns(ups.SERVICES["ups_ground"][1])


def test_tokenize_row_drops_lb_token_and_skips_letter_rows():
    weight, prices = ups.tokenize_row(price_row(1, ROW1, 198, lb=True))
    assert weight == 1
    assert [w["text"] for w in prices] == ROW1
    assert ups.tokenize_row([word("Letter**", 57, 192), word("$30.56", 133, 192)]) is None


def test_tokenize_row_rejects_non_price_tokens():
    with pytest.raises(ups.ParseError):
        ups.tokenize_row(price_row(5, ["12.85", "n/a", "15.46"], 50, xs=HEADER_X[:3]))


def test_assign_columns_requires_one_price_per_column():
    header = ups.parse_header(header_line())
    with pytest.raises(ups.ParseError, match="9 prices for 10"):
        ups.assign_columns(price_row(2, ROW2[:9], 210, xs=HEADER_X[:9])[1:], header)


def test_assign_columns_rejects_misaligned_price():
    header = ups.parse_header(header_line())
    shifted = [x + 30 for x in HEADER_X]
    with pytest.raises(ups.ParseError, match="not under column"):
        ups.assign_columns(price_row(2, ROW2, 210, xs=shifted)[1:], header)


def test_assign_columns_normalizes_money():
    header = ups.parse_header(header_line())
    prices = ups.assign_columns(price_row(1, ROW1, 198)[1:], header)
    assert prices[0] == "11.99" and prices[-1] == "56.96"


def test_parse_rate_page_fixture():
    table = ups.parse_rate_page(fixture_page(), page=91)
    assert table.page == 91
    assert set(table.rows) == {1, 2}
    assert table.rows[1][:7] == ["11.99", "12.38", "13.51", "14.10", "14.60", "14.83", "15.03"]
    assert table.rows[2][6] == "17.40"


def test_parse_rate_page_rejects_duplicate_weight():
    words = fixture_page() + price_row(2, ROW2, 222)
    with pytest.raises(ups.ParseError, match="appears twice"):
        ups.parse_rate_page(words, page=1)


def test_service_on_page_needs_heading_and_domestic_subheading():
    assert ups.service_on_page(["UPS® Ground*", "U.S. 48 – Domestic", "PACKAGE"]) == "ups_ground"
    assert ups.service_on_page(["Domestic", "UPS Next Day Air®", "Guaranteed"]) == "ups_next_day_air"
    assert ups.service_on_page(["UPS® Ground*", "Alaska – Domestic"]) is None
    assert ups.service_on_page(["UPS Next Day Air® Early", "U.S. 48 – Domestic"]) is None
    assert ups.service_on_page(["UPS 2nd Day Air A.M.®*", "U.S. 48 – Domestic"]) is None
    assert ups.service_on_page(["UPS 3 Day Select® from Canada", "Domestic"]) is None


def test_fuel_rows_parse_and_lower_median():
    text = ("Effective date ... Export Import Nov. 18, 2024-Nov. 24, 2024 16.00% 16.00% $0.452 per lb. 22.50% 26.25% "
            "Nov. 11, 2024-Nov. 17, 2024 16.00% 15.75% $0.448 per lb. 22.00% 25.75% "
            "Nov. 4, 2024-Nov. 10, 2024 16.25% 16.00% $0.452 per lb. 22.25% 26.00% previous fedex freight ...")
    rows = ups.parse_fuel_rows(text)
    assert [r.start.isoformat() for r in rows] == ["2024-11-18", "2024-11-11", "2024-11-04"]
    assert rows[0].percents == ["16.00%", "16.00%", "22.50%", "26.25%"]
    from decimal import Decimal
    assert ups.lower_median([Decimal("16.25"), Decimal("16.00"), Decimal("16.00"), Decimal("16.50")]) == Decimal("16.00")


def test_real_2026_ground_page_when_available():
    pdfplumber = pytest.importorskip("pdfplumber")
    try:
        path = raw_path(ups.rules.GUIDES[2026]["file"])
    except FileNotFoundError as error:
        pytest.skip(str(error))
    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
        page = pdf.pages[90]
        assert ups.service_on_page(page.extract_text().splitlines()) == "ups_ground"
        table = ups.parse_rate_page(page.extract_words(x_tolerance=1.5), page=91)
    zones, excluded = table.header.zone_columns(ups.SERVICES["ups_ground"][1])
    assert table.rows[1][0] == "11.99"
    assert excluded == ["44**", "45**", "46**"]
    assert min(table.rows) == 1 and max(table.rows) == 35

## UPS rate-table pipeline — report

**Files written** (all under ~/parcel-rates-issue-2):
- `data/pipeline/ups.py` — parser + table writers; `uv run python -m data.pipeline.ups` regenerates everything (~2.5 min, dominated by pdfplumber text extraction over the 216-page guides).
- `data/pipeline/ups_rules.py` — curated literals (quotes carry the amounts; numbers are extracted from the quote so a figure can never drift from its citation).
- `data/processed/ups/{base_rates,exceptions,surcharges,fuel_surcharge,announced_increase,dim_weight}.csv` — 9,800 / 25 / 199 / 8 / 4 / 4 rows.
- `data/tests/golden/ups_2023.csv … ups_2026.csv` — 25–26 cells each (5 per service: 70 lb z8, 70 lb z2, 1 lb z8, 20 lb z5 on page 1, 50 lb z4 on page 2; plus 2026 Ground z2 1 lb = 11.99, verified against `pdftotext -layout`, checked_by `agent 2026-10-23`).
- `data/tests/test_ups_parser.py` — 15 tests (line grouping, header/zone-code mapping incl. 3-digit air codes, AK/HI column exclusion, row tokenizing, column-count and x-alignment validation, synthetic page fixture, heading/subheading classification, fuel-row parsing, one real-page test on the 2026 guide).
- No manifest rows added; `docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md` regenerated by the shared report tool.

**Test result:** `832 passed, 2 warnings in 156.43s` (full suite; the 2 warnings are USPS's documented exceptions). No UPS invariant anomalies at all: all 20 (service, year) tables are complete 2–8 × 1–70 and monotonic. `test_invariants.py` emits no UPS warnings because AK/HI columns are excluded at parse time; their exclusion is documented in exceptions.csv.

**Parser approach:** pages are located by heading regex + subheading ("Domestic" / "U.S. 48 – Domestic"), which rejects Next Day Air Early, 2nd Day Air A.M., 3 Day Select from Canada, and the 2025+ Alaska/Hawaii-origin Ground tables (zones 9–11). Zone codes 102–108/132–138/202–208/302–308/2–8 map to zones 2–8; asterisked codes (124*/125*/126*, 224**…, 44**/45**/46**) are excluded. Each row must have exactly one price per header column, each within 18 pt of its column centre; weights must run 1..150 contiguously across the page set — any violation raises ParseError (no guessing). Quirks handled: the printed page number line above the table ("50 ups.com") and the 2023–24 vertical "DAILY RATES" margin label.

**Effective dates used:** 2023 → 2022-12-27; 2024 → 2024-07-01; 2025 → 2024-12-23; 2026 → 2026-09-07 (as printed in each guide).

**Exceptions documented (25):** 20 × `ak_hi_zone` (one per service/year; for Saver and 3 Day Select the note says the US48 table has no AK/HI columns); 5 × `other`: July-2024 revision stands in for the Dec-26-2023 edition; Sept-2026 revision stands in for the Dec-22-2025 edition; no all-customer peak residential surcharge in the Jan-2023 demand doc (volume-tiered only); no 2026 demand-surcharge document; 2025 peak rows cover only through 2025-01-18.

**Rule changes seen between years (all in surcharges.csv / RULE_CHANGES.md):**
- Residential: ground 5.25 → 5.65 → 6.10 → 6.50; air/3DS 5.85 → 6.20 → 6.55 → 7.00.
- Delivery Area: commercial 3.70 → 3.95 → 4.20 → 4.50; residential 5.30 ground/5.55 air → 5.70/5.85 → 6.15 → 6.55 (ground=air from 2025); commercial extended 4.50 → 4.90 → 5.35 → 5.70; residential extended 7.15 → 7.70 → 8.30 → 8.85.
- Additional Handling zone bands change in 2026 from (2 | 3-4 | 5+) to (2 | 3-4 | 5-6 | 7+). Zone-2 amounts: weight 29.00 → 34.50 → 43.50 → 46.50; length/width/L+G 18.50 → 22.00 → 28.00 → 30.00; packaging 16.50 → 19.50 → 25.00 → 26.75. Thresholds stable (>50 lb, >48 in, >30 in, L+G >105 in); 2026 adds a cubic-size criterion (>10,368 cu in, stored as `nonstandard_volume`, min_volume_cuft 6).
- Large Package (oversize, L+G >130 or length >96): commercial zone 2 135 → 160 → 205 → 219.50, residential 160 → 190 → 240 → 254.50; 2026 adds weight >110 lb and cubic >17,280 cu in criteria and the 4-band structure.
- Dimensional weight: divisor 139 all years; 2026 rounds each fractional dimension *up* ("1.1 will be considered 2"), earlier guides round to the nearest inch.
- Peak: AH 3.50 (Jan 2023, Jan–Sep 2024) → 7.75 / 9.95 in the 2024 season; LPS 40.00 → 84.75 / 99.00; 2024-25 season all-customer ground residential 0.25 / 0.50, all air packages 1.00 / 2.00 (stored as `peak_base`, applies_to air+3DS).
- Fuel proxies (FedEx lower-median of the snapshot window, is_proxy true): ground 18.00 / 16.25 / 20.50 / 26.25, express 19.25 / 16.00 / 19.25 / 28.75 for 2023–2026.
- Announced increase: 6.9 (2023), 5.9 (2024, 2025, 2026) — all secondary sources.

**Not sourced / limitations (stated plainly):**
- No UPS primary GRI document; all announced_increase rows are `secondary`.
- No 2026 demand surcharges, no 2025-26 peak season, no Dec-2023 or Dec-2025 guide editions on disk (documented as exceptions).
- UPS fuel history unavailable; rows are FedEx-derived proxies. The citation test requires the quoted row to contain `default_percent`, so default_percent is the (lower) median weekly value, with the mean stated in notes, as the brief suggested.
- The schema has no width threshold column: the AH width rule (>30 in) carries the threshold only in notes. Likewise there is no "residential variant" column, so DAS and Large Package commercial vs residential rows are separate rows distinguished by surcharge_id and notes; they share an exclusive_group, so an engine that ignores the residential flag would pick the higher (residential) amount for commercial parcels.
- The January 2023 demand PDF's text layer has no spaces; its quotes reproduce that (e.g. `AdditionalHandling3 $6.50perpackage $3.50perpackage`).
- fuel_applies is `true` everywhere on the strength of the guides' general statement that fuel may apply to surcharges; this is an assumption, stated in every row's notes.

**Shared tests / helpers:**
- `report_changes.py` keys `dim_weight` by `effective_from`, so every year prints as "rule removed / new rule" rather than a diff of the rounding text; and it keys surcharges without effective_from/to, so windowed rows (peak) with the same key collapse to one per year (dict overwrite) and the window amounts are not all reported. Worth adding effective_from to the surcharge key, or making dim_weight key on nothing.
- `common.pdf_page_text` reopens the PDF for every cited row; the citation tests take ~2 min for UPS alone. Caching the opened PDF per file would make the suite much faster.
- An earlier intermediate run showed one failure in `data/tests/test_fedex_parser.py` (another agent's in-progress file); it passes in the final run. `data/raw/manifest.csv` shows as modified in git but contains no UPS row changes from me.

- [ ] Next-year increase slider projecting the following year.

**Done when** both views render from the API, respond to controls and filters, and have component tests.

data/raw/fedex/2024:
# API contract

The FastAPI backend (`backend/`) serves JSON under `/api`. The frontend talks to
it only through these endpoints. Types below are the Pydantic models
(`backend/app/api/models.py`) and the TypeScript types
(`frontend/src/api/types.ts`), which must stay in sync; a contract test in each
side checks the example payloads in `docs/api-examples/`.

Money is a number in USD rounded to cents. Weights in pounds, lengths in inches,
distances in miles. Years are price-list labels (see `docs/data/SCHEMA.md`).

## Shared types

```ts
type Carrier = "usps" | "ups" | "fedex";
type Tier = "ground" | "two_three_day" | "next_day";
type DeliveryArea = "none" | "das" | "extended";
type UspsRateCard = "commercial" | "retail";

interface Parcel {
  weight_lb: number;            // > 0, <= 70
  length_in?: number;           // all three or none; > 0
  width_in?: number;
  height_in?: number;
  distance_miles: number;       // >= 0
  residential: boolean;
  speed: Tier;
  quantity?: number;            // default 1, integer >= 1
  price_charged?: number;       // overrides Controls.flat_price for this row
  delivery_area?: DeliveryArea; // default "none"
  nonstandard_packaging?: boolean; // default false
}

interface Controls {
  year: number;                 // default: latest year with all three carriers (2026)
  as_of?: string;               // ISO date; default the year's January effective date
  usps_rate_card: UspsRateCard; // default "commercial"
  fuel_override_percent?: { ground?: number; express?: number }; // replaces the yearly default
  peak: boolean;                // default false; when true, as_of moves into the year's peak window
  flat_price: number;           // what the shop charges per parcel; default 9.99
}

interface LineItem {
  kind: "base" | "surcharge" | "fuel";
  label: string;                // carrier's own name, e.g. "Residential Surcharge"
  amount: number;
  surcharge_id?: string;        // links to surcharges.csv
  source?: string;              // "file p.N" for display
}

interface Quote {
  carrier: Carrier;
  service_id: string;
  service_name: string;
  tier: Tier;
  zone: number;
  billable_weight_lb: number;
  dim_weight_lb: number | null;
  line_items: LineItem[];
  total: number;
  margin: number;               // price charged minus total
  available: boolean;           // false when the service cannot carry this parcel
  unavailable_reason?: string;  // e.g. "FedEx Ground serves business addresses only"
}
```

## Endpoints

### GET /api/meta
Years per carrier, services, default controls, fuel defaults per year, the
zone bands, and the data limitations text shown in the UI footer.

### GET /api/sample-parcels
The bundled illustrative parcel mix as `Parcel[]`, with a `description`.

### POST /api/quote  (question 1)
Request `{ parcel: Parcel, controls: Controls }`. Response
`{ quotes: Quote[], cheapest_by_tier: Record<Tier, {carrier, service_id, total}> }`,
quotes sorted by total within the requested tier first, then the other tiers.

### POST /api/breakeven  (question 2)
Request `{ controls: Controls, residential: boolean, weights_lb?: number[], distances_miles?: number[] }`
(defaults: weights 1..70 step 1, distances at every zone band midpoint).
Response: a grid of cells `{ weight_lb, distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, winner: {carrier, service_id, total}, runner_up: {...}, saving }`
for the ground tier, plus `breakeven_weight_lb` per distance band: the lightest
weight at which USPS stops winning against UPS and against FedEx.

### POST /api/blended  (question 3)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, segment?: SegmentFilter }`.
Response per carrier: parcels shipped, blended cost per parcel, base vs
surcharge vs fuel split (absolute and share), surcharge breakdown by kind,
margin per parcel, share of parcels shipped at a loss, and the cheapest
carrier per parcel (a "best mix" row). Each parcel uses the cheapest service
of that carrier in the parcel's speed tier.

### POST /api/yearly  (question 4)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, next_year_increase_percent?: number }`.
Response per carrier and year: blended cost per parcel under that year's
prices and rules, the year-over-year change, the carrier's announced average
increase for comparison, and the driver breakdown: for each parcel segment
(weight band, zone band, residential, speed), its contribution to the change
in dollars per parcel. Optional projected next year from the slider.

### Segments
`SegmentFilter = { weight_band?: string, zone_band?: string, residential?: boolean, speed?: Tier }`.
Weight bands: `≤1`, `1–5`, `5–10`, `10–20`, `20–70` lb. Zone bands: `1–2`, `3–4`, `5–6`, `7–8`.

## Engine rules the endpoints share

- **Zone** from `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv` per carrier: the band
  whose `min_miles <= distance <= max_miles`.
- **Billable weight** per carrier and `as_of` from `dim_weight.csv`: dimensions
  rounded per the row's rounding rule, dimensional weight = volume / divisor
  rounded up, only when volume exceeds `min_volume_cuin`; billable = max(actual
  rounded up to the next weight step, dimensional). USPS Ground Advantage keeps
  its ounce steps for parcels under 1 lb.
- **Base rate**: the first weight step `>= billable weight` in the zone, for
  the service, rate card (`list` for UPS and FedEx, the USPS control otherwise)
  and year.
- **Surcharges**: every rule of that carrier and year whose window contains
  `as_of`, whose `applies_to` covers the service, whose `address_type`
  matches, and whose thresholds the parcel meets; peak conditions only when
  `controls.peak`. Rules in the same `exclusive_group` do not stack: the
  highest amount wins. Percent surcharges apply to the base rate.
- **Fuel**: `percent x (base + surcharges flagged fuel_applies)`, percent from
  `fuel_surcharge.csv` for the year and service group (ground services use
  `ground`, all others `express`) unless overridden. USPS has none.
- **Availability**: FedEx Ground for business addresses only, Home Delivery for
  residential only (from `services.csv`); weight over 70 lb is rejected.
- **as_of**: defaults to the base-rate `effective_date` of the year for each
  carrier. With `peak: true` it is December 10 of the year, inside every
  carrier's peak window. `as_of` therefore also selects time-varying rules such
  as the USPS dimensional divisor (166 until 2026-07-11, 139 after) and the
  2026 USPS 8 % transportation increase.
- **Cheapest per tier**: among available services of the tier, lowest total.
- The engine never hardcodes an amount; every number comes from
  `data/processed/`.

## Errors
422 with `{ detail: [{ loc, msg }] }` for invalid input (Pydantic default),
with messages written for the shop owner, e.g. "weight_lb must be at most 70".
````

# Decisions

Running log of the choices made for this project, in the order they were made.
Each entry says what was decided, the alternatives considered, and why.
See `docs/ASSIGNMENT.md` for the brief and `docs/agent-log/` for the agent
conversations that led here.

## 2026-10-22 — Problem, user and scope

**Problem.** A small online shop sends a few hundred to a few thousand parcels
a month, has no negotiated carrier contract, and pays the published list
prices of FedEx, UPS and the Postal Service. Today the carrier is chosen by
habit. The dashboard helps the owner choose the carrier per kind of parcel,
and check whether the flat shipping price charged to customers still covers
the real cost once surcharges and yearly price increases are included.

**Questions the dashboard answers.**

1. For a given parcel (weight, dimensions, distance, residential or business,
   required speed), which service is cheapest once surcharges are included,
   and what are the line items of that price?
2. Where are the breakeven points between the Postal Service and FedEx or UPS
   ground, by weight and distance?
3. For the owner's whole set of parcels, what is the blended cost per parcel
   with each carrier, and how much of it is surcharges rather than base rate?
4. How did that blended cost change year by year under each year's published
   prices, compared with the average increase the carriers announced, and
   which kinds of parcels in the mix drove the change?

**Scope decisions.**

- Timebox: issues are sized to fit about five hours of focused work (the
  brief's upper bound). Extras are tracked separately and only started if
  time remains. Time actually spent is recorded by the owner, not estimated.
- Services: three speed tiers across the three carriers — ground, two to
  three day, and next day. Weight capped at 70 lb (the USPS maximum).
- Years covered: decided after the data survey (issue 1), based on what can
  actually be downloaded and parsed reliably.
- Parcel input: CSV upload plus a bundled illustrative sample mix. Columns:
  weight, length, width, height, distance in miles, residential flag,
  required speed, and an optional per-parcel price charged to the customer.
  Dimensional weight is computed from the dimensions.
- Price charged to the customer: a single flat price is the MVP control. The
  optional per-parcel column overrides it when present.
- Fuel and peak surcharges: a documented per-year default taken from the
  published history, a slider to stress test the fuel percentage, and a peak
  season toggle. A next-year increase slider sits on the year-over-year view.
- Zone from distance: a documented distance-band to zone mapping. Real
  ZIP-to-ZIP zones are a bonus, not MVP.
- The app never fetches live data; all rate tables are committed.

## 2026-10-22 — Stack

| Area | Decision | Alternatives considered | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend | FastAPI, Pydantic models, pandas over committed CSV tables loaded in memory, managed with `uv` | DuckDB; SQLite | Rate cards are a few thousand rows. No database keeps Docker and setup trivial. |
| Data collection | Python scripts under `data/` that download the carriers' published rate documents, parse them (pdfplumber for PDFs), and write normalized CSVs that are committed | Hand-typed tables | Reproducible, documents provenance, and qualifies for the scraping bonus. |
| Frontend | Vite + React + TypeScript, Recharts for line and bar charts, a custom SVG heatmap for the breakeven map, plain CSS with design tokens | Chart.js (needs a matrix plugin for heatmaps); Plotly (over 1 MB, poor on mobile); Tailwind | Small bundle, declarative, the heatmap is a trivial grid. |
| Docker | `docker compose` with two services: uvicorn backend and an nginx container serving the Vite build and proxying `/api` | Single multi-stage image with FastAPI serving static files | Clean separation, one command for the reviewer. |
| Tests | pytest for pipeline, rate engine and API; Vitest + Testing Library for components; Playwright end to end at 1440 and 375 px with screenshots reviewed for UX | — | Required by the brief and by us. |
| Workflow | Private GitHub repo, one issue per task, a branch and git worktree per issue, parallel agents each in their own worktree, pull requests merged with merge commits | Commit straight to main | Keeps history and lets agents work in parallel without stepping on each other. |
| Agent log | `SessionEnd` hook exports every session (and subagent) transcript to `docs/agent-log/<session-id>.md` and commits it; home directory path redacted | Manual export | Required by the brief, zero effort once set up. |

## 2026-10-22 — Year range and data policy (from the data survey, issue #1)

Full findings in `docs/data/QUALITY.md`; sources per file in `data/raw/<carrier>/SOURCES.md`.

- **Years: 2023 through 2026**, under each year's January list prices
  (USPS 2023 uses the July 2023 tables, when Ground Advantage launched).
  2022 is dropped from the MVP because USPS sold a different product set.
  FedEx 2027 rates are already published and are kept as an optional forward year.
- **Base rates are parsed** from USPS CSV zips, FedEx XLSX (2022, 2025–2027)
  and text PDFs (FedEx 2023–2024, UPS all years), each validated against
  hand-checked prices.
- **Surcharge rules are curated** into a CSV with a source file and page per
  row, rather than parsed from prose PDFs.
- **Fuel surcharge:** per-year default from FedEx's published history,
  applied to UPS as a proxy and flagged; the UI slider overrides it. USPS has none.
- **Announced increases:** FedEx and USPS from primary sources; UPS from
  trade press, marked secondary.
- **Raw files:** only spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML snapshots are
  committed (about 8 MB). All PDFs are gitignored and restored by
  `data/fetch_raw.py` from `data/raw/manifest.csv` (URL, SHA-256, size),
  fetched one at a time with a pause between requests.
- **Citations:** every curated row carries file, page and verbatim quote,
  and a test checks the quote against the document.
- **USPS dimensional weight** verified in the DMM: divisor 166, then 139 from
  2026-07-12, above 1,728 cubic inches, all zones.
- **Schema** for all processed tables and the parcel CSV is fixed in
  `docs/data/SCHEMA.md` before any parser is written.

cd ~/parcel-rates-issue-4/frontend && cat > src/api/types.ts <<'EOF'
/**
 * Types mirroring docs/API.md. Keep in sync with backend/app/api/models.py.
 *
 * Shared types and request bodies are copied verbatim from the contract.
 * Response shapes for /meta, /sample-parcels, /breakeven, /blended and /yearly
 * are described only in prose in docs/API.md; the shapes below are the
 * frontend's reading of that prose. Fields marked "CONTRACT GAP" are the
 * places the contract should pin down (see the issue #4 report).
 */

export type Carrier = "usps" | "ups" | "fedex";
export type Tier = "ground" | "two_three_day" | "next_day";
export type DeliveryArea = "none" | "das" | "extended";
export type UspsRateCard = "commercial" | "retail";
export type FuelGroup = "ground" | "express";

export const CARRIERS: readonly Carrier[] = ["usps", "ups", "fedex"] as const;
export const TIERS: readonly Tier[] = ["ground", "two_three_day", "next_day"] as const;
export const DELIVERY_AREAS: readonly DeliveryArea[] = ["none", "das", "extended"] as const;

export interface Parcel {
  weight_lb: number; // > 0, <= 70
  length_in?: number; // all three or none; > 0
  width_in?: number;
  height_in?: number;
  distance_miles: number; // >= 0
  residential: boolean;
  speed: Tier;
  quantity?: number; // default 1, integer >= 1
  price_charged?: number; // overrides Controls.flat_price for this row
  delivery_area?: DeliveryArea; // default "none"
  nonstandard_packaging?: boolean; // default false
}

export interface Controls {
  year: number;
  as_of?: string; // ISO date
  usps_rate_card: UspsRateCard;
  fuel_override_percent?: { ground?: number; express?: number };
  peak: boolean;
  flat_price: number;
}

export interface LineItem {
  kind: "base" | "surcharge" | "fuel";
  label: string;
  amount: number;
  surcharge_id?: string;
  source?: string;
}

export interface Quote {
  carrier: Carrier;
  service_id: string;
  service_name: string;
  tier: Tier;
  zone: number;
  billable_weight_lb: number;
  dim_weight_lb: number | null;
  line_items: LineItem[];
  total: number;
  margin: number;
  available: boolean;
  unavailable_reason?: string;
}

/* ---------- GET /api/meta ---------- */

export interface ServiceInfo {
  carrier: Carrier;
  service_id: string;
  display_name: string;
  tier: Tier;
  residential_allowed: boolean;
  business_allowed: boolean;
}

/** One row of fuel_surcharge.csv. USPS has none. */
export interface FuelDefault {
  carrier: Carrier;
  year: number;
  service_group: FuelGroup;
  default_percent: number;
  is_proxy: boolean; // UPS uses FedEx history as a proxy
}

export interface ZoneBand {
  carrier: Carrier;
  zone: number;
  min_miles: number;
  max_miles: number | null; // null = open-ended (zone 8)
}

export interface Meta {
  /** Years with base rates, per carrier (UPS has no 2027). */
  years: Record<Carrier, number[]>;
  services: ServiceInfo[];
  default_controls: Controls;
  fuel_defaults: FuelDefault[];
  zone_bands: ZoneBand[];
  /** Paragraphs shown in the footer. CONTRACT GAP: string vs string[]. */
  limitations: string[];
}

/* ---------- GET /api/sample-parcels ---------- */

/** CONTRACT GAP: the contract says "Parcel[] with a description"; an array cannot carry one. */
export interface SampleParcels {
  description: string;
  parcels: Parcel[];
}

/* ---------- POST /api/quote ---------- */

export interface QuoteRequest {
  parcel: Parcel;
  controls: Controls;
}

export interface CarrierPick {
  carrier: Carrier;
  service_id: string;
  total: number;
}

export interface QuoteResponse {
  quotes: Quote[];
  /** CONTRACT GAP: a tier with no available service; modelled as null. */
  cheapest_by_tier: Record<Tier, CarrierPick | null>;
}

/* ---------- POST /api/breakeven ---------- */

export interface BreakevenRequest {
  controls: Controls;
  residential: boolean;
  weights_lb?: number[];
  distances_miles?: number[];
}

export interface BreakevenCell {
  weight_lb: number;
  distance_miles: number;
  zone_usps: number;
  zone_private: number;
  winner: CarrierPick;
  runner_up: CarrierPick;
  saving: number;
}

export interface BreakevenLine {
  distance_miles: number;
  /** Lightest weight at which USPS stops winning; null if it never does. */
  vs_ups_lb: number | null;
  vs_fedex_lb: number | null;
}

export interface BreakevenResponse {
  cells: BreakevenCell[];
  breakeven_weight_lb: BreakevenLine[];
}

/* ---------- POST /api/blended ---------- */

export type WeightBand = "≤1" | "1–5" | "5–10" | "10–20" | "20–70";
export type ZoneBandLabel = "1–2" | "3–4" | "5–6" | "7–8";
export const WEIGHT_BANDS: readonly WeightBand[] = ["≤1", "1–5", "5–10", "10–20", "20–70"] as const;
export const ZONE_BANDS: readonly ZoneBandLabel[] = ["1–2", "3–4", "5–6", "7–8"] as const;

export interface SegmentFilter {
  weight_band?: WeightBand;
  zone_band?: ZoneBandLabel;
  residential?: boolean;
  speed?: Tier;
}

export interface BlendedRequest {
  parcels: Parcel[];
  controls: Controls;
  segment?: SegmentFilter;
}

export interface CostSplit {
  base: number;
  surcharges: number;
  fuel: number;
}

export interface SurchargeShare {
  label: string;
  surcharge_id?: string;
  amount_per_parcel: number;
  share: number; // 0..1 of the blended cost
}

export interface BlendedCarrier {
  carrier: Carrier | "best_mix";
  parcels_shipped: number; // sum of quantity
  /** CONTRACT GAP: parcels the carrier cannot carry in the tier, excluded from the average. */
  parcels_unavailable: number;
  cost_per_parcel: number;
  split_per_parcel: CostSplit;
  split_share: CostSplit; // 0..1
  surcharge_breakdown: SurchargeShare[];
  margin_per_parcel: number;
  loss_share: number; // 0..1 of parcels shipped at a loss
}

export interface BlendedResponse {
  carriers: BlendedCarrier[]; // usps, ups, fedex, best_mix
  /** best_mix only: how many parcels each carrier takes. */
  best_mix_counts?: Partial<Record<Carrier, number>>;
}

/* ---------- POST /api/yearly ---------- */

export interface YearlyRequest {
  parcels: Parcel[];
  controls: Controls;
  next_year_increase_percent?: number;
}

export interface YearPoint {
  year: number;
  cost_per_parcel: number | null; // null when the carrier has no prices that year
  change_percent: number | null;
  /** CONTRACT GAP: USPS announces per service; the backend should collapse to one number. */
  announced_increase_percent: number | null;
  announced_source: "primary" | "secondary" | null;
  projected?: boolean;
}

export interface YearlyCarrier {
  carrier: Carrier;
  points: YearPoint[];
}

export interface DriverContribution {
  dimension: "weight_band" | "zone_band" | "residential" | "speed";
  band: string;
  contribution_per_parcel: number;
}

export interface YearlyDriver {
  carrier: Carrier;
  from_year: number;
  to_year: number;
  contributions: DriverContribution[];
}

export interface YearlyResponse {
  carriers: YearlyCarrier[];
  drivers: YearlyDriver[];
}

/* ---------- Errors ---------- */

export interface ValidationIssue {
  loc: (string | number)[];
  msg: string;
  type?: string;
}

export interface ValidationErrorBody {
  /** Pydantic default is an array; FastAPI HTTPException gives a string. */
  detail: ValidationIssue[] | string;
}

import type {
  BlendedRequest,
  BlendedResponse,
  BreakevenRequest,
  BreakevenResponse,
  Meta,
  QuoteRequest,
  QuoteResponse,
  SampleParcels,
  ValidationErrorBody,
  ValidationIssue,
  YearlyRequest,
  YearlyResponse,
} from "./types";

export const API_BASE = "/api";

/** A readable problem with one input field, for display to the shop owner. */
export interface FieldProblem {
  field: string;
  message: string;
}

export class ApiError extends Error {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly problems: FieldProblem[];

  constructor(status: number, message: string, problems: FieldProblem[] = []) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ApiError";
    this.status = status;
    this.problems = problems;
  }
}

/** Turn a Pydantic `loc` like ["body","parcels",3,"weight_lb"] into "parcels row 4 · weight_lb". */
export function describeLoc(loc: readonly (string | number)[]): string {
  const parts = loc[0] === "body" || loc[0] === "query" ? loc.slice(1) : loc;
  return parts
    .map((p) => (typeof p === "number" ? `row ${p + 1}` : p))
    .join(" · ");
}

function isIssue(x: unknown): x is ValidationIssue {
  return (
    typeof x === "object" &&
    x !== null &&
    Array.isArray((x as ValidationIssue).loc) &&
    typeof (x as ValidationIssue).msg === "string"
  );
}

export function problemsFromBody(body: unknown): FieldProblem[] {
  if (typeof body !== "object" || body === null || !("detail" in body)) return [];
  const detail = (body as ValidationErrorBody).detail;
  if (typeof detail === "string") return [{ field: "", message: detail }];
  if (!Array.isArray(detail)) return [];
  return detail.filter(isIssue).map((d) => ({ field: describeLoc(d.loc), message: d.msg }));
}

async function readJson(res: Response): Promise<unknown> {
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!text) return null;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function statusMessage(status: number): string {
  if (status === 422) return "Some inputs were not accepted.";
  if (status === 404) return "The rate service does not know this request.";
  if (status >= 500) return "The rate service had a problem. Try again in a moment.";
  return `The rate service answered with status ${status}.`;
}

export interface ApiClient {
  meta(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Meta>;
  sampleParcels(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SampleParcels>;
  quote(body: QuoteRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<QuoteResponse>;
  breakeven(body: BreakevenRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<BreakevenResponse>;
  blended(body: BlendedRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<BlendedResponse>;
  yearly(body: YearlyRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<YearlyResponse>;
}

export interface ClientOptions {
  baseUrl?: string;
  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
}

export function createHttpClient({ baseUrl = API_BASE, fetchImpl }: ClientOptions = {}): ApiClient {
  const doFetch = fetchImpl ?? ((input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => fetch(input, init));

  async function request<T>(path: string, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
    let res: Response;
    try {
      res = await doFetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, {
        ...init,
        headers: { Accept: "application/json", ...(init.body ? { "Content-Type": "application/json" } : {}) },
      });
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === "AbortError") throw err;
      throw new ApiError(0, "Cannot reach the rate service. Is the backend running?");
    }
    const body = await readJson(res);
    if (!res.ok) {
      const problems = problemsFromBody(body);
      throw new ApiError(res.status, statusMessage(res.status), problems);
    }
    if (body === null) throw new ApiError(res.status, "The rate service sent an empty answer.");
    return body as T;
  }

  const post = <T>(path: string, body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal) =>
    request<T>(path, { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body), signal });

  return {
    meta: (signal) => request<Meta>("/meta", { signal }),
    sampleParcels: (signal) => request<SampleParcels>("/sample-parcels", { signal }),
    quote: (body, signal) => post<QuoteResponse>("/quote", body, signal),
    breakeven: (body, signal) => post<BreakevenResponse>("/breakeven", body, signal),
    blended: (body, signal) => post<BlendedResponse>("/blended", body, signal),
    yearly: (body, signal) => post<YearlyResponse>("/yearly", body, signal),
  };
}

/** `?mock=1` serves typed mock responses; the mock module is a separate lazy chunk. */
export function isMockMode(search: string = typeof window === "undefined" ? "" : window.location.search): boolean {
  return new URLSearchParams(search).get("mock") === "1";
}

export function createMockClient(delayMs = 350): ApiClient {
  const load = () => import("./mocks");
  const wait = <T>(fn: () => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T> =>
    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      setTimeout(() => {
        Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(resolve, reject);
      }, delayMs);
    });
  return {
    meta: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockMeta),
    sampleParcels: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockSampleParcels),
    quote: (body) => wait(async () => (await load()).mockQuote(body)),
    breakeven: (body) => wait(async () => (await load()).mockBreakeven(body)),
    blended: (body) => wait(async () => (await load()).mockBlended(body)),
    yearly: (body) => wait(async () => (await load()).mockYearly(body)),
  };
}

export function createClient(): ApiClient {
  return isMockMode() ? createMockClient() : createHttpClient();
}
