# API contract

The FastAPI backend (`backend/`) serves JSON under `/api`. The frontend talks to
it only through these endpoints. Types below are the Pydantic models
(`backend/app/api/models.py`) and the TypeScript types
(`frontend/src/api/types.ts`), which must stay in sync; a contract test in each
side checks the example payloads in `docs/api-examples/`.

Money is a number in USD rounded to cents. Weights in pounds, lengths in inches,
distances in miles. Years are price-list labels (see `docs/data/SCHEMA.md`).

## Shared types

```ts
type Carrier = "usps" | "ups" | "fedex";
type Tier = "ground" | "two_three_day" | "next_day";
type DeliveryArea = "none" | "das" | "extended";
type UspsRateCard = "commercial" | "retail";

interface Parcel {
  weight_lb: number;            // > 0, <= 70
  length_in?: number;           // all three or none; > 0
  width_in?: number;
  height_in?: number;
  distance_miles: number;       // >= 0
  residential: boolean;
  speed: Tier;
  quantity?: number;            // default 1, integer >= 1
  price_charged?: number;       // overrides Controls.flat_price for this row
  delivery_area?: DeliveryArea; // default "none"
  nonstandard_packaging?: boolean; // default false
}

interface Controls {
  year?: number;                // omitted or null: latest year with all three carriers (2026);
                                // a year no carrier publishes is a 422
  as_of?: string;               // ISO date; default the year's January effective date
  usps_rate_card: UspsRateCard; // default "commercial"
  fuel_override_percent?: { ground?: number; express?: number }; // replaces the yearly default
  peak: boolean;                // default false; when true, as_of moves into the year's peak window
  flat_price: number;           // what the shop charges per parcel; default 9.99
}

interface LineItem {
  kind: "base" | "surcharge" | "fuel";
  label: string;                // carrier's own name, e.g. "Residential Surcharge"
  amount: number;
  surcharge_id?: string;        // links to surcharges.csv
  source?: string;              // "file p.N" for display
  condition?: string;           // surcharges.csv condition, for grouping surcharges by kind
}

interface Quote {
  carrier: Carrier;
  service_id: string;
  service_name: string;
  tier: Tier;
  zone: number;
  billable_weight_lb: number;
  dim_weight_lb: number | null;
  line_items: LineItem[];
  total: number;
  margin: number;               // price charged minus total
  available: boolean;           // false when the service cannot carry this parcel
  unavailable_reason?: string;  // e.g. "FedEx Ground serves business addresses only"
  as_of: string | null;         // ISO date the rules were resolved for
}
// An unavailable quote has line_items: [] and total: 0, margin: 0; zone and
// weights are null when they were not reached. Clients must check `available`.
```

## Endpoints

### GET /api/health
`{"status": "ok"}` for the Docker health check.

### GET /api/meta
Years per carrier, services (with `rate_card_notes`), default controls
(including the default `as_of` per carrier), fuel defaults per year with
`is_proxy`, the zone bands, the segment band labels, and the data limitations
text shown in the UI footer. Shape: `MetaResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`.

### GET /api/sample-parcels
The bundled illustrative parcel mix as `Parcel[]`, with a `description`.

### POST /api/quote  (question 1)
Request `{ parcel: Parcel, controls: Controls }`. Response
`{ quotes: Quote[], cheapest_by_tier: Record<Tier, {carrier, service_id, total}> }`,
quotes sorted by total within the requested tier first, then the other tiers
(unavailable quotes last within a tier). Only carriers that publish the
requested year are quoted (2027 is FedEx only). A tier with no available
service maps to `null` in `cheapest_by_tier`.

### POST /api/breakeven  (question 2)
Request `{ controls: Controls, residential: boolean, weights_lb?: number[], distances_miles?: number[] }`
(defaults: weights 1..70 step 1, distances at every zone band midpoint).
Response: a grid of cells `{ weight_lb, distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, winner: {carrier, service_id, total}, runner_up: {...}, saving, totals: Record<Carrier, number> }`
for the ground tier (FedEx Ground for business, Home Delivery for residential),
plus `breakeven_weight_lb: [{ distance_miles, zone_usps, zone_private, vs_ups, vs_fedex }]`
per distance band: the lightest grid weight at which the USPS total is >= the
rival's total, `null` when USPS wins at every weight. The default distances are
each USPS band's midpoint (rounded down) and, for the open last band, the
previous band's upper edge + 200 miles.

### GET /api/breakeven
Same response with the default grid; query parameters `residential`
(default true), `year`, `peak`, `usps_rate_card`.

### POST /api/blended  (question 3)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, segment?: SegmentFilter }`.
Response per carrier: parcels shipped, blended cost per parcel, base vs
surcharge vs fuel split (absolute and share), surcharge breakdown by kind,
margin per parcel, share of parcels shipped at a loss, and the cheapest
carrier per parcel (a "best mix" row). Each parcel uses the cheapest service
of that carrier in the parcel's speed tier.

Shape: `BlendedResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`: `year`,
`parcels_considered`, `revenue_per_parcel`, `carriers[]` and `best_mix`. Each
carrier row (and `best_mix`) is a `Summary`: `parcels_shipped`,
`parcels_unavailable` (quantity no service of the carrier could carry),
`total_cost`, `cost_per_parcel`, `split.{base,surcharges,fuel}.{per_parcel,total,share}`,
`surcharges_by_condition[] {condition, total, per_parcel, share_of_cost}`,
`margin_per_parcel`, `total_margin`, `loss_share`, `parcels_at_loss`; carrier
rows add `carrier` and `services_used` (service_id -> parcels), `best_mix`
adds `parcels_by_carrier`. Everything is weighted by `quantity`.

### POST /api/yearly  (question 4)
Request `{ parcels: Parcel[], controls: Controls, next_year_increase_percent?: number }`.
Response per carrier and year: blended cost per parcel under that year's
prices and rules, the year-over-year change, the carrier's announced average
increase for comparison, and the driver breakdown: for each parcel segment
(weight band, zone band, residential, speed), its contribution to the change
in dollars per parcel. Optional projected next year from the slider.

Rules: each year is priced at its own base-rate effective date per carrier
(December 10 of that year when `peak`); `controls.as_of` and `controls.year`
are ignored. `fuel_override_percent` applies to every year. Only parcels the
carrier can ship in every one of its years are compared (`parcels_used`,
`parcels_excluded`). Years a carrier lacks are absent.

Shape: `YearlyResponse` in `backend/app/api/models.py`: `carriers[] {carrier,
parcels_used, parcels_excluded, years[], projected}`; `projected` is
`{year, increase_percent, cost_per_parcel}` or `null`. Each year row:
`year`, `as_of`, `cost_per_parcel`, `summary` (the blended `Summary`),
`services_used`, `change_vs_previous {from_year, dollars_per_parcel, percent}`
(null for the first year), `announced_increase {percent, basis, services,
source_type}` where `basis` is `"all"` (the carrier-wide row), 
`"average_of_services"` (plain average of the rows for the services used,
listed in `services`) or `"none"`, `drivers` (per dimension a list of
`{segment, parcels, change_per_parcel, change_total}`; the rounded
`change_per_parcel` values add up exactly to the rounded change), `fuel`
(`{ground, express}` each `{default_percent, is_proxy, applied_percent}`, null
for USPS) and `warnings` (e.g. a surcharge kind present the year before but
with no rules recorded this year).

### Segments
`SegmentFilter = { weight_band?: string, zone_band?: string, residential?: boolean, speed?: Tier }`.
Weight bands: `≤1`, `1–5`, `5–10`, `10–20`, `20–70` lb. Zone bands: `1–2`, `3–4`, `5–6`, `7–8`.

## Engine rules the endpoints share

- **Zone** from `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv` per carrier: the band
  whose `min_miles <= distance <= max_miles`.
- **Billable weight** per carrier and `as_of` from `dim_weight.csv`: dimensions
  rounded per the row's rounding rule, dimensional weight = volume / divisor
  rounded up, only when volume exceeds `min_volume_cuin`; billable = max(actual
  rounded up to the next weight step, dimensional). The row is the one whose
  window contains `as_of`. Weight steps are the service's own table steps, so
  USPS Ground Advantage keeps its ounce steps under 1 lb (and the USPS commercial
  Priority Mail cards their 0.5 lb step). A billable weight above the heaviest
  step makes the service unavailable; USPS caps dimensional weight at 70 lb
  as its dim_weight row states.
- **Base rate**: the first weight step `>= billable weight` in the zone, for
  the service, rate card (`list` for UPS and FedEx, the USPS control otherwise)
  and year.
- **Surcharges**: every rule of that carrier and year whose window contains
  `as_of`, whose `applies_to` covers the service, whose `address_type`
  matches, and whose thresholds the parcel meets; peak conditions only when
  `controls.peak`. Rules in the same `exclusive_group` do not stack: the
  highest amount wins. Percent surcharges apply to the base rate.
- **Fuel**: `percent x (base + surcharges flagged fuel_applies)`, percent from
  `fuel_surcharge.csv` for the year and service group (ground services use
  `ground`, all others `express`) unless overridden. USPS has none.
- **Availability**: FedEx Ground for business addresses only, Home Delivery for
  residential only (from `services.csv`); weight over 70 lb is rejected.
- **as_of**: defaults to the base-rate `effective_date` of the year for each
  carrier, or `controls.as_of` when given. With `peak: true` it is December 10
  of the year (overriding `controls.as_of`), inside every carrier's peak window
  for which peak rows are recorded. `as_of` therefore also selects time-varying rules such
  as the USPS dimensional divisor (166 until 2026-07-11, 139 after) and the
  2026 USPS 8 % transportation increase.
- **Cheapest per tier**: among available services of the tier, lowest total.
- **Thresholds, windows and peak add-ons**: see "Matching rules" in
  `docs/data/SCHEMA.md` (bands inclusive on billable weight, a lone minimum weight
  strict on actual weight, dimensions strict, `effective_to` inclusive, peak
  add-ons only on top of the charge they add to).
- The engine never hardcodes an amount; every number comes from
  `data/processed/`.

## Errors
422 with `{ detail: [{ loc, msg }] }` for invalid input (Pydantic default),
with messages written for the shop owner, e.g. "weight_lb must be at most 70";
each entry also carries the Pydantic error `type`. Errors inside a parcel list
are prefixed "Parcel N: ". Real request/response pairs for every endpoint are
in `docs/api-examples/`, regenerated by `backend/scripts/export_api_examples.py`.
"""Pydantic models for the API contract (docs/API.md).

These mirror frontend/src/api/types.ts. Field constraints double as the 422
messages a shop owner sees (see app/api/errors.py).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import date
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator

Carrier = Literal["usps", "ups", "fedex"]
Tier = Literal["ground", "two_three_day", "next_day"]
DeliveryArea = Literal["none", "das", "extended"]
UspsRateCard = Literal["commercial", "retail"]
WeightBand = Literal["≤1", "1–5", "5–10", "10–20", "20–70"]
ZoneBand = Literal["1–2", "3–4", "5–6", "7–8"]

MAX_WEIGHT_LB = 70  # app cap from docs/API.md (USPS maximum); not a price
MAX_PARCELS = 10_000


# ---- requests -------------------------------------------------------------
class Parcel(BaseModel):
    weight_lb: float = Field(gt=0, le=MAX_WEIGHT_LB)
    length_in: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)
    width_in: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)
    height_in: float | None = Field(default=None, gt=0)
    distance_miles: float = Field(ge=0)
    residential: bool
    speed: Tier
    quantity: int = Field(default=1, ge=1)
    price_charged: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0)
    delivery_area: DeliveryArea = "none"
    nonstandard_packaging: bool = False

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _all_or_no_dimensions(self) -> "Parcel":
        given = [v is not None for v in (self.length_in, self.width_in, self.height_in)]
        if any(given) and not all(given):
            raise ValueError("give length_in, width_in and height_in together, or none of them")
        return self


class FuelOverride(BaseModel):
    ground: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=100)
    express: float | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=100)


class Controls(BaseModel):
    year: int | None = Field(default=None, description="default: latest year with all three carriers")
    as_of: date | None = None
    usps_rate_card: UspsRateCard = "commercial"
    fuel_override_percent: FuelOverride | None = None
    peak: bool = False
    flat_price: float = Field(default=9.99, ge=0)


class SegmentFilter(BaseModel):
    weight_band: WeightBand | None = None
    zone_band: ZoneBand | None = None
    residential: bool | None = None
    speed: Tier | None = None


class QuoteRequest(BaseModel):
    parcel: Parcel
    controls: Controls = Field(default_factory=Controls)


class BreakevenRequest(BaseModel):
    controls: Controls = Field(default_factory=Controls)
    residential: bool = True
    weights_lb: list[float] | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=200)
    distances_miles: list[float] | None = Field(default=None, min_length=1, max_length=50)

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def _grid_in_range(self) -> "BreakevenRequest":
        for w in self.weights_lb or []:
            if not 0 < w <= MAX_WEIGHT_LB:
                raise ValueError(f"every weight in weights_lb must be above 0 and at most {MAX_WEIGHT_LB}")
        for d in self.distances_miles or []:
            if d < 0:
                raise ValueError("distances_miles cannot be negative")
        return self

# Visual direction: the shipping ledger

The dashboard reads like a printed price sheet or a merchant's ledger, not like
a SaaS dashboard. Warm paper, black ink, hairline rules, figures set in a
newspaper serif, and colour reserved for meaning.

## Why it fits

The user is a shop owner deciding where a few dollars per parcel go. The
decision lives in a handful of numbers: which carrier is cheapest, what one
parcel costs, whether the flat price still leaves a margin. A ledger puts those
numbers first, in the largest type on the page, and pushes everything else
(assumptions, sliders, provenance) into small, quiet type around them. Rules
and columns instead of cards make it feel like an account the owner keeps, and
they print well for an accountant.

## Hierarchy

1. **The answer** (cheapest carrier, cost per parcel, margin): display serif,
   `--text-figure`, tabular figures, carrier or money colour.
2. **The question** each section answers: display serif, `--text-xl`.
3. **The owner's parcel set**: once loaded, a one-line strip (count, share to
   homes, speed split) with the full summary behind "Details", so the
   questions and the answer stay above the fold, also on a phone.

### Rule for every question view (issues #5 and #6)

The answer is the largest element of its section. Put it first under the
question, in `.answer > .answer__figure` (`--text-figure`), with a short
`.answer__caption` saying what it is ("UPS Ground, $8.41 per parcel, $1.58
margin"). Nothing else in the section, including the question (`--text-xl`),
chart titles and table figures, may be set larger. Charts and tables come
after the answer and explain it.
4. **Assumptions** (year, rate card, fuel, peak, flat price): a left rail in the
   UI face at `--text-sm`, always visible on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones
   behind a one-line summary bar.

## Palette (`src/styles/tokens.css`)

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--paper` | `#F5F1E8` | `#15140F` | page |
| `--sheet` | `#FBF9F4` | `#1E1C17` | rail, inputs, raised panels |
| `--ink` | `#1C1B18` | `#EDE8DC` | text, rules, focus ring |
| `--ink-muted` | `#5E5A50` | `#A9A292` | secondary text (6.1:1 / 7.3:1) |
| `--carrier-usps` | `#1F4E9A` | `#7FA8EE` | USPS everywhere (7.1:1 / 7.7:1) |
| `--carrier-ups` | `#7A4E0F` | `#D9A35A` | UPS everywhere (6.4:1 / 8.2:1) |
| `--carrier-fedex` | `#9C2A7E` | `#E68AC9` | FedEx everywhere (6.1:1 / 7.8:1) |
| `--loss` | `#B3261E` | `#F2877E` | negative margin (5.8:1 / 7.5:1) |
| `--profit` | `#1D6B3F` | `#6FCB94` | positive margin (5.8:1 / 9.4:1) |
| `--mock` | `#8A5A00` | `#E8B860` | the mock-data banner only |

Contrast ratios are against `--paper` and meet WCAG AA for body text in both
themes. Carrier hues follow the brands loosely (postal blue, brown, purple)
so the owner recognises them without a legend. Blue and purple are close for
some colour-vision deficiencies, so colour is never the only cue: every
carrier mark carries its name or initial, and money always carries a sign and
the word "loss" or "margin".

Each carrier also has a `-wash` tint for backgrounds and heatmap cells
(issue #5 scales intensity between the wash and the full colour).

## Type

- **Newsreader** (display serif, optical sizes) for questions and figures.
  A newspaper face gives the editorial voice and has good tabular numerals.
- **IBM Plex Sans** for the interface: labels, controls, tables. Industrial,
  slightly technical, legible at 12-14 px.

Both load from Google Fonts with `display=swap`; fallbacks are Georgia and
Helvetica/Arial. All figures use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so
columns of prices line up.

## Spacing and shape

A 4 px base (`--space-1` … `--space-8`: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 72 px) with a
deliberate jump to 48-72 px between sections, so sections read as chapters.
Corners are nearly square (`--radius: 2px`). Separation comes from hairline
rules (`--rule`) and one heavy rule under the masthead and active tab, not
from shadows; the only shadow is on the mobile controls sheet, which really
does sit above the page.

## Motion

Only opacity and transform, 120-220 ms, for the sheet and tab underline. All
of it is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

## Charts (for issues #5 and #6)

- Use the carrier tokens for series and cells; read them in JS with
  `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--carrier-usps")`
  or the `carrierColor()` helper in `src/lib/carriers.ts`, so dark mode works.
- Axis text in `--ink-muted`, gridlines in `--rule`, no chart borders.
- Announced increases and projections are dashed lines in the carrier colour.
# Frontend

Vite + React + TypeScript dashboard. Design direction and rules: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Run locally

Node 18.18+ (Docker uses Node 22).

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev            # http://localhost:5173
```

The dev server proxies `/api` to the backend at `VITE_API_TARGET`, default
`http://localhost:8001` (port 8000 is used by another app on the dev machine).
Start the backend on that port from the repository root:

```sh
cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8001
```

To point at a backend elsewhere: `VITE_API_TARGET=http://localhost:9000 npm run dev`
(or put the variable in `frontend/.env.local`).

Without a backend, open `http://localhost:5173/?mock=1`: the app serves the backend's
recorded example responses from `src/api/__fixtures__/` and shows a "Mock data" banner.
Mock answers do not change with the inputs.

## Scripts

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | dev server with the `/api` proxy |
| `npm run test` | Vitest + Testing Library, including the API contract test |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc -b --noEmit` |
| `npm run build` | type-check and build into `dist/` |

## API contract

`src/api/types.ts` mirrors `docs/API.md` and `backend/app/api/models.py`.
`src/api/contract.test.ts` checks every example payload in `src/api/__fixtures__/`
(copied from `docs/api-examples/`) against the runtime guards in `src/api/guards.ts`, so
a change on either side fails the tests until both agree.

import { useId, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { useApi, useLoad } from "./api/ApiContext";
import { isMockMode } from "./api/client";
import { ControlRail, assumptionsLine } from "./components/controls/ControlRail";
import { ParcelSetPanel } from "./components/parcels/ParcelSetPanel";
import { QuestionTabs } from "./components/QuestionTabs";
import { Footer } from "./components/Footer";
import { useParcelSet } from "./hooks/useParcelSet";
import { useUrlState } from "./hooks/useUrlState";
import { useMediaQuery } from "./hooks/useMediaQuery";
import { INERT_WHILE_SHEET, SHEET_QUERY, useSheet } from "./hooks/useSheet";
import { controlsFromMeta, type ViewId } from "./state/urlState";
import type { ViewProps } from "./views/types";
import { QuoteView } from "./views/QuoteView";
import { BreakevenView } from "./views/BreakevenView";
import { BlendedView } from "./views/BlendedView";
import { YearlyView } from "./views/YearlyView";

const VIEW_COMPONENTS: Record<ViewId, (p: ViewProps) => JSX.Element> = {
  quote: QuoteView,
  breakeven: BreakevenView,
  blended: BlendedView,
  yearly: YearlyView,
};


export function App() {
  const api = useApi();
  const [metaAttempt, setMetaAttempt] = useState(0);
  const metaState = useLoad((signal) => api.meta(signal), [api, metaAttempt]);
  const meta = metaState.status === "ok" ? metaState.data : null;
  const metaDefaults = useMemo(() => (meta ? controlsFromMeta(meta.defaults) : null), [meta]);
  const [state, dispatch] = useUrlState(metaDefaults);
  const parcelSet = useParcelSet();
  const isSheet = useMediaQuery(SHEET_QUERY);
  const sheet = useSheet(isSheet);
  const railId = useId();
  const railTitleId = useId();
  const inert = { [INERT_WHILE_SHEET]: "" };
  const mock = isMockMode();

  const viewProps: ViewProps = { controls: state.controls, meta, parcels: parcelSet.set?.parcels ?? null };

  return (
    <>
      <a className="skip-link" href="#main" {...inert}>
        Skip to the questions
      </a>
      {mock && (
        <p className="mock-banner" role="note" {...inert}>
          <strong>Mock data.</strong> Recorded example answers from the rate service; they do not change with your inputs.
        </p>
      )}
      <header className="masthead" {...inert}>
        <div className="masthead__inner">
          <p className="kicker masthead__edition">
            {state.controls.year} published list prices · USPS, UPS, FedEx
          </p>
          <h1 className="masthead__title">Parcel Rates</h1>
          <p className="masthead__deck">
            Which carrier is cheapest for each kind of parcel you ship, and does your flat shipping price still cover
            the real cost after surcharges and yearly increases?
          </p>
        </div>
      </header>

      <div className="mobile-bar" {...inert}>
        <p className="mobile-bar__line">{assumptionsLine(state)}</p>
        <button
          ref={sheet.toggleRef}
          type="button"
          className="btn mobile-bar__toggle"
          aria-expanded={sheet.open}
          aria-controls={railId}
          onClick={() => sheet.setOpen(!sheet.open)}
        >
          Adjust
        </button>
      </div>

      <div className="layout">
        {sheet.open && (
          <div className="sheet-backdrop" aria-hidden="true" onClick={sheet.close} />
        )}
        <aside
          id={railId}
          ref={sheet.sheetRef}
          className={`rail ${sheet.open ? "rail--open" : ""}`}
          aria-labelledby={railTitleId}
          {...(sheet.open ? { role: "dialog", "aria-modal": true } : {})}
        >
          <div className="rail__head">
            <h2 id={railTitleId} className="kicker rail__title">
              Assumptions
            </h2>
            <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet rail__close" onClick={sheet.close}>
              Done
            </button>
          </div>
          <ControlRail
            state={state}
            dispatch={dispatch}
            meta={meta}
            metaStatus={metaState.status === "ok" ? "ok" : metaState.status}
            onRetryMeta={() => setMetaAttempt((n) => n + 1)}
          />
        </aside>

        <main id="main" className="main" tabIndex={-1} {...inert}>
          <ParcelSetPanel
            set={parcelSet.set}
            status={parcelSet.status}
            zoneBands={meta?.zone_bands}
            onLoadSample={parcelSet.loadSample}
            onLoadFile={parcelSet.loadFile}
            onClear={parcelSet.clear}
          />
          <QuestionTabs
            active={state.view}
            onSelect={(view) => dispatch({ type: "view", view })}
            renderPanel={(id) => {
              const View = VIEW_COMPONENTS[id];
              return <View {...viewProps} />;
            }}
          />
          <Footer meta={meta} status={metaState.status} />
        </main>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}

import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { Parcel } from "../api/types";
import { useApi } from "../api/ApiContext";
import { ApiError } from "../api/client";
import { parseParcelCsv, type CsvProblem } from "../lib/parcelCsv";
import { fromParcelOut } from "../lib/parcels";

export interface ParcelSet {
  parcels: Parcel[];
  source: "sample" | "upload";
  name: string;
  description?: string;
}

export type ParcelSetStatus =
  | { kind: "idle" }
  | { kind: "loading"; what: "sample" | "file" }
  | { kind: "error"; message: string; problems: CsvProblem[]; fileName?: string }
  | { kind: "notice"; message: string; problems: CsvProblem[]; fileName?: string };

const STORAGE_KEY = "parcel-rates:parcel-set:v2";
export const MAX_FILE_BYTES = 5 * 1024 * 1024;

function readStored(): ParcelSet | null {
  try {
    const raw = sessionStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    if (!raw) return null;
    const value = JSON.parse(raw) as ParcelSet;
    return Array.isArray(value?.parcels) && value.parcels.length > 0 ? value : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function store(set: ParcelSet | null) {
  try {
    if (set) sessionStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(set));
    else sessionStorage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  } catch {
    // Storage full or blocked (private mode): the set stays in memory only.
  }
}

/** FileReader rather than Blob.text(): same result, and it also works in jsdom. */
function readFileText(file: File): Promise<string> {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const reader = new FileReader();
    reader.onload = () => resolve(typeof reader.result === "string" ? reader.result : "");
    reader.onerror = () => reject(reader.error ?? new Error("read failed"));
    reader.readAsText(file);
  });
}

export function useParcelSet() {
  const api = useApi();
  const [set, setSet] = useState<ParcelSet | null>(readStored);
  const [status, setStatus] = useState<ParcelSetStatus>({ kind: "idle" });

  useEffect(() => store(set), [set]);

  // Each load (or clear) takes a new generation; a load that finishes after a newer one started
  // is dropped, so a slow sample request cannot overwrite a file the owner uploaded meanwhile.
  const generation = useRef(0);
  const begin = () => ++generation.current;
  const isLatest = (g: number) => g === generation.current;

  const loadSample = useCallback(async () => {
    const g = begin();
    setStatus({ kind: "loading", what: "sample" });
    try {
      const sample = await api.sampleParcels();
      if (!isLatest(g)) return;
      setSet({ parcels: sample.parcels.map(fromParcelOut), source: "sample", name: "Sample mix", description: sample.description });
      setStatus({ kind: "idle" });
    } catch (err) {
      if (!isLatest(g)) return;
      const message =
        err instanceof ApiError ? err.message : "The sample mix could not be loaded. Try again in a moment.";
      setStatus({ kind: "error", message, problems: [] });
    }
  }, [api]);

  const loadFile = useCallback(async (file: File) => {
    const g = begin();
    if (file.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES) {
      setStatus({
        kind: "error",
        message: `${file.name} is larger than 5 MB. Group identical parcels with the quantity column.`,
        problems: [],
        fileName: file.name,
      });
      return;
    }
    setStatus({ kind: "loading", what: "file" });
    let text: string;
    try {
      text = await readFileText(file);
    } catch {
      if (!isLatest(g)) return;
      setStatus({ kind: "error", message: `${file.name} could not be read.`, problems: [], fileName: file.name });
      return;
    }
    if (!isLatest(g)) return;
    const result = parseParcelCsv(text);
    if (result.errors.length > 0) {
      setStatus({
        kind: "error",
        message: `${file.name} was not loaded: ${result.errors.length} problem${result.errors.length > 1 ? "s" : ""} to fix.`,
        problems: result.errors,
        fileName: file.name,
      });
      return;
    }
    setSet({ parcels: result.parcels, source: "upload", name: file.name });
    setStatus(
      result.warnings.length > 0
        ? { kind: "notice", message: `${file.name} loaded, with notes:`, problems: result.warnings, fileName: file.name }
        : { kind: "idle" },
    );
  }, []);

  const clear = useCallback(() => {
    begin();
    setSet(null);
    setStatus({ kind: "idle" });
  }, []);

  return { set, status, loadSample, loadFile, clear };
}
import type { Carrier } from "../api/types";

/** CSS variable for a carrier's colour; use in style props so dark mode follows. */
export const carrierVar = (c: Carrier) => `var(--carrier-${c})`;
export const carrierWashVar = (c: Carrier) => `var(--carrier-${c}-wash)`;

/** Resolved colour, for libraries that need a concrete value (e.g. Recharts fills). */
export function carrierColor(c: Carrier, el: Element = document.documentElement): string {
  return getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue(`--carrier-${c}`).trim();
}
import type { Carrier, Tier } from "../api/types";

const usd = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", { style: "currency", currency: "USD" });
const int = new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US");

export const formatUsd = (n: number) => usd.format(n);
export const formatInt = (n: number) => int.format(n);
export const formatShare = (share: number) => `${Math.round(share * 100)}%`;
export const formatPercent = (n: number) => `${Number.isInteger(n) ? n : n.toFixed(2).replace(/0$/, "")}%`;

export const CARRIER_NAME: Record<Carrier, string> = { usps: "USPS", ups: "UPS", fedex: "FedEx" };
export const TIER_NAME: Record<Tier, string> = {
  ground: "Ground",
  two_three_day: "2–3 day",
  next_day: "Next day",
};
import type { FuelGroup, MetaDefaults, UspsRateCard } from "../api/types";

/**
 * The controls as the UI holds them: every field resolved. Assignable to the request
 * type `Controls`, which leaves fields with a server default optional.
 */
export interface ControlsState {
  year: number;
  usps_rate_card: UspsRateCard;
  peak: boolean;
  flat_price: number;
  fuel_override_percent?: { ground?: number; express?: number };
}

export function controlsFromMeta(d: MetaDefaults): ControlsState {
  return { year: d.year, usps_rate_card: d.usps_rate_card, peak: d.peak, flat_price: d.flat_price };
}

export const VIEWS = ["quote", "breakeven", "blended", "yearly"] as const;
export type ViewId = (typeof VIEWS)[number];

export interface AppState {
  controls: ControlsState;
  view: ViewId;
}

export const FALLBACK_CONTROLS: ControlsState = {
  year: 2026,
  usps_rate_card: "commercial",
  peak: false,
  flat_price: 9.99,
};

export const FUEL_MIN = 0;
export const FUEL_MAX = 40;
export const PRICE_MAX = 1000;

const KEYS = {
  year: "year",
  card: "usps",
  fuelGround: "fuel_ground",
  fuelExpress: "fuel_express",
  peak: "peak",
  price: "price",
  view: "view",
} as const;

/** Params the app owns; anything else in the query string (e.g. mock=1) is preserved. */
const OWNED = new Set<string>(Object.values(KEYS));

function num(params: URLSearchParams, key: string, min: number, max: number): number | undefined {
  const raw = params.get(key);
  if (raw === null || raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
  const n = Number(raw);
  return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= min && n <= max ? n : undefined;
}

export function readState(search: string, defaults: ControlsState = FALLBACK_CONTROLS): AppState {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
  const year = num(params, KEYS.year, 2000, 2100);
  const card = params.get(KEYS.card);
  const ground = num(params, KEYS.fuelGround, FUEL_MIN, FUEL_MAX);
  const express = num(params, KEYS.fuelExpress, FUEL_MIN, FUEL_MAX);
  const price = num(params, KEYS.price, 0, PRICE_MAX);
  const view = params.get(KEYS.view);
  const fuel: Partial<Record<FuelGroup, number>> = {
    ...(ground !== undefined ? { ground } : {}),
    ...(express !== undefined ? { express } : {}),
  };
  const controls: ControlsState = {
    year: year !== undefined && Number.isInteger(year) ? year : defaults.year,
    usps_rate_card: card === "retail" || card === "commercial" ? card : defaults.usps_rate_card,
    peak: params.has(KEYS.peak) ? params.get(KEYS.peak) === "1" : defaults.peak,
    flat_price: price ?? defaults.flat_price,
    ...(Object.keys(fuel).length > 0 ? { fuel_override_percent: fuel } : {}),
  };
  return { controls, view: (VIEWS as readonly string[]).includes(view ?? "") ? (view as ViewId) : "quote" };
}

/** Serialize, leaving out values equal to the defaults so shared links stay short. */
export function writeState(state: AppState, currentSearch = "", defaults: ControlsState = FALLBACK_CONTROLS): string {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(currentSearch);
  for (const key of OWNED) params.delete(key);
  const c = state.controls;
  if (c.year !== defaults.year) params.set(KEYS.year, String(c.year));
  if (c.usps_rate_card !== defaults.usps_rate_card) params.set(KEYS.card, c.usps_rate_card);
  if (c.fuel_override_percent?.ground !== undefined) params.set(KEYS.fuelGround, String(c.fuel_override_percent.ground));
  if (c.fuel_override_percent?.express !== undefined) params.set(KEYS.fuelExpress, String(c.fuel_override_percent.express));
  if (c.peak !== defaults.peak) params.set(KEYS.peak, c.peak ? "1" : "0");
  if (c.flat_price !== defaults.flat_price) params.set(KEYS.price, String(c.flat_price));
  if (state.view !== "quote") params.set(KEYS.view, state.view);
  const out = params.toString();
  return out ? `?${out}` : "";
}

/* ---------- reducer ---------- */

export type Action =
  | { type: "year"; year: number }
  | { type: "card"; card: UspsRateCard }
  | { type: "fuel"; group: FuelGroup; percent: number }
  | { type: "fuelReset"; group: FuelGroup }
  | { type: "peak"; peak: boolean }
  | { type: "price"; price: number }
  | { type: "view"; view: ViewId }
  | { type: "replace"; state: AppState };

function withFuel(c: ControlsState, group: FuelGroup, percent: number | undefined): ControlsState {
  const { [group]: _dropped, ...rest } = c.fuel_override_percent ?? {};
  const next = percent === undefined ? rest : { ...rest, [group]: percent };
  const { fuel_override_percent: _old, ...base } = c;
  return Object.keys(next).length > 0 ? { ...base, fuel_override_percent: next } : base;
}

export function reducer(state: AppState, action: Action): AppState {
  const set = (controls: ControlsState): AppState => ({ ...state, controls });
  switch (action.type) {
    case "year":
      // A new year has its own fuel defaults; an override from another year would mislead.
      return set(withFuel(withFuel({ ...state.controls, year: action.year }, "ground", undefined), "express", undefined));
    case "card":
      return set({ ...state.controls, usps_rate_card: action.card });
    case "fuel":
      return set(withFuel(state.controls, action.group, Math.min(FUEL_MAX, Math.max(FUEL_MIN, action.percent))));
    case "fuelReset":
      return set(withFuel(state.controls, action.group, undefined));
    case "peak":
      return set({ ...state.controls, peak: action.peak });
    case "price":
      return set({ ...state.controls, flat_price: Math.min(PRICE_MAX, Math.max(0, action.price)) });
    case "view":
      return { ...state, view: action.view };
    case "replace":
      return action.state;
  }
}

export interface QuestionTabsProps {
  active: ViewId;
  onSelect: (id: ViewId) => void;
  renderPanel: (id: ViewId) => ReactNode;
}

const tabId = (id: ViewId) => `tab-${id}`;
const panelId = (id: ViewId) => `panel-${id}`;

/** WAI-ARIA tabs with automatic activation; arrow keys, Home and End move between questions. */
export function QuestionTabs({ active, onSelect, renderPanel }: QuestionTabsProps) {
  const refs = useRef<Partial<Record<ViewId, HTMLButtonElement | null>>>({});
  const activeDef = QUESTIONS.find((q) => q.id === active) ?? QUESTIONS[0]!;

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const i = QUESTIONS.findIndex((q) => q.id === active);
    const last = QUESTIONS.length - 1;
    const next =
      e.key === "ArrowRight" ? (i === last ? 0 : i + 1)
      : e.key === "ArrowLeft" ? (i === 0 ? last : i - 1)
      : e.key === "Home" ? 0
      : e.key === "End" ? last
      : null;
    if (next === null) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    const id = QUESTIONS[next]!.id;
    onSelect(id);
    refs.current[id]?.focus();
  };

  return (
    <div className="questions">
      <div className="questions__tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Questions" onKeyDown={onKeyDown}>
        {QUESTIONS.map((q) => (
          <button
            key={q.id}
            ref={(el) => {
              refs.current[q.id] = el;
            }}
            id={tabId(q.id)}
            type="button"
            role="tab"
            aria-selected={q.id === active}
            aria-controls={panelId(q.id)}
            tabIndex={q.id === active ? 0 : -1}
            className="questions__tab"
            onClick={() => onSelect(q.id)}
          >
            <span className="questions__num">{String(q.number).padStart(2, "0")}</span>
            <span className="questions__short">{q.short}</span>
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <section
        id={panelId(activeDef.id)}
        role="tabpanel"
        aria-labelledby={tabId(activeDef.id)}
        className="questions__panel"
        tabIndex={0}
      >
        <p className="kicker">Question {activeDef.number}</p>
        <h2 className="questions__question">{activeDef.question}</h2>
        {renderPanel(activeDef.id)}
      </section>
    </div>
  );
}

import type {
  BlendedRequest,
  BlendedResponse,
  BreakevenRequest,
  BreakevenResponse,
  HealthResponse,
  Meta,
  QuoteRequest,
  QuoteResponse,
  SampleParcels,
  HttpErrorBody,
  ValidationErrorBody,
  ValidationIssue,
  YearlyRequest,
  YearlyResponse,
} from "./types";

import {
  ContractError,
  asBlendedResponse,
  asBreakevenResponse,
  asHealth,
  asMeta,
  asQuoteResponse,
  asSampleParcels,
  asYearlyResponse,
} from "./guards";

export const API_BASE = "/api";

/** A readable problem with one input field, for display to the shop owner. */
export interface FieldProblem {
  field: string;
  message: string;
}

export class ApiError extends Error {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly problems: FieldProblem[];
  /** Set when a 2xx answer did not match the contract (src/api/types.ts). */
  readonly contract?: { endpoint: string; path: string; detail: string };

  constructor(
    status: number,
    message: string,
    problems: FieldProblem[] = [],
    contract?: { endpoint: string; path: string; detail: string },
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "ApiError";
    this.status = status;
    this.problems = problems;
    if (contract) this.contract = contract;
  }
}

/** Turn a Pydantic `loc` like ["body","parcels",3,"weight_lb"] into "parcels row 4 · weight_lb". */
export function describeLoc(loc: readonly (string | number)[]): string {
  const parts = loc[0] === "body" || loc[0] === "query" ? loc.slice(1) : loc;
  return parts
    .map((p) => (typeof p === "number" ? `row ${p + 1}` : p))
    .join(" · ");
}

function isIssue(x: unknown): x is ValidationIssue {
  return (
    typeof x === "object" &&
    x !== null &&
    Array.isArray((x as ValidationIssue).loc) &&
    typeof (x as ValidationIssue).msg === "string"
  );
}

export function problemsFromBody(body: unknown): FieldProblem[] {
  if (typeof body !== "object" || body === null || !("detail" in body)) return [];
  const detail = (body as ValidationErrorBody | HttpErrorBody).detail;
  if (typeof detail === "string") return [{ field: "", message: detail }];
  if (!Array.isArray(detail)) return [];
  return detail.filter(isIssue).map((d) => ({ field: describeLoc(d.loc), message: d.msg }));
}

async function readJson(res: Response): Promise<unknown> {
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!text) return null;
  try {
    return JSON.parse(text);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function statusMessage(status: number): string {
  if (status === 422) return "Some inputs were not accepted.";
  if (status === 404) return "The rate service does not know this request.";
  if (status >= 500) return "The rate service had a problem. Try again in a moment.";
  return `The rate service answered with status ${status}.`;
}

export interface ApiClient {
  health(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<HealthResponse>;
  meta(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<Meta>;
  sampleParcels(signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<SampleParcels>;
  quote(body: QuoteRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<QuoteResponse>;
  breakeven(body: BreakevenRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<BreakevenResponse>;
  blended(body: BlendedRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<BlendedResponse>;
  yearly(body: YearlyRequest, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<YearlyResponse>;
}

export interface ClientOptions {
  baseUrl?: string;
  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
}

export function createHttpClient({ baseUrl = API_BASE, fetchImpl }: ClientOptions = {}): ApiClient {
  const doFetch = fetchImpl ?? ((input: RequestInfo | URL, init?: RequestInit) => fetch(input, init));

  /** Fetch, map HTTP errors to ApiError, and check a 2xx body with the endpoint's guard. */
  async function request<T>(path: string, guard: (v: unknown) => T, init: RequestInit = {}): Promise<T> {
    let res: Response;
    try {
      res = await doFetch(`${baseUrl}${path}`, {
        ...init,
        headers: { Accept: "application/json", ...(init.body ? { "Content-Type": "application/json" } : {}) },
      });
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof DOMException && err.name === "AbortError") throw err;
      throw new ApiError(0, "Cannot reach the rate service. Is the backend running?");
    }
    const body = await readJson(res);
    if (!res.ok) {
      const problems = problemsFromBody(body);
      throw new ApiError(res.status, statusMessage(res.status), problems);
    }
    if (body === null) throw new ApiError(res.status, "The rate service sent an empty answer.");
    try {
      return guard(body);
    } catch (err) {
      if (!(err instanceof ContractError)) throw err;
      const endpoint = `${init.method ?? "GET"} ${baseUrl}${path}`;
      const field = err.path || "(body)";
      throw new ApiError(
        res.status,
        `The rate service answered ${endpoint} in an unexpected shape (${field}: expected ${err.expected}). ` +
          "The frontend and backend versions probably differ.",
        [],
        { endpoint, path: field, detail: err.message },
      );
    }
  }

  const get = <T>(path: string, guard: (v: unknown) => T, signal?: AbortSignal) => request(path, guard, { signal });
  const post = <T>(path: string, guard: (v: unknown) => T, body: unknown, signal?: AbortSignal) =>
    request(path, guard, { method: "POST", body: JSON.stringify(body), signal });

  return {
    health: (signal) => get("/health", asHealth, signal),
    meta: (signal) => get("/meta", asMeta, signal),
    sampleParcels: (signal) => get("/sample-parcels", asSampleParcels, signal),
    quote: (body, signal) => post("/quote", asQuoteResponse, body, signal),
    breakeven: (body, signal) => post("/breakeven", asBreakevenResponse, body, signal),
    blended: (body, signal) => post("/blended", asBlendedResponse, body, signal),
    yearly: (body, signal) => post("/yearly", asYearlyResponse, body, signal),
  };
}

/** `?mock=1` serves typed mock responses; the mock module is a separate lazy chunk. */
export function isMockMode(search: string = typeof window === "undefined" ? "" : window.location.search): boolean {
  return new URLSearchParams(search).get("mock") === "1";
}

export function createMockClient(delayMs = 350): ApiClient {
  const load = () => import("./mocks");
  const wait = <T>(fn: () => T | Promise<T>): Promise<T> =>
    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      setTimeout(() => {
        Promise.resolve().then(fn).then(resolve, reject);
      }, delayMs);
    });
  return {
    health: () => wait(() => ({ status: "ok" as const })),
    meta: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockMeta),
    sampleParcels: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockSampleParcels),
    quote: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockQuote()),
    breakeven: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockBreakeven()),
    blended: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockBlended()),
    yearly: () => wait(async () => (await load()).mockYearly()),
  };
}

export function createClient(): ApiClient {
  return isMockMode() ? createMockClient() : createHttpClient();
}
import { createContext, useContext, useEffect, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { ApiError, createClient, type ApiClient } from "./client";

const ApiContext = createContext<ApiClient | null>(null);

export function ApiProvider({ client, children }: { client?: ApiClient; children: ReactNode }) {
  const [value] = useState<ApiClient>(() => client ?? createClient());
  return <ApiContext.Provider value={value}>{children}</ApiContext.Provider>;
}

export function useApi(): ApiClient {
  const c = useContext(ApiContext);
  if (!c) throw new Error("useApi must be used inside <ApiProvider>");
  return c;
}

export type Loadable<T> =
  | { status: "idle" }
  | { status: "loading" }
  | { status: "ok"; data: T }
  | { status: "error"; error: ApiError | Error };

/** Run `load` whenever `deps` change; aborts the previous request. */
export function useLoad<T>(load: ((signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<T>) | null, deps: readonly unknown[]): Loadable<T> {
  const [state, setState] = useState<Loadable<T>>({ status: load ? "loading" : "idle" });
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!load) {
      setState({ status: "idle" });
      return;
    }
    const ctrl = new AbortController();
    setState({ status: "loading" });
    load(ctrl.signal).then(
      (data) => !ctrl.signal.aborted && setState({ status: "ok", data }),
      (error: unknown) => {
        if (ctrl.signal.aborted) return;
        setState({ status: "error", error: error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error)) });
      },
    );
    return () => ctrl.abort();
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, deps);
  return state;
}

Two extra files cover years where not every carrier publishes prices: `breakeven-2027.json`

script, so regenerate them the same way if the backend changes.

Each file is `{ request: {method, path, body}, response: {status, body} }`.

They are used by:

- `src/api/contract.test.ts`, which validates every response body against the runtime
  guards in `src/api/guards.ts` (which follow `src/api/types.ts`), so drift between the
  backend and the frontend types fails the tests;
- `src/api/mocks.ts`, which serves these recorded responses in tests and in the
  `?mock=1` dev mode. Mock responses are the recorded examples: they do not react to the
  request (a different parcel or year returns the same recorded answer).

export interface Controls {
  year?: number | null; // null/absent: latest year with all three carriers
  as_of?: string | null; // ISO date
  usps_rate_card?: UspsRateCard; // default "commercial"
  fuel_override_percent?: FuelOverride | null;
  peak?: boolean; // default false
  flat_price?: number; // default 9.99
}

export interface SegmentFilter {
  weight_band?: WeightBand | null;
  zone_band?: ZoneBandLabel | null;
  residential?: boolean | null;
  speed?: Tier | null;
}

export interface QuoteRequest {
  parcel: Parcel;
  controls?: Controls;
}

export interface BreakevenRequest {
  controls?: Controls;
  residential?: boolean; // default true
  weights_lb?: number[] | null; // 1..200 values, each in (0, 70]
  distances_miles?: number[] | null; // 1..50 values, each >= 0
}

export interface BlendedRequest {
  parcels: Parcel[]; // 1..10,000
  controls?: Controls;
  segment?: SegmentFilter | null;
}

export interface YearlyRequest {
  parcels: Parcel[]; // 1..10,000
  controls?: Controls;
  next_year_increase_percent?: number | null; // -50..100
}

/* ---------- shared response pieces ---------- */

export interface LineItem {
  kind: "base" | "surcharge" | "fuel";
  label: string;
  amount: number;
  surcharge_id: string | null;
  source: string | null; // "file p.N" for display
  condition: string | null; // surcharges.csv condition, for grouping

export interface SplitPart {
  per_parcel: number;
  total: number;
  share: number; // 0..1
}

export interface Split {
  base: SplitPart;
  surcharges: SplitPart;
  fuel: SplitPart;
}

export interface ConditionTotal {
  condition: string;
  total: number;
  per_parcel: number;
  share_of_cost: number;
}

/** Everything weighted by quantity. */
export interface Summary {
  parcels_shipped: number;
  parcels_unavailable: number;
  total_cost: number;
  cost_per_parcel: number;
  split: Split;
  surcharges_by_condition: ConditionTotal[];
  margin_per_parcel: number;
  total_margin: number;
  loss_share: number; // 0..1
  parcels_at_loss: number;
}

export interface CarrierBlended extends Summary {
  carrier: Carrier;
  services_used: Record<string, number>; // service_id -> parcels
}

export interface BestMix extends Summary {
  parcels_by_carrier: Record<string, number>;
}

export interface BlendedResponse {
  year: number;
  parcels_considered: number;
  revenue_per_parcel: number;
  carriers: CarrierBlended[];
  best_mix: BestMix;
}

/* ---------- POST /api/yearly ---------- */

export interface Change {
  from_year: number;
  dollars_per_parcel: number;
  percent: number | null;
}

export interface Announced {
  percent: number | null;
  basis: "all" | "average_of_services" | "none";
  services: string[];
  source_type: string | null; // "primary" | "secondary"
}

export interface Driver {
  segment: string;
  parcels: number;
  change_per_parcel: number;
  change_total: number;
}

export interface Drivers {
  weight_band: Driver[];
  zone_band: Driver[];
  residential: Driver[];
  speed: Driver[];
}

export interface FuelGroupUsed {
  default_percent: number | null;
  is_proxy: boolean | null;
  applied_percent: number | null;
}

export interface YearRow {
  year: number;
  as_of: string | null;
  cost_per_parcel: number;
  summary: Summary;
  services_used: string[];
  change_vs_previous: Change | null; // null for the first year
  announced_increase: Announced;
  drivers: Drivers | null;
  fuel: { ground: FuelGroupUsed; express: FuelGroupUsed } | null; // null for USPS
  warnings: string[];
}

export interface Projection {
  year: number;
  increase_percent: number;
  cost_per_parcel: number;
}

export interface CarrierYears {
  carrier: Carrier;
  parcels_used: number;
  parcels_excluded: number;
  years: YearRow[];
  projected: Projection | null;
}

export interface YearlyResponse {

}

"""Question 4: blended cost per parcel year over year, against the announced
increase, with the parcel segments that drove the change."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import replace
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal

from .blended import per_parcel_quotes, summarize
from .rules import PEAK_CONDITIONS, resolve_as_of
from .segments import DIMENSIONS, segment_of
from .tables import RateTables, in_window
from .types import Controls, Parcel, Quote, Totals

ZERO = Decimal("0")
CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def _r(value: Decimal, places: str = "0.01") -> float:
    return float(value.quantize(Decimal(places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def allocate_cents(values: dict[str, Decimal], total: Decimal) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Round each value to cents so the rounded values still add up to the
    rounded total (largest remainder)."""
    target = total.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    floors = {k: (v / CENT).to_integral_value(rounding="ROUND_FLOOR") for k, v in values.items()}
    remainder = int(target / CENT - sum(floors.values()))
    order = sorted(values, key=lambda k: (values[k] / CENT - floors[k]), reverse=True)
    if remainder < 0:
        order = list(reversed(order))
    step = 1 if remainder >= 0 else -1
    for k in order[: abs(remainder)]:
        floors[k] += step
    return {k: float(floors[k] * CENT) for k in values}


def announced_increase(tables: RateTables, carrier: str, year: int, services_used: list[str], usps_card: str) -> dict:
    rows = [
        r
        for r in tables.increases
        if r.carrier == carrier and r.year == year and r.rate_card in ("", "list", usps_card)
    ]
    overall = [r for r in rows if r.product_scope == "all"]
    if overall:
        r = overall[0]
        return {
            "percent": float(r.percent),
            "basis": "all",
            "services": [],
            "source_type": r.source_type,
        }
    scoped = [r for r in rows if r.product_scope in services_used]
    if not scoped:
        return {"percent": None, "basis": "none", "services": [], "source_type": None}
    avg = sum((r.percent for r in scoped), ZERO) / len(scoped)
    return {
        "percent": _r(avg, "0.01"),
        "basis": "average_of_services",
        "services": sorted({r.product_scope for r in scoped}),
        "source_type": ",".join(sorted({r.source_type for r in scoped})),
    }


def conditions_in_force(tables: RateTables, carrier: str, year: int, controls: Controls) -> set[str]:
    """Non-peak surcharge conditions with at least one rule in force."""
    as_of = resolve_as_of(tables, carrier, year, controls)
    return {
        r.condition
        for r in tables.surcharges.get((carrier, year), [])
        if r.condition not in PEAK_CONDITIONS and as_of and in_window(as_of, r.effective_from, r.effective_to)
    }


def fuel_used(tables: RateTables, carrier: str, year: int, controls: Controls) -> dict | None:
    """Fuel percent per service group for the year: the table default, whether
    it is a proxy, and the percent actually applied (override or default).
    None for a carrier without a fuel surcharge (USPS)."""
    if carrier not in tables.fuel_carriers:
        return None
    out = {}
    override = controls.fuel_override_percent
    for group in ("ground", "express"):
        row = tables.fuel.get((carrier, year, group))
        forced = getattr(override, group) if override is not None else None
        default = float(row.default_percent) if row else None
        out[group] = {
            "default_percent": default,
            "is_proxy": row.is_proxy if row else None,
            "applied_percent": float(forced) if forced is not None else default,
        }
    return out


def _drivers(
    tables: RateTables,
    parcels: list[Parcel],
    prev: list[Quote],
    cur: list[Quote],
    n: int,
) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
    total_change = sum(((c.total - p.total) * x.quantity for x, p, c in zip(parcels, prev, cur)), ZERO)
    out: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
    segs = [segment_of(tables, p) for p in parcels]
    for dim in DIMENSIONS:
        change: dict[str, Decimal] = {}
        count: dict[str, int] = {}
        for x, s, p, c in zip(parcels, segs, prev, cur):
            key = s[dim]
            change[key] = change.get(key, ZERO) + (c.total - p.total) * x.quantity
            count[key] = count.get(key, 0) + x.quantity
        per_parcel = {k: v / n for k, v in change.items()}
        rounded = allocate_cents(per_parcel, total_change / n)
        out[dim] = [
            {
                "segment": k,
                "parcels": count[k],
                "change_per_parcel": rounded[k],
                "change_total": _r(change[k]),
            }
            for k in sorted(change, key=lambda k: -abs(change[k]))
        ]
    return out


# Quotes every parcel for every carrier and year without caching: about 1 s per
# 1,000 parcels on a laptop. Requests are capped at 10,000 parcels (api/models.py);
# a small shop's monthly mix of a few thousand parcels answers in a few seconds.
def yearly(
    tables: RateTables,
    parcels: list[Parcel],
    controls: Controls,
    next_year_increase_percent: float | None = None,
) -> dict:
    result = []
    for carrier in tables.carriers():
        years = tables.years_for(carrier)
        per_year: dict[int, list[Quote | None]] = {}
        for y in years:
            cy = replace(controls, year=y, as_of=None)
            per_year[y] = per_parcel_quotes(tables, carrier, parcels, cy, year=y)

        # Like-for-like: only parcels the carrier can ship in every year.
        keep = [i for i in range(len(parcels)) if all(per_year[y][i] is not None for y in years)]
        used = [parcels[i] for i in keep]
        n = sum(p.quantity for p in used)
        excluded = sum(p.quantity for p in parcels) - n

        rows = []
        prev_y: int | None = None
        prev_cost: Decimal | None = None
        prev_conditions: set[str] = set()
        for y in years:
            conditions = conditions_in_force(tables, carrier, y, replace(controls, year=y, as_of=None))
            missing = sorted(prev_conditions - conditions)
            quotes = [per_year[y][i] for i in keep]
            totals = Totals()
            for p, q in zip(used, quotes):
                totals.add(q, p.quantity)
            cost = totals.total / n if n else ZERO
            services = sorted({q.service_id for q in quotes})
            row = {
                "year": y,
                "as_of": quotes[0].as_of.isoformat() if quotes else None,
                "cost_per_parcel": _r(cost),
                "summary": summarize(totals),
                "services_used": services,
                "change_vs_previous": None,
                "announced_increase": announced_increase(
                    tables, carrier, y, services, controls.usps_rate_card
                ),
                "drivers": None,
                "fuel": fuel_used(tables, carrier, y, controls),
                "warnings": (
                    [f"No {y} rules recorded for: {', '.join(missing)}; surcharges may be understated"]
                    if missing
                    else []
                ),
            }
            if prev_y is not None and n:
                diff = cost - prev_cost
                row["change_vs_previous"] = {
                    "from_year": prev_y,
                    "dollars_per_parcel": _r(diff),
                    "percent": _r(diff / prev_cost * 100, "0.01") if prev_cost else None,
                }
                prev_quotes = [per_year[prev_y][i] for i in keep]
                row["drivers"] = _drivers(tables, used, prev_quotes, quotes, n)
            rows.append(row)
            prev_y, prev_cost, prev_conditions = y, cost, conditions

        projected = None
        if next_year_increase_percent is not None and rows and n:
            last = rows[-1]
            factor = Decimal(1) + Decimal(str(next_year_increase_percent)) / Decimal(100)
            projected = {
                "year": last["year"] + 1,
                "increase_percent": next_year_increase_percent,
                "cost_per_parcel": _r(prev_cost * factor),
            }
        result.append(
            {
                "carrier": carrier,
                "parcels_used": n,
                "parcels_excluded": excluded,
                "years": rows,
                "projected": projected,
            }
        )
    return {"carriers": result}
"""Parcel segments used by the segment filter and the yearly driver breakdown.

Band labels and edges come from docs/API.md ("Segments"). Zone bands use the
USPS zone of the parcel's distance, the finest of the carriers' band tables.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from .rules import zone_for
from .tables import RateTables
from .types import Parcel

# (label, lower bound exclusive, upper bound inclusive)
WEIGHT_BANDS: tuple[tuple[str, float, float], ...] = (
    ("≤1", 0.0, 1.0),
    ("1–5", 1.0, 5.0),
    ("5–10", 5.0, 10.0),
    ("10–20", 10.0, 20.0),
    ("20–70", 20.0, 70.0),
)
ZONE_BANDS: tuple[tuple[str, int, int], ...] = (
    ("1–2", 1, 2),
    ("3–4", 3, 4),
    ("5–6", 5, 6),
    ("7–8", 7, 8),
)
SEGMENT_CARRIER = "usps"
DIMENSIONS = ("weight_band", "zone_band", "residential", "speed")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SegmentFilter:
    weight_band: str | None = None
    zone_band: str | None = None
    residential: bool | None = None
    speed: str | None = None


def weight_band(parcel: Parcel) -> str:
    for label, low, high in WEIGHT_BANDS:
        if low < parcel.weight_lb <= high:
            return label
    return WEIGHT_BANDS[-1][0]


def zone_band(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel) -> str:
    zone = zone_for(tables, SEGMENT_CARRIER, parcel.distance_miles)
    for label, low, high in ZONE_BANDS:
        if zone is not None and low <= zone <= high:
            return label
    return ZONE_BANDS[-1][0]


def residential_label(parcel: Parcel) -> str:
    return "residential" if parcel.residential else "business"


def segment_of(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {
        "weight_band": weight_band(parcel),
        "zone_band": zone_band(tables, parcel),
        "residential": residential_label(parcel),
        "speed": parcel.speed,
    }


def matches(tables: RateTables, parcel: Parcel, f: SegmentFilter | None) -> bool:
    if f is None:
        return True
    if f.weight_band is not None and weight_band(parcel) != f.weight_band:
        return False
    if f.zone_band is not None and zone_band(tables, parcel) != f.zone_band:
        return False
    if f.residential is not None and parcel.residential != f.residential:
        return False
    if f.speed is not None and parcel.speed != f.speed:
        return False
    return True

npm WARN deprecated whatwg-encoding@3.1.1: Use @exodus/bytes instead for a more spec-conformant and faster implementation

added 236 packages in 2s
def per_parcel_quotes(
    tables: RateTables, carrier: str, parcels: list[Parcel], controls: Controls, year: int | None = None
) -> list[Quote | None]:
    """Each parcel at the carrier's cheapest available service in its tier."""
    return [cheapest_for_carrier(tables, carrier, p.speed, p, controls, year=year) for p in parcels]


def blended(
    tables: RateTables,
    parcels: list[Parcel],
    controls: Controls,
    segment: SegmentFilter | None = None,
) -> dict:
    selected = [p for p in parcels if matches(tables, p, segment)]
    carriers = [c for c in tables.carriers() if (c, controls.year) in tables.base_effective]

    quotes_by_carrier: dict[str, list[Quote | None]] = {}
    results = []
    for carrier in carriers:
        quotes = per_parcel_quotes(tables, carrier, selected, controls)
        quotes_by_carrier[carrier] = quotes
        totals = Totals()
        unavailable = 0
        services: dict[str, int] = {}
        for parcel, q in zip(selected, quotes):
            if q is None:
                unavailable += parcel.quantity
                continue
            totals.add(q, parcel.quantity)
            services[q.service_id] = services.get(q.service_id, 0) + parcel.quantity
        results.append({"carrier": carrier, **summarize(totals, unavailable), "services_used": services})

    best = Totals()
    best_unavailable = 0
    counts: dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in carriers}
    for i, parcel in enumerate(selected):
        options = [quotes_by_carrier[c][i] for c in carriers if quotes_by_carrier[c][i] is not None]
        if not options:
            best_unavailable += parcel.quantity
            continue
        q = min(options, key=lambda x: x.total)
        best.add(q, parcel.quantity)
        counts[q.carrier] += parcel.quantity

    revenue = sum((price_charged(p, controls) * p.quantity for p in selected), ZERO)
    n = sum(p.quantity for p in selected)
    return {
        "year": controls.year,
        "parcels_considered": n,
        "revenue_per_parcel": _r(revenue / n) if n else 0.0,
        "carriers": results,
        "best_mix": {**summarize(best, best_unavailable), "parcels_by_carrier": counts},
    }

import { useId } from "react";
import type { FuelGroup } from "../../api/types";
import { FUEL_MAX, FUEL_MIN } from "../../state/urlState";
import type { FuelDefaultInfo } from "../../lib/fuel";
import { formatPercent } from "../../lib/format";

export interface FuelSliderProps {
  group: FuelGroup;
  label: string;
  hint: string;
  override: number | undefined;
  defaultInfo: FuelDefaultInfo | null;
  onChange: (percent: number) => void;
  onReset: () => void;
}

const STEP = 0.25;

export function FuelSlider({ group, label, hint, override, defaultInfo, onChange, onReset }: FuelSliderProps) {
  const id = useId();
  const value = override ?? defaultInfo?.percent ?? 0;
  const isOverridden = override !== undefined;

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

/**
 * Formatting shared by the Q3 and Q4 views (issue #6). Lives here rather than in src/lib
 * so the parallel Q1/Q2 branch is not touched; src/lib/format.ts has the base formatters.
 */
import type { Carrier, Tier } from "../../api/types";
import { CARRIER_NAME, TIER_NAME, formatUsd } from "../../lib/format";

/** "+$1.23" / "−$1.23" (true minus sign), "$0.00" for zero. */
export function signedUsd(n: number): string {
  const r = Math.round(n * 100) / 100;
  if (r === 0) return formatUsd(0);
  return `${r > 0 ? "+" : "−"}${formatUsd(Math.abs(r))}`;
}

/** "+4.1%" / "−2.0%" with one decimal. */
export function signedPct(n: number, digits = 1): string {
  const r = Number(n.toFixed(digits));
  if (r === 0) return `0${digits ? "." + "0".repeat(digits) : ""}%`;
  return `${r > 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(r).toFixed(digits)}%`;
}

/** Share 0..1 as "71%". */
export const pct0 = (share: number) => `${Math.round(share * 100)}%`;

export const carrierName = (c: Carrier | string) => CARRIER_NAME[c as Carrier] ?? c;

  additional_handling_packaging: "Handling: packaging",

  nonstandard_volume: "Non-standard size",
  nonstandard_length: "Non-standard length",
  oversize: "Oversize",
};

export function conditionLabel(condition: string): string {
  return CONDITION_LABEL[condition] ?? condition.replace(/_/g, " ").replace(/^./, (c) => c.toUpperCase());
}

export const tierName = (t: string) => TIER_NAME[t as Tier] ?? t;

function panelSampleButton(): HTMLButtonElement | null {

/* ---------- chart frame: title, text summary, chart or table ---------- */

export function ChartFrame({
  title,
  summary,
  chart,
  table,
  aside,
}: {
  title: string;
  summary: ReactNode;
  chart: ReactNode;
  table: ReactNode;
  aside?: ReactNode;
}) {

  const titleId = useId();
  const bodyId = useId();
  return (
    <figure className="chart" aria-labelledby={titleId}>

        </h3>
        <button

          aria-controls={bodyId}

      <div id={bodyId} className="chart__body">

      </div>

    </figure>
  );
}

/* ---------- colours for Recharts ---------- */

const DARK = "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)";

/** Resolve CSS custom properties to concrete colours; re-resolves when the colour scheme flips. */
export function useCssColors<K extends string>(vars: Record<K, string>): Record<K, string> {
  const read = () => {
    const style = typeof document === "undefined" ? null : getComputedStyle(document.documentElement);
    const out = {} as Record<K, string>;
    for (const k in vars) out[k] = style?.getPropertyValue(vars[k]).trim() || "currentColor";
    return out;
  };
  const [colors, setColors] = useState(read);
  const key = JSON.stringify(vars);
  useEffect(() => {
    setColors(read());
    const mq = typeof window !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia(DARK) : null;
    if (!mq) return;
    const onChange = () => setColors(read());
    mq.addEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    return () => mq.removeEventListener?.("change", onChange);
    // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
  }, [key]);
  return colors;
}

/* ---------- loading that keeps the last answer ---------- */

/** The latest successful data, so controls re-query without blanking the view. */
export function useLastData<T>(state: Loadable<T>): T | null {
  const [last, setLast] = useState<T | null>(state.status === "ok" ? state.data : null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (state.status === "ok") setLast(state.data);
  }, [state]);
  return state.status === "ok" ? state.data : last;
}

export function LoadProblem({ error }: { error: Error }) {
  const problems = error instanceof ApiError ? error.problems : [];
  return (
    <div className="problems problems--error" role="alert">
      <p className="problems__title">{error.message}</p>
      {problems.length > 0 && (
        <ul className="problems__list">
          {problems.slice(0, 8).map((p, i) => (
            <li key={i}>
              {p.field && <span className="problems__where">{p.field}</span>}
              <span>{p.message}</span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

/** Debounce a fast-changing value (slider) before it reaches the API. */
export function useDebounced<T>(value: T, ms: number): T {
  const [v, setV] = useState(value);
  useEffect(() => {
    const t = setTimeout(() => setV(value), ms);
    return () => clearTimeout(t);
  }, [value, ms]);
  return v;
}

/** Track a media query, for chart sizes that differ on phones. */
export function useNarrow(query = "(max-width: 39.999rem)"): boolean {
  const get = () => (typeof window !== "undefined" && window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia(query).matches : false);
  const [m, setM] = useState(get);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof window === "undefined" || !window.matchMedia) return;
    const mq = window.matchMedia(query);
    const on = () => setM(mq.matches);
    on();
    mq.addEventListener?.("change", on);
    return () => mq.removeEventListener?.("change", on);
  }, [query]);
  return m;
}

import { useEffect, useState } from "react";

/** True while the media query matches. False where matchMedia is missing (old browsers, jsdom). */
export function useMediaQuery(query: string): boolean {
  const get = () => typeof window !== "undefined" && typeof window.matchMedia === "function" && window.matchMedia(query).matches;
  const [matches, setMatches] = useState(get);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (typeof window.matchMedia !== "function") return;
    const mql = window.matchMedia(query);
    const onChange = () => setMatches(mql.matches);
    onChange();
    mql.addEventListener("change", onChange);
    return () => mql.removeEventListener("change", onChange);
  }, [query]);
  return matches;
}
