```
The Q3 "blended cost" and Q4 "year over year" views from issue #6 are built and working against the real backend. Tests (118, 26 of them new), typecheck and build all pass. The work is on branch `issue-6-blended-yearly` in `~/parcel-rates-issue-6` in 4 commits, not pushed. The servers on 8788 and 5174 are stopped and the working tree is clean.

**What's built**
- **Q3:**
  - **Answer:** the answer comes first and is the largest thing on the page: "USPS $21.09 per parcel", then the other carriers with their gap. Below it is the best mix (cheapest carrier per parcel) with its saving against the cheapest single carrier.
  - **Price verdict:** a red (or green) box asks "Does your $9.99 shipping price cover the cost?" and answers "No. You lose $10.98 per parcel with USPS". It also shows the share of parcels shipped at a loss and a margin table per carrier plus the best mix. Every amount has a sign and the word "loss" or "margin".
  - **Segment chips:** weight, zone band, address and speed. They re-query `/api/blended` with the segment, show "N of 300 parcels in this segment", and repeat the segment's result next to that count because the answer may be scrolled out of view. An empty segment says so.
  - **Cost chart:** Recharts stacked horizontal bars per carrier split into base, the top three surcharge kinds, "other surcharges" and fuel. Each row label shows the total and the surcharge and fuel shares.
  - **Parcels a carrier can't ship:** listed in a note under the chart.
- **Q4:**
  - **Answer:** "USPS +18.5% since 2023". USPS is the cheapest in 2026, the latest year all carriers publish. The caption gives $17.80 → $21.09 (+$3.29), the announced increases compounded over the same years (+16.4%, so the mix rose 2.1 points more than announced), and UPS and FedEx for the same years.
  - **Next-year slider:** starts at USPS's latest announced increase (6.5%), sends the value to the API after a short pause, shows the projected cost and has a reset button.
  - **Line chart:** each carrier has its own marker shape plus its colour. Dashed lines show the announced-increase path compounded from the first year, and dotted segments show the projection.
  - **Warnings:** points with a note get a "!" badge, and the notes are listed in plain words below the chart.
  - **Fuel:** a "How much of the change is fuel?" sentence per carrier and a small table of the fuel percent per year, with proxy years marked.
  - **Drivers:** a diverging bar chart of segment contributions. You choose carrier, year pair and dimension with chips. Bars are sorted by size, and a sentence names the top driver.
- **Both views:**
  - **Empty state:** "Load the sample mix" and "Upload CSV" buttons when no parcels are loaded.
  - **Accessibility:** every chart has a visible text summary and a "Show as table" toggle. Carrier colour is always paired with the name or a marker shape. The chips are 44 px tall.
- **Tests and docs:** the tests use the mock client and the existing fixtures; no new fixtures were needed. I appended a Q3/Q4 section to `frontend/DESIGN.md`.

**Shared code and files outside the brief**
- No shared helper existed for signed money, surcharge labels, chips or the chart frame, so they live in my own folder: `src/views/blended/money.ts`, `common.tsx` + `common.css`, `SegmentChips.tsx` and the test helper `testUtils.tsx`. Q4 imports them from there.
- `common.css` defines new colour variables on `:root` (`--q3-*` for the cost split, `--q4-up`/`--q4-down` for the driver bars), so they are global variables even though they sit in a view file.

**Screenshot review (12 files in `frontend/e2e/screenshots/q3-*.png` and `q4-*.png`)**
None of the screenshots showed horizontal page scroll. Problems I found and fixed:
- Chart row labels were cut off on the left ("JSPS", "urcharges").
- The driver chart's axis wasted its left half when every change was positive, had odd tick values (+$0.04), and its ticks were crowded on mobile.
- On mobile the margin table wrapped "−$10.98 / loss" onto two lines; the loss-share bar is now hidden there.
- The FedEx 2027 warning showed raw surcharge IDs; it now uses readable names.
- The fuel table stretched across the full width.
- The fuel colour in dark mode was too bright.
- Choosing a segment changed the answer out of view, which is why the result now also appears next to the parcel count.

What I left as is:
- The UPS and FedEx lines nearly overlap, because their costs really are within cents. Marker shapes and the table tell them apart.
- The assumptions rail appears mid-page in the full-page captures; it is the existing sticky rail, not part of these views.

**API and contract problems**
- **Mid-year editions:** `/api/yearly` returns no warning for the UPS 2024 (effective 1 Jul) and UPS 2026 (effective 7 Sep) price lists. The view works the note out itself from `as_of` (any month from March on). That rule also flags USPS 2023 (July tables), which is correct but comes from the frontend, not the backend.
- **Empty-state buttons:** `ViewProps` carries no load-sample or upload handlers, and I didn't edit `App.tsx`. The views accept optional `onLoadSample`/`onUploadCsv` props. When they aren't passed, as now, the buttons press the "Your parcels" panel's own sample button and file input. Passing the real handlers from `App.tsx` would be cleaner.
- **Projection:** the API applies one next-year percentage to every carrier, so the slider's projection uses USPS's announced figure for UPS and FedEx too. The view says so.
- **Carrier colours:** the palette checker rates the existing USPS and FedEx colours as hard to tell apart for colour-blind readers, in both themes. DESIGN.md already expected this, so I paired colour with names and marker shapes rather than changing the global tokens.
- **Bundle size:** Recharts now sits in the main bundle, at 181 KB gzipped, which is within the 300 KB budget. Lazy-loading the views would need a change in `App.tsx`.

**What the sample mix shows (300 parcels, 2026 prices)**
- **Cheapest carrier:** USPS at $21.09 per parcel, against UPS $42.68 and FedEx $43.15. Picking the cheapest carrier for each parcel (USPS 275, FedEx 15, UPS 10) gets $19.98, saving $1.11 per parcel ($332 on the set).
- **Loss at $9.99:** even with USPS the shop loses $10.98 per parcel, and 71% of parcels (214 of 300) ship at a loss. With UPS or FedEx every parcel loses money. Most of UPS's and FedEx's extra cost is fuel and surcharges: fuel is 21% of their cost and the residential surcharge alone is $4.90 per parcel.
- **Yearly change:** USPS rose 18.5% from 2023 to 2026, above the 16.4% announced; the 2025→2026 step was +10.7% against 6.5% announced. UPS and FedEx rose about 28–29% against about 18.8% announced. Fuel explains most of their 2025→2026 jump: UPS +$4.61 per parcel, of which fuel +$2.69 (58%); FedEx +$4.55, of which fuel +$2.72 (60%), as ground fuel went from 20.5% to 26.25%. Home deliveries are the top driver for UPS in that step: +$3.59 of the $4.61 (78%).

```
cd ~/parcel-rates-issue-6/frontend/src/views/yearly && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='logic.ts'; s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index('export function driverSentence'):s.index('/* ---------- warnings')]
new='''/** Change per parcel *within* the segment: its own parcels' change, independent of its size. */
export function withinChange(d: Driver): number {
  return d.parcels > 0 ? Math.round((d.change_total / d.parcels) * 100) / 100 : 0;
}

/** The segment whose own parcels moved most in the direction of the overall change. */
export function fastestSegment(list: Driver[], overall: number): Driver | null {
  const withParcels = list.filter((d) => d.parcels > 0);
  if (withParcels.length === 0) return null;
  const sign = overall >= 0 ? 1 : -1;
  return withParcels.reduce((best, d) => (sign * withinChange(d) > sign * withinChange(best) ? d : best));
}

export function driverSentence(carrier: Carrier, row: YearRow, dim: Dimension): string | null {
  const ch = row.change_vs_previous;
  const list = row.drivers?.[dim];
  if (!ch || !list || list.length === 0) return null;
  const top = sortedDrivers(list)[0]!;
  const name = carrierName(carrier);
  const span = `${ch.from_year} to ${row.year}`;
  const what = segmentPhrase(dim, top.segment);
  const share = ch.dollars_per_parcel !== 0 ? Math.round((top.change_per_parcel / ch.dollars_per_parcel) * 100) : null;
  const shareText = share !== null && share > 0 ? `, ${share}% of it` : "";
  const direction = top.change_per_parcel >= 0 ? "added" : "took off";
  const first =
    `Largest contributor: ${what} (${top.parcels} of them) ${direction} ${formatUsd(Math.abs(top.change_per_parcel))} per parcel ` +
    `of ${name}'s ${signedUsd(ch.dollars_per_parcel)} change from ${span}${shareText}.`;
  const fast = fastestSegment(list, ch.dollars_per_parcel);
  if (!fast) return first;
  const verb = ch.dollars_per_parcel >= 0 ? "rising" : "falling";
  if (fast.segment === top.segment) return `${first} Its own parcels also changed fastest: ${signedUsd(withinChange(fast))} each.`;
  const fastWhat = segmentPhrase(dim, fast.segment);
  const fastShare = Math.round((fast.parcels / list.reduce((n, d) => n + d.parcels, 0)) * 100);
  return (
    `${first} Fastest ${verb}: ${fastWhat}, ${signedUsd(withinChange(fast))} each, ` +
    `but they are only ${fastShare}% of the parcels (${fast.parcels}), so they move the average less.`
  );
}

'''
s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

import { YearChart } from "./yearly/YearChart";
import { DriverChart } from "./yearly/DriverChart";
import { pointNotes } from "./yearly/logic";
import { stubResizeObserver } from "./blended/testUtils";

vi.mock("recharts", async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import("recharts")>();
  return {
    ...actual,
    ResponsiveContainer: ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) =>
      isValidElement(children) ? cloneElement(children as ReactElement<{ width: number; height: number }>, { width: 600, height: 300 }) : null,
  };
});

beforeEach(() => stubResizeObserver());

const FOCUSABLE = 'a[href], button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';

function expectNoHiddenFocusStop(container: HTMLElement) {
  const hidden = container.querySelector('[aria-hidden="true"]');
  expect(hidden).not.toBeNull();
  expect(hidden!.querySelector("svg")).not.toBeNull(); // the chart really rendered
  expect(hidden!.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE)).toHaveLength(0);
  expect(hidden!.querySelector('[role="application"]')).toBeNull();
}

describe("charts inside aria-hidden wrappers", () => {
  it("cost split chart has no focus stop", () => {
    const { container } = render(<CostSplitChart data={mockBlendedResponse} />);
    expectNoHiddenFocusStop(container);
  });

  it("year chart has no focus stop", () => {
    const { container } = render(<YearChart data={mockYearlyResponse} notes={pointNotes(mockYearlyResponse)} />);
    expectNoHiddenFocusStop(container);
  });

  it("driver chart has no focus stop", () => {
    const ups = mockYearlyResponse.carriers.find((c) => c.carrier === "ups")!;
    const row = ups.years.find((y) => y.year === 2026)!;
    const { container } = render(<DriverChart carrier="ups" row={row} dim="speed" />);
    expectNoHiddenFocusStop(container);
  });
});
EOF

4. **Fuel step:** `biggestFuelStep` now returns nothing when no year was a rise, and its comment says so. Tested with a FedEx version whose cost only ever falls.
5. **No parcels at a loss:** Q3 now says "Every parcel covers its cost with USPS." If the best mix would still lose money on some parcels, it adds that share. Tested.
6. **Colour tokens:** the `--q3-*` and `--q4-*` colours moved into `src/styles/tokens.css` for both light and dark. `common.css` now just points there, and `DESIGN.md` says where they live.

1	# Processed data schema
2	
3	All tables live under `data/processed/` as UTF-8 CSV with a header row. Column
4	names are snake_case. Money is a decimal string with two places in USD. Dates
5	are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Booleans are `true` or `false`. Empty string means null.
6	
7	Two kinds of tables:
8	
9	- **Parsed** tables are generated by `data/pipeline/` from the raw files and
10	  are never edited by hand (`base_rates.csv`).
11	- **Curated** tables are transcribed from the documents. Every row carries a
12	  citation (`source_file`, `source_ref` or `source_page`, `source_quote`) and
13	  the test suite checks that the quote, including the amount, appears on the
14	  cited page of the cited file.
15	
16	`year` everywhere is the price-list label: the list prices that took effect in
17	January of that year (USPS 2023 uses the July 9 2023 tables; FedEx 2027 is the
18	forward year). `effective_date`, `effective_from` and `effective_to` record the
19	actual dates, because some rules change inside a year.
20	
21	## Layout
22	
23	Each carrier's pipeline writes only to its own directory, so parsers can be
24	built independently and never conflict:
25	
26	```
27	data/processed/
28	  services.csv                 shared, curated
29	  zone_from_distance.csv       shared, curated
30	  usps/  base_rates.csv  surcharges.csv  fuel_surcharge.csv  announced_increase.csv  dim_weight.csv  exceptions.csv
31	  ups/   (same files)
32	  fedex/ (same files)
33	```
34	
35	The backend loads every carrier directory and concatenates tables of the
36	same name. A carrier with no fuel surcharge ships a header-only file.
37	
38	## Identifiers
39	
40	| Field | Values |
41	|---|---|
42	| `carrier` | `usps`, `ups`, `fedex` |
43	| `rate_card` | USPS: `retail` (counter price) or `commercial` (online postage, the default for USPS in the dashboard, switchable to retail). UPS and FedEx: `list` (Daily Rates / Standard List Rates, what a shipper without a contract pays). `services.csv` explains in one line what each card means for each carrier. The README repeats this. |
44	| `tier` | `ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day` |
45	| `service_id` | see `services.csv` |
46	| `unit` | `usd` (flat amount) or `percent` |
47	
48	## services.csv (shared, curated)
49	
50	| Column | Type | Notes |
51	|---|---|---|
52	| carrier | id | |
53	| service_id | id | `usps_ground_advantage`, `usps_priority_mail`, `usps_priority_mail_express`, `ups_ground`, `ups_3_day_select`, `ups_2nd_day_air`, `ups_next_day_air_saver`, `ups_next_day_air`, `fedex_ground`, `fedex_home_delivery`, `fedex_express_saver`, `fedex_2day`, `fedex_standard_overnight`, `fedex_priority_overnight` |
54	| display_name | text | Carrier's own name |
55	| tier | tier | Speed tier the service competes in |
56	| residential_allowed | bool | FedEx Ground is business only; Home Delivery is residential only |
57	| business_allowed | bool | |
58	| rate_cards | text | Comma-separated list of rate cards published for this service: `retail,commercial` for USPS, `list` for UPS and FedEx |
59	| rate_card_notes | text | One line per card, `card: meaning`, separated by `;`. E.g. USPS: `retail: price paid at the Post Office counter; commercial: price paid with online postage or shipping software, no contract needed`. UPS: `list: published Daily Rates for shippers without a negotiated contract` |
60	| max_weight_lb | int | 70 for USPS, 150 for UPS and FedEx (the app caps at 70) |
61	| notes | text | |
62	
63	## base_rates.csv (parsed, per carrier)
64	
65	One row per price cell.
66	
67	| Column | Type | Notes |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| carrier | id | |
70	| service_id | id | |
71	| rate_card | id | |
72	| year | int | |
73	| effective_date | date | |
74	| zone | int | USPS 1–9 (rows for both 1 and 2 even when equal); UPS and FedEx 2–8 |
75	| max_weight_lb | decimal | Upper bound of the weight step in pounds. USPS Ground Advantage ounce steps are `0.25`, `0.5`, `0.75`, `0.9999` (15.999 oz), then `1` … `70`. UPS and FedEx `1` … `70` |
76	| price | money | |
77	| source_file | path | Relative to `data/raw/` |
78	| source_ref | text | Sheet name, or PDF file page index (1-based) |
79	
80	Alaska and Hawaii columns (UPS zones 44–46, FedEx AK/HI zones, USPS zone 9
81	when the document marks it as such) are parsed only if they fall out of the
82	same table; they are excluded from the dashboard and listed in
83	`exceptions.csv` with kind `ak_hi_zone` so the exclusion is explicit.
84	
85	### Invariants: warnings, with every exception documented
86	
87	The invariant checks never silently pass. Each anomaly is either listed in the
88	carrier's `exceptions.csv` (then the test emits a warning) or it fails the test.
89	This forces every oddity in a rate card to be written down.
90	
91	Checks:
92	
93	- For each (carrier, service_id, rate_card, year): every zone in the carrier's
94	  range is present with the same set of weight steps, strictly increasing,
95	  with no gaps up to 70 lb.
96	- Within a zone, price is non-decreasing with weight. Within a weight step,
97	  price is non-decreasing with zone.
98	- Prices have at most two decimals and no float artifacts (e.g. `15.999000000000001` in a weight label).
99	- Every `source_file` exists in `data/raw/manifest.csv`.
100

103	| Column | Notes |

106	| zone, max_weight_lb | Cell, or empty for a whole table |
107	| kind | `ak_hi_zone`, `rounding_artifact`, `non_monotonic`, `missing_cell`, `page_shift`, `step_structure_change`, `other` |
108	| note | What the document shows and how the parser treats it |
109	| source_file, source_ref | Where to look |
110	
111	### Golden samples
112	
113	`data/tests/golden/<carrier>_<year>.csv` holds hand-checked cells with the
114	`base_rates.csv` columns plus `checked_by` (person or "agent" plus date) and
115	`source_ref`. The parsed output must match every golden cell exactly.
116	
117	Mandatory cells for each (service_id, rate_card, year), because column and
118	page shifts in the PDFs corrupt exactly these corners:
119	
120	1. heaviest weight step (70 lb) in the farthest zone
121	2. heaviest weight step in the nearest zone
122	3. lightest weight step in the farthest zone
123	4. at least two interior cells on different pages or sheets of the source
124	
125	Minimum five cells per (service_id, rate_card, year).
126	
127	## surcharges.csv (curated, per carrier)
128	
129	One row per surcharge rule, per year and effective window. A rule applies when
130	every non-empty threshold column is met and the `as_of` date falls inside its
131	window.
132	
133	| Column | Type | Notes |
134	|---|---|---|
135	| carrier | id | |
136	| year | int | |
137	| rate_card | id | Empty means all rate cards |
138	| surcharge_id | id | Stable id, e.g. `ups_residential_ground_2025` |
139	| display_name | text | Carrier's own name |
140	| condition | enum | `residential`, `delivery_area`, `delivery_area_extended`, `additional_handling_weight`, `additional_handling_length`, `additional_handling_width`, `additional_handling_packaging`, `oversize`, `nonstandard_length`, `nonstandard_volume`, `peak_residential`, `peak_additional_handling`, `peak_oversize`, `peak_base`, `transportation_time_limited` |
141	| applies_to | text | `all`, `ground`, `air`, or a comma-separated list of `service_id` |
142	| address_type | enum | `any`, `residential` or `commercial`. Carriers price delivery-area and large-package surcharges differently for homes and businesses; a rule only applies to parcels of its address type |
143	| min_weight_lb | decimal | Billable weight threshold |
144	| max_weight_lb | decimal | For banded tables such as USPS peak add-ons |
145	| min_length_in | decimal | Longest side |
146	| min_width_in | decimal | Second-longest side (UPS and FedEx additional handling: over 30 in) |
147	| min_length_plus_girth_in | decimal | |
148	| min_volume_cuft | decimal | |
149	| zone_min | int | |
150	| zone_max | int | |
151	| amount | decimal | |
152	| unit | unit | |
153	| exclusive_group | text | Rules in the same group do not stack; the highest matching amount applies |
154	| effective_from | date | |
155	| effective_to | date | Empty means open-ended |
156	| fuel_applies | bool | Whether the carrier applies the fuel surcharge on top of this charge |
157	| source_file | path | |
158	| source_page | int | File page index, 1-based; empty for HTML or XLSX |
159	| source_quote | text | Verbatim snippet containing the amount |
160	| notes | text | |
161	
162	Peak rules apply only when the dashboard's peak toggle is on. Rules with
163	`address_type` `residential` or `commercial` apply only to parcels of that kind.
164	Delivery area rules apply when the parcel's `delivery_area` is `das` or
165	`extended`. `additional_handling_packaging` rules apply when the parcel is
166	flagged `nonstandard_packaging` (UPS and FedEx: non-corrugated or cylindrical
167	packaging; USPS from 2026: tubes or rolls, cans, wooden or metal boxes, liquids
168	in glass).
169	
170	## fuel_surcharge.csv (curated, per carrier)
171	
172	| Column | Type | Notes |
173	|---|---|---|
174	| carrier | id | USPS ships a header-only file |
175	| year | int | |
176	| service_group | enum | `ground`, `express` |
177	| default_percent | decimal | Yearly default used by the dashboard |
178	| basis | text | Always "base rate plus surcharges flagged fuel_applies"; recorded per row so a carrier-specific deviation can be stated |
179	| window_start | date | Window of published weekly values the default was taken from |
180	| window_end | date | |
181	| is_proxy | bool | `true` for UPS rows derived from FedEx history |
182	| source_file | path | |
183	| source_ref | text | |
184	| source_quote | text | |
185	| notes | text | |
186	
187	### Engine tests for fuel
188	
189	The rate engine applies the fuel percent to the base rate plus every applied
190	surcharge whose `fuel_applies` is `true`, and to nothing else. Tests use
191	synthetic rows: one surcharge flagged `true`, one flagged `false`, a known
192	percent, and assert the fuel line item equals `percent × (base + flagged)` to
193	the cent, that the slider override replaces the yearly default, and that USPS
194	quotes carry no fuel line.
195	
196	## announced_increase.csv (curated, per carrier)
197	
198	| Column | Type | Notes |
199	|---|---|---|
200	| carrier | id | |
201	| year | int | |
202	| product_scope | text | `all`, a `service_id`, or the carrier's product name |
203	| rate_card | id | Empty means all |
204	| percent | decimal | Negative for a decrease (USPS Ground Advantage launch, July 2023); the citation quote then reads "decrease N percent" |
205	| source_type | enum | `primary` (carrier document) or `secondary` (trade press) |
206	| source_file | path | |
207	| source_ref | text | |
208	| source_quote | text | |
209	
210	## dim_weight.csv (curated, per carrier)
211	
212	Dimensional weight parameters change over time (USPS moved from 166 to 139
213	on 2026-07-12), so rows carry an effective window and the engine resolves the
214	row by `as_of` date.
215	
216	| Column | Type | Notes |
217	|---|---|---|
218	| carrier | id | |
219	| year | int | |
220	| effective_from | date | |
221	| effective_to | date | Empty means open-ended |
222	| divisor | int | |
223	| min_volume_cuin | int | 0 for UPS and FedEx; 1728 for USPS |
224	| rounding | text | e.g. "round each dimension to nearest inch, round dim weight up to next pound" |
225	| source_file | path | |
226	| source_ref | text | |
227	| source_quote | text | |
228	
229	## Rules that change over time
230	
231	Every parameter that can move a parcel's price is stored per year and per
232	effective window: base rates, surcharge amounts and thresholds, fuel defaults,
233	dimensional-weight divisor and threshold. The engine takes an `as_of` date
234	(default: the year's January effective date) and never hardcodes a value.
235	
236	`uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes` diffs consecutive years of
237	every curated table and writes `docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md`: one line per
238	parameter that changed, with old and new values and the citation. The parser
239	agents must populate every year so this report is complete, and the report is
240	reviewed before the engine is built so year-over-year comparisons account for
241	every change, not only base rates.
242	
243	## zone_from_distance.csv (shared, curated)
244	
245	| Column | Type | Notes |
246	|---|---|---|
247	| carrier | id | USPS bands differ from UPS and FedEx bands |
248	| zone | int | |
249	| min_miles | int | Inclusive |
250	| max_miles | int | Inclusive; empty for the last band |
251	| source_file | path | Must be a file listed in the manifest (add a row and run the fetcher; never download by hand) |
252	| source_quote | text | Verbatim |
253	| notes | text | e.g. how a band was derived when the carrier publishes zones only by ZIP pair |
254	
255	## Raw manifest: data/raw/manifest.csv
256	
257	| Column | Notes |
258	|---|---|
259	| carrier | `usps`, `ups`, `fedex` |
260	| year | or empty |
261	| path | relative to `data/raw/` |
262	| url | exact URL; Wayback URLs use the `id_` passthrough form |
263	| method | `direct` or `wayback` |
264	| sha256 | hex digest |
265	| bytes | size |
266	| in_git | `true` for spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML; `false` for PDFs |
267	| content | one line |
268	
269	`python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores missing files sequentially with pauses
270	and verifies checksums; issue #13 scripts the discovery that produces this file.
271	
272	## Parcel set input (CSV uploaded in the UI)
273	
274	| Column | Type | Notes |
275	|---|---|---|
276	| weight_lb | decimal | Required |
277	| length_in, width_in, height_in | decimal | Optional; dimensional weight only when all three are present |
278	| distance_miles | int | Required |
279	| residential | bool | Required |
280	| speed | tier | Required |
281	| quantity | int | Optional, default 1 |
282	| price_charged | money | Optional; overrides the flat price control for that row |
283	| delivery_area | enum | Optional: `none` (default), `das`, `extended` |
284	| nonstandard_packaging | bool | Optional, default `false`. Packaging that triggers handling fees: not a corrugated box, cylindrical, a can or wooden or metal box, liquids in glass |
285	
286	The USPS rate card (`commercial` default, `retail` optional) is a dashboard
287	control, not a parcel column. UPS and FedEx have a single `list` card.
288

"""Shared conventions for the per-carrier pipelines.

Column lists mirror docs/data/SCHEMA.md. Every pipeline writes only to
PROCESSED_DIR / <carrier> and reads raw files through `raw_path`, which
refuses files that are not in the manifest or not on disk.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import html
import re
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterable

DATA_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
RAW_DIR = DATA_DIR / "raw"
PROCESSED_DIR = DATA_DIR / "processed"
MANIFEST = RAW_DIR / "manifest.csv"

CARRIERS = ("usps", "ups", "fedex")
RATE_CARDS = {"usps": ("retail", "commercial"), "ups": ("list",), "fedex": ("list",)}
ZONES = {"usps": range(1, 10), "ups": range(2, 9), "fedex": range(2, 9)}
MAX_WEIGHT_LB = 70
USPS_OUNCE_STEPS = ("0.25", "0.5", "0.75", "0.9999")

COLUMNS = {
    "services": [
        "carrier", "service_id", "display_name", "tier", "residential_allowed",
        "business_allowed", "rate_cards", "rate_card_notes", "max_weight_lb", "notes",
    ],
    "base_rates": [
        "carrier", "service_id", "rate_card", "year", "effective_date", "zone",
        "max_weight_lb", "price", "source_file", "source_ref",
    ],
    "exceptions": [
        "carrier", "service_id", "rate_card", "year", "zone", "max_weight_lb",
        "kind", "note", "source_file", "source_ref",
    ],
    "surcharges": [
        "carrier", "year", "rate_card", "surcharge_id", "display_name", "condition",
        "applies_to", "address_type", "min_weight_lb", "max_weight_lb", "min_length_in",
        "min_width_in", "min_length_plus_girth_in", "min_volume_cuft", "zone_min", "zone_max",
        "amount", "unit", "exclusive_group", "effective_from", "effective_to",
        "fuel_applies", "source_file", "source_page", "source_quote", "notes",
    ],
    "fuel_surcharge": [
        "carrier", "year", "service_group", "default_percent", "basis",
        "window_start", "window_end", "is_proxy", "source_file", "source_ref",
        "source_quote", "notes",
    ],
    "announced_increase": [
        "carrier", "year", "product_scope", "rate_card", "percent", "source_type",
        "source_file", "source_ref", "source_quote",
    ],
    "dim_weight": [
        "carrier", "year", "effective_from", "effective_to", "divisor",
        "min_volume_cuin", "rounding", "source_file", "source_ref", "source_quote",
    ],
    "zone_from_distance": [
        "carrier", "zone", "min_miles", "max_miles", "source_file", "source_quote", "notes",
    ],
}
ADDRESS_TYPES = ("any", "residential", "commercial")
CURATED_TABLES = ("surcharges", "fuel_surcharge", "announced_increase", "dim_weight")
EXCEPTION_KINDS = (
    "ak_hi_zone", "rounding_artifact", "non_monotonic", "missing_cell",
    "page_shift", "step_structure_change", "other",
)
SURCHARGE_CONDITIONS = (
    "residential", "delivery_area", "delivery_area_extended",
    "additional_handling_weight", "additional_handling_length",
    "additional_handling_width", "additional_handling_packaging", "oversize",
    "nonstandard_length", "nonstandard_volume", "peak_residential",
    "peak_additional_handling", "peak_oversize", "peak_base",
    "transportation_time_limited",
)


def money(value: Decimal | str | float) -> str:
    """Format a price with exactly two decimals, rounding half up."""
    return str(Decimal(str(value)).quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP))


def weight_label(value: Decimal | str | float) -> str:
    """Normalize a weight step label: integers as '12', ounce steps as in USPS_OUNCE_STEPS."""
    dec = Decimal(str(value)).normalize()
    if dec == dec.to_integral_value():
        return str(int(dec))
    text = format(dec, "f")
    return text if text in USPS_OUNCE_STEPS else text


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def manifest_rows() -> list[dict]:
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))


def manifest_paths() -> set[str]:
    return {row["path"] for row in manifest_rows()}


def raw_path(relative: str) -> Path:
    """Return the on-disk path of a raw file, insisting it is in the manifest and present."""
    if relative not in manifest_paths():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{relative} is not listed in data/raw/manifest.csv")
    path = RAW_DIR / relative
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"{relative} is missing; run `python3 data/fetch_raw.py`")
    return path


def processed_path(carrier: str, table: str) -> Path:
    if carrier == "shared":
        return PROCESSED_DIR / f"{table}.csv"
    return PROCESSED_DIR / carrier / f"{table}.csv"


def write_table(carrier: str, table: str, rows: Iterable[dict]) -> Path:
    """Write rows with the schema's column order. Missing keys become empty strings;
    unknown keys are an error so typos cannot slip through."""
    columns = COLUMNS[table]
    path = processed_path(carrier, table)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    rows = list(rows)
    for row in rows:
        unknown = set(row) - set(columns)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"{table}: unknown columns {sorted(unknown)}")
    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=columns, lineterminator="\n")
        writer.writeheader()
        for row in rows:
            writer.writerow({column: row.get(column, "") for column in columns})
    return path


def read_table(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    if not path.is_file():
        return []
    with path.open(newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return list(csv.DictReader(handle))


_WHITESPACE = re.compile(r"\s+")


def normalize_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Collapse whitespace and unify quotes/dashes so quotes can be matched across PDF line breaks."""
    text = text.replace("’", "'").replace("‘", "'").replace("“", '"').replace("”", '"')
    text = text.replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-").replace(" ", " ")
    return _WHITESPACE.sub(" ", text).strip().lower()


@lru_cache(maxsize=4)
def _open_pdf(path: Path):
    import pdfplumber

    return pdfplumber.open(path)


@lru_cache(maxsize=2048)
def pdf_page_text(path: Path, page: int) -> str:
    """Text of a 1-based page index, via pdfplumber. Open documents and extracted
    pages are cached, so citing many rows from one guide stays fast."""
    pdf = _open_pdf(path)
    if page < 1 or page > len(pdf.pages):
        raise IndexError(f"{path.name} has {len(pdf.pages)} pages, asked for {page}")
    return pdf.pages[page - 1].extract_text() or ""


def html_text(path: Path) -> str:
    raw = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    raw = re.sub(r"<(script|style)[^>]*>.*?</\1>", " ", raw, flags=re.S | re.I)
    return html.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", raw))


def xlsx_text(path: Path, sheet: str | None = None) -> str:
    import openpyxl

    book = openpyxl.load_workbook(path, read_only=True, data_only=True)
    sheets = [book[sheet]] if sheet and sheet in book.sheetnames else book.worksheets
    parts: list[str] = []
    for ws in sheets:
        for row in ws.iter_rows(values_only=True):
            parts.extend(str(cell) for cell in row if cell is not None)
    return " ".join(parts)


def source_text(source_file: str, source_ref: str | int | None) -> str:
    """Text of the cited location: PDF page, XLSX sheet, or whole HTML/CSV file."""
    path = raw_path(source_file)
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix == ".pdf":
        return pdf_page_text(path, int(source_ref))
    if suffix == ".xlsx":
        return xlsx_text(path, str(source_ref) if source_ref else None)
    if suffix in {".htm", ".html"}:
        return html_text(path)
    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

1	"""Tracked raw files must be present and match their manifest checksum."""
2	from __future__ import annotations
3	
4	import hashlib
5	
6	import pytest
7	
8	from data.pipeline.common import RAW_DIR, manifest_rows
9	
10	
11	def sha256_of(path) -> str:
12	    digest = hashlib.sha256()
13	    with path.open("rb") as handle:
14	        for chunk in iter(lambda: handle.read(1 << 20), b""):
15	            digest.update(chunk)
16	    return digest.hexdigest()
17	
18

332	# Zone distance bands, DMM 608.9.4.2 (live page, fetched 2026-10-23).
333	# USPS: zone 1 up to 50 miles, zone 2 to 150, zone 3 to 300, zone 4 to 600,
334	# zone 5 to 1,000, zone 6 to 1,400, zone 7 to 1,800, zone 8 beyond; zone 9 is
335	# not a distance band (Palau, Micronesia, Marshall Islands).
336	# UPS and FedEx publish zones only by ZIP pair; their zone 2 covers 0-150 miles
337	# (USPS zones 1 and 2 together) and their zone n for n >= 3 uses the USPS zone n band.
338	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

340	USPS_ZONE_BANDS = [

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE                                               Contact: David P. Coleman
Sept. 5, 2024                                                       david.p.coleman@usps.gov
                                                                                usps.com/news



     U.S. Postal Service Proposes Temporary Rate Changes
                for 2024 Holiday Shipping Season

WASHINGTON — The U.S. Postal Service filed notice today with the Postal Regulatory
Commission (PRC) regarding a temporary price change for some package services for the
2024 peak holiday season. This temporary price adjustment is to help cover extra handling
costs to ensure a successful peak season.

The planned peak-season pricing, which was approved by the governors of the Postal Service
on Aug. 8, would affect prices on the following commercial and retail domestic competitive
parcels: Priority Mail Express (PME), Priority Mail (PM) and USPS Ground Advantage. No
other products or services would be affected. Pending favorable review by the PRC, the
temporary rates would go into effect at midnight Central on Oct. 6 and remain in place until
midnight Central on Jan. 19, 2025.

This seasonal adjustment will bring prices for the Postal Service’s commercial and retail
customers in line with competitive practices.

As a strategic part of the Delivering for America 10-year plan, these temporary changes will
support the Postal Service in creating a revitalized organization capable of achieving our
public service mission — providing a nationwide, integrated network for the delivery of mail and
packages at least six days a week — in a cost-effective and financially sustainable manner
over the long term, just as the U.S. Congress has intended.

The planned price changes include:

Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage: Zone 1-4
    • Commercial:
            o $0.30 cents increase for Zones 1-4, 0-3 lbs.
            o $0.45 cents increase for Zones 1-4, 4-10 lbs.
            o $0.75 cents increase for Zones 1-4, 11-25 lbs.
            o $3.00 increase for Zones 1-4, 26-70 lbs.

Priority Mail Zone 5-9

            o $1.25 increase for Zones 5-9, 4-10 lbs.
            o $2.75 increase for Zones 5-9, 11-25 lbs.
            o $7.00 increase for Zones 5-9, 26-70 lbs.

USPS Ground Advantage Zone 5-9
         o $0.35 cents increase for Zones 5-9, 0-3 lbs.
         o $0.75 cents increase for Zones 5-9, 4-10 lbs.
         o $1.25 increase for Zones 5-9, 11-25 lbs.
         o $5.50 increase for Zones 5-9, 26-70 lbs.
                                                         2


Priority Mail and USPS Ground Advantage: Zone 1-4
        Retail:
            o $0.40 cents increase for Zones 1-4, 0-3 lbs.

            o $0.95 cents increase for Zones 1-4, 11-25 lbs.
            o $4.00 increase for Zones 1-4, 26-70 lbs

Priority Mail Zone 5-9
               o $0.90 cents increase for Zones 5-9, 0-3 lbs.

The PRC will review the proposed prices before they are scheduled to take effect Oct. 6.
Complete USPS price filings, with prices for all products, can be found on the PRC website’s
Daily Listings section at prc.gov/dockets/daily. Price change tables are also available on the
Postal Explorer website at pe.usps.com/PriceChange/Index.

Notably, the Postal Service has some of the lowest postage rates in the industrialized world

20	    COLUMNS, RATE_CARDS, ZONES, money, raw_path, weight_label, write_table,
21	)

23	CARRIER = "usps"
24	ZONE_HEADER = re.compile(r"^\s*zone\s*(\d)\s*$", re.I)
25	WEIGHT_CELL = re.compile(r"^\d+(\.\d+)?$")
26	OUNCES_PER_POUND = Decimal(16)
27	POUND_PRECISION = Decimal("0.0001")
28	
29	
30	def find_zone_header(rows: list[list[str]]) -> tuple[int, dict[int, int]]:
31	    """Return (row index, {zone: column index}) of the first row whose cells read 'Zone 1' .. 'Zone 9'.
32	
33	    The preamble above it (title, flat-rate prices, 'Weight Not Over' line) is irregular,
34	    so the header is located by content rather than by position."""
35	    for index, row in enumerate(rows):
36	        zones = {}
37	        for column, cell in enumerate(row):
38	            match = ZONE_HEADER.match(cell)
39	            if match:
40	                zones[int(match.group(1))] = column
41	        if 1 in zones:
42	            return index, zones
43	    raise ValueError("no 'Zone 1' header row found")
44	
45	
46	def ounces_to_pounds(ounces: str) -> str:
47	    """'4' -> '0.25', '15.999000000000001' -> '0.9999' (truncated to 4 decimals, so the
48	    float artifact in the CSV cannot leak into the label)."""
49	    pounds = (Decimal(ounces) / OUNCES_PER_POUND).quantize(POUND_PRECISION, rounding=ROUND_DOWN)
50	    return weight_label(pounds)
51	
52	
53	def parse_price_csv(text: str) -> tuple[list[tuple[str, dict[int, str]]], list[str]]:
54	    """Parse one Postal Explorer price CSV into ([(max_weight_lb, {zone: price})], skipped_labels).
55	
56	    Weight rows start with a number; the unit is ounces while the table is under a
57	    'Weight Not Over (ounces)' line and switches to pounds at the 'Weight Not Over
58	    (pounds)' marker row. Non-numeric first cells (flat-rate rows, 'Oversized',
59	    footnotes) are skipped and reported."""
60	    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))
61	    header_index, zone_columns = find_zone_header(rows)
62	    unit = "oz" if any("ounce" in cell.lower() for row in rows[:header_index] for cell in row) else "lb"
63	    steps: list[tuple[str, dict[int, str]]] = []
64	    skipped: list[str] = []
65	    for row in rows[header_index + 1:]:
66	        first = row[0].strip() if row else ""
67	        if not first:
68	            continue
69	        if "pound" in first.lower() or "(lbs" in first.lower():
70	            unit = "lb"
71	            continue
72	        if not WEIGHT_CELL.match(first):
73	            skipped.append(first)
74	            continue
75	        label = ounces_to_pounds(first) if unit == "oz" else weight_label(Decimal(first))
76	        prices = {}
77	        for zone, column in zone_columns.items():
78	            cell = row[column].strip() if column < len(row) else ""
79	            if not cell:
80	                raise ValueError(f"step {first}: empty price for zone {zone}")
81	            prices[zone] = money(cell)
82	        steps.append((label, prices))
83	    if not steps:
84	        raise ValueError("no weight rows below the zone header")
85	    return steps, skipped

89	    with zipfile.ZipFile(raw_path(zip_relative)) as archive:
90	        return archive.read(member).decode("utf-8-sig")

274	def amounts_in(quote: str) -> list[str]:
275	    """Dollar amounts in a quote, in order, as two-decimal strings."""
276	    return [m.replace(",", "") for m in re.findall(r"\$\s?([\d,]+\.\d{2})", quote)]

52	    def zone_columns(self, code_map: dict[str, int]) -> tuple[dict[int, int], list[str]]:
53	        """Return {column index: zone} for the carrier's zones and the excluded codes (AK/HI/PR)."""
54	        zones, excluded = {}, []

75	def group_lines(words: list[dict], tolerance: float = ROW_TOLERANCE) -> list[list[dict]]:

301	    return rows
302	
303	
304	def large_package_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
305	    spec = rules.LARGE_PACKAGE[year]
306	    rows = []
307	    for (address, criterion), quote in spec["quotes"].items():
308	        thresholds, note = rules.LPS_CRITERIA[criterion]
309	        rows.extend(banded_rows(
310	            year, quote, spec["bands"], surcharge_id=f"ups_large_package_{address}_{criterion}_{year}",
311	            display_name="Large Package Surcharge", condition="oversize", applies_to="all", address_type=address,
312	            exclusive_group="ups_handling", source_page=str(spec["page"]),
313	            notes=(f"{address.capitalize()} deliveries only. Criterion: {note}. Large Packages carry a 90 lb minimum "
314	                   f"billable weight (not modelled). {rules.FUEL_NOTE[year]}"), **thresholds))
315	    return rows
316	
317	
318	def peak_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
319	    spec = rules.PEAK.get(year)
320	    if not spec:
321	        return []
322	    rows = []
323	    for item in spec["rows"]:
324	        amounts = rules.amounts_in(item["quote"])
325	        if len(amounts) != len(item["windows"]):
326	            raise ValueError(f"{year} {item['condition']}: {len(amounts)} amounts for {len(item['windows'])} windows")
327	        for amount, window in zip(amounts, item["windows"]):
328	            if window is None:
329	                continue
330	            start, end = window
331	            rows.append(surcharge_row(
332	                year, surcharge_id=f"ups_{item['condition']}_{year}_{start}", display_name="Demand Surcharge",
333	                condition=item["condition"], applies_to=item["applies_to"], amount=amount,
334	                address_type="residential" if item["condition"] == "peak_residential" else "any",
335	                exclusive_group=item["condition"], effective_from=start, effective_to=end,
336	                source_file=spec["file"], source_page=str(item["page"]), source_quote=item["quote"],
337	                notes="; ".join(filter(None, [spec["note"], item.get("note"),
338	                                              "fuel_applies assumed from the guide's statement that fuel may apply to surcharges"]))))
339	    return rows
340	
341	
342	def surcharges() -> list[dict]:
343	    rows = []
344	    for year in rules.YEARS:
345	        rows += residential_rows(year) + delivery_area_rows(year) + additional_handling_rows(year)
346	        rows += large_package_rows(year) + peak_rows(year)
347	    return rows
348	
349	
350	def announced_increase() -> list[dict]:
351	    rows = []
352	    for year, spec in rules.ANNOUNCED_INCREASE.items():
353	        match = re.search(r"(\d+\.\d+)%", spec["quote"])
354	        if not match:
355	            raise ValueError(f"{year}: no percent in {spec['quote']!r}")
356	        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "product_scope": "all", "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD,
357	                     "percent": match.group(1), "source_type": "secondary", "source_file": spec["file"],
358	                     "source_ref": "", "source_quote": spec["quote"]})
359	    return rows
360	
361	
362	def dim_weight() -> list[dict]:
363	    rows = []
364	    for year, spec in rules.DIM_WEIGHT.items():
365	        guide = rules.GUIDES[year]
366	        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "effective_from": guide["effective_date"],
367	                     "effective_to": "", "divisor": "139", "min_volume_cuin": "0", "rounding": spec["rounding"],
368	                     "source_file": guide["file"], "source_ref": str(spec["page"]), "source_quote": spec["quote"]})
369	    return rows
370	
371	
372	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
373	# Fuel surcharge proxies from the FedEx historical pages
374	
375	MONTHS = {"jan": 1, "feb": 2, "mar": 3, "apr": 4, "may": 5, "jun": 6, "jul": 7, "aug": 8, "sep": 9, "oct": 10, "nov": 11, "dec": 12}
376	DATE = r"(?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|June?|July?|Aug|Sept?|Oct|Nov|Dec)\.? \d{1,2}, \d{4}"
377	WEEK_ROW = re.compile(rf"({DATE})\s*[-\u2013\u2014]\s*({DATE})")
378	PERCENT = re.compile(r"\d+\.\d+%")
379	
380	
381	def parse_date(text: str) -> date:
382	    month, day, year = re.match(r"([A-Za-z]+)\.? (\d{1,2}), (\d{4})", text).groups()
383	    return date(int(year), MONTHS[month[:3].lower()], int(day))
384	
385	
386	@dataclass
387	class WeekRow:
388	    start: date
389	    end: date
390	    text: str          # row text as it appears in the collapsed page text
391	    percents: list[str]
392	
393	
394	def parse_fuel_rows(page_text: str) -> list[WeekRow]:
395	    """Weekly rows of the first (package) table on a FedEx historical fuel page."""
396	    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", page_text)
397	    starts = [m for m in WEEK_ROW.finditer(text)]
398	    rows = []
399	    for current, following in zip(starts, starts[1:] + [None]):
400	        end = following.start() if following else len(text)
401	        segment = text[current.start():end]
402	        segment = segment.split(" previous ")[0].split(" Previous ")[0].strip()
403	        percents = PERCENT.findall(segment)
404	        if not percents:
405	            continue
406	        rows.append(WeekRow(parse_date(current.group(1)), parse_date(current.group(2)), segment, percents))
407	    if not rows:
408	        raise ValueError("no weekly fuel rows found")
409	    return rows
410	
411	
412	def lower_median(values: list[Decimal]) -> Decimal:
413	    ordered = sorted(values)
414	    return ordered[(len(ordered) - 1) // 2]
415	
416	
417	def fuel_proxy_rows(year: int) -> list[dict]:
418	    spec = rules.FUEL_PROXY_SOURCES[year]
419	    rows = parse_fuel_rows(html_text(raw_path(spec["file"])))
420	    out = []
421	    for group, index in spec["percent_index"].items():
422	        values = [Decimal(r.percents[index].rstrip("%")) for r in rows]
423	        median = lower_median(values)
424	        mean = sum(values) / len(values)
425	        chosen = next(r for r in rows if Decimal(r.percents[index].rstrip("%")) == median)
426	        token = chosen.percents[index]
427	        quote = chosen.text[:chosen.text.index(token) + len(token)]
428	        out.append({
429	            "carrier": rules.CARRIER, "year": str(year), "service_group": group, "default_percent": f"{median:.2f}",
430	            "basis": "base rate plus surcharges flagged fuel_applies",
431	            "window_start": min(r.start for r in rows).isoformat(), "window_end": max(r.end for r in rows).isoformat(),
432	            "is_proxy": "true", "source_file": spec["file"], "source_ref": "", "source_quote": quote,
433	            "notes": (f"Proxy: UPS publishes no retrievable weekly fuel history. default_percent is the lower median of the "
434	                      f"{len(values)} weekly FedEx {group} percentages in this snapshot (mean {mean:.2f}%); the quoted row is "
435	                      f"the most recent week at the median. {spec['layout']}."),
436	        })
437	    return out
438	
439	
440	def fuel_surcharge() -> list[dict]:
441	    rows = []
442	    for year in rules.YEARS:
443	        rows += fuel_proxy_rows(year)
444	    return rows
445	
446	
447	def exceptions(parsed: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
448	    rows = [dict(row) for row in parsed]
449	    for note in rules.EXCEPTION_NOTES:
450	        rows.append({"carrier": rules.CARRIER, "rate_card": rules.RATE_CARD, **note})
451	    return rows
452	
453	
454	def main() -> None:
455	    base_rows, parsed_exceptions = [], []
456	    for year in rules.YEARS:
457	        rows, year_exceptions = parse_guide(year)
458	        base_rows += rows
459	        parsed_exceptions += year_exceptions
460	        print(f"{year}: {len(rows)} rate cells")
461	    builders = (
462	        ("base_rates", lambda: base_rows),
463	        ("exceptions", lambda: exceptions(parsed_exceptions)),
464	        ("surcharges", surcharges),
465	        ("fuel_surcharge", fuel_surcharge),
466	        ("announced_increase", announced_increase),
467	        ("dim_weight", dim_weight),
468	    )
469	    for table, build in builders:
470	        rows = build()
471	        path = write_table(rules.CARRIER, table, rows)
472	        print(f"wrote {path.name}: {len(rows)} rows")
473	
474	
475	if __name__ == "__main__":
476	    main()
477

348	}
349	TAGS = {"all": "", HOME: "", EXPRESS: "_express", OVERNIGHT: "_overnight", DEFERRED: "_deferred"}

351	
352	def year_of(day: date) -> int:
353	    """Price-list year in force on `day`; 2022 for days before the 2023 list (not in scope)."""
354	    return max((year for year, start in EFFECTIVE.items() if start <= day), default=min(EFFECTIVE) - 1)
355	
356	
357	def peak_rows() -> list[dict]:
358	    rows = []
359	    for file, condition, applies, name, windows in PEAK:
360	        group = "peak_non_standard" if condition in {"peak_additional_handling", "peak_oversize"} else ""
361	        for amount, quote, start, end in windows:
362	            cursor, last = date.fromisoformat(start), date.fromisoformat(end)
363	            while cursor <= last:
364	                year = year_of(cursor)
365	                stop = min(last, EFFECTIVE[year + 1] - timedelta(days=1)) if year + 1 in EFFECTIVE else last
366	                if year >= 2023:
367	                    rows.append(rule(year, f"fedex_{condition}{TAGS[applies]}_{cursor.isoformat()}", name, condition, applies,
368	                                     amount, file, quote, effective_from=cursor.isoformat(), effective_to=stop.isoformat(),
369	                                     exclusive_group=group,
370	                                     notes=PEAK_NOTES[condition] + f"; document window {start} to {end}, split at the January list date"))
371	                cursor = stop + timedelta(days=1)
372	    return rows
373	
374	
375	def surcharge_rows() -> list[dict]:
376	    return residential_rows() + das_rows() + additional_handling_rows() + oversize_rows() + peak_rows()

98	def tokenize_pdf_row(tokens: list[str], expected_columns: int) -> tuple[int, list[str]] | None:
99	    """Turn the whitespace tokens of one PDF text line into (weight, prices).
100	
101	    Returns None for lines that are not weight rows (headers, footnotes, page
102	    numbers). Raises ParseError when a weight row has the wrong number of
103	    price columns, so a shifted column can never be silently accepted.
104	    """
105	    tokens = [t.lstrip("$") for t in tokens if t != "$"]  # "$ 10.70" or "$107.00"
106	    if not tokens:
107	        return None
108	    first = tokens[0]
109	    rest = tokens[1:]
110	    if WEIGHT_TOKEN.match(first):
111	        weight = int(first)
112	        if rest and rest[0] in {"lb.", "lbs.", "lb", "lbs"}:
113	            rest = rest[1:]

128	        raise ParseError(

138	    words = [w for w in page.extract_words(keep_blank_chars=False, use_text_flow=False) if w.get("upright", True)]

182	def split_express_blocks(rows: list[tuple]) -> dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[tuple]]]:
183	    """Split a stacked U.S. express sheet into service blocks.
184	
185	    A block is a title row whose text is one of EXPRESS_SERVICES, immediately
186	    followed by a `Zones` header row. Returns {service_id: (zone_columns, rows)}
187	    where zone_columns are the column indexes of zones 2-8 and rows are the
188	    rows up to the next blank row. Only the first block per service counts
189	    (the Multiweight section repeats the titles with a `Weight` header).
190	    """
191	    blocks: dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[tuple]]] = {}
192	    for index, row in enumerate(rows[:-1]):
193	        service = EXPRESS_SERVICES.get(clean_title(row[0]))
194	        header = rows[index + 1]

203	                break
204	            body.append(body_row)

300	            parsed = tokenize_pdf_row(tokens, len(PDF_EXPRESS_COLUMNS))
301	            if parsed is None:
302	                continue
303	            weight, prices = parsed
304	            zone = int(express.group(1))
305	            for service, price in zip(PDF_EXPRESS_COLUMNS, prices):
306	                if service in EXPRESS_SERVICES.values() and weight <= MAX_WEIGHT_LB:
307	                    cells.append(Cell(service, zone, weight, money(price), str(page_index)))
308	        else:
309	            parsed = tokenize_pdf_row(tokens, len(ZONES[CARRIER]))
310	            if parsed is None:
311	                continue
312	            weight, prices = parsed
313	            if weight > MAX_WEIGHT_LB:
314	                continue
315	            for zone, price in zip(ZONES[CARRIER], prices):
316	                for service in GROUND_SERVICES:
317	                    cells.append(Cell(service, zone, weight, money(price), str(page_index)))
318	    return cells
319	
320	
321	def parse_pdf(relative: str) -> tuple[date, list[Cell]]:
322	    import pdfplumber
323	
324	    path = raw_path(relative)
325	    cells: list[Cell] = []
326	    with pdfplumber.open(path) as pdf:
327	        cover = pdf.pages[0].extract_text() or ""
328	        match = EFFECTIVE_LONG.search(cover)
329	        if not match:
330	            raise ParseError(f"{relative}: no 'Effective Month d, yyyy' on the cover")
331	        effective = datetime.strptime(match.group(1), "%B %d, %Y").date()
332	        for index, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, 1):
333	            try:
334	                cells.extend(parse_pdf_page(page, index))
335	            except ParseError as error:
336	                raise ParseError(f"{relative} page {index}: {error}") from error
337	    return effective, cells
338	
339	
340	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- tables
341	
342	def base_rate_rows() -> list[dict]:
343	    rows: list[dict] = []
344	    for year, relative in SOURCES.items():
345	        effective, cells = parse_pdf(relative) if relative.endswith(".pdf") else parse_xlsx(year, relative)
346	        check_complete(cells, year)
347	        for cell in sorted(cells, key=lambda c: (c.service_id, c.zone, c.weight)):
348	            rows.append({
349	                "carrier": CARRIER, "service_id": cell.service_id, "rate_card": RATE_CARD,
350	                "year": year, "effective_date": effective.isoformat(), "zone": cell.zone,
351	                "max_weight_lb": weight_label(cell.weight), "price": cell.price,
352	                "source_file": relative, "source_ref": cell.source_ref,
353	            })
354	    return rows
355	
356	
357	FUEL_ROW = re.compile(
358	    r"((?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|June|July|Aug|Sept|Oct|Nov|Dec)\.? \d{1,2}, \d{4})\s*[–-]\s*"
359	    r"((?:Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|June|July|Aug|Sept|Oct|Nov|Dec)\.? \d{1,2}, \d{4})"
360	    r"((?:\s+(?:\d+\.\d+%|\$\d+\.\d+ per lb\.)){4,5})"
361	)
362	MONTHS = {"Jan": 1, "Feb": 2, "Mar": 3, "Apr": 4, "May": 5, "June": 6, "July": 7,
363	          "Aug": 8, "Sept": 9, "Oct": 10, "Nov": 11, "Dec": 12}
364	
365	
366	def parse_fuel_date(text: str) -> date:
367	    month, day, year = re.match(r"([A-Za-z]+)\.? (\d{1,2}), (\d{4})", text).groups()
368	    return date(int(year), MONTHS[month], int(day))
369	
370	
371	def fuel_history_rows(relative: str) -> list[dict]:
372	    """Weekly rows of an archived historical-fuel-surcharge page.
373	
374	    Two layouts exist: 2023 (Express package %, express freight $/lb, export %,
375	    import %, Ground %) and 2024+ (Ground %, package %, freight $/lb, export %,
376	    import %; 2026 merges export and import into one column). The Ground
377	    column is identified by position: last in the 2023 layout, first otherwise.
378	    Matching runs on entity-decoded text (the pages contain `&nbsp;`); each
379	    quote is cut right after the value used so it is a verbatim substring of
380	    the raw page too.
381	    """
382	    text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", html.unescape(html_text(raw_path(relative))).replace("\xa0", " "))
383	    header = text.split("Previous FedEx Freight")[0]
384	    ground_first = "FedEx Ground, FedEx Home Delivery" in header
385	    if not ground_first and "FedEx Ground Surcharge" not in header:
386	        raise ParseError(f"{relative}: unrecognised fuel history table layout")
387	    rows = []
388	    for match in FUEL_ROW.finditer(text):
389	        values = [(m.group(0), m.end()) for m in re.finditer(r"\d+\.\d+%|\$\d+\.\d+ per lb\.", match.group(3))]
390	        percents = [(v, end) for v, end in values if v.endswith("%")]
391	        ground, express = (percents[0], percents[1]) if ground_first else (percents[-1], percents[0])
392	        offset = match.start(3)
393	        rows.append({
394	            "start": parse_fuel_date(match.group(1)), "end": parse_fuel_date(match.group(2)),
395	            "ground": Decimal(ground[0].rstrip("%")), "express": Decimal(express[0].rstrip("%")),
396	            "quote": {"ground": text[match.start():offset + ground[1]], "express": text[match.start():offset + express[1]]},
397	        })
398	    if not rows:
399	        raise ParseError(f"{relative}: no weekly fuel rows found")
400	    return rows
401	
402	
403	def median_row(rows: list[dict], column: str) -> dict:
404	    """The row holding the lower median of `column` (a value that appears in the table)."""
405	    ordered = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: (r[column], r["start"]))
406	    return ordered[(len(ordered) - 1) // 2]
407	
408	
409	def fuel_surcharge_rows() -> list[dict]:
410	    out: list[dict] = []
411	    for year, relative in FUEL_HISTORY.items():
412	        rows = fuel_history_rows(relative)
413	        starts, ends = min(r["start"] for r in rows), max(r["end"] for r in rows)
414	        for group in ("ground", "express"):
415	            pick = median_row(rows, group)
416	            values = sorted(r[group] for r in rows)
417	            out.append({
418	                "carrier": CARRIER, "year": year, "service_group": group,
419	                "default_percent": str(pick[group]),
420	                "basis": "base rate plus surcharges flagged fuel_applies",
421	                "window_start": starts.isoformat(), "window_end": ends.isoformat(),
422	                "is_proxy": "false", "source_file": relative, "source_ref": "",
423	                "source_quote": pick["quote"][group],
424	                "notes": (
425	                    f"Lower median of the {len(rows)} weekly {'Ground/Home Delivery' if group == 'ground' else 'domestic package (Express)'} "
426	                    f"values in this snapshot (range {values[0]}%-{values[-1]}%); the quoted row is the week carrying that value. "
427	                    f"The snapshot covers only the weeks listed, not the whole year."
428	                ),
429	            })
430	    out.extend(fedex_rules.fuel_proxy_rows(out))
431	    return out
432	
433	
434	def main() -> None:
435	    write_table(CARRIER, "base_rates", base_rate_rows())
436	    write_table(CARRIER, "exceptions", fedex_rules.EXCEPTIONS)
437	    write_table(CARRIER, "surcharges", fedex_rules.surcharge_rows())
438	    write_table(CARRIER, "fuel_surcharge", fuel_surcharge_rows())
439	    write_table(CARRIER, "announced_increase", fedex_rules.ANNOUNCED_INCREASES)
440	    write_table(CARRIER, "dim_weight", fedex_rules.DIM_WEIGHT)
441	    print("wrote data/processed/fedex/*.csv")
442	
443	
444	if __name__ == "__main__":
445	    main()
446	
```

</details>

```
# Data availability and quality report

Issue #1. Survey date: 2026-10-22. Three agents, one per carrier, searched for
the published (non-contract, retail) US domestic parcel rates of USPS, UPS and
FedEx for 2022 through 2026, downloaded what they could, and recorded every
file with its URL, retrieval method and parse notes in
`data/raw/<carrier>/SOURCES.md`. This report consolidates their findings and
records the decisions that follow from them.

## Summary

| | USPS | UPS | FedEx |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base rate tables | Every price change 2022–2026 (15 events) | Yearly Daily Rates guide, 2022–2026 | Yearly Standard List Rates, 2022–2027 |
| Best format | CSV zip per price change (clean) | Text PDF only (tables span ~4 pages per service) | XLSX for 2022, 2025, 2026, 2027; text PDF for 2023, 2024 |
| Surcharge rules | Footnotes in Notice 123 PDFs | Surcharge section of the same guide (3-column prose) | Yearly "surcharge and fee changes" PDFs (2022, 2024–2026) plus Service Guides |
| Residential / delivery area | None (confirmed) | Residential, DAS, extended DAS amounts in guide; ZIP list not downloaded | Residential, DAS amounts; DAS ZIP lists downloaded for every year |
| Dimensional weight | Over 1,728 cu in, greater of actual and dim weight; divisor 166 (DMM 123 and 133, March 2024 capture) and 139 from 2026-07-12 (DMM, live), no zone restriction; verified | Divisor 139, round up to next pound (verified in 2026 guide) | Divisor 139 (verified in every Service Guide 2022–2026) |
| Fuel surcharge | None | No weekly history retrievable; only index-to-percent tables | Weekly history page, one ~13-week snapshot saved per year |
| Peak / demand surcharges | Peak price tables per season (2022, 2024, 2025, 2026; none in 2023) | Demand surcharge PDFs 2022–2024 | Dated notices; amounts inside Service Guides, not isolated |
| Announced average increase | USPS press releases, per product (primary source) | Secondary news sources only (5.9% 2022, 6.9% 2023, 5.9% 2024–2026) | FedEx's own rate-change pages: 5.9% every year except 6.9% in 2023 (primary) |
| Access | Direct, needs a browser User-Agent | assets.ups.com blocks curl; fetched through Wayback passthrough | fedex.com blocks this host entirely; everything via the Wayback Machine |
| Raw size | 26 MB (48 files) | 40 MB (23 files) | 74 MB (56 files) |

## Per carrier

### USPS

- **Coverage.** All 15 price changes from January 2022 to October 2026, each
  with a Notice 123 PDF and a Postal Explorer CSV zip. Press releases give the
  announced average increase per product for most changes.
- **Services.** Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express 1–70 lb by zone 1–9
  in every file. Ground Advantage exists from 2023-07-09; before that the
  equivalent lineage is First-Class Package Service (up to 15.999 oz) plus
  USPS Retail Ground (1–70 lb).
- **Parse difficulty.** Low. Each CSV block has a short irregular preamble,
  then a `,Zone 1,…,Zone 9` header and one row per weight step. One float
  artifact (`15.999000000000001`). Surcharge rules are not in the CSVs; they
  are footnotes beside the tables in the PDFs, which pdftotext interleaves
  with price rows. Reading them by hand into a curated table is faster and
  safer than parsing them.
- **Dimensional weight, verified.** Notice 123 only states the one cubic
  foot rule; the divisor is in the Domestic Mail Manual sections 123
  (Priority Mail) and 133 (Ground Advantage). Saved under
  `data/raw/usps/dmm/`: the March 2024 Wayback captures say "divide the
  result by 166"; the 2026-10-22 live pages say "divide the result by 139"
  with a `[7-12-26]` change marker. Neither restricts the rule by zone.
- **Gaps.** No bulk zone matrix without an order
  form; the free per-origin zone chart is a form POST on postcalc.usps.com.
- **Quirks.** 2026 has three states: January base, a time-limited +8%
  transportation surcharge from April, and the October peak table.

### UPS

- **Coverage.** A full Daily Rates guide for every year 2022–2026, with all
  five target services, zones 2–8 plus 44–46, 1–150 lb, and the surcharge
  section. Demand surcharge PDFs for 2022–2024 and fuel index tables for
  several dates.
- **Parse difficulty.** Medium. Text PDFs; `pdftotext -layout` gives aligned
  columns on rate pages, but each service table spans about four pages with a
  repeated header strip, and page numbering shifts between the 158–165 page
  guides (2022–2024) and the 216 page guides (2025–2026). The surcharge pages
  are three-column prose with inline tables and need regex extraction.
- **Gaps.** No weekly fuel surcharge history anywhere accessible (the UPS
  page is JavaScript-rendered and Wayback snapshots carry no values). No
  UPS-authored source for the announced increases, only trade press. 2027 not
  announced as of 2026-10-13. DAS ZIP list not downloaded.
- **Editions.** Mid-year updates exist for 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026; the
  December original is missing for 2024 and 2026, so those years use the
  mid-year revision.

### FedEx

- **Coverage.** Standard List Rates for 2022–2027 with all six target
  services, surcharge change documents for 2022 and 2024–2026, Service Guides
  2022–2026, DAS ZIP lists for every year, fuel trigger tables and one
  historical fuel snapshot per year, and FedEx's own rate-change pages with
  the announced increase.
- **Parse difficulty.** Low for the XLSX years (one sheet per market, stacked
  blocks per service, `Zones 2 3 4 …` header). Medium for 2023 and 2024,
  which are PDF only but consistently laid out. Surcharge change PDFs are
  four-column old/new tables with wrapped cells.
- **Gaps.** No XLSX for 2023 and 2024. No 2023 surcharge change document
  (use the 2024 one's "old" column). Demand surcharge amounts are inside the
  Service Guides rather than isolated. Only one ~13-week fuel window per year.
- **Quirks.** 2026 rates were revised on June 1 2026 and the XLSX predates
  that revision; the PDF captured on 2026-10-22 includes it.

## Decisions

1. **Year range: 2023 through 2026** for the year-over-year view, four price
   points under each year's January list prices. 2022 is excluded from the
   MVP because USPS had a different product set (the Ground Advantage lineage
   starts in July 2023). For USPS 2023 the July 2023 tables are used and
   labelled as such. 2027 FedEx rates are already published and are kept as
   an optional forward year (issue #11).
2. **Parse order by confidence.** USPS CSVs first, FedEx XLSX years next,
   then the FedEx and UPS PDF years. Each parser is validated against
   hand-checked prices from the documents.
3. **Surcharge rules are curated, not parsed.** Amounts for residential,
   delivery area, additional handling, oversize, nonstandard and peak are
   transcribed into `data/processed/surcharges.csv` with the source file and
   page for each row. The PDFs are kept as evidence, not as pipeline input.
4. **Fuel surcharge default per year.** FedEx is the only carrier with a
   retrievable history. The per-year default for both UPS and FedEx is taken
   from the FedEx historical snapshots (the two carriers' percentages track
   each other closely), recorded with its source window, and flagged as an
   approximation. The slider in the UI is the user's override. USPS has none.
5. **Announced increases.** FedEx and USPS from primary sources. UPS from
   trade press, marked as secondary in `announced_increase.csv`.
6. **Dimensional weight.** Divisor 139 for UPS and FedEx on every billable
   parcel. For USPS, dim weight applies only above 1,728 cubic inches, with
   divisor 166 through 2026-07-11 and 139 from 2026-07-12, verified against
   the DMM captures in `data/raw/usps/dmm/`.
7. **Raw files in git.** Only the spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML
   snapshots are committed (about 8 MB). No PDF is tracked. Every raw file,
   tracked or not, is listed in `data/raw/manifest.csv` with its URL
   (Wayback passthrough form where applicable), SHA-256 and size, and
   `python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores the missing ones one at a time with
   a pause between requests, retrying with backoff, and verifies checksums.
8. **Citations are tested.** Every hand-curated row (surcharges, fuel,
   announced increases, dimensional weight, zone bands) cites a file, a
   page and a verbatim quote containing the amount; a test opens the cited
   page and checks the quote is there (skipped with a message when the raw
   file has not been fetched).
9. **Zones.** Distance bands stand in for ZIP-to-ZIP zones (issue #9 is the
   bonus). The band table is documented in `data/processed/zone_from_distance.csv`.

## Known limitations to state in the README

- List prices only; any shipper with a negotiated contract pays less.
- Zones are approximated from distance, not looked up from ZIP pairs.
- UPS fuel surcharge history is a proxy taken from FedEx.
- UPS announced-increase percentages come from trade press.
- Peak surcharges are modelled as a toggle with that year's amounts, not by
  ship date.
```

**Tool call:** `SubagentHandback` <sub>toolu_01QWLFU3eat8HqE4Ho3ykvDi</sub>

- `message`:

```
Review of PR #15 (aivuk/parcel-rates, branch issue-2-rate-tables → main), worktree ~/parcel-rates-issue-2. Ran the full suite (`uv run --directory ~/parcel-rates-issue-2 pytest data/tests -q`): 838 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 2 documented-exception warnings. I independently re-derived and cross-checked many numbers against the raw PDFs/XLSX myself (pdftotext/openpyxl), not just against the parser's own output.

## CRITICAL

**FedEx `surcharges.csv`: three logically-stackable rule families share the same (empty) `exclusive_group`, which per SCHEMA.md means "do not stack, highest amount wins."**
File: `data/pipeline/fedex_rules.py` (`residential_rows()` via `rule()` default `exclusive_group=""`, and `peak_rows()` line ~360 `group = "peak_non_standard" if condition in {"peak_additional_handling","peak_oversize"} else ""`).
37 rows in `data/processed/fedex/surcharges.csv` across conditions `residential`, `peak_base`, `peak_residential` all have `exclusive_group = ""`. Their `applies_to`/`address_type` and effective windows genuinely overlap: e.g. `fedex_residential_express_2025` ($6.55, all of 2025-01-06..2026-01-04, applies to the 4 Express services) and `fedex_peak_base_express_2025-10-27` ($1.05, 2025-10-27..2025-11-23, same Express services) both have `exclusive_group=""`. Same pattern for `fedex_residential_home_delivery_*` vs `fedex_peak_residential_*`. SCHEMA.md's text ("Rules in the same group do not stack; the highest matching amount applies") has no documented exception for blank — a literal/naive engine implementation that groups rows by `exclusive_group` string equality will treat these as mutually exclusive and silently drop the lower-amount row, undercharging every FedEx Express/Home-Delivery-residential shipment made during any demand/peak window (a large, recurring share of shipments, every year 2023-2027). UPS (`ups.py`) and USPS (`usps_rules.py`) never leave this column blank except one harmless singleton row (`usps_transportation_time_limited_2026`, which collides with nothing) — FedEx is the outlier.
Fix: give these FedEx rows real, distinct group names (e.g. `fedex_residential`, `fedex_peak_base`, `fedex_peak_residential`), matching the UPS/USPS convention, or explicitly document in SCHEMA.md that an empty `exclusive_group` means "never exclusive" and confirm the (not-yet-built) rate engine implements that special case.

## MEDIUM

1. **`data/processed/services.csv`: `fedex_home_delivery` max_weight_lb is 70, `fedex_ground` is 150.** Both services share one rate table ("FedEx Ground® and FedEx Home Delivery® ... Zones 2-8", confirmed 1-150 lb in the raw XLSX, and `data/pipeline/fedex_rules.py` EXCEPTIONS note literally says "one table ... (1-150 lb, same structure); fedex_home_delivery rows are a copy of the fedex_ground rows"). SCHEMA.md's own rule is "150 for UPS and FedEx (the app caps at 70)" — Home Delivery should be 150, not 70. Low price-risk today because `base_rates.csv` is already globally truncated to ≤70 lb for every carrier/service by `MAX_WEIGHT_LB` in the parsers, but the field is simply wrong and will mislead anything (UI, validation) that trusts it.

2. **`services.csv` has zero test coverage.** It's hand-written (no pipeline script ever calls `write_table(..., "services", ...)`) and is the only table in the schema not covered by any test — no column check, no enum check (`tier`, `rate_cards`), no citation requirement. The bug above went undetected because nothing checks this file at all.

3. **No structural/invariant tests on `surcharges.csv`** (the table the PR itself flags as highest-risk: hand-transcribed, verbatim quotes). `test_invariants.py` is rich for `base_rates.csv` (coverage, monotonicity, clean money, zone ranges) but surcharges.csv has nothing analogous: no duplicate-`surcharge_id` check, no `effective_from <= effective_to` check, and `applies_to` (comma-separated service ids) is never validated against `services.csv`'s known ids/`all`/`ground`/`air` — unlike `condition` and `address_type`, which `test_citations.py` does check. I wrote a one-off script and manually confirmed no duplicates, no inverted dates, and no bad `applies_to` tokens exist today across all three carriers, but nothing in CI would catch a regression.

4. **`test_golden_corner_cells_present` (data/tests/test_golden.py) enforces only 3 of SCHEMA.md's 4 mandated golden corners.** It checks heaviest/farthest, heaviest/nearest, lightest/farthest, and a `MIN_CELLS=5` total, but never checks requirement 4 ("at least two interior cells on different pages or sheets of the source") — exactly the case the schema says golden cells exist to catch (column/page shifts). A golden set could pass with 5 cells all from one page/sheet.

## LOW

5. **Stale/self-contradicting comment**, `data/pipeline/usps_rules.py` ~line 261: says "the citation test cannot match a negative percent, so those two rows are not recorded here" — but the two Ground Advantage 2023 decrease rows (-3.2%, -0.7%) are recorded immediately below in `ANNOUNCED_BY_CARD`, and `test_citations.amount_variants()` does strip a leading `-` before searching the quote, so the test handles negative percents fine (verified: `usps/announced_increase.csv` rows 13-14 carry these and the suite passes). Harmless but misleading for future maintainers.

6. **Reproducibility: silent skip on missing raw files.** `test_citations.py` does `pytest.skip()` per-row when a cited raw file isn't on disk. Raw PDFs are `in_git=false` (not committed); on a bare clone before running `data/fetch_raw.py`, nearly every curated-row citation check would silently skip rather than fail, and a default pytest summary can look "green" while verifying almost nothing. Not a problem right now — in this worktree all raw files are present and the suite genuinely ran 838/838 with 0 skips — but worth a CI guard (e.g., fail if skip count > 0) given how central this check is to the PR's correctness story.

## What I verified as correct (not padding — these were the main candidates for real bugs and I checked them against the source documents directly, not just against the parser's own output)

- USPS 2024 peak press release (`press_2024-09-05_peak2024_temporary_rates.pdf`) vs `usps_rules.PEAK[2024]`: all ~40 transcribed amounts matched verbatim.
- UPS Delivery Area Surcharge, Large Package Surcharge and Additional Handling tables for 2025 and 2026 (guide pages 179-185) vs `ups_rules.py` literals: exact match, including the 2026 four-zone-band restructuring (BANDS_4).
- FedEx `surcharge_and_fee_changes_2026.pdf` Additional Handling and Oversize Charge tables vs `fedex_rules.AH`/`OVERSIZE` 2026 entries, including the "Zones 5-6 *Effective July 14, 2025" mid-year interim-increase window split: exact match, and I confirmed the window-splitting code (`additional_handling_rows`/`oversize_rows`) produces non-overlapping, gap-free effective windows for that interim bump.
- FedEx 2027 demand-surcharges Wayback page vs `fedex_rules.PEAK` DEM27 entries (the new Overnight-vs-Deferred split, $1.30/$2.55/$1.30 and $1.20/$2.35/$1.20): exact match.
- FedEx 2026 XLSX `base_rates.csv`: checked several cells not in the golden files (e.g. `fedex_priority_overnight` zone4/17lb, zone8/32lb; `fedex_ground` zone6/45lb) directly against `openpyxl`-read spreadsheet values — all correct — and confirmed the parser correctly stops each service block at the first blank row, so it does not accidentally pull in the adjacent "FedEx International Ground: Canada" sub-table that also happens to use weight label 45.
- UPS's apparent "duplicate" peak-surcharge rows spanning the January price-list boundary (e.g. `ups_peak_additional_handling_2024_2024-11-24` and `ups_peak_additional_handling_2025_2024-11-24`, same window, same amount) are harmless: they share the same `exclusive_group` (the condition name) and the same amount, so "highest matching amount" dedups them correctly — not a double-charge.
- UPS/FedEx Additional-Handling-vs-Large-Package/Oversize exclusivity (`ups_handling`, FedEx `non_standard`) is correctly shared across all the relevant criteria and matches each carrier's own stated "only one charge, highest wins" rule.
- No hardcoded secrets, no SQL/XSS/auth surface (not applicable to a static data pipeline); `data/fetch_raw.py` already paces network calls per the docs.

Files most relevant to the findings above: `~/parcel-rates-issue-2/data/pipeline/fedex_rules.py`, `~/parcel-rates-issue-2/data/processed/fedex/surcharges.csv`, `~/parcel-rates-issue-2/data/processed/services.csv`, `~/parcel-rates-issue-2/data/tests/test_golden.py`, `~/parcel-rates-issue-2/data/tests/test_citations.py`, `~/parcel-rates-issue-2/data/pipeline/usps_rules.py`, `~/parcel-rates-issue-2/docs/data/SCHEMA.md`.
