# Parcel rates: USPS, UPS and FedEx list prices for a small online shop

A dashboard that prices a shop's own parcels at the published prices of the
three US parcel carriers, for every year from 2023 to 2026, and shows which
carrier is cheapest, where the breakeven points are, how much of the bill is
surcharges, and how the cost moved year by year.

## Run it

Requires Docker with Compose v2. No accounts, keys or database setup.

```sh
docker compose up --build
```

Then open **http://localhost:8088**. The first build takes a minute or two.
Click "Load sample mix" to load an illustrative example parcel set, or upload your
own CSV (columns below). Stop with `Ctrl+C`, then `docker compose down`.

Only port 8088 is published. nginx serves the built dashboard and proxies
`/api/` to the backend container, which is not reachable from the host. The
rate tables are baked into the backend image; the app never fetches anything
from the carriers at run time.

## The problem and the user

The user is the owner of a small online shop that sends a few hundred to a few
thousand parcels a month, has no negotiated carrier contract, and therefore
pays published prices. The carrier is usually chosen by habit, and the flat
shipping price charged to customers was set once and not revisited.

The dashboard supports two decisions: which carrier and service to use for
each kind of parcel, and whether the flat shipping price still covers the real
cost once surcharges and yearly price increases are included.

### What it answers

| # | Question | The view |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | For one parcel (weight, size, distance, home or business, speed), which service is cheapest once surcharges are included, and what are the line items? | The cheapest total for the chosen speed comes first, with its saving over the next cheapest and the margin against your price. Below it, every carrier's cheapest service ranked, each with base rate, every surcharge (with its source page) and fuel. The form can start from one of your loaded parcels. |
| 2 | Where are the breakeven points between the Postal Service and FedEx or UPS ground, by weight and distance? | A weight by distance heatmap coloured by the cheapest ground carrier, for home or business delivery, with a heavy line where USPS stops winning and a plain-words readout of the breakeven weights; every cell's prices on hover, tap or focus, and the grid as a table. |
| 3 | For the whole parcel set, what is the blended cost per parcel with each carrier, and how much of it is surcharges? | The cheapest single carrier's cost per parcel and the "best mix" (cheapest carrier per parcel), then a yes or no on whether your shipping price covers the cost, the margin per parcel and the share shipped at a loss per carrier. A stacked chart (or table) splits the cost into base, the largest surcharges and fuel. Chips narrow everything to one kind of parcel (weight, distance, home or business, speed). |
| 4 | How did that blended cost change year by year, compared with the average increase the carriers announced, and which parcels drove it? | The cheapest carrier's change since the first year against the compounded announced increases, a year by year chart (dollars or index) with the announced path, how much of the biggest rise was fuel, the segments that drove each step, and a next-year slider that projects the cost. |

Global controls: price year, USPS rate card, fuel surcharge override, peak
season toggle, and the flat price charged per parcel.

Parcel CSV columns: `weight_lb, length_in, width_in, height_in,
distance_miles, residential, speed` (`ground`, `two_three_day`, `next_day`),
plus optional `quantity`, `price_charged`, `delivery_area`,
`nonstandard_packaging`. The full schema is in
[docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md).

**The sample mix** is an illustrative home-goods shop, an example and not real
shipping data, generated by `backend/scripts/make_sample_parcels.py` with a
fixed seed: 200 rows, 307 parcels, mostly light ground parcels in boxes under
one cubic foot (about 80 % under 5 lb), about 7 % bulky boxes over one cubic
foot, 4 % two to three day and 1 % next day, about 80 % to homes, distances
weighted toward the middle zones, and a handful in delivery areas. Ground rows
leave `price_charged` empty and use the flat price control; expedited rows
carry what a shop would charge at checkout, $19.99 for two to three day and
$39.99 for next day, because real shops charge more for faster shipping. At the
default controls (2026, USPS commercial, $9.99) the mix opens near break-even:
USPS, the cheapest carrier, costs $10.98 per parcel against $10.67 charged on
average (−$0.31 per parcel), and the 40 % of parcels shipped at a loss are
mostly the bulky boxes, parcels over 5 lb and the far zones.

## Data provenance

All prices come from the carriers' own published rate documents:

| Carrier | Base rates | Surcharge rules | Years |
|---|---|---|---|
| USPS | Postal Explorer CSV zips per price change; Notice 123 PDFs | Notice 123 footnotes; Domestic Mail Manual for dimensional weight | 2023 (July tables, Ground Advantage launch) to 2026 |
| UPS | Daily Rates guide PDF per year | Surcharge section of the same guide; demand surcharge PDFs | 2023 to 2026 |
| FedEx | Standard List Rates XLSX (PDF for 2023 and 2024) | Yearly surcharge-change PDFs and Service Guides | 2023 to 2026, plus 2027 as a forward year |

**Collection.** Every raw file is listed in
[data/raw/manifest.csv](data/raw/manifest.csv) with its URL, retrieval method,
SHA-256 and size, and each carrier folder has a `SOURCES.md` describing what
each file is. `python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores missing files one at a
time, with a pause and jitter between requests, backoff on errors, an
identifying User-Agent and checksum verification. UPS and FedEx block direct
downloads from scripts, so 78 of the 135 files are fetched through the Wayback
Machine (`method=wayback`).

**What is committed.** Spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML snapshots (58
files, about 9 MB) are in git. The PDFs (77 files, about 137 MB) are not; run
`python3 data/fetch_raw.py` to get them. The processed tables in
`data/processed/` are committed, so the app and the backend tests never need
the raw files.

**Regenerating `data/processed/`** (needs the PDFs, so fetch first):

```sh
python3 data/fetch_raw.py                     # standard library only
uv run python -m data.pipeline.usps
uv run python -m data.pipeline.ups
uv run python -m data.pipeline.fedex
uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes # rewrites docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md
```

Base rates are parsed. Surcharges, fuel defaults, announced increases,
dimensional weight rules and the distance-to-zone bands are curated by hand
in `data/pipeline/*_rules.py`, each row with the source file, page and a
verbatim quote. Details: [docs/data/QUALITY.md](docs/data/QUALITY.md) (survey
and decisions), [docs/data/SCHEMA.md](docs/data/SCHEMA.md) (tables) and
[docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md](docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md) (every rule that
changed between years).

### Rate cards

| Carrier | Card | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| USPS | `commercial` (default) | Price paid with online postage or shipping software; no contract or volume needed |
| USPS | `retail` | Price paid at the Post Office counter |
| UPS | `list` | Published Daily Rates, what a shipper without a contract pays |
| FedEx | `list` | Published Standard List Rates, same meaning |

Commercial is the USPS default because a small online seller buys labels
through a marketplace or shipping software, which gives commercial prices to
anyone. Comparing UPS and FedEx list prices against USPS retail would
overstate what the shop pays the Postal Service. The retail card is one switch
away in the controls.

## Key choices

- **Stack.** Python 3.12, FastAPI and Pydantic for the rate engine and API,
  managed with `uv`. Vite, React and TypeScript for the dashboard, Recharts
  for line and bar charts and a hand-drawn SVG heatmap. Two containers behind
  one `docker compose` command. Reasons and alternatives are in
  [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md).
- **CSV in memory, no database.** The rate tables are about 40,000 rows of
  committed CSV, loaded once at startup. Nothing to configure.
- **Curated rules with tested citations.** Surcharge prose in PDFs is too
  irregular to parse reliably, so the amounts were transcribed by hand. A test
  opens each cited page and checks that the quote, including the amount, is
  there.
- **Golden cells.** `data/tests/golden/<carrier>_<year>.csv` holds price cells
  checked by hand against the documents, including the corners of every
  table; the parsed output must match them exactly.
- **Time-varying rules.** Every rule carries `effective_from` and an inclusive
  `effective_to`, and a quote is priced on an `as_of` date. This handles
  mid-year changes such as the USPS dimensional divisor moving from 166 to 139
  on 2026-07-12, peak windows and the 2026 USPS transportation surcharge.
- **Ledger design.** The answer to each question is the largest thing in its
  section; assumptions sit in a quiet side rail. See
  [frontend/DESIGN.md](frontend/DESIGN.md).

## Known limitations

- List prices only: a shipper with a negotiated contract pays less.
- Zones are estimated from distance bands, not looked up from ZIP code pairs.
- The UPS fuel surcharge default is a proxy taken from FedEx's published
  history (no UPS history is retrievable); the slider overrides it.
- UPS announced increases come from trade press, not from UPS itself.
- UPS peak (demand) surcharge documents for the 2025-26 and 2026-27 seasons
  are not in the sources, so UPS 2025 and 2026 peak quotes carry no peak
  charges.
- FedEx 2027 surcharges are incomplete (only the Home Delivery residential
  charge and January peak rows), so 2027 totals understate surcharges.
- Peak surcharges are a toggle that prices on December 10 of the year, not by
  ship date.
- UPS and FedEx bill a large or oversize package at a minimum of 90 lb. That
  minimum is not modelled, so the base rate of such parcels is understated;
  the surcharge itself is included (issue #18).
- Weight is capped at 70 lb, the USPS maximum. Alaska and Hawaii are out of
  scope.
- UPS 2024 and 2026 use the mid-year revision of the Daily Rates guide,
  because the December original could not be retrieved.

The same list is returned by `GET /api/meta` and shown in the app.

## What I would improve next

Open issues in the repository, in rough priority order:

- #18 model the 90 lb minimum billable weight for large and oversize packages.
- #14 capture the UPS 2025-26 and 2026-27 demand surcharge documents.
- #9 real ZIP-to-ZIP zones instead of distance bands.
- #10 per-parcel price column and order-value shipping rules (free shipping
  over a threshold).
- #11 next-year projection from announced increases.
- #13 script the source discovery so data collection runs end to end without
  an agent.
- #8 Playwright end-to-end tests at desktop and phone widths.

## Local development without Docker

Needs Python 3.12 with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Node 18.18 or
newer (the image uses Node 22).

```sh
# backend on http://localhost:8787
cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8787

# frontend on http://localhost:5173, proxies /api to localhost:8787
cd frontend && npm ci && npm run dev
```

`VITE_API_TARGET` points the dev proxy elsewhere. `http://localhost:5173/?mock=1`
runs the frontend alone on recorded API responses. The API contract is in
[docs/API.md](docs/API.md), with example payloads in `docs/api-examples/`
(regenerated by `uv run --directory backend python scripts/export_api_examples.py`).

## Tests

| Suite | Command | What it covers |
|---|---|---|
| Data | `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1 uv run pytest` (repository root) | Schema, parsers against golden cells, table invariants, manifest, citations |
| Data, full | `python3 data/fetch_raw.py && uv run pytest` | Same, with every citation checked against its PDF page |
| Backend | `cd backend && uv run pytest` | Rate engine against hand-computed quotes, rule resolution, analysis and API |
| Frontend | `cd frontend && npm ci && npm test` | Components with Testing Library and the API contract test |
| Frontend types | `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` | |

Without the PDFs, the citation and PDF parser tests fail with a message
telling you to fetch them; `ALLOW_MISSING_RAW=1` skips them on purpose
instead. End-to-end Playwright tests come with issue #8.

## Repository layout

```
backend/            FastAPI app (app/), tests, scripts; Dockerfile
frontend/           Vite + React dashboard; Dockerfile and nginx config
data/raw/           manifest.csv, SOURCES.md per carrier, committed raw files
data/pipeline/      parsers and curated rules that write data/processed/
data/processed/     the rate tables the app loads
data/tests/         data tests and golden cells
docs/               decisions, API contract, data docs, agent log
docker-compose.yml  the reviewer run path
```

## How this was built: the agent log

The project was built with Claude Code, one GitHub issue per task, each in its
own branch and git worktree, merged through pull requests. Every session and
subagent transcript is exported to [docs/agent-log/](docs/agent-log/) as
Markdown by a `SessionEnd` hook (`.claude/hooks/export-session.sh`), with the
prompts, the agent's responses and its tool calls. Home directory paths are
redacted. [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) is the running log of the
decisions those conversations led to.
# Decisions

Running log of the choices made for this project, in the order they were made.
Each entry says what was decided, the alternatives considered, and why.
See `docs/ASSIGNMENT.md` for the brief and `docs/agent-log/` for the agent
conversations that led here.

## 2026-10-22 — Problem, user and scope

**Problem.** A small online shop sends a few hundred to a few thousand parcels
a month, has no negotiated carrier contract, and pays the published list
prices of FedEx, UPS and the Postal Service. Today the carrier is chosen by
habit. The dashboard helps the owner choose the carrier per kind of parcel,
and check whether the flat shipping price charged to customers still covers
the real cost once surcharges and yearly price increases are included.

**Questions the dashboard answers.**

1. For a given parcel (weight, dimensions, distance, residential or business,
   required speed), which service is cheapest once surcharges are included,
   and what are the line items of that price?
2. Where are the breakeven points between the Postal Service and FedEx or UPS
   ground, by weight and distance?
3. For the owner's whole set of parcels, what is the blended cost per parcel
   with each carrier, and how much of it is surcharges rather than base rate?
4. How did that blended cost change year by year under each year's published
   prices, compared with the average increase the carriers announced, and
   which kinds of parcels in the mix drove the change?

**Scope decisions.**

- Timebox: issues are sized to fit about five hours of focused work (the
  brief's upper bound). Extras are tracked separately and only started if
  time remains. Time actually spent is recorded by the owner, not estimated.
- Services: three speed tiers across the three carriers — ground, two to
  three day, and next day. Weight capped at 70 lb (the USPS maximum).
- Years covered: decided after the data survey (issue 1), based on what can
  actually be downloaded and parsed reliably.
- Parcel input: CSV upload plus a bundled illustrative sample mix. Columns:
  weight, length, width, height, distance in miles, residential flag,
  required speed, and an optional per-parcel price charged to the customer.
  Dimensional weight is computed from the dimensions.
- Price charged to the customer: a single flat price is the MVP control. The
  optional per-parcel column overrides it when present.
- Fuel and peak surcharges: a documented per-year default taken from the
  published history, a slider to stress test the fuel percentage, and a peak
  season toggle. A next-year increase slider sits on the year-over-year view.
- Zone from distance: a documented distance-band to zone mapping. Real
  ZIP-to-ZIP zones are a bonus, not MVP.
- The app never fetches live data; all rate tables are committed.

## 2026-10-22 — Stack

| Area | Decision | Alternatives considered | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Backend | FastAPI, Pydantic models, pandas over committed CSV tables loaded in memory, managed with `uv` | DuckDB; SQLite | Rate cards are a few thousand rows. No database keeps Docker and setup trivial. |
| Data collection | Python scripts under `data/` that download the carriers' published rate documents, parse them (pdfplumber for PDFs), and write normalized CSVs that are committed | Hand-typed tables | Reproducible, documents provenance, and qualifies for the scraping bonus. |
| Frontend | Vite + React + TypeScript, Recharts for line and bar charts, a custom SVG heatmap for the breakeven map, plain CSS with design tokens | Chart.js (needs a matrix plugin for heatmaps); Plotly (over 1 MB, poor on mobile); Tailwind | Small bundle, declarative, the heatmap is a trivial grid. |
| Docker | `docker compose` with two services: uvicorn backend and an nginx container serving the Vite build and proxying `/api` | Single multi-stage image with FastAPI serving static files | Clean separation, one command for the reviewer. |
| Tests | pytest for pipeline, rate engine and API; Vitest + Testing Library for components; Playwright end to end at 1440 and 375 px with screenshots reviewed for UX | — | Required by the brief and by us. |
| Workflow | Private GitHub repo, one issue per task, a branch and git worktree per issue, parallel agents each in their own worktree, pull requests merged with merge commits | Commit straight to main | Keeps history and lets agents work in parallel without stepping on each other. |
| Agent log | `SessionEnd` hook exports every session (and subagent) transcript to `docs/agent-log/<session-id>.md` and commits it; home directory path redacted | Manual export | Required by the brief, zero effort once set up. |

## 2026-10-22 — Year range and data policy (from the data survey, issue #1)

Full findings in `docs/data/QUALITY.md`; sources per file in `data/raw/<carrier>/SOURCES.md`.

- **Years: 2023 through 2026**, under each year's January list prices
  (USPS 2023 uses the July 2023 tables, when Ground Advantage launched).
  2022 is dropped from the MVP because USPS sold a different product set.
  FedEx 2027 rates are already published and are kept as an optional forward year.
- **Base rates are parsed** from USPS CSV zips, FedEx XLSX (2022, 2025–2027)
  and text PDFs (FedEx 2023–2024, UPS all years), each validated against
  hand-checked prices.
- **Surcharge rules are curated** into a CSV with a source file and page per
  row, rather than parsed from prose PDFs.
- **Fuel surcharge:** per-year default from FedEx's published history,
  applied to UPS as a proxy and flagged; the UI slider overrides it. USPS has none.
- **Announced increases:** FedEx and USPS from primary sources; UPS from
  trade press, marked secondary.
- **Raw files:** only spreadsheets, CSV zips and small HTML snapshots are
  committed (about 8 MB). All PDFs are gitignored and restored by
  `data/fetch_raw.py` from `data/raw/manifest.csv` (URL, SHA-256, size),
  fetched one at a time with a pause between requests.
- **Citations:** every curated row carries file, page and verbatim quote,
  and a test checks the quote against the document.
- **USPS dimensional weight** verified in the DMM: divisor 166, then 139 from
  2026-07-12, above 1,728 cubic inches, all zones.
- **Schema** for all processed tables and the parcel CSV is fixed in
  `docs/data/SCHEMA.md` before any parser is written.

# Visual direction: the shipping ledger

The dashboard reads like a printed price sheet or a merchant's ledger, not like
a SaaS dashboard. Warm paper, black ink, hairline rules, figures set in a
newspaper serif, and colour reserved for meaning.

## Why it fits

The user is a shop owner deciding where a few dollars per parcel go. The
decision lives in a handful of numbers: which carrier is cheapest, what one
parcel costs, whether the flat price still leaves a margin. A ledger puts those
numbers first, in the largest type on the page, and pushes everything else
(assumptions, sliders, provenance) into small, quiet type around them. Rules
and columns instead of cards make it feel like an account the owner keeps, and
they print well for an accountant.

## Hierarchy

1. **The answer** (cheapest carrier, cost per parcel, margin): display serif,
   `--text-figure`, tabular figures, carrier or money colour.
2. **The question** each section answers: display serif, `--text-xl`.
3. **The owner's parcel set**: once loaded, a one-line strip (count, share to
   homes, speed split) with the full summary behind "Details", so the
   questions and the answer stay above the fold, also on a phone.

### Rule for every question view (issues #5 and #6)

The answer is the largest element of its section. Put it first under the
question, in `.answer > .answer__figure` (`--text-figure`), with a short
`.answer__caption` saying what it is ("UPS Ground, $8.41 per parcel, $1.58
margin"). Nothing else in the section, including the question (`--text-xl`),
chart titles and table figures, may be set larger. Charts and tables come
after the answer and explain it.
4. **Assumptions** (year, rate card, fuel, peak, flat price): a left rail in the
   UI face at `--text-sm`, always visible on desktop, a bottom sheet on phones
   behind a one-line summary bar.

## Palette (`src/styles/tokens.css`)

| Token | Light | Dark | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--paper` | `#F5F1E8` | `#15140F` | page |
| `--sheet` | `#FBF9F4` | `#1E1C17` | rail, inputs, raised panels |
| `--ink` | `#1C1B18` | `#EDE8DC` | text, rules, focus ring |
| `--ink-muted` | `#5E5A50` | `#A9A292` | secondary text (6.1:1 / 7.3:1) |
| `--carrier-usps` | `#1F4E9A` | `#7FA8EE` | USPS everywhere (7.1:1 / 7.7:1) |
| `--carrier-ups` | `#7A4E0F` | `#D9A35A` | UPS everywhere (6.4:1 / 8.2:1) |
| `--carrier-fedex` | `#9C2A7E` | `#E68AC9` | FedEx everywhere (6.1:1 / 7.8:1) |
| `--loss` | `#B3261E` | `#F2877E` | negative margin (5.8:1 / 7.5:1) |
| `--profit` | `#1D6B3F` | `#6FCB94` | positive margin (5.8:1 / 9.4:1) |
| `--mock` | `#8A5A00` | `#E8B860` | the mock-data banner only |

Contrast ratios are against `--paper` and meet WCAG AA for body text in both
themes. Carrier hues follow the brands loosely (postal blue, brown, purple)
so the owner recognises them without a legend. Blue and purple are close for
some colour-vision deficiencies, so colour is never the only cue: every
carrier mark carries its name or initial, and money always carries a sign and
the word "loss" or "margin".

Each carrier also has a `-wash` tint for backgrounds and heatmap cells
(issue #5 scales intensity between the wash and the full colour).

## Type

- **Newsreader** (display serif, optical sizes) for questions and figures.
  A newspaper face gives the editorial voice and has good tabular numerals.
- **IBM Plex Sans** for the interface: labels, controls, tables. Industrial,
  slightly technical, legible at 12-14 px.

Both load from Google Fonts with `display=swap`; fallbacks are Georgia and
Helvetica/Arial. All figures use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so
columns of prices line up.

## Spacing and shape

A 4 px base (`--space-1` … `--space-8`: 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 72 px) with a
deliberate jump to 48-72 px between sections, so sections read as chapters.
Corners are nearly square (`--radius: 2px`). Separation comes from hairline
rules (`--rule`) and one heavy rule under the masthead and active tab, not
from shadows; the only shadow is on the mobile controls sheet, which really
does sit above the page.

## Motion

Only opacity and transform, 120-220 ms, for the sheet and tab underline. All
of it is disabled under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.

## Charts (for issues #5 and #6)

- Use the carrier tokens for series and cells; read them in JS with
  `getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue("--carrier-usps")`
  or the `carrierColor()` helper in `src/lib/carriers.ts`, so dark mode works.
- Axis text in `--ink-muted`, gridlines in `--rule`, no chart borders.
- Announced increases and projections are dashed lines in the carrier colour.

## Questions 3 and 4 (issue #6)

Code: `src/views/blended/` (Q3) and `src/views/yearly/` (Q4). The pieces every
view shares live in one place: formatting and margin wording in `src/lib/format.ts`,
carrier names, colours and years in `src/lib/carriers.ts`, hooks (`useDebounced`,
`useLastData`, `useCssColors`) in `src/hooks/`, UI (`ChartFrame`, `ChipGroup`,
`NeedParcels`, `LoadProblem`) in `src/components/`, and their CSS in
`src/styles/views.css`, `chips.css` and `chart.css`.

**Q3, blended cost.** Answer first: the cheapest single carrier and its blended
cost per parcel (`--text-figure`), the others with their gap, then the
"best mix" (cheapest carrier per parcel) and its saving. Directly under it, the
verdict box answers "does my shipping price cover the cost?" in the money
colour (`--loss` or `--profit` border and wash), `--text-2xl`, with the share of
parcels shipped at a loss and a margin table per carrier (signed amount plus
the word "loss" or "margin", and a loss-share meter). Then the segment chips
(radio-like toggle buttons, 44 px tall, a check mark on the selected one so the
state is not colour alone), which re-query `/api/blended` and repeat the
segment's result next to the parcel count, because the answer above may be off
screen. Then the stacked cost split.

- Cost split colours (tokens in `src/styles/tokens.css`): neutral `--q3-base` for the
  base rate, a single teal ramp `--q3-sur-1..4` for surcharge kinds (darkest =
  largest kind; beyond three kinds they fold into "Other surcharges"), and
  `--q3-fuel` (ink) for fuel. Teal sits outside the carrier and money hues.
  Each carrier's row label carries its name, total and surcharge/fuel shares,
  so the split reads without the legend.

**Q4, year over year.** Answer first: for the carrier cheapest in the latest
year every carrier publishes, the percent change from its first year, with the
dollars and the announced increases compounded over the same years. A
next-year slider (default: that carrier's latest announced increase) sits in a
raised `--sheet` panel with the projected cost. The line chart uses solid
carrier lines with a marker shape per carrier (USPS circle, UPS square, FedEx
triangle; blue and purple are close under protanopia, see the validator note
below), dashed lines for the announced-increase path and dotted segments for
the projection. A "Scale" toggle switches to an index (each carrier's first
year = 100, announced paths and projection indexed the same way); it is the
default on phones, where the dollar gap between USPS and the others flattens
the slopes. Points with a note carry a "!" badge; the notes are listed in
plain words under the chart. "How much of the change is fuel?" sits right
under the chart with a small per-year fuel table. The driver chart is a
diverging bar chart from zero: warm `--q4-up` when a segment made parcels
dearer, cool `--q4-down` when cheaper (neither is the loss/profit pair), sorted
by size. Each row label gives both the contribution to the total (what the
bars show, they add up to the change) and the change per parcel within the
segment ("each", `change_total / parcels`), so a small segment that rose fast
is not hidden by a big one; the sentence names the largest contributor and,
when different, the fastest-rising segment.

**Accessibility.** Every chart is a `<figure>` with a visible text summary as
its caption and a "Show as table" toggle (`aria-pressed`). The chart SVG is
`aria-hidden`; the summary and the table carry the content. Carrier colour is
never alone: names, marker shapes or row labels go with it.

**Colour check.** The dataviz palette validator flags the carrier trio as below
the CVD target (USPS/FedEx ΔE about 5 under protanopia, light and dark), which
DESIGN.md already anticipated; Q3/Q4 therefore always pair carrier colour with
the carrier name or a marker shape.

## Q1 quote and Q2 breakeven views (issue #5)

Code in `src/views/QuoteView.tsx`, `src/views/BreakevenView.tsx` and the folders
`src/views/quote/` and `src/views/breakeven/`, each with its own CSS file. Helpers the
two views share with Q3 and Q4 (margin wording, carriers per year, debounce, the
view-level note, error and skeleton classes, the small segmented toggle) live in
`src/lib/`, `src/hooks/` and `src/styles/views.css` (see Questions 3 and 4 above).

**Q1.** The answer (cheapest total for the chosen speed) sits directly under the
question at `--text-figure`, followed by carrier and service at `--text-lg` and the
margin with a sign and the word "margin" or "loss". Below a heavy rule, the form
(left, 17 rem) and the explanation (right) share a two-column grid that stacks under
52 rem. The form prices live with a 300 ms debounce; the previous answer stays visible
at 55 % opacity while the next one loads, so typing never flashes a skeleton. Each
carrier row is a disclosure button: rank, carrier name in its colour, a stacked bar
(base solid, surcharges hatched, fuel wash with an outline, so the three parts differ
by texture and not only by tint), total and the difference to the cheapest. Line items
carry their source under the label in small muted type. Unavailable services are struck
through and muted, with the reason in words. When dimensional weight sets the billable
weight, a ruled note shows actual, dimensional and billable weight per service. Server
422 messages appear under the input they concern, in `--loss`, and the input gets
`aria-invalid`.

**Q2.** The figure is the lightest weight at which USPS Ground Advantage stops being
cheapest, with a caption naming the distances and rivals; one plain sentence per
distance band (neighbouring bands that read the same are merged) follows. The map is a
hand-built SVG: rows are weights, columns the zone-band midpoints, cell colour is the
winner's carrier colour mixed with its wash in four fixed saving steps (under $1,
$1–3, $3–10, $10+), so the legend means the same on every map. A heavy ink line marks
where USPS stops or starts winning and a dotted line where UPS and FedEx swap; runs
tall enough carry the carrier name. Colour is therefore never the only cue. The grid is
a roving-tabindex `role="grid"` (arrows, Home/End, PageUp/PageDown, Escape closes the
tooltip); hover, tap or focus shows every carrier's total. "Show as table" swaps the
map for a sticky-header table. At 375 px the map fits without horizontal scroll (columns
shrink, headers abbreviate to "z5").
# Frontend

Vite + React + TypeScript dashboard. Design direction and rules: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Run locally

Node 18.18+ (Docker uses Node 22).

```sh
npm ci
npm run dev            # http://localhost:5173
```

The dev server proxies `/api` to the backend at `VITE_API_TARGET`, default
`http://localhost:8787`. Start the backend on that port from the repository root:

```sh
cd backend && uv run uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8787
```

In Docker the built app is served by nginx instead, which proxies `/api` to the
backend container; see the root README.

To point at a backend elsewhere: `VITE_API_TARGET=http://localhost:9000 npm run dev`
(or put the variable in `frontend/.env.local`).

Without a backend, open `http://localhost:5173/?mock=1`: the app serves the backend's
recorded example responses from `src/api/__fixtures__/` and shows a "Mock data" banner.
Mock answers do not change with the inputs.

## Scripts

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` | dev server with the `/api` proxy |
| `npm run test` | Vitest + Testing Library, including the API contract test |
| `npm run typecheck` | `tsc -b --noEmit` |
| `npm run build` | type-check and build into `dist/` |

## API contract

`src/api/types.ts` mirrors `docs/API.md` and `backend/app/api/models.py`.
`src/api/contract.test.ts` checks every example payload in `src/api/__fixtures__/`
(copied from `docs/api-examples/`) against the runtime guards in `src/api/guards.ts`, so
a change on either side fails the tests until both agree.

import { useCallback, useId, useMemo, useRef, useState } from "react";
import { useApi, useLoad } from "./api/ApiContext";
import { isMockMode } from "./api/client";
import { ControlRail, assumptionsLine } from "./components/controls/ControlRail";
import { ParcelSetPanel } from "./components/parcels/ParcelSetPanel";
import { QuestionTabs } from "./components/QuestionTabs";
import { Footer } from "./components/Footer";
import { useParcelSet } from "./hooks/useParcelSet";
import { useUrlState } from "./hooks/useUrlState";
import { useMediaQuery } from "./hooks/useMediaQuery";
import { INERT_WHILE_SHEET, SHEET_QUERY, useSheet } from "./hooks/useSheet";
import { controlsFromMeta, type ViewId } from "./state/urlState";
import type { ViewProps } from "./views/types";
import { QuoteView } from "./views/QuoteView";
import { BreakevenView } from "./views/BreakevenView";
import { BlendedView } from "./views/BlendedView";
import { YearlyView } from "./views/YearlyView";

const VIEW_COMPONENTS: Record<ViewId, (p: ViewProps) => JSX.Element> = {
  quote: QuoteView,
  breakeven: BreakevenView,
  blended: BlendedView,
  yearly: YearlyView,
};


export function App() {
  const api = useApi();
  const [metaAttempt, setMetaAttempt] = useState(0);
  const metaState = useLoad((signal) => api.meta(signal), [api, metaAttempt]);
  const meta = metaState.status === "ok" ? metaState.data : null;
  const metaDefaults = useMemo(() => (meta ? controlsFromMeta(meta.defaults) : null), [meta]);
  const [state, dispatch] = useUrlState(metaDefaults);
  const parcelSet = useParcelSet();
  const isSheet = useMediaQuery(SHEET_QUERY);
  const sheet = useSheet(isSheet);
  const railId = useId();
  const railTitleId = useId();
  const inert = { [INERT_WHILE_SHEET]: "" };
  const mock = isMockMode();

  const fileInputRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const openFilePicker = useCallback(() => fileInputRef.current?.click(), []);

  const viewProps: ViewProps = {
    controls: state.controls,
    meta,
    parcels: parcelSet.set?.parcels ?? null,
    onLoadSample: parcelSet.loadSample,
    onUploadCsv: openFilePicker,
  };

  return (
    <>
      <a className="skip-link" href="#main" {...inert}>
        Skip to the questions
      </a>
      {mock && (
        <p className="mock-banner" role="note" {...inert}>
          <strong>Mock data.</strong> Recorded example answers from the rate service; they do not change with your inputs.
        </p>
      )}
      <header className="masthead" {...inert}>
        <div className="masthead__inner">
          <p className="kicker masthead__edition">
            {state.controls.year} published list prices · USPS, UPS, FedEx
          </p>
          <h1 className="masthead__title">Parcel Rates</h1>
          <p className="masthead__deck">
            Which carrier is cheapest for each kind of parcel you ship, and does your flat shipping price still cover
            the real cost after surcharges and yearly increases?
          </p>
        </div>
      </header>

      <div className="mobile-bar" {...inert}>
        <p className="mobile-bar__line">{assumptionsLine(state)}</p>
        <button
          ref={sheet.toggleRef}
          type="button"
          className="btn mobile-bar__toggle"
          aria-expanded={sheet.open}
          aria-controls={railId}
          onClick={() => sheet.setOpen(!sheet.open)}
        >
          Adjust
        </button>
      </div>

      <div className="layout">
        {sheet.open && (
          <div className="sheet-backdrop" aria-hidden="true" onClick={sheet.close} />
        )}
        <aside
          id={railId}
          ref={sheet.sheetRef}
          className={`rail ${sheet.open ? "rail--open" : ""}`}
          aria-labelledby={railTitleId}
          {...(sheet.open ? { role: "dialog", "aria-modal": true } : {})}
        >
          <div className="rail__head">
            <h2 id={railTitleId} className="kicker rail__title">
              Assumptions
            </h2>
            <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet rail__close" onClick={sheet.close}>
              Done
            </button>
          </div>
          <ControlRail
            state={state}
            dispatch={dispatch}
            meta={meta}
            metaStatus={metaState.status === "ok" ? "ok" : metaState.status}
            onRetryMeta={() => setMetaAttempt((n) => n + 1)}
          />
        </aside>

        <main id="main" className="main" tabIndex={-1} {...inert}>
          <ParcelSetPanel
            set={parcelSet.set}
            status={parcelSet.status}
            zoneBands={meta?.zone_bands}
            onLoadSample={parcelSet.loadSample}
            onLoadFile={parcelSet.loadFile}
            onClear={parcelSet.clear}
            fileInputRef={fileInputRef}
          />
          <QuestionTabs
            active={state.view}
            onSelect={(view) => dispatch({ type: "view", view })}
            renderPanel={(id) => {
              const View = VIEW_COMPONENTS[id];
              return <View {...viewProps} />;
            }}
          />
          <Footer meta={meta} status={metaState.status} />
        </main>
      </div>
    </>
  );
}
import { useRef, type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode } from "react";
import type { ViewId } from "../state/urlState";
import { QUESTIONS } from "../views/types";

export interface QuestionTabsProps {
  active: ViewId;
  onSelect: (id: ViewId) => void;
  renderPanel: (id: ViewId) => ReactNode;
}

const tabId = (id: ViewId) => `tab-${id}`;
const panelId = (id: ViewId) => `panel-${id}`;

/** WAI-ARIA tabs with automatic activation; arrow keys, Home and End move between questions. */
export function QuestionTabs({ active, onSelect, renderPanel }: QuestionTabsProps) {
  const refs = useRef<Partial<Record<ViewId, HTMLButtonElement | null>>>({});
  const activeDef = QUESTIONS.find((q) => q.id === active) ?? QUESTIONS[0]!;

  const onKeyDown = (e: KeyboardEvent<HTMLDivElement>) => {
    const i = QUESTIONS.findIndex((q) => q.id === active);
    const last = QUESTIONS.length - 1;
    const next =
      e.key === "ArrowRight" ? (i === last ? 0 : i + 1)
      : e.key === "ArrowLeft" ? (i === 0 ? last : i - 1)
      : e.key === "Home" ? 0
      : e.key === "End" ? last
      : null;
    if (next === null) return;
    e.preventDefault();
    const id = QUESTIONS[next]!.id;
    onSelect(id);
    refs.current[id]?.focus();
  };

  return (
    <div className="questions">
      <div className="questions__tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="Questions" onKeyDown={onKeyDown}>
        {QUESTIONS.map((q) => (
          <button
            key={q.id}
            ref={(el) => {
              refs.current[q.id] = el;
            }}
            id={tabId(q.id)}
            type="button"
            role="tab"
            aria-selected={q.id === active}
            aria-controls={panelId(q.id)}
            tabIndex={q.id === active ? 0 : -1}
            className="questions__tab"
            onClick={() => onSelect(q.id)}
          >
            <span className="questions__num">{String(q.number).padStart(2, "0")}</span>
            <span className="questions__short">{q.short}</span>
          </button>
        ))}
      </div>
      <section
        id={panelId(activeDef.id)}
        role="tabpanel"
        aria-labelledby={tabId(activeDef.id)}
        className="questions__panel"
        tabIndex={0}
      >
        <p className="kicker">Question {activeDef.number}</p>
        <h2 className="questions__question">{activeDef.question}</h2>
        {renderPanel(activeDef.id)}
      </section>
    </div>
  );
}
import { useEffect, useId, useMemo, useRef, useState, type RefObject } from "react";
import type { ZoneBand } from "../../api/types";
import { TIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { CSV_TEMPLATE } from "../../lib/parcelCsv";
import { summarize, type ParcelSummary as Summary } from "../../lib/summary";
import type { ParcelSet, ParcelSetStatus } from "../../hooks/useParcelSet";
import { ParcelSummary } from "./ParcelSummary";
import { formatInt, formatShare, TIER_NAME } from "../../lib/format";

export interface ParcelSetPanelProps {
  set: ParcelSet | null;
  status: ParcelSetStatus;
  /** Zone bands from /api/meta; the USPS ones bucket the distance distribution. */
  zoneBands?: ZoneBand[];
  onLoadSample: () => void;
  onLoadFile: (file: File) => void;
  onClear: () => void;
  /** The CSV file input, so the question views' "Upload CSV" buttons can open the same picker. */
  fileInputRef?: RefObject<HTMLInputElement>;
}

const TEMPLATE_HREF = `data:text/csv;charset=utf-8,${encodeURIComponent(CSV_TEMPLATE)}`;
const MAX_LISTED = 12;

function Problems({ status }: { status: Extract<ParcelSetStatus, { kind: "error" | "notice" }> }) {
  const shown = status.problems.slice(0, MAX_LISTED);
  const rest = status.problems.length - shown.length;
  return (
    <div
      className={`problems ${status.kind === "error" ? "problems--error" : "problems--notice"}`}
      role={status.kind === "error" ? "alert" : "status"}
    >
      <p className="problems__title">{status.message}</p>
      {shown.length > 0 && (
        <ul className="problems__list">
          {shown.map((p, i) => (
            <li key={i}>
              <span className="problems__where">{p.row === null ? "File" : `Row ${p.row}`}</span>
              <span>{p.message}</span>
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
      {rest > 0 && <p className="problems__more">and {rest} more. Fix these first; the rest often share the same cause.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}

/** One line: count, share to homes, speed split. */
function StripFacts({ summary }: { summary: Summary }) {
  return (
    <p className="strip__facts">
      <span className="strip__count">
        <span className="figure">{formatInt(summary.parcels)}</span> parcels
      </span>
      <span>{formatShare(summary.residentialShare)} to homes</span>
      <span>
        {TIERS.filter((t) => summary.byTier[t] > 0)
          .map((t) => `${formatShare(summary.byTier[t])} ${TIER_NAME[t].toLowerCase()}`)
          .join(" · ")}
      </span>
    </p>
  );
}

export function ParcelSetPanel({ set, status, zoneBands, onLoadSample, onLoadFile, onClear, fileInputRef }: ParcelSetPanelProps) {
  const fileId = useId();
  const headingId = useId();
  const detailsId = useId();
  const ownRef = useRef<HTMLInputElement>(null);
  const inputRef = fileInputRef ?? ownRef;
  const summary = useMemo(() => (set ? summarize(set.parcels, zoneBands) : null), [set, zoneBands]);
  const busy = status.kind === "loading";
  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState(false);

  // A newly loaded set starts collapsed, so the questions stay above the fold.
  useEffect(() => setExpanded(false), [set]);

  const fileInput = (
    <input
      ref={inputRef}
      id={fileId}
      className="visually-hidden"
      type="file"
      accept=".csv,text/csv"
      disabled={busy}
      onChange={(e) => {
        const file = e.target.files?.[0];
        if (file) onLoadFile(file);
        if (inputRef.current) inputRef.current.value = "";
      }}
    />
  );
  const uploadLabel = (text: string) => (
    <label htmlFor={fileId} className="btn file-btn">
      {busy && status.what === "file" ? "Reading file…" : text}
    </label>
  );
  const sampleButton = (
    <button type="button" className={`btn ${set ? "" : "btn--primary"}`} onClick={onLoadSample} disabled={busy}>
      {busy && status.what === "sample" ? "Loading sample…" : set ? "Use the sample mix" : "Load sample mix"}
    </button>
  );
  const templateLink = (
    <a className="btn btn--quiet" href={TEMPLATE_HREF} download="parcel-set-template.csv">
      CSV template
    </a>
  );
  const problems = (status.kind === "error" || status.kind === "notice") && <Problems status={status} />;

  if (!set || !summary) {
    return (
      <section className="parcels" aria-labelledby={headingId} aria-busy={busy}>
        <header className="parcels__head">
          <h2 id={headingId} className="parcels__title">
            Your parcels
          </h2>
          <div className="parcels__actions">
            {sampleButton}
            {fileInput}
            {uploadLabel("Upload CSV")}
            {templateLink}
          </div>
        </header>
        {problems}
        <div className="parcels__empty">
          <p className="parcels__empty-lead">No parcels loaded yet.</p>
          <p>
            Questions 3 and 4 price your whole mix. Load the sample (an illustrative home-goods shop, not real data) to explore, or upload a CSV with one row per kind
            of parcel: weight, distance, home or business, speed, and how many you ship.
          </p>
        </div>
      </section>
    );
  }

  return (
    <section className="parcels parcels--loaded" aria-labelledby={headingId} aria-busy={busy}>
      <div className="strip">
        <div className="strip__main">
          <h2 id={headingId} className="kicker strip__title">
            Your parcels
            <span className="strip__source"> · {set.source === "sample" ? "sample mix, an example" : set.name}</span>
          </h2>
          <StripFacts summary={summary} />
        </div>
        <div className="strip__actions">
          <button
            type="button"
            className="btn"
            aria-expanded={expanded}
            aria-controls={detailsId}
            onClick={() => setExpanded((e) => !e)}
          >
            {expanded ? "Hide details" : "Details"}
          </button>
          {fileInput}
          {uploadLabel("Replace CSV")}
        </div>
      </div>
      {problems}
      <div id={detailsId} className="parcels__details" hidden={!expanded}>
        {set.description && <p className="parcels__source">{set.description}</p>}
        <ParcelSummary summary={summary} />
        <div className="parcels__actions">
          {sampleButton}
          {templateLink}
          <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet" onClick={onClear}>
            Clear the set
          </button>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}
import type { Bucket, ParcelSummary as Summary } from "../../lib/summary";
import { TIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { formatInt, formatShare, TIER_NAME } from "../../lib/format";

function MiniBars({ title, unit, buckets }: { title: string; unit: string; buckets: Bucket[] }) {
  const max = Math.max(...buckets.map((b) => b.share), 0.0001);
  return (
    <figure className="minibars">
      <figcaption className="kicker">{title}</figcaption>
      <table className="minibars__table">
        <caption className="visually-hidden">
          Parcels by {title.toLowerCase()}, share of the set
        </caption>
        <tbody>
          {buckets.map((b) => (
            <tr key={b.label}>
              <th scope="row">
                {b.label}
                {unit && <span className="minibars__unit"> {unit}</span>}
                {b.detail && <span className="minibars__detail">{b.detail}</span>}
              </th>
              <td className="minibars__bar" aria-hidden="true">
                <span style={{ transform: `scaleX(${b.share / max})` }} />
              </td>
              <td className="minibars__value">
                {formatShare(b.share)}
                <span className="visually-hidden"> ({formatInt(b.count)} parcels)</span>
              </td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </figure>
  );
}

export function ParcelSummary({ summary }: { summary: Summary }) {
  return (
    <div className="summary">
      <dl className="summary__facts">
        <div className="summary__lead">
          <dt className="kicker">Parcels in the set</dt>
          <dd className="figure summary__count">{formatInt(summary.parcels)}</dd>
          <dd className="summary__sub">
            {formatInt(summary.rows)} row{summary.rows === 1 ? "" : "s"} · mean {summary.meanWeightLb.toFixed(1)} lb
          </dd>
        </div>
        <div>
          <dt className="kicker">To homes</dt>
          <dd className="figure summary__fact">{formatShare(summary.residentialShare)}</dd>
          <dd className="summary__sub">residential addresses</dd>
        </div>
        <div>
          <dt className="kicker">Speed</dt>
          <dd className="summary__tiers">
            {TIERS.map((t) => (
              <span key={t}>
                <span className="summary__tier-share">{formatShare(summary.byTier[t])}</span> {TIER_NAME[t]}
              </span>
            ))}
          </dd>
        </div>
        {summary.withOwnPrice > 0 && (
          <div className="summary__wide">
            <dt className="visually-hidden">Own price</dt>
            <dd className="summary__note">
              <strong>{formatInt(summary.withOwnPrice)}</strong> parcel{summary.withOwnPrice === 1 ? " has its" : "s have their"}{" "}
              own price, which overrides the flat price.
            </dd>
          </div>
        )}
      </dl>
      <div className="summary__dists">
        <MiniBars title="Weight" unit="lb" buckets={summary.weight} />
        <MiniBars title="Distance, USPS zone" unit="" buckets={summary.distance} />
      </div>

import { useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";

/** Mirrors the CSS breakpoint below which the settings rail becomes a bottom sheet. */
export const SHEET_QUERY = "(max-width: 63.999rem)";

const FOCUSABLE =
  'a[href], button:not([disabled]), input:not([disabled]):not([type="hidden"]), select:not([disabled]), textarea:not([disabled]), [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';

/** Elements marked with this attribute become inert while the sheet is open. */
export const INERT_WHILE_SHEET = "data-inert-while-sheet";

function focusables(root: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[] {
  return [...root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(FOCUSABLE)].filter((el) => !el.closest("[hidden]"));
}

/**
 * Modal bottom sheet: focus moves in on open, Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, the rest of the
 * page is inert, Escape closes, and focus returns to the button that opened it.
 */
export function useSheet(isSheet: boolean) {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const toggleRef = useRef<HTMLButtonElement>(null);
  const sheetRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
  const active = open && isSheet;

  // Focus goes back to the opener in the effect cleanup, after `inert` is lifted from it.
  const close = useCallback(() => setOpen(false), []);

  // Growing past the breakpoint turns the sheet back into the always-visible rail.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (!isSheet) setOpen(false);
  }, [isSheet]);

  useEffect(() => {
    const sheet = sheetRef.current;
    if (!active || !sheet) return;
    focusables(sheet)[0]?.focus();

    const outside = [...document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(`[${INERT_WHILE_SHEET}]`)];
    outside.forEach((el) => el.setAttribute("inert", ""));

    const onKey = (e: KeyboardEvent) => {
      if (e.key === "Escape") {
        e.preventDefault();
        close();
        return;
      }
      if (e.key !== "Tab") return;
      const items = focusables(sheet);
      const first = items[0];
      const last = items[items.length - 1];
      if (!first || !last) return;
      const current = document.activeElement;
      if (e.shiftKey && (current === first || !sheet.contains(current))) {
        e.preventDefault();
        last.focus();
      } else if (!e.shiftKey && (current === last || !sheet.contains(current))) {
        e.preventDefault();
        first.focus();
      }
    };
    document.addEventListener("keydown", onKey);
    return () => {
      document.removeEventListener("keydown", onKey);
      outside.forEach((el) => el.removeAttribute("inert"));
      toggleRef.current?.focus();
    };
  }, [active, close]);

  return { open: active, setOpen, close, toggleRef, sheetRef };
}
import type { FuelGroup, MetaDefaults, UspsRateCard } from "../api/types";

/**
 * The controls as the UI holds them: every field resolved. Assignable to the request
 * type `Controls`, which leaves fields with a server default optional.
 */
export interface ControlsState {
  year: number;
  usps_rate_card: UspsRateCard;
  peak: boolean;
  flat_price: number;
  fuel_override_percent?: { ground?: number; express?: number };
}

export function controlsFromMeta(d: MetaDefaults): ControlsState {
  return { year: d.year, usps_rate_card: d.usps_rate_card, peak: d.peak, flat_price: d.flat_price };
}

export const VIEWS = ["quote", "breakeven", "blended", "yearly"] as const;
export type ViewId = (typeof VIEWS)[number];

export interface AppState {
  controls: ControlsState;
  view: ViewId;
}

export const FALLBACK_CONTROLS: ControlsState = {
  year: 2026,
  usps_rate_card: "commercial",
  peak: false,
  flat_price: 9.99,
};

export const FUEL_MIN = 0;
export const FUEL_MAX = 40;
export const PRICE_MAX = 1000;

const KEYS = {
  year: "year",
  card: "usps",
  fuelGround: "fuel_ground",
  fuelExpress: "fuel_express",
  peak: "peak",
  price: "price",
  view: "view",
} as const;

/** Params the app owns; anything else in the query string (e.g. mock=1) is preserved. */
const OWNED = new Set<string>(Object.values(KEYS));

function num(params: URLSearchParams, key: string, min: number, max: number): number | undefined {
  const raw = params.get(key);
  if (raw === null || raw.trim() === "") return undefined;
  const n = Number(raw);
  return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= min && n <= max ? n : undefined;
}

export function readState(search: string, defaults: ControlsState = FALLBACK_CONTROLS): AppState {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(search);
  const year = num(params, KEYS.year, 2000, 2100);
  const card = params.get(KEYS.card);
  const ground = num(params, KEYS.fuelGround, FUEL_MIN, FUEL_MAX);
  const express = num(params, KEYS.fuelExpress, FUEL_MIN, FUEL_MAX);
  const price = num(params, KEYS.price, 0, PRICE_MAX);
  const view = params.get(KEYS.view);
  const fuel: Partial<Record<FuelGroup, number>> = {
    ...(ground !== undefined ? { ground } : {}),
    ...(express !== undefined ? { express } : {}),
  };
  const controls: ControlsState = {
    year: year !== undefined && Number.isInteger(year) ? year : defaults.year,
    usps_rate_card: card === "retail" || card === "commercial" ? card : defaults.usps_rate_card,
    peak: params.has(KEYS.peak) ? params.get(KEYS.peak) === "1" : defaults.peak,
    flat_price: price ?? defaults.flat_price,
    ...(Object.keys(fuel).length > 0 ? { fuel_override_percent: fuel } : {}),
  };
  return { controls, view: (VIEWS as readonly string[]).includes(view ?? "") ? (view as ViewId) : "quote" };
}

/** Serialize, leaving out values equal to the defaults so shared links stay short. */
export function writeState(state: AppState, currentSearch = "", defaults: ControlsState = FALLBACK_CONTROLS): string {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(currentSearch);
  for (const key of OWNED) params.delete(key);
  const c = state.controls;
  if (c.year !== defaults.year) params.set(KEYS.year, String(c.year));
  if (c.usps_rate_card !== defaults.usps_rate_card) params.set(KEYS.card, c.usps_rate_card);
  if (c.fuel_override_percent?.ground !== undefined) params.set(KEYS.fuelGround, String(c.fuel_override_percent.ground));
  if (c.fuel_override_percent?.express !== undefined) params.set(KEYS.fuelExpress, String(c.fuel_override_percent.express));
  if (c.peak !== defaults.peak) params.set(KEYS.peak, c.peak ? "1" : "0");
  if (c.flat_price !== defaults.flat_price) params.set(KEYS.price, String(c.flat_price));
  if (state.view !== "quote") params.set(KEYS.view, state.view);
  const out = params.toString();
  return out ? `?${out}` : "";
}

/* ---------- reducer ---------- */

export type Action =
  | { type: "year"; year: number }
  | { type: "card"; card: UspsRateCard }
  | { type: "fuel"; group: FuelGroup; percent: number }
  | { type: "fuelReset"; group: FuelGroup }
  | { type: "peak"; peak: boolean }
  | { type: "price"; price: number }
  | { type: "view"; view: ViewId }
  | { type: "replace"; state: AppState };

function withFuel(c: ControlsState, group: FuelGroup, percent: number | undefined): ControlsState {
  const { [group]: _dropped, ...rest } = c.fuel_override_percent ?? {};
  const next = percent === undefined ? rest : { ...rest, [group]: percent };
  const { fuel_override_percent: _old, ...base } = c;
  return Object.keys(next).length > 0 ? { ...base, fuel_override_percent: next } : base;
}

export function reducer(state: AppState, action: Action): AppState {
  const set = (controls: ControlsState): AppState => ({ ...state, controls });
  switch (action.type) {
    case "year":
      // A new year has its own fuel defaults; an override from another year would mislead.
      return set(withFuel(withFuel({ ...state.controls, year: action.year }, "ground", undefined), "express", undefined));
    case "card":
      return set({ ...state.controls, usps_rate_card: action.card });
    case "fuel":
      return set(withFuel(state.controls, action.group, Math.min(FUEL_MAX, Math.max(FUEL_MIN, action.percent))));
    case "fuelReset":
      return set(withFuel(state.controls, action.group, undefined));
    case "peak":
      return set({ ...state.controls, peak: action.peak });
    case "price":
      return set({ ...state.controls, flat_price: Math.min(PRICE_MAX, Math.max(0, action.price)) });
    case "view":
      return { ...state, view: action.view };
    case "replace":
      return action.state;
  }
}

import { useEffect, useId, useState } from "react";

/** One-line summary of the assumptions, shown in the mobile bar. */
export function assumptionsLine(state: AppState): string {
  const c = state.controls;
  const o = c.fuel_override_percent;
  const fuel = o

  return [String(c.year), `USPS ${c.usps_rate_card}`, fuel, c.peak ? "peak" : null, `${formatUsd(c.flat_price)} charged`]

function PriceInput({ value, onCommit }: { value: number; onCommit: (n: number) => void }) {
  const id = useId();
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState(value.toFixed(2));
  const [problem, setProblem] = useState<string | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => setDraft(value.toFixed(2)), [value]);

  const commit = () => {
    const cleaned = draft.trim().replace(/^\$/, "");
    const n = Number(cleaned);
    if (cleaned === "" || !Number.isFinite(n) || n < 0 || n > 1000) {
      setProblem("Enter a price between $0 and $1,000");
      return;
    }
    setProblem(null);
    onCommit(Math.round(n * 100) / 100);
  };

  return (
    <div className="control">
      <label htmlFor={id} className="control__label">
        Flat price you charge per parcel
      </label>
      <div className={`money-input ${problem ? "money-input--invalid" : ""}`}>
        <span aria-hidden="true">$</span>
        <input
          id={id}
          inputMode="decimal"
          autoComplete="off"
          value={draft}
          aria-invalid={problem ? true : undefined}
          aria-describedby={`${id}-hint`}
          onChange={(e) => setDraft(e.target.value)}
          onBlur={commit}
          onKeyDown={(e) => {
            if (e.key === "Enter") commit();
          }}
        />
      </div>
      <p id={`${id}-hint`} className={problem ? "control__error" : "control__hint"}>

          </span>
        ) : (

        {isOverridden && (
          <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet fuel__reset" onClick={onReset}>

import { useEffect, useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { useApi, useLoad } from "../api/ApiContext";
import { ApiError } from "../api/client";
import type { QuoteResponse } from "../api/types";
import { draftToParcel, DEFAULT_DRAFT, type Draft } from "./quote/draft";
import { QuoteForm } from "./quote/QuoteForm";
import { problemsByField, zonesByCarrier, type FormField } from "./quote/quoteModel";

import type { ViewProps } from "./types";

import "./quote/quote.css";
import { useDebounced } from "../hooks/useDebounced";
import { CARRIER_NAME, carriersForYear, missingCarriersNote } from "../lib/carriers";

export interface QuoteViewProps extends ViewProps {
  /** Wait this long after the last keystroke before asking for a quote. */
  debounceMs?: number;
  initialDraft?: Draft;
}

export function QuoteView({ controls, meta, parcels, debounceMs = 300, initialDraft = DEFAULT_DRAFT }: QuoteViewProps) {
  const api = useApi();
  const [draft, setDraft] = useState<Draft>(initialDraft);
  const [attempt, setAttempt] = useState(0);
  const built = useMemo(() => draftToParcel(draft), [draft]);
  const requestKey = built.parcel ? JSON.stringify({ parcel: built.parcel, controls }) : null;
  const settledKey = useDebounced(requestKey, debounceMs);

  const state = useLoad<QuoteResponse>(
    settledKey ? (signal) => api.quote(JSON.parse(settledKey), signal) : null,
    [api, settledKey, attempt],
  );

  // Keep the last answer on screen (dimmed) while the next one loads, so typing does not flash.
  const [last, setLast] = useState<{ key: string; data: QuoteResponse } | null>(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (state.status === "ok" && settledKey) setLast({ key: settledKey, data: state.data });
  }, [state, settledKey]);

  const apiError = state.status === "error" ? state.error : null;
  const serverProblems = apiError instanceof ApiError && apiError.status === 422 ? problemsByField(apiError.problems) : null;
  const errors: Partial<Record<FormField, string[]>> = { ...(serverProblems?.byField ?? {}) };
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(built.errors ?? {})) errors[k as FormField] = [v];

  const pending = requestKey !== settledKey || state.status === "loading";
  const shown = state.status === "ok" ? state.data : apiError ? null : (last?.data ?? null);
  // Fresh only when the answer on screen is the one for the inputs as they are now.
  const fresh = state.status === "ok" && settledKey === requestKey;
  const stale = shown !== null && !fresh;
  const actualLb = built.parcel?.weight_lb ?? 0;

  const available = carriersForYear(meta, controls.year);
  const yearNote = missingCarriersNote(available, controls.year, CARRIER_NAME);
  const blocked = built.errors !== null || serverProblems !== null;

  return (
    <div className="qv">
      {yearNote && (
        <p className="view-note" role="note">
          {yearNote}
        </p>
      )}

      <div className="qv__answer" aria-live="polite" aria-busy={pending}>
        {blocked ? (
          <div className="answer qa">
            <p className="kicker">Cheapest for this parcel</p>
            <p className="answer__figure qa__none">$—.——</p>
            <p className="answer__caption">Fix the input marked in “Your parcel” to see the price.</p>
          </div>
        ) : apiError ? (
          <div className="view-error" role="alert">
            <p className="view-error__title">The quote could not be priced.</p>
            <p>{apiError.message}</p>
            <button type="button" className="btn" onClick={() => setAttempt((n) => n + 1)}>
              Try again
            </button>
          </div>
        ) : shown ? (
          <div className={stale ? "is-stale" : undefined}>
            <QuoteAnswer res={shown} tier={draft.speed} flatPrice={controls.flat_price} />
          </div>
        ) : (
          <div className="answer qa" data-testid="quote-loading">
            <p className="kicker">Cheapest for this parcel</p>
            <p className="answer__figure skeleton skeleton--figure" aria-label="Pricing…">
              $00.00
            </p>
            <p className="skeleton skeleton--line" aria-hidden="true" />
          </div>
        )}
      </div>

      <div className="qv__grid">
        <QuoteForm
          draft={draft}
          onChange={setDraft}
          errors={errors}
          zones={shown && !stale ? zonesByCarrier(shown.quotes) : null}
          parcels={parcels}
        />
        <div className="qv__detail">
          {serverProblems && serverProblems.other.length > 0 && (
            <ul className="view-error" role="alert">
              {serverProblems.other.map((p, i) => (
                <li key={i}>{p.field ? `${p.field}: ${p.message}` : p.message}</li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          )}
          {shown && !blocked ? (
            <div className={stale ? "is-stale" : undefined}>
              <QuoteBreakdown
                res={shown}
                tier={draft.speed}
                actualLb={actualLb}
                onTier={(t) => setDraft({ ...draft, speed: t })}
              />
            </div>
          ) : !apiError && !blocked ? (
            <div className="skeleton-rows" aria-hidden="true">
              <span className="skeleton skeleton--row" />
              <span className="skeleton skeleton--row" />
              <span className="skeleton skeleton--row" />
            </div>
          ) : null}
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}
import { useId, type ReactNode } from "react";
import type { Carrier, DeliveryArea, Parcel, Tier } from "../../api/types";
import { CARRIERS, TIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { draftFromParcel, draftWeight, type Draft } from "./draft";
import type { FormField } from "./quoteModel";
import { CARRIER_NAME } from "../../lib/carriers";
import { TIER_NAME } from "../../lib/format";

export interface QuoteFormProps {
  draft: Draft;
  onChange: (next: Draft) => void;
  /** Messages per field: local shape checks and the server's 422 messages. */
  errors: Partial<Record<FormField, string[]>>;
  /** Zone per carrier from the last quote, shown under the distance. */
  zones: Partial<Record<Carrier, number>> | null;
  parcels: Parcel[] | null;
}

const AREA_LABEL: Record<DeliveryArea, string> = {
  none: "Standard area",
  das: "Remote (DAS)",
  extended: "Extended remote",
};

function zoneLine(zones: Partial<Record<Carrier, number>>): string | null {
  const entries = CARRIERS.filter((c) => zones[c] !== undefined).map((c) => [c, zones[c]!] as const);
  if (entries.length === 0) return null;
  const distinct = new Set(entries.map(([, z]) => z));
  if (distinct.size === 1) return `Zone ${entries[0]![1]}${entries.length > 1 ? " for every carrier" : ` (${CARRIER_NAME[entries[0]![0]]})`}`;
  return entries.map(([c, z]) => `${CARRIER_NAME[c]} zone ${z}`).join(" · ");
}

function parcelLabel(p: Parcel, i: number): string {
  const dims = p.length_in ? ` · ${p.length_in}×${p.width_in}×${p.height_in} in` : "";
  return `#${i + 1}: ${p.weight_lb} lb${dims} · ${p.distance_miles} mi · ${p.residential ? "home" : "business"} · ${TIER_NAME[p.speed]}`;
}

const MAX_PICKS = 300;

function Errors({ id, messages }: { id: string; messages: string[] | undefined }) {
  if (!messages || messages.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <p id={id} className="control__error qf__error">
      {messages.join(" ")}
    </p>
  );
}

function Field({ label, htmlFor, children, hint }: { label: string; htmlFor?: string; children: ReactNode; hint?: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <div className="qf__field">
      <label className="control__label" htmlFor={htmlFor}>
        {label}
      </label>
      {children}
      {hint}
    </div>
  );
}

export function QuoteForm({ draft, onChange, errors, zones, parcels }: QuoteFormProps) {

  const described = (field: FormField) => (errors[field]?.length ? { "aria-describedby": id(`${field}-err`), "aria-invalid": true } : {});
  const weight = draftWeight(draft);
  const ozUsed = draft.oz.trim() !== "" && weight !== null && !Number.isNaN(weight);

          <select
            id={id("pick")}
            className="select"

            <option value="">Choose a parcel…</option>
            {parcels.slice(0, MAX_PICKS).map((p, i) => (

            ))}
          </select>
        </Field>
      )}

      <fieldset className="control qf__group">
        <legend className="control__label">Weight</legend>
        <div className="qf__pair">
          <label className="qf__unit">
            <input
              className="qf__input"
              inputMode="decimal"
              value={draft.lb}
              onChange={(e) => set("lb", e.target.value)}
              aria-label="Weight in pounds"
              {...described("weight")}
            />
            <span aria-hidden="true">lb</span>
          </label>
          <label className="qf__unit">
            <input
              className="qf__input"
              inputMode="decimal"
              value={draft.oz}
              onChange={(e) => set("oz", e.target.value)}
              aria-label="Plus ounces"
              {...described("weight")}
              placeholder="0"
            />
            <span aria-hidden="true">oz</span>
          </label>
        </div>
        <p className="control__hint">
          {ozUsed ? `= ${weight} lb. ` : ""}Ounces help for light parcels: USPS prices them in ounce steps under 1 lb.
        </p>
        <Errors id={id("weight-err")} messages={errors.weight} />
      </fieldset>

      <fieldset className="control qf__group">
        <legend className="control__label">
          Box size <span className="qf__optional">optional, inches</span>
        </legend>
        <div className="qf__dims">
          {(["length", "width", "height"] as const).map((k, i) => (
            <label key={k} className="qf__unit">
              <input
                className="qf__input"
                inputMode="decimal"
                value={draft[k]}
                onChange={(e) => set(k, e.target.value)}
                aria-label={`${k[0]!.toUpperCase()}${k.slice(1)} in inches`}
                {...described("dims")}
              />
              {i < 2 && <span aria-hidden="true">×</span>}
            </label>
          ))}
        </div>
        <p className="control__hint">Large light boxes are billed by size (dimensional weight).</p>
        <Errors id={id("dims-err")} messages={errors.dims} />
      </fieldset>

      <Field
        label="Distance"
        htmlFor={id("distance")}
        hint={
          <>
            {zoneText && (
              <p className="control__hint qf__zone" aria-live="polite">
                {zoneText}

            <Errors id={id("distance-err")} messages={errors.distance} />

        }
      >
        <label className="qf__unit">
          <input
            id={id("distance")}
            className="qf__input"
            inputMode="decimal"
            value={draft.distance}
            onChange={(e) => set("distance", e.target.value)}
            {...described("distance")}
          />
          <span aria-hidden="true">miles</span>
        </label>
      </Field>

      <fieldset className="control qf__group">
        <legend className="control__label">Delivered to</legend>

              <input
