import { useState } from "react";
import type { Quote, QuoteResponse, Tier } from "../../api/types";
import { TIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { dimDrivers, tierView } from "./quoteModel";
import { QuoteRow, shortService } from "./QuoteRow";
import { CARRIER_NAME, carrierVar } from "../../lib/carriers";
import { formatUsd, marginClass, marginText, TIER_NAME } from "../../lib/format";

export interface QuoteAnswerProps {
  res: QuoteResponse;
  tier: Tier;
  flatPrice: number;
}

/** The answer: the cheapest service for the chosen speed, its total as the largest figure. */
export function QuoteAnswer({ res, tier, flatPrice }: QuoteAnswerProps) {
  const pick = res.cheapest_by_tier[tier];
  const best = pick && res.quotes.find((q) => q.service_id === pick.service_id && q.tier === tier);
  if (!pick || !best) {
    return (
      <div className="answer qa">
        <p className="kicker">Cheapest for this parcel · {TIER_NAME[tier]}</p>
        <p className="answer__figure qa__none">None</p>
        <p className="answer__caption">No {TIER_NAME[tier].toLowerCase()} service can carry this parcel. The reasons are listed below.</p>
      </div>
    );
  }
  const price = best.margin + best.total; // the price charged the server used (flat price or override)
  return (
    <div className="answer qa">
      <p className="kicker">Cheapest for this parcel · {TIER_NAME[tier]}</p>
      <p className="answer__figure qa__figure" data-testid="quote-answer">
        {formatUsd(best.total)}
      </p>
      <p className="qa__service">
        <span className="qa__carrier" style={{ color: carrierVar(best.carrier) }}>
          {CARRIER_NAME[best.carrier]}
        </span>{" "}
        {shortService(best)}
      </p>
      <p className={`qa__margin ${marginClass(best.margin)}`}>
        {marginText(best.margin)} <span className="qa__against">against your {formatUsd(Number.isFinite(price) ? price : flatPrice)} price</span>
      </p>
    </div>
  );
}

function DimNote({ quotes, actualLb }: { quotes: Quote[]; actualLb: number }) {
  const drivers = dimDrivers(quotes, actualLb);
  if (drivers.length === 0) return null;
  const heaviest = Math.max(...drivers.map((q) => q.billable_weight_lb ?? 0));
  return (
    <section className="qdim" aria-labelledby="qdim-title">
      <h3 id="qdim-title" className="kicker">
        Billed by size, not weight
      </h3>
      <p className="qdim__text">
        Carriers bill the larger of the actual weight and the dimensional weight (length × width × height ÷ the
        carrier's divisor), so this {actualLb} lb box is billed as up to {heaviest} lb.
      </p>
      <table className="qdim__table">
        <thead>
          <tr>
            <th scope="col">Service</th>
            <th scope="col" className="num">
              Actual
            </th>
            <th scope="col" className="num">
              Dimensional
            </th>
            <th scope="col" className="num">
              Billable
            </th>
          </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
          {drivers.map((q) => (
            <tr key={q.service_id}>
              <th scope="row">{q.service_name}</th>
              <td className="num">{actualLb} lb</td>
              <td className="num">{q.dim_weight_lb} lb</td>
              <td className="num qdim__billable">{q.billable_weight_lb} lb</td>
            </tr>
          ))}
        </tbody>
      </table>
    </section>
  );
}

export interface QuoteBreakdownProps {
  res: QuoteResponse;
  tier: Tier;
  actualLb: number;
  onTier: (t: Tier) => void;
}

/** The ranked list, the size note and the other speeds: everything that explains the answer. */
export function QuoteBreakdown({ res, tier, actualLb, onTier }: QuoteBreakdownProps) {
  const view = tierView(res, tier);
  const [openId, setOpenId] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const scale = Math.max(0, ...view.ranked.map((q) => q.total));
  const cheapest = view.ranked[0]?.total ?? 0;
  const others = TIERS.filter((t) => t !== tier);

  return (
    <div className="qbreak">
      <section aria-labelledby="qrank-title">
        <div className="qbreak__head">
          <h3 id="qrank-title" className="qbreak__title">
            Every carrier, {TIER_NAME[tier].toLowerCase()}
          </h3>
          <p className="qkey" aria-hidden="true">
            <span className="qkey__sw qkey__sw--base" /> base <span className="qkey__sw qkey__sw--surcharge" /> surcharges{" "}
            <span className="qkey__sw qkey__sw--fuel" /> fuel
          </p>
        </div>
        {view.ranked.length > 0 && (
          <ol className="qrank">
            {view.ranked.map((q, i) => (
              <QuoteRow
                key={q.service_id}
                quote={q}
                rank={i + 1}
                cheapest={cheapest}
                scale={scale}
                open={openId === q.service_id}
                onToggle={() => setOpenId(openId === q.service_id ? null : q.service_id)}
              />
            ))}
          </ol>
        )}
        {view.alternatives.length > 0 && (
          <p className="qalt">
            Also available, dearer:{" "}
            {view.alternatives.map((q, i) => (
              <span key={q.service_id}>
                {i > 0 && " · "}
                {q.service_name} {formatUsd(q.total)}
              </span>
            ))}
          </p>
        )}
        {view.unavailable.length > 0 && (
          <ul className="qunavail" aria-label="Services that cannot carry this parcel">
            {view.unavailable.map((q) => (
              <li key={q.service_id}>
                <span className="qunavail__name">{q.service_name}</span>
                <span className="qunavail__reason">Not available: {q.unavailable_reason ?? "no reason given"}</span>
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        )}
      </section>

      <DimNote quotes={res.quotes.filter((q) => q.tier === tier)} actualLb={actualLb} />

      <section className="qtiers" aria-labelledby="qtiers-title">
        <h3 id="qtiers-title" className="kicker">
          Other speeds, cheapest each
        </h3>
        <ul>
          {others.map((t) => {
            const pick = res.cheapest_by_tier[t];
            const q = pick && res.quotes.find((x) => x.service_id === pick.service_id && x.tier === t);
            return (
              <li key={t}>
                <span className="qtiers__tier">{TIER_NAME[t]}</span>
                <span className="qtiers__what">
                  {q ? (
                    <>
                      <span style={{ color: carrierVar(q.carrier) }}>{CARRIER_NAME[q.carrier]}</span> {shortService(q)}
                    </>
                  ) : (
                    "no service can carry it"
                  )}
                </span>
                <span className="qtiers__total">{pick ? formatUsd(pick.total) : "—"}</span>
                <button type="button" className="btn btn--quiet qtiers__go" onClick={() => onTier(t)}>
                  Quote {TIER_NAME[t].toLowerCase()}
                </button>
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      </section>
    </div>
  );
}
import { useId } from "react";
import type { Quote } from "../../api/types";
import { splitOf } from "./quoteModel";
import { CARRIER_NAME, carrierVar, carrierWashVar } from "../../lib/carriers";
import { formatUsd } from "../../lib/format";

/** Base, surcharges and fuel as one bar; widths are shares of `scale` (the dearest row's total). */
export function StackedBar({ quote, scale }: { quote: Quote; scale: number }) {
  const s = splitOf(quote.line_items);
  const pct = (n: number) => `${scale > 0 ? (n / scale) * 100 : 0}%`;
  const c = quote.carrier;
  const label = `Base ${formatUsd(s.base)}, surcharges ${formatUsd(s.surcharges)}, fuel ${formatUsd(s.fuel)}`;
  return (
    <span className="qbar" role="img" aria-label={label} title={label}>
      <span className="qbar__part qbar__part--base" style={{ width: pct(s.base), background: carrierVar(c) }} />
      <span
        className="qbar__part qbar__part--surcharge"
        style={{
          width: pct(s.surcharges),
          backgroundImage: `repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, ${carrierVar(c)} 0 2px, ${carrierWashVar(c)} 2px 5px)`,
        }}
      />
      <span
        className="qbar__part qbar__part--fuel"
        style={{ width: pct(s.fuel), background: carrierWashVar(c), borderColor: carrierVar(c) }}
      />
    </span>
  );
}

/** "UPS Ground" -> "Ground" when the carrier name is already shown beside it. */
export const shortService = (q: Pick<Quote, "carrier" | "service_name">) =>
  q.service_name.replace(new RegExp(`^${CARRIER_NAME[q.carrier]} `), "");

export interface QuoteRowProps {
  quote: Quote;
  rank: number;
  cheapest: number;
  scale: number;
  open: boolean;
  onToggle: () => void;
}

export function QuoteRow({ quote, rank, cheapest, scale, open, onToggle }: QuoteRowProps) {
  const panelId = useId();
  const delta = quote.total - cheapest;
  const s = splitOf(quote.line_items);
  return (
    <li className={`qr ${open ? "qr--open" : ""}`}>
      <button type="button" className="qr__head" aria-expanded={open} aria-controls={panelId} onClick={onToggle}>
        <span className="qr__rank" aria-hidden="true">
          {rank}
        </span>
        <span className="qr__who">
          <span className="qr__carrier" style={{ color: carrierVar(quote.carrier) }}>
            {CARRIER_NAME[quote.carrier]}
          </span>
          <span className="qr__service">{shortService(quote)}</span>
        </span>
        <span className="qr__bar">
          <StackedBar quote={quote} scale={scale} />
        </span>
        <span className="qr__money">
          <span className="qr__total">{formatUsd(quote.total)}</span>
          <span className="qr__delta">{rank === 1 ? "cheapest" : `+${formatUsd(delta)}`}</span>
        </span>
        <span className="qr__chev" aria-hidden="true" />
        <span className="visually-hidden">{open ? ", hide line items" : ", show line items"}</span>
      </button>
      <div id={panelId} className="qr__panel" hidden={!open}>
        <table className="qitems">
          <caption className="visually-hidden">
            Line items of {quote.service_name}
          </caption>
          <thead>
            <tr>
              <th scope="col">Item</th>
              <th scope="col" className="num">
                Amount
              </th>
            </tr>
          </thead>
          <tbody>
            {quote.line_items.map((li, i) => (
              <tr key={i} className={`qitems__row qitems__row--${li.kind}`}>
                <th scope="row">
                  <span className="qitems__kind">{li.kind === "base" ? "Base" : li.kind === "fuel" ? "Fuel" : "Surcharge"}</span>
                  <span className="qitems__label">{li.label}</span>
                  {li.source && <cite className="qitems__src">{li.source}</cite>}
                </th>
                <td className="num">{formatUsd(li.amount)}</td>
              </tr>
            ))}
          </tbody>
          <tfoot>
            <tr>
              <th scope="row">
                Total{" "}
                <span className="qitems__sub">
                  base {formatUsd(s.base)} · surcharges {formatUsd(s.surcharges)} · fuel {formatUsd(s.fuel)}
                </span>
              </th>
              <td className="num">{formatUsd(quote.total)}</td>
            </tr>
          </tfoot>
        </table>
        <p className="qr__facts">
          Zone {quote.zone ?? "—"} · billed as {quote.billable_weight_lb ?? "—"} lb
          {quote.dim_weight_lb !== null ? ` (dimensional weight ${quote.dim_weight_lb} lb)` : ""}
          {quote.as_of ? ` · rules as of ${quote.as_of}` : ""}
        </p>
      </div>
    </li>
  );
}

/** The quote form as the user types it: strings, so half-typed numbers survive. */
export interface Draft {

export const parseNum = (s: string): number | null => {

  if (t === "") return null;
  const n = Number(t);
  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : NaN;
};

import "../styles/chart.css";
import { useId, useState, type ReactNode } from "react";

/** A chart with its title, a text summary, and a table alternative behind a toggle. */
export function ChartFrame({
  title,
  summary,
  chart,
  table,
  aside,
  controls,
}: {
  title: string;
  summary: ReactNode;
  /** Controls that change the chart (e.g. a scale toggle); shown in chart mode only. */
  controls?: ReactNode;
  chart: ReactNode;
  table: ReactNode;
  aside?: ReactNode;
}) {
  const [asTable, setAsTable] = useState(false);
  const titleId = useId();
  const bodyId = useId();
  return (
    <figure className="chart" aria-labelledby={titleId}>
      <div className="chart__head">
        <h3 id={titleId} className="chart__title">
          {title}
        </h3>
        <button
          type="button"
          className="btn btn--quiet chart__toggle"
          aria-controls={bodyId}
          aria-pressed={asTable}
          onClick={() => setAsTable((t) => !t)}
        >
          {asTable ? "Show as chart" : "Show as table"}
        </button>
      </div>
      <figcaption className="chart__summary">{summary}</figcaption>
      <div id={bodyId} className="chart__body">
        {asTable ? (
          <div className="chart__table-wrap">{table}</div>
        ) : (
          <>
            {controls && <div className="chart__controls">{controls}</div>}
            <div aria-hidden="true">{chart}</div>
          </>
        )}
      </div>
      {aside}
    </figure>
  );
}
import "../styles/chips.css";
import { useId } from "react";

export interface ChipOption<T> {
  value: T;
  label: string;
}

/** A row of toggle chips that behaves like a radio group; an "All" option usually clears the choice. */
export function ChipGroup<T>({
  legend,
  options,
  value,
  onChange,
  equals = (a, b) => a === b,
}: {
  legend: string;
  options: ChipOption<T>[];
  value: T;
  onChange: (v: T) => void;
  equals?: (a: T, b: T) => boolean;
}) {
  const id = useId();
  return (
    <div className="chips" role="group" aria-labelledby={id}>
      <span id={id} className="chips__legend">
        {legend}
      </span>
      <div className="chips__row">
        {options.map((o) => {
          const on = equals(o.value, value);
          return (
            <button
              key={o.label}
              type="button"
              className={`chip ${on ? "chip--on" : ""}`}
              aria-pressed={on}
              onClick={() => onChange(o.value)}
            >
              {o.label}
            </button>
          );
        })}
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

import type { SegmentFilter, Tier, WeightBand, ZoneBandLabel } from "../../api/types";
import { TIERS } from "../../api/types";
import { ChipGroup } from "../../components/ChipGroup";
import { tierName } from "../../lib/format";

const DEFAULT_WEIGHTS: WeightBand[] = ["≤1", "1–5", "5–10", "10–20", "20–70"];
const DEFAULT_ZONES: ZoneBandLabel[] = ["1–2", "3–4", "5–6", "7–8"];

export function SegmentChips({
  value,
  onChange,
  weightBands = DEFAULT_WEIGHTS,
  zoneBands = DEFAULT_ZONES,
}: {
  value: SegmentFilter;
  onChange: (next: SegmentFilter) => void;
  weightBands?: readonly string[];
  zoneBands?: readonly string[];
}) {
  const set = <K extends keyof SegmentFilter>(key: K, v: SegmentFilter[K]) => onChange({ ...value, [key]: v });
  return (
    <div className="segments">
      <ChipGroup<WeightBand | null>
        legend="Weight"
        value={value.weight_band ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("weight_band", v)}
        options={[
          { value: null, label: "All" },
          ...weightBands.map((w) => ({ value: w as WeightBand, label: `${w} lb` })),
        ]}
      />
      <ChipGroup<ZoneBandLabel | null>
        legend="Distance (USPS zone)"
        value={value.zone_band ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("zone_band", v)}
        options={[
          { value: null, label: "All" },
          ...zoneBands.map((z) => ({ value: z as ZoneBandLabel, label: `Zones ${z}` })),
        ]}
      />
      <ChipGroup<boolean | null>
        legend="Address"
        value={value.residential ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("residential", v)}
        options={[
          { value: null, label: "All" },
          { value: true, label: "Homes" },
          { value: false, label: "Businesses" },
        ]}
      />
      <ChipGroup<Tier | null>
        legend="Speed"
        value={value.speed ?? null}
        onChange={(v) => set("speed", v)}
        options={[{ value: null, label: "All" }, ...TIERS.map((t) => ({ value: t, label: tierName(t) }))]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

/** "1–5 lb · homes" for the answer kicker; empty when no segment is set. */
export function describeSegment(s: SegmentFilter | null): string {
  if (!s) return "";
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (s.weight_band) parts.push(`${s.weight_band} lb`);
  if (s.zone_band) parts.push(`zones ${s.zone_band}`);
  if (s.residential != null) parts.push(s.residential ? "homes" : "businesses");
  if (s.speed) parts.push(tierName(s.speed).toLowerCase());
  return parts.join(" · ");
}

import { useMemo, useState } from "react";
import { useApi, useLoad } from "../../api/ApiContext";
import type { BlendedResponse, Carrier, Parcel, SegmentFilter } from "../../api/types";
import type { ControlsState } from "../../state/urlState";
import type { Meta } from "../../api/types";
import { blendedAnswer, cleanSegment, totalQuantity, type BlendedAnswer } from "./logic";
import { SegmentChips, describeSegment } from "./SegmentChips";
import { CostSplitChart } from "./CostSplitChart";
import { LoadProblem } from "../../components/LoadProblem";
import { NeedParcels, type ParcelActions } from "../../components/NeedParcels";
import { useLastData } from "../../hooks/useLastData";
import { carrierName, carrierVar } from "../../lib/carriers";
import { formatInt, formatShare, formatUsd, marginClass, marginText, signedUsd } from "../../lib/format";

export interface BlendedPanelProps extends ParcelActions {
  controls: ControlsState;
  meta: Meta | null;
  parcels: Parcel[] | null;
}

export function BlendedPanel({ controls, meta, parcels, onLoadSample, onUploadCsv }: BlendedPanelProps) {
  if (!parcels || parcels.length === 0) {
    return (
      <NeedParcels
        what="Load the sample mix or upload a CSV to see what each carrier costs per parcel across the whole set, how much of it is surcharges, and whether your shipping price covers it."
        onLoadSample={onLoadSample}
        onUploadCsv={onUploadCsv}
      />
    );
  }
  return <Blended controls={controls} meta={meta} parcels={parcels} />;
}

function Blended({ controls, meta, parcels }: { controls: ControlsState; meta: Meta | null; parcels: Parcel[] }) {
  const api = useApi();
  const [segment, setSegment] = useState<SegmentFilter>({});
  const clean = cleanSegment(segment);
  const controlsKey = JSON.stringify(controls);
  const segKey = JSON.stringify(clean);
  const state = useLoad(
    (signal) => api.blended({ parcels, controls, ...(clean ? { segment: clean } : {}) }, signal),
    [api, parcels, controlsKey, segKey],
  );
  const data = useLastData(state);
  const total = useMemo(() => totalQuantity(parcels), [parcels]);
  const loading = state.status === "loading";

  return (
    <div className="q3" aria-busy={loading}>
      {state.status === "error" && <LoadProblem error={state.error} />}
      {!data && loading && <p className="q-loading">Pricing {formatInt(total)} parcels with every carrier…</p>}
      {data && (
        <Body
          data={data}
          controls={controls}
          segment={clean}
          total={total}
          chips={
            <SegmentChips
              value={segment}
              onChange={setSegment}
              weightBands={meta?.segments.weight_bands}
              zoneBands={meta?.segments.zone_bands}
            />
          }
          stale={loading}
        />
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

function Body({
  data,

            {formatUsd(shown)}
          </span>{" "}
          per parcel with {carrierName(pick)} in {last.year + 1}, from {formatUsd(last.cost_per_parcel)} in {last.year} (
          {signedUsd(shown - last.cost_per_parcel)}). The dotted lines in the chart apply the same increase to every carrier.
        </p>
      </div>
    </section>
  );
}

function Notes({ notes }: { notes: PointNote[] }) {
  if (notes.length === 0) return null;
  return (
    <div className="q-notes point-notes" data-testid="point-notes">
      <p className="kicker">Notes on the points marked !</p>
      <ul>
        {notes.map((n, i) => (
          <li key={i} className={`point-notes__item point-notes__item--${n.kind}`}>
            <strong style={{ color: carrierVar(n.carrier) }}>
              {carrierName(n.carrier)} {n.year}
            </strong>
            {n.kind === "warning" ? " (incomplete data): " : ": "}
            {n.text}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  );
}

function Drivers({ data, defaultCarrier, refYear }: { data: YearlyResponse; defaultCarrier: Carrier; refYear: number }) {
  const withDrivers = data.carriers.filter((c) => c.years.some((y) => y.drivers));
  const [carrier, setCarrier] = useState<Carrier>(defaultCarrier);
  const c = withDrivers.find((x) => x.carrier === carrier) ?? withDrivers[0];
  const steps = c ? c.years.filter((y) => y.drivers && y.change_vs_previous) : [];
  const defaultTo = [...steps].reverse().find((y) => y.year <= refYear)?.year ?? steps.at(-1)?.year;
  const [toYear, setToYear] = useState<number | undefined>(defaultTo);
  const row = steps.find((y) => y.year === toYear) ?? steps.find((y) => y.year === defaultTo);
  const [dim, setDim] = useState<Dimension | null>(null);
  if (!c || !row || !row.drivers) return null;
  const activeDim = dim ?? strongestDimension(row.drivers);

  return (
    <section className="q-block drivers" aria-label="What drove the change">
      <div className="q-block__head">
        <h3 className="q-block__title">Which parcels drove the change?</h3>
      </div>
      <div className="segments">
        <ChipGroup<Carrier>
          legend="Carrier"
          value={c.carrier}
          onChange={(v) => {
            setCarrier(v);
            setToYear(undefined);
          }}
          options={withDrivers.map((x) => ({ value: x.carrier, label: carrierName(x.carrier) }))}
        />
        <ChipGroup<number>
          legend="Between"
          value={row.year}
          onChange={setToYear}
          options={steps.map((y) => ({ value: y.year, label: `${y.change_vs_previous!.from_year}→${y.year}` }))}
        />
        <ChipGroup<Dimension>
          legend="Split by"
          value={activeDim}
          onChange={setDim}
          options={DIMENSIONS.map((d) => ({ value: d, label: DIMENSION_LABEL[d] }))}
        />
      </div>
      <DriverChart carrier={c.carrier} row={row} dim={activeDim} />
    </section>
  );
}

function Excluded({ data }: { data: YearlyResponse }) {
  const ex = data.carriers.filter((c) => c.parcels_excluded > 0);
  if (ex.length === 0) return null;
  return (
      {fuelCarriers.some((c) => c.years.some((y) => y.fuel?.ground.is_proxy)) && (
        <p className="fuel-strip__foot">* Proxy: no published figure for that carrier and year, so FedEx’s published fuel history stands in. The rail’s fuel slider overrides every year.</p>
      )}
      {carriers.some((c) => !c.years.some((y) => y.fuel)) && <p className="fuel-strip__foot">USPS charges no fuel surcharge.</p>}
    </div>
  );

  const scaleToggle = (
    <ChipGroup<Scale>
      legend="Scale"
      value={scale}
      onChange={setScaleChoice}
      options={[
        { value: "dollars", label: "Dollars" },
        { value: "index", label: "Index (first year = 100)" },
      ]}
    />
  );

  return (
    <ChartFrame
      title="Cost per parcel, year by year"
      summary={summary}
      controls={scaleToggle}
      chart={chart}
      table={table}
            <th scope="row">{segmentLabel(dim, d.segment)}</th>
            <td className="num">{d.parcels}</td>
            <td className="num">{signedUsd(d.change_per_parcel)}</td>
            <td className="num">{signedUsd(withinChange(d))}</td>
            <td className="num">{signedUsd(d.change_total)}</td>
          </tr>
        ))}
        {ch && (

            <th scope="row">All parcels</th>
            <td className="num">{list.reduce((n, d) => n + d.parcels, 0)}</td>
            <td className="num">{signedUsd(ch.dollars_per_parcel)}</td>
            <td className="num">{signedUsd(ch.dollars_per_parcel)}</td>
            <td className="num">—</td>
          </tr>
        )}
      </tbody>
    </table>
  );

  const summary = (
    <>
      <span className="driver-sentence" data-testid="driver-sentence">
        {sentence ?? "No change to break down."}
      </span>{" "}
      Bars add up to the {ch ? signedUsd(ch.dollars_per_parcel) : formatUsd(0)} per parcel change for {carrierName(carrier)}; to the right
      a segment made parcels dearer, to the left cheaper. “Each” is the change for that segment’s own parcels, which does not
      depend on how many of them you ship.
    </>
  );

  return <ChartFrame title={`What drove ${carrierName(carrier)}’s change, by ${DIMENSION_LABEL[dim].toLowerCase()}`} summary={summary} chart={chart} table={table} />;
}

export function niceTicks(lo: number, hi: number, target = 4): number[] {
  const span = Math.max(hi - lo, 0.01);
  const raw = span / target;
  const mag = 10 ** Math.floor(Math.log10(raw));
  const step = [1, 2, 2.5, 5, 10].map((m) => m * mag).find((s) => s >= raw) ?? 10 * mag;
  const start = Math.floor(lo / step) * step;

/**
 * Turn the draft into a request parcel. Only shape problems are caught here (empty, not a
 * number, two of three dimensions); ranges are left to the server so its 422 messages show.

export function draftToParcel(d: Draft): { parcel: Parcel; errors: null } | { parcel: null; errors: LocalErrors } {
  const errors: LocalErrors = {};
  const weight = draftWeight(d);
  if (weight === null) errors.weight = "Enter the weight.";
  else if (Number.isNaN(weight)) errors.weight = "Weight must be a number.";
  const dims = [d.length, d.width, d.height].map(parseNum);
  const filled = dims.filter((x) => x !== null).length;
  if (dims.some((x) => Number.isNaN(x))) errors.dims = "Dimensions must be numbers.";
  else if (filled > 0 && filled < 3) errors.dims = "Give all three dimensions, or leave all three empty.";
  const distance = parseNum(d.distance);
  if (distance === null) errors.distance = "Enter the distance.";
  else if (Number.isNaN(distance)) errors.distance = "Distance must be a number.";
  if (Object.keys(errors).length > 0) return { parcel: null, errors };
  const parcel: Parcel = {
    weight_lb: weight!,
    distance_miles: distance!,
    residential: d.residential,
    speed: d.speed,
    delivery_area: d.area,
    nonstandard_packaging: d.nonstandard,
    ...(filled === 3 ? { length_in: dims[0]!, width_in: dims[1]!, height_in: dims[2]! } : {}),
  };
  return { parcel, errors: null };
}

const str = (n: number | null | undefined) => (n === null || n === undefined ? "" : String(n));

export function draftFromParcel(p: Parcel): Draft {
  const whole = Math.floor(p.weight_lb);
  const oz = Math.round((p.weight_lb - whole) * 16 * 100) / 100;
  return {
    lb: p.weight_lb < 1 ? "" : String(oz > 0 && whole >= 1 ? whole : p.weight_lb),
    oz: p.weight_lb < 1 ? String(Math.round(p.weight_lb * 16 * 100) / 100) : oz > 0 ? String(oz) : "",
    length: str(p.length_in),
    width: str(p.width_in),
    height: str(p.height_in),
    distance: String(p.distance_miles),
    residential: p.residential,
    speed: p.speed,
    area: p.delivery_area ?? "none",
    nonstandard: p.nonstandard_packaging ?? false,
  };
}

import { expect, type Locator, type Page, type Response, type TestInfo } from "@playwright/test";

export type ViewId = "quote" | "breakeven" | "blended" | "yearly";

export const isMobile = (info: TestInfo) => info.project.name === "mobile";

/** Wait for the next answer from an API endpoint, e.g. `nextResponse(page, "/api/quote")`. */
export function nextResponse(page: Page, path: string, method = "POST"): Promise<Response> {
  return page.waitForResponse((r) => new URL(r.url()).pathname === path && r.request().method() === method);
}

/** Open the app (optionally with a query string) and wait until the price lists have loaded. */
export async function openApp(page: Page, search = ""): Promise<void> {
  const meta = nextResponse(page, "/api/meta", "GET");
  await page.goto(`/${search}`);
  expect((await meta).ok()).toBe(true);
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Parcel Rates" })).toBeVisible();
}

/** Click "Load sample mix" and wait for the strip to show the parcel count. */
export async function loadSample(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  const sample = nextResponse(page, "/api/sample-parcels", "GET");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Load sample mix" }).click();
  expect((await sample).ok()).toBe(true);
  await expect(page.locator(".strip__count")).toContainText("307 parcels");
}

export const tab = (page: Page, view: ViewId): Locator => page.locator(`#tab-${view}`);
export const panel = (page: Page): Locator => page.getByRole("tabpanel");

/** Switch to a question and wait for its API answer. */
export async function showView(page: Page, view: ViewId): Promise<void> {
  if (view === "quote") {
    await tab(page, view).click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId("quote-answer")).toBeVisible();
    return;
  }
  const answer = nextResponse(page, `/api/${view}`);
  await tab(page, view).click();
  expect((await answer).ok()).toBe(true);
  const id = { breakeven: "breakeven-answer", blended: "q3-answer", yearly: "q4-answer" }[view];
  await expect(page.getByTestId(id)).toBeVisible();
}

/** The settings: the side rail on desktop, the bottom sheet behind "Adjust" on phones. */
export async function openSettings(page: Page, info: TestInfo): Promise<Locator> {
  if (isMobile(info)) {
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Adjust" }).click();
    const sheet = page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Assumptions" });
    await expect(sheet).toBeVisible();
    return sheet;
  }
  return page.getByRole("complementary", { name: "Assumptions" });
}

export async function closeSettings(page: Page, info: TestInfo): Promise<void> {
  if (!isMobile(info)) return;
  await page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Assumptions" }).getByRole("button", { name: "Done" }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Assumptions" })).toHaveCount(0);
}

/** The Q1 form, by its accessible name. */
export const quoteForm = (page: Page): Locator => page.getByRole("form", { name: "Your parcel" });

/** Replace a text input's value and wait for the quote the change triggers (debounced 300 ms). */
export async function fillAndQuote(page: Page, input: Locator, value: string): Promise<Response> {
  const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
  await input.fill(value);
  return quote;
}

/** Set the Q1 box size and wait for the new quote. */
export async function setBox(page: Page, l: string, w: string, h: string): Promise<void> {
  const form = quoteForm(page);
  await form.getByLabel("Length in inches").fill(l);
  await form.getByLabel("Width in inches").fill(w);
  const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
  await form.getByLabel("Height in inches").fill(h);
  expect((await quote).ok()).toBe(true);
  await expect(page.locator(".is-stale")).toHaveCount(0);
}

/** Text of the Q1 answer figure once the answer on screen is fresh. */
export async function quoteTotal(page: Page): Promise<string> {
  await expect(page.locator(".qv__answer")).toHaveAttribute("aria-busy", "false");
  await expect(page.locator(".is-stale")).toHaveCount(0);
  return (await page.getByTestId("quote-answer").innerText()).trim();
}

import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { fillAndQuote, loadSample, nextResponse, openApp, quoteForm, quoteTotal, setBox } from "./helpers";

test.describe("Q1, quote one parcel", () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
    await openApp(page);
    expect((await quote).ok()).toBe(true);
  });

  test("the sample mix loads and the strip shows the count", async ({ page }) => {
    await loadSample(page);
    await expect(page.locator(".strip__facts")).toContainText("80% to homes");
    await expect(page.getByRole("combobox", { name: "Start from one of your parcels" })).toBeVisible();
  });

  test("a typical parcel: answer figure, cheapest carrier, line items with a source", async ({ page }) => {
    // Default form: 3 lb, 12×10×6 in, 600 miles, to a home, ground.
    expect(await quoteTotal(page)).toMatch(/^\$\d+\.\d{2}$/);
    await expect(page.locator(".qa__service")).toContainText("USPS Ground Advantage");
    await expect(page.locator(".qa__margin")).toContainText(/margin|loss/);

    const rows = page.locator(".qrank > li");
    await expect(rows).toHaveCount(3);
    await expect(rows.first().locator(".qr__delta")).toHaveText("cheapest");

    const first = rows.first().getByRole("button");
    await expect(first).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    await first.click();
    await expect(first).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
    const items = rows.first().getByRole("table");
    await expect(items).toBeVisible();
    await expect(items.locator(".qitems__row--base")).toHaveCount(1);
    await expect(items.locator("cite.qitems__src").first()).not.toBeEmpty();
    await expect(items.locator("tfoot")).toContainText(await page.getByTestId("quote-answer").innerText());
  });

  test("a bulky light box shows the billed-by-size note", async ({ page }) => {
    await setBox(page, "24", "20", "18");
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Billed by size, not weight" })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.locator(".qdim__text")).toContainText("this 3 lb box is billed as up to");
  });

  test("changing the speed tier re-prices the parcel", async ({ page }) => {
    const ground = await quoteTotal(page);
    const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
    await quoteForm(page).getByRole("radio", { name: "Next day" }).check();
    await quote;
    await expect(page.locator(".qa").locator(".kicker")).toContainText("Next day");
    const nextDay = await quoteTotal(page);
    expect(Number(nextDay.slice(1))).toBeGreaterThan(Number(ground.slice(1)));
    await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Every carrier, next day" })).toBeVisible();
  });

  test("a weight over 70 lb shows the server's message at the input", async ({ page }) => {
    const pounds = quoteForm(page).getByLabel("Weight in pounds");
    const res = await fillAndQuote(page, pounds, "75");
    expect(res.status()).toBe(422);
    await expect(pounds).toHaveAttribute("aria-invalid", "true");
    const describedBy = await pounds.getAttribute("aria-describedby");
    const message = page.locator(`[id="${describedBy}"]`);
    await expect(message).toBeVisible();
    await expect(message).toContainText(/70/);
    await expect(page.locator(".qa__none")).toBeVisible();
  });
});

cd ~/parcel-rates-issue-8/frontend/e2e && cat > controls.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { closeSettings, nextResponse, openApp, openSettings, quoteTotal } from "./helpers";

type QuoteBody = { controls: { year?: number; usps_rate_card?: string; peak?: boolean; fuel_override_percent?: Record<string, number> } };

test.describe("Global controls", () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
    await openApp(page);
    expect((await quote).ok()).toBe(true);
  });

  test("2027 prices show the FedEx-only note", async ({ page }, info) => {
    const settings = await openSettings(page, info);
    const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
    await settings.getByLabel("Price list year").selectOption("2027");
    expect(((await quote).request().postDataJSON() as QuoteBody).controls.year).toBe(2027);
    await closeSettings(page, info);
    await expect(page.getByRole("note").filter({ hasText: "2027 prices are published by FedEx only" })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.locator(".masthead__edition")).toContainText("2027");
  });

  test("USPS retail prices change the Q1 total", async ({ page }, info) => {
    const commercial = await quoteTotal(page);
    const settings = await openSettings(page, info);
    const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
    await settings.getByRole("radio", { name: /Retail/ }).check();
    expect(((await quote).request().postDataJSON() as QuoteBody).controls.usps_rate_card).toBe("retail");
    await closeSettings(page, info);
    await expect(page.getByTestId("quote-answer")).not.toHaveText(commercial);
    const retail = await quoteTotal(page);
    expect(Number(retail.slice(1))).toBeGreaterThan(Number(commercial.slice(1)));
  });

  test("fuel slider override and reset", async ({ page }, info) => {
    const settings = await openSettings(page, info);
    const ground = settings.getByRole("slider", { name: "Ground" });
    const value = settings.locator('.fuel[data-group="ground"] .fuel__value');
    const before = await value.innerText();
    const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
    await ground.focus();
    await page.keyboard.press("ArrowRight");
    await expect(value).not.toHaveText(before);
    const body = (await quote).request().postDataJSON() as QuoteBody;
    expect(body.controls.fuel_override_percent?.ground).toBeDefined();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/fuel_ground=/);

    const reset = settings.getByRole("button", { name: /Reset\s+ground fuel/ });
    await reset.click();
    await expect(value).toHaveText(before);
    await expect(reset).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(page).not.toHaveURL(/fuel_ground=/);
    await closeSettings(page, info);
  });

  test("peak toggle prices inside the peak window", async ({ page }, info) => {
    const settings = await openSettings(page, info);
    const quote = nextResponse(page, "/api/quote");
    const peak = settings.getByRole("switch", { name: "Peak season surcharges" });
    await peak.check();
    await expect(peak).toBeChecked();
    expect(((await quote).request().postDataJSON() as QuoteBody).controls.peak).toBe(true);
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/peak=1/);
    await closeSettings(page, info);
    if (info.project.name === "mobile") await expect(page.locator(".mobile-bar__line")).toContainText("peak");
  });

  test("URL state survives a reload", async ({ page }, info) => {
    const settings = await openSettings(page, info);
    await settings.getByLabel("Price list year").selectOption("2025");
    await settings.getByRole("radio", { name: /Retail/ }).check();
    await closeSettings(page, info);
    await page.locator("#tab-breakeven").click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/year=2025/);
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/usps=retail/);
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/view=breakeven/);

    const breakeven = nextResponse(page, "/api/breakeven");
    await page.reload();
    const body = (await breakeven).request().postDataJSON() as QuoteBody;
    expect(body.controls.year).toBe(2025);
    expect(body.controls.usps_rate_card).toBe("retail");
    await expect(page.locator("#tab-breakeven")).toHaveAttribute("aria-selected", "true");
    const again = await openSettings(page, info);
    await expect(again.getByLabel("Price list year")).toHaveValue("2025");
    await expect(again.getByRole("radio", { name: /Retail/ })).toBeChecked();
  });
});
EOF

import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { openApp } from "./helpers";

const HEADER = "weight_lb,length_in,width_in,height_in,distance_miles,residential,speed,quantity";

function csv(rows: string[]) {
  return { name: "parcels.csv", mimeType: "text/csv", buffer: Buffer.from([HEADER, ...rows].join("\n") + "\n") };
}

test.describe("CSV upload", () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
    await openApp(page);
  });

  test("a small valid file loads into the strip", async ({ page }) => {
    await page.locator('input[type="file"]').setInputFiles(
      csv(["2,10,8,4,300,true,ground,5", "12,18,14,10,1500,false,two_three_day,2", "0.5,,,,80,true,next_day,1"]),
    );
    await expect(page.locator(".strip__count")).toContainText("8 parcels");
    await expect(page.locator(".strip__source")).toContainText("parcels.csv");
    await expect(page.getByRole("alert")).toHaveCount(0);
  });

  test("a file with an error names the row", async ({ page }) => {
    await page.locator('input[type="file"]').setInputFiles(csv(["2,10,8,4,300,true,ground,5", "95,10,8,4,300,true,ground,1"]));
    const alert = page.getByRole("alert");
    await expect(alert).toBeVisible();
    await expect(alert.locator(".problems__where").first()).toHaveText("Row 3");
    await expect(alert).toContainText("70");
    await expect(page.locator(".strip__count")).toHaveCount(0);
  });
});
EOF
cat > mobile-sheet.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { isMobile, openApp } from "./helpers";

test.describe("Settings sheet on phones", () => {
  test.beforeEach(async ({ page }, info) => {
    test.skip(!isMobile(info), "the sheet exists only below 64 rem");
    await openApp(page);
  });

  test("opens as a modal dialog, traps focus and closes on Escape", async ({ page }) => {
    const adjust = page.getByRole("button", { name: "Adjust" });
    await expect(page.getByRole("complementary", { name: "Assumptions" })).toBeHidden();
    await adjust.click();
    const sheet = page.getByRole("dialog", { name: "Assumptions" });
    await expect(sheet).toBeVisible();
    await expect(sheet).toHaveAttribute("aria-modal", "true");
    await expect(adjust).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "true");
    await expect(page.locator("main")).toHaveAttribute("inert", "");

    // Focus starts inside and Tab wraps around without leaving the sheet.
    const inSheet = () => page.evaluate(() => !!document.activeElement?.closest('[role="dialog"]'));
    expect(await inSheet()).toBe(true);
    const first = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.outerHTML);
    for (let i = 0; i < 25; i++) {
      await page.keyboard.press("Tab");
      expect(await inSheet()).toBe(true);
    }
    await page.keyboard.press("Shift+Tab");
    expect(await inSheet()).toBe(true);
    expect(first).toBeTruthy();

    await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
    await expect(sheet).toHaveCount(0);
    await expect(adjust).toBeFocused();
    await expect(adjust).toHaveAttribute("aria-expanded", "false");
    await expect(page.locator("main")).not.toHaveAttribute("inert", "");
  });
});
EOF

import AxeBuilder from "@axe-core/playwright";
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";
import { loadSample, openApp, showView, type ViewId } from "./helpers";

/**
 * axe on every question view, light and dark. Serious and critical violations fail the test;
 * moderate and minor ones are attached to the report for review.
 *
 * Exclusions:
 * - `.recharts-wrapper`: the Recharts SVG sits inside an aria-hidden wrapper and is described by
 *   the figure caption and the "Show as table" alternative (see DESIGN.md, Accessibility).
 */
const VIEWS: ViewId[] = ["quote", "breakeven", "blended", "yearly"];
const BLOCKING = new Set(["serious", "critical"]);

for (const scheme of ["light", "dark"] as const) {
  test.describe(`axe, ${scheme}`, () => {
    test.use({ colorScheme: scheme });

    for (const view of VIEWS) {
      test(`${view} has no serious or critical violations`, async ({ page }, info) => {
        await openApp(page);
        await loadSample(page);
        await showView(page, view);
        await expect(page.locator(".is-stale")).toHaveCount(0);

        const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
          .withTags(["wcag2a", "wcag2aa", "wcag21a", "wcag21aa", "wcag22aa", "best-practice"])
          .exclude(".recharts-wrapper")
          .analyze();
        await info.attach("axe-violations.json", {

cd ~/parcel-rates-issue-8/frontend/e2e && cat > screenshots.spec.ts <<'EOF'
import { expect, test, type Page } from "@playwright/test";
import path from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { isMobile, loadSample, openApp, openSettings, setBox, showView, type ViewId } from "./helpers";

/**
 * Full-page captures of every view for the UX review (docs/ux-review.md), run with
 * `npm run e2e:update-screens`. Deterministic: the fixed sample mix, default controls,
 * the default quote form, reduced motion, settled charts and the page scrolled to the top.
 */
const DIR = path.join(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "screenshots");

/** Resolve once nothing inside the charts has changed for a few frames (Recharts animates in). */
async function chartsSettled(page: Page): Promise<void> {
  await page.waitForFunction(
    () => {
      const w = window as unknown as { __snap?: string; __same?: number };
      const snap = [...document.querySelectorAll(".recharts-wrapper, .hm__svg")].map((e) => e.innerHTML).join("|");
      w.__same = snap === w.__snap ? (w.__same ?? 0) + 1 : 0;
      w.__snap = snap;
      return w.__same >= 5;
    },
    undefined,
    { polling: "raf" },
  );
}

async function capture(page: Page, name: string, project: string, scheme: string): Promise<void> {
  await expect(page.locator(".is-stale")).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.locator('[aria-busy="true"]')).toHaveCount(0);
  await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
  await chartsSettled(page);
  // The settings rail is sticky: without this it lands mid-page in a full-page capture.
  await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));
  await page.evaluate(() => new Promise((r) => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(r))));
  await page.screenshot({
    path: path.join(DIR, `${name}-${project}-${scheme}.png`),
    fullPage: true,
    animations: "disabled",
    caret: "hide",
  });
}

const VIEWS: { name: string; view: ViewId; setup?: (page: Page) => Promise<void> }[] = [
  {
    name: "q1-typical",
    view: "quote",
    setup: async (page) => {
      // Open the cheapest row so the line items and their sources are in the shot.
      await page.locator(".qrank > li").first().getByRole("button").click();
    },
  },
  { name: "q1-bulky", view: "quote", setup: (page) => setBox(page, "24", "20", "18") },
  { name: "q2", view: "breakeven" },
  { name: "q3", view: "blended" },
  { name: "q4", view: "yearly" },
];

for (const scheme of ["light", "dark"] as const) {
  test.describe(`screens, ${scheme} @screens`, () => {
    test.use({ colorScheme: scheme, reducedMotion: "reduce" });

    for (const v of VIEWS) {
      test(v.name, async ({ page }, info) => {
        await openApp(page);
        await loadSample(page);
        await showView(page, v.view);
        await v.setup?.(page);
        await capture(page, v.name, info.project.name, scheme);
      });
    }

    test("settings-sheet", async ({ page }, info) => {
      test.skip(!isMobile(info), "the sheet exists on phones only");
      await openApp(page);
      await loadSample(page);
      await showView(page, "quote");
      await page.evaluate(() => window.scrollTo(0, 0));
      await openSettings(page, info);
      await page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready);
      await page.screenshot({ path: path.join(DIR, `settings-sheet-${info.project.name}-${scheme}.png`), animations: "disabled", caret: "hide" });
    });
  });
}
EOF

function Yearly({ controls, parcels }: { controls: ControlsState; parcels: Parcel[] }) {
  const api = useApi();
  const [increase, setIncrease] = useState<number | null>(null);
  const sent = useDebounced(increase, 250);
  const controlsKey = JSON.stringify(controls);
  const state = useLoad(
    (signal) => api.yearly({ parcels, controls, ...(sent !== null ? { next_year_increase_percent: sent } : {}) }, signal),
    [api, parcels, controlsKey, sent],
  );
  const data = useLastData(state);
  const total = useMemo(() => totalQuantity(parcels), [parcels]);

  // The slider starts at the pick carrier's latest announced increase, which the first answer tells us.
  useEffect(() => {
    if (increase !== null || !data) return;
    const ref = referenceYear(data);
    const d = ref !== null ? defaultIncrease(pickCarrier(data, ref)) : null;
    if (d !== null) setIncrease(d);
  }, [data, increase]);

  const loading = state.status === "loading";
  return (
    <div className="q4" aria-busy={loading}>
  50% {
    opacity: 0.45;
  }
}

.is-stale {
  opacity: 0.55;
  transition: opacity var(--duration-fast);
}

.is-loss {
  color: var(--loss);
}

.is-profit {

  grid-template-columns: repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr));
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);
}

.questions__tab {
  display: grid;
  gap: 2px;
  align-content: start;
  min-height: 3.5rem;
  padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3) var(--space-3) 0;
  border: 0;
  background: transparent;
  text-align: left;
  cursor: pointer;
  color: var(--ink-muted);
  position: relative;
}

.questions__tab::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  left: 0;
  right: var(--space-3);
  bottom: -1px;
  height: 4px;
  background: var(--ink);
  transform: scaleX(0);
  transform-origin: left;
  transition: transform var(--duration) var(--ease-out);
}

.questions__tab:hover {
  color: var(--ink);
}

.questions__tab:hover::after {
  transform: scaleX(0.25);
}

.questions__tab[aria-selected="true"] {
  color: var(--ink);
}

.questions__tab[aria-selected="true"]::after {
  transform: scaleX(1);
}

.questions__num {
  font-family: var(--font-display);
  font-size: var(--text-lg);
  line-height: 1;
}

.questions__short {
  font-size: var(--text-sm);
  font-weight: 600;
  line-height: 1.2;
}

.questions__panel {
  padding-top: var(--space-6);
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--space-3);
}

.questions__panel:focus-visible {
  outline-offset: 6px;
  box-shadow: none;
}

/* The question is context; the answer figure below it is the largest thing in the section. */
.questions__question {
  font-size: var(--text-xl);
  font-weight: 500;

```
/**
 * The chart SVGs sit inside an aria-hidden wrapper (the text summary and table carry the
 * content), so nothing inside may take focus. Recharts 3 turns on its accessibility layer by
 * default (tabIndex=0, role="application" on the svg); the charts switch it off.
 * jsdom gives ResponsiveContainer no size, so it is replaced by a fixed-size pass-through.
 */
import { cloneElement, isValidElement, type ReactElement, type ReactNode } from "react";
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { render } from "@testing-library/react";
import { mockBlendedResponse, mockYearlyResponse } from "../api/mocks";
import { CostSplitChart } from "./blended/CostSplitChart";
import { YearChart } from "./yearly/YearChart";
import { DriverChart } from "./yearly/DriverChart";
import { pointNotes } from "./yearly/logic";
import { stubResizeObserver } from "./blended/testUtils";

vi.mock("recharts", async (importOriginal) => {
  const actual = await importOriginal<typeof import("recharts")>();
  return {
    ...actual,
    ResponsiveContainer: ({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) =>
      isValidElement(children) ? cloneElement(children as ReactElement<{ width: number; height: number }>, { width: 600, height: 300 }) : null,
  };
});

beforeEach(() => stubResizeObserver());

const FOCUSABLE = 'a[href], button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex="-1"])';

function expectNoHiddenFocusStop(container: HTMLElement) {
  const hidden = container.querySelector('[aria-hidden="true"]');
  expect(hidden).not.toBeNull();
  expect(hidden!.querySelector("svg")).not.toBeNull(); // the chart really rendered
  expect(hidden!.querySelectorAll(FOCUSABLE)).toHaveLength(0);
  expect(hidden!.querySelector('[role="application"]')).toBeNull();
}

describe("charts inside aria-hidden wrappers", () => {
  it("cost split chart has no focus stop", () => {
    const { container } = render(<CostSplitChart data={mockBlendedResponse} />);
    expectNoHiddenFocusStop(container);
  });

  font-size: var(--text-xl);
}

.strip__actions {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: var(--space-2);
}

@media (max-width: 39.999rem) {
  .strip__actions .btn {
    min-height: 2.25rem;
    padding-block: var(--space-1);
  }
}

.parcels__details {
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--space-5);
  padding-top: var(--space-4);
  border-top: 1px dashed var(--rule);

```
# UX review of the end-to-end screenshots (issue #8)

Screenshots: `frontend/e2e/screenshots/`, captured by `npm run e2e:update-screens`
against `docker compose up` with the sample mix loaded, default controls (2026,
USPS commercial, default fuel, no peak, $9.99) and the default Q1 parcel (3 lb,
12 × 10 × 6 in, 600 miles, to a home, ground). Desktop is 1440 × 900 at 1×,
mobile is 375 × 812 at 2× with touch. Every view is captured full page, scrolled
to the top first, in light and dark.

Reviewed for: the answer as the largest element, readability of numbers,
overflow, tap targets (44 px), chart legibility on a phone, colour-blind
safety, dark mode, loading and empty states, and consistency between views.

Severity: **high** blocks or misleads the user, **medium** slows them down or
hides something, **low** polish. Status: **fixed** (in this branch, recaptured),
**open** (left as is, with the reason).

## Summary of changes made

| # | Finding | Severity | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | On phones the answer of every question sat below the first screen (masthead deck plus two rows of tabs pushed it to about 790 px of 812) | high | Masthead deck hidden below 40 rem; the four tabs stay on one row with `--text-xs` labels. The answer figure now starts at about 540-620 px on all four views |
| 2 | The phone assumptions bar cut the line with an ellipsis, so "$9.99 charged" (the input behind every margin) was never visible | medium | Bar wraps to two lines (`line-clamp: 2`) |
| 3 | Tap targets under 44 px on touch: "Details" and "Replace CSV" (36 px), quiet buttons such as "Quote 2–3 day", "Show as table", "Done" (40 px), the fuel sliders (16 px track), the flat price input (41 px) | medium | `@media (pointer: coarse)`: `.btn` and the price input `min-height: 44px`, fuel slider track 44 px |
| 4 | Q4 line chart: UPS and FedEx prices are within cents of each other, FedEx is drawn last and hid the UPS line and its square markers completely, in dollars and index scale | medium | UPS line drawn wider (5.5 px) with a larger marker, so it shows as a brown casing around FedEx where they overlap |
| 5 | axe (serious): the fuel table under the Q4 chart scrolls sideways on phones but could not be reached by keyboard; the same latent problem in every "Show as table" view | medium | Both wrappers are focusable `role="region"` with a label |
| 6 | The selected chip's check mark came from CSS `content` and became part of the button name ("✓ Dollars"). `content: "✓" / ""` is mis-read by Chromium 131 ("✓ " / "Dollars") | low | The mark is an `aria-hidden` span |
| 7 | axe (moderate): the phone assumptions bar was outside any landmark | low | `role="region"`, "Current assumptions" |

All 59 functional and axe tests pass on both projects after the changes; the
screenshots in the folder are the recaptured ones.

## Per screenshot

### Q1, typical parcel (`q1-typical-*`)

Works:
- The answer ($8.95, USPS Ground Advantage, "+$1.04 margin against your $9.99
  price") is the largest element and sits directly under the question; the
  margin carries a sign and the word, not only green.
- The ranked rows read at a glance: rank, carrier name in its colour, stacked
  bar (base solid, surcharges hatched, fuel outlined, so the parts differ by
  texture), total and "+$20.95". The open row shows each line item with its
  source file, which is the trust anchor of the whole app.
- "Billed by size, not weight" appears for this default box too (12 × 10 × 6 in
  is 6 lb dimensional for UPS and FedEx), which is correct and teaches the rule
  on the first screen.
- Dark mode: carrier colours keep their contrast; the hatching stays visible.

Issues:
- Phone: the answer was below the fold (finding 1, **fixed**); the
  assumptions bar hid the flat price (finding 2, **fixed**); "Quote 2–3 day"
  and "Quote next day" were 40 px (finding 3, **fixed**).
- The USPS bar in the ranked list is short next to $30 rivals; that is the
  data, the figure next to it carries the number. **Open**, by design.
- "Not a box" checkbox is 20 px, but the whole label (≥ 44 px tall) is the
  target. **Open**, acceptable.

### Q1, bulky parcel (`q1-bulky-*`, 24 × 20 × 18 in, 3 lb)

Works: the answer updates and the size note explains why a 3 lb box is billed
as a much heavier one, with actual, dimensional and billable weight per
service in a compact table that fits 375 px without scrolling.

Issues: none beyond the Q1 items above.

### Q2, breakeven map (`q2-*`)

Works:
- "27 lb" is the answer figure, with a caption naming the distances and the
  rivals, then one sentence per distance band. A reader who never looks at the
  map still gets the answer.
- The map fits 375 px with no horizontal scroll (columns shrink, headers
  abbreviate to "z5"); heavy ink lines mark where USPS stops winning and
  carrier names label each run, so the regions read without colour (blue and
  purple are close under protanopia).
- Dark mode: cells keep their order of intensity; run labels stay legible.

Issues:
- In the 27-50 lb band at zones 5-6 the winner alternates between UPS and
  FedEx almost every pound, so that band is a stack of thin slivers. This is
  the data (the two carriers are within cents of each other there) and the
  sentence above already says "mostly". **Open**.
- On phones the "FedEx" run label touches the cell edge at 800 mi. **Open**,
  low: the label stays readable and the colour and tooltip agree.
- The saving legend is a grey ramp while the cells ramp in each carrier's hue.
  It reads as "darker = bigger saving" and is the same on every map. **Open**,
  low.

### Q3, blended cost (`q3-*`)

Works:
- "USPS $10.98 per parcel" is the answer, the verdict box answers the owner's
  real question in plain words ("No. You lose $0.31 per parcel with USPS",
  "40 % of parcels (124 of 307) ship at a loss"), in the loss colour with the
  word "loss" on every figure.
- Segment chips are 44 px tall on phones, the selected one has a check mark,
  and the parcel count next to them repeats the segment's result.
- The cost split ranks base, surcharges and fuel per carrier; each row label
  carries its name and shares, so it reads without the legend.

Issues:
- The verdict headline is set large and on a phone wraps to two lines; it is
  still smaller than the answer figure. **Open**, intended (DESIGN.md).
- Surcharge kinds below about 1 % (remote area, extended remote area) are
  slivers too thin to see in the split chart, yet listed in the legend. The
  table view has the numbers. **Open**, low.

### Q4, year over year (`q4-*`)

Works:
- "USPS +19.7%" with "$9.17 → $10.98 … announced +16.4 % … 3.3 points more
  than announced" answers the question in one sentence.
- The next-year panel ($11.70 in 2027 at +6.5 %) is raised and separate from
  the chart; the slider is 44 px tall.
- The scale defaults to index on phones, where dollars flatten the USPS slope.
  Points with a note carry "!", and the notes are listed under the chart.

Issues:
- UPS hidden under FedEx in the line chart (finding 4, **fixed**).
- Fuel table not keyboard-scrollable on phones (finding 5, **fixed**).
- The view asks the API twice on open: once with the controls, then with the
  next-year increase the first answer suggests. For about 250 ms the answer is
  dimmed as stale. **Open**, low: no layout shift, and the e2e helpers wait for
  the second answer.
- The driver bars use the warm `--q4-up` colour, close to UPS brown, even when
  the chart is about USPS. The chart title names the carrier and DESIGN.md
  keeps `--q4-up`/`--q4-down` apart from the money colours on purpose.
  **Open**, low; worth revisiting with the palette.
- The page is long on a phone (about 4,500 px). Each block has its own heading
  and the answer is first, so this is acceptable. **Open**.

### Settings sheet on phones (`settings-sheet-mobile-*`)

Works: opens as a modal dialog over a dimmed page, focus starts inside and is
trapped (tested), Escape and "Done" close it and return focus to "Adjust". The
segmented USPS card control and the price input are large; dark mode keeps the
selected state clear (inverted).

Issues: fuel sliders and "Done" were under 44 px (finding 3, **fixed**).

## Loading and empty states

Not in the screenshot set (captures wait for answers), but covered by tests:
Q3 and Q4 show "Load the sample mix or upload a CSV" with both actions before a
set is loaded (`q3-blended.spec.ts`), Q1 keeps the previous answer dimmed while
the next one loads, and a 422 shows the server's message under the weight
input with `aria-invalid` (`q1-quote.spec.ts`).

## Capture notes

- Captures are deterministic in content (fixed sample, fixed controls,
  reduced motion, CSS transitions finished, charts unchanged for five frames,
  fonts loaded, page scrolled to the top). A recapture can still differ by a
  few thousand anti-aliased pixels, so the images are for review, not pixel
  assertions.
- The README images in `docs/screenshots/` are the desktop light captures
  cropped above the footer and resized to 1200 px wide, plus two phone first
  screens, quantised to 256-colour PNG and passed through `optipng`.

127	## surcharges.csv (curated, per carrier)

129	One row per surcharge rule, per year and effective window. A rule applies when
130	every non-empty threshold column is met and the `as_of` date falls inside its
131	window.

135	| carrier | id | |

160	Peak rules apply only when the dashboard's peak toggle is on. Residential rules

165

181	### Engine tests for fuel
182	
183	The rate engine applies the fuel percent to the base rate plus every applied
184	surcharge whose `fuel_applies` is `true`, and to nothing else. Tests use
185	synthetic rows: one surcharge flagged `true`, one flagged `false`, a known
186	percent, and assert the fuel line item equals `percent × (base + flagged)` to
187	the cent, that the slider override replaces the yearly default, and that USPS
188	quotes carry no fuel line.

206	Dimensional weight parameters change over time (USPS moved from 166 to 139
207	on 2026-07-12), so rows carry an effective window and the engine resolves the
208	row by `as_of` date.

223	## Rules that change over time
224	
225	Every parameter that can move a parcel's price is stored per year and per
226	effective window: base rates, surcharge amounts and thresholds, fuel defaults,
227	dimensional-weight divisor and threshold. The engine takes an `as_of` date
228	(default: the year's January effective date) and never hardcodes a value.
229	
230	`uv run python -m data.pipeline.report_changes` diffs consecutive years of
231	every curated table and writes `docs/data/RULE_CHANGES.md`: one line per
232	parameter that changed, with old and new values and the citation. The parser
233	agents must populate every year so this report is complete, and the report is
234	reviewed before the engine is built so year-over-year comparisons account for
235	every change, not only base rates.
236

241	| carrier | id | USPS bands differ from UPS and FedEx bands |

245	| source_file | path | Must be a file listed in the manifest (add a row and run the fetcher; never download by hand) |
246	| source_quote | text | Verbatim |
247	| notes | text | e.g. how a band was derived when the carrier publishes zones only by ZIP pair |

253	| carrier | `usps`, `ups`, `fedex` |
254	| year | or empty |
255	| path | relative to `data/raw/` |

261	| content | one line |
262	
263	`python3 data/fetch_raw.py` restores missing files sequentially with pauses
264	and verifies checksums; issue #13 scripts the discovery that produces this file.
265	
266	## Parcel set input (CSV uploaded in the UI)
267	
268	| Column | Type | Notes |
269	|---|---|---|
270	| weight_lb | decimal | Required |
271	| length_in, width_in, height_in | decimal | Optional; dimensional weight only when all three are present |
272	| distance_miles | int | Required |
273	| residential | bool | Required |
274	| speed | tier | Required |
275	| quantity | int | Optional, default 1 |
276	| price_charged | money | Optional; overrides the flat price control for that row |
277	| delivery_area | enum | Optional: `none` (default), `das`, `extended` |
278	
279	The USPS rate card (`commercial` default, `retail` optional) is a dashboard
280	control, not a parcel column. UPS and FedEx have a single `list` card.

119	def write_table(carrier: str, table: str, rows: Iterable[dict]) -> Path:
120	    """Write rows with the schema's column order. Missing keys become empty strings;
121	    unknown keys are an error so typos cannot slip through."""
122	    columns = COLUMNS[table]
123	    path = processed_path(carrier, table)
124	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
125	    rows = list(rows)
126	    for row in rows:

128	        if unknown:
129	            raise ValueError(f"{table}: unknown columns {sorted(unknown)}")
130	    with path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
131	        writer = csv.DictWriter(handle, fieldnames=columns, lineterminator="\n")
132	        writer.writeheader()

176	    parts: list[str] = []
177	    for ws in sheets:

  with all fetched docs; absence-of-evidence only).
- Peak season: temporary price changes replace the base tables (prices in the "_peak" PDFs/zips are the full tables, not an
  add-on). Windows: 2022-10-02→2023-01-22; none in 2023; 2024-10-06→2025-01-19; 2025-10-05→2026-01-18; 2026-10-04→2027-01-17.
  2026 additionally has the 2026-04-26→2027-01-17 transportation-related increase stacked under the peak prices.

## E. Zone chart

- zones/postalpro_zone_charts_page.html — https://postalpro.usps.com/operations/zone-charts (scraped HTML, 2026-10-22).
  Links to: Domestic Zone Chart tool, "Zone Charts Matrix Technical Guide" (/national-zone-charts-matrix/ZoneChartsMatrixTechnicalGuide,
  effective June 2024 — the link returned an HTML page, not a PDF, so it was not kept), "Zone Charts Order Form" (/Zone_Charts_Order_Form,
  dated 2026-07-12), Zone 10 test files. The full National Zone Charts Matrix (origin ZIP3 x destination ZIP3 → zone) is
  obtained via the order form, not as an open bulk download on that page.
- zones/postcalc_domestic_zone_chart_page.html — https://postcalc.usps.com/DomesticZoneChart (scraped HTML). Form-driven tool:
  given an origin ZIP3 it returns the zone for every destination ZIP3 range (with "same NDC" and 5-digit exceptions), optionally as
  an Excel-formatted table; endpoints seen in the page: `/DomesticZoneChart/GetZoneChart` and `/DomesticZoneChart/GetZone`
  (POST form, chart date selectable). That is the practical free source: ~1,000 ZIP3 requests build the full matrix.
  Zones are distance-based (DMM 608.9 ranges; zone 9 = non-contiguous/territories); not verified here beyond the page text.

## B. Price-file CSV zips (Postal Explorer "Price Files – CSV" / "Notice 123.zip")

Method: direct download from `https://pe.usps.com/resources/PriceChange/<name>` (names below).
Format: ZIP of ~50 CSV files (one per product). Relevant retail files inside each zip:
`PM Retail.csv`, `PME Retail.csv`, and `USPS Ground Advantage Retail.csv` (2023-07 onward) /
`FCPS.csv`, `USPS Retail Ground.csv`, `Parcel Select Ground.csv` (2022-01 … 2023-01).
Also `PM Comm.csv`, `PME Comm.csv`, `USPS Ground Advantage Comm.csv` (commercial, out of scope).

Layout (checked on 2026-10-04 zip): a 1–2 line title row (`Priority Mail - Retail,,Final,,9/14/2026`),
flat-rate rows, then a header `Weight Not Over (Lbs),Zones` / `,Zone 1,…,Zone 9` followed by one row
per weight step (ounces for Ground Advantage: 4, 8, 12, 15.999; then pounds 1–70). ~90 lines per file.
Parse difficulty: **clean CSV, but with irregular preamble rows** — locate the `Zone 1` header row
programmatically, then read the numeric block; a float like `15.999000000000001` appears for the
15.999-oz step. Surcharge footnotes are NOT in the CSVs (they are only in the PDF).

## D. Surcharge rules (what the fetched documents say)

From the Notice 123 PDFs (footnotes beside the Priority Mail / PME / Ground Advantage tables):
- Nonstandard length fees: "Parcels that exceed 22 inches but not greater than 30 inches in length, add $…" and
  "Parcels that exceed 30 inches in length, add $…". Over-30-in amounts seen: $15.00 (2022-01, "Effective April 3, 2022"), $15.00 (2023-07),
  $18.00 (2025-01), $21.00 (2026-07 and 2026-10). Ground Advantage over-30-in: $7.00 (2023-07), $8.40 (2025-01), $10.00 (2026).
- Volume fee: "Parcels that exceed 2 cubic feet (3456 cubic inches), add $…": $15.00 (2022), $25.00 (2023-07 PM/PME),
  $35.00 (2026 PM/PME), $21.00 (2026 Ground Advantage).
  The 22–30 in amounts are in the same footnotes; read them per year from the PDF (not extracted here).
- Dimensional weight: every year's footnote says "Parcels that exceed one cubic foot (1,728 cubic inches) are charged based on
  the actual weight or the dimensional weight, whichever is greater". The divisor and the zone scope are NOT stated in
  Notice 123 (it refers to DMM 123/223). Web summaries say divisor 166 through 2026-07-11 and 139 from 2026-07-12 for
  PME/PM/GA/Parcel Select (the 2026-05-11 press release confirms a divisor change "to industry standards" but does not
  print the number) — **divisor values and zone applicability (zones 1–4 vs 5–9 in earlier years) are unverified from
  saved files; source DMM 123.1.6 / 223.1.6 for the year in question**.
- Residential / delivery-area surcharges: none found in any Notice 123 or press release; the 2023-09-19 release explicitly
  says no extra fees for residential delivery or Saturday delivery. USPS has no such surcharge for retail parcels (consistent
  with all fetched docs; absence-of-evidence only).
- Peak season: temporary price changes replace the base tables (prices in the "_peak" PDFs/zips are the full tables, not an
  add-on). Windows: 2022-10-02→2023-01-22; none in 2023; 2024-10-06→2025-01-19; 2025-10-05→2026-01-18; 2026-10-04→2027-01-17.
  2026 additionally has the 2026-04-26→2027-01-17 transportation-related increase stacked under the peak prices.

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from data.pipeline.common import CARRIERS, processed_path, read_table


def carriers_with_output(table: str) -> list[str]:
    return [carrier for carrier in CARRIERS if processed_path(carrier, table).is_file()]


def pytest_generate_tests(metafunc: pytest.Metafunc) -> None:

        metafunc.parametrize("carrier", list(CARRIERS))

"""Every curated row cites a file, a location and a verbatim quote containing the
amount. This test opens the cited location and checks the quote is really there.
Rows whose raw file has not been fetched are skipped with a message."""
from __future__ import annotations

import pytest

from data.pipeline.common import (
    CARRIERS, COLUMNS, CURATED_TABLES, SURCHARGE_CONDITIONS, normalize_text,
    processed_path, read_table, source_text,
)

AMOUNT_COLUMN = {
    "surcharges": "amount",
    "fuel_surcharge": "default_percent",
    "announced_increase": "percent",
    "dim_weight": "divisor",
}


def curated_rows():
    for carrier in CARRIERS:
        for table in CURATED_TABLES:
            for index, row in enumerate(read_table(processed_path(carrier, table))):
                yield pytest.param(carrier, table, row, id=f"{carrier}-{table}-{index}")
    for index, row in enumerate(read_table(processed_path("shared", "zone_from_distance"))):
        yield pytest.param("shared", "zone_from_distance", row, id=f"zone-{index}")


def amount_variants(value: str) -> set[str]:
    """'6.55' may be printed as '$6.55' or '6.55'; '5.9' as '5.9%'; '166' as '166'."""
    value = value.strip()
    variants = {value}
    try:
        number = float(value)
        if number == int(number):
            variants.add(str(int(number)))
        variants.add(f"{number:.2f}")
        variants.add(f"{number:,.2f}")
    except ValueError:
        pass
    return {v.lower() for v in variants}


@pytest.mark.parametrize("owner,table,row", list(curated_rows()))
def test_quote_is_in_cited_source(owner, table, row):
    assert list(row.keys()) == COLUMNS[table], f"{table} columns differ from schema"
    if table == "surcharges":
        assert row["condition"] in SURCHARGE_CONDITIONS, row["condition"]
    quote = row["source_quote"]
    assert quote.strip(), f"{table}: empty source_quote"
    amount = row.get(AMOUNT_COLUMN.get(table, ""), "")
    if amount:
        assert any(v in quote.lower() for v in amount_variants(amount)), f"quote does not contain the amount {amount}: {quote}"
    ref = row.get("source_page") or row.get("source_ref") or None
    try:
        text = source_text(row["source_file"], ref)
    except FileNotFoundError as error:
        pytest.skip(str(error))
    assert normalize_text(quote) in normalize_text(text), (
        f"quote not found at {row['source_file']} [{ref}]: {quote[:120]}"
    )

"""Hand-checked golden cells must match the parsed output exactly, and every
(service, rate_card, year) must have the mandatory corner cells."""
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from decimal import Decimal
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from data.pipeline.common import ZONES, read_table

GOLDEN_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "golden"
REQUIRED_EXTRA = {"checked_by"}
MIN_CELLS = 5


def golden_rows(carrier: str) -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(GOLDEN_DIR.glob(f"{carrier}_*.csv")):
        rows.extend(read_table(path))
    return rows


def test_golden_cells_match(carrier, base_rates):
    golden = golden_rows(carrier)
    if not golden:
        pytest.fail(f"{carrier}: no golden samples in {GOLDEN_DIR}")
    index = {
        (r["service_id"], r["rate_card"], r["year"], int(r["zone"]), Decimal(r["max_weight_lb"])): r["price"]
        for r in base_rates
    }
    mismatches = []
    for g in golden:
        assert REQUIRED_EXTRA <= set(g), f"golden row lacks {REQUIRED_EXTRA}: {g}"
        key = (g["service_id"], g["rate_card"], g["year"], int(g["zone"]), Decimal(g["max_weight_lb"]))
        parsed = index.get(key)
        if parsed is None or Decimal(parsed) != Decimal(g["price"]):
            mismatches.append((key, g["price"], parsed, g.get("source_ref")))
    assert not mismatches, "golden mismatches (key, expected, parsed, source_ref):\n" + "\n".join(map(str, mismatches))


def test_golden_corner_cells_present(carrier, base_rates):
    golden = golden_rows(carrier)
    by_table = defaultdict(list)
    for g in golden:
        by_table[(g["service_id"], g["rate_card"], g["year"])].append(g)
    parsed_tables = defaultdict(list)
    for r in base_rates:
        parsed_tables[(r["service_id"], r["rate_card"], r["year"])].append(r)
    problems = []
    for key, rows in parsed_tables.items():
        steps = sorted({Decimal(r["max_weight_lb"]) for r in rows})
        zones = sorted({int(r["zone"]) for r in rows} & set(ZONES[carrier]))
        heaviest, lightest, nearest, farthest = steps[-1], steps[0], zones[0], zones[-1]
        cells = {(int(g["zone"]), Decimal(g["max_weight_lb"])) for g in by_table.get(key, [])}
        for name, cell in {
            "heaviest/farthest": (farthest, heaviest),
            "heaviest/nearest": (nearest, heaviest),
            "lightest/farthest": (farthest, lightest),
        }.items():
            if cell not in cells:
                problems.append(f"{key}: missing golden corner {name} = zone {cell[0]}, {cell[1]} lb")
        if len(cells) < MIN_CELLS:
            problems.append(f"{key}: only {len(cells)} golden cells, need {MIN_CELLS}")
    assert not problems, "\n".join(problems)
